"""Conversion-ratio switch: absorbed probe excursion vs swept displacement.

Mechanism
---------
A 100-second path can be decomposed into (i) excursion that was probed but NOT
converted into net displacement (the wicks beyond the bar endpoints, printed on
bars that actually traded size) and (ii) net displacement that WAS realised
(the beta-residual move of the mid).  Empirically the first component precedes
continuation toward the probed side -- the endpoint mid is a stale sample of
where aggression actually reached, and the mid catches up -- while the second is
transient price impact of a level being swept and mean-reverts.  The switch
between the two regimes is the *conversion ratio*

    c = |net residual displacement| / (|net residual displacement| + probed path)

both measured in units of the name's own robust grid quantum (a slowly-varying
low quantile of non-zero absolute returns, deliberately NOT a fast volatility
estimate).  Low c  -> the book absorbed the probes, unfilled pressure remains,
go WITH the excursion side.  High c -> the path was fully converted into a net
move, transient impact dominates, go AGAINST the displacement.  Everything is
scaled by a saturating gate in the volume absorbed over the window relative to
average bar volume, since neither mechanism exists without traded size.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows / positive lags, hence causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_TINY = 1e-12

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)

@register_factor
class ConversionRatioSwitchedProbeExcursionVsSweptDisplacement(BaseFactor):
    """Switch between probe-excursion continuation and swept-level snapback."""
    factor_id = 'conversion_ratio_switched_probe_excursion_vs_swe'
    name = 'Conversion-ratio switch: absorbed probe excursion vs swept displacement'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Blends probe-gated range-normalised wick asymmetry (continuation) with beta-residual net displacement in grid-quantum units (snapback) using weights (1-c) and -c, where c is the fraction of the probed path converted into net residual displacement, scaled by a saturating absorbed-volume gate and ranked cross-sectionally.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _win = 10
    _q_window = 240
    _q_min = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _vol_window = 60
    _adv_window = 240
    _absorb_scale = 1.5
    _shrink = 0.25
    _c_prior = 0.5
    _d_scale = 4.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        absr = ret.abs()
        nz = absr.where(absr > _TINY)
        q = nz.rolling(self._q_window, min_periods=self._q_min).quantile(0.2)
        q = q.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        mkt_bd = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt_bd, self._beta_window)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (ret - beta * mkt_bd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hi_end = _pair_max(open_, close)
        lo_end = _pair_min(open_, close)
        hi = _pair_max(high, hi_end)
        lo = _pair_min(low, lo_end)
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        up_w = (hi - hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_w = (lo_end - lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        asym = ((up_w - dn_w) / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        wick = ((up_w + dn_w) / px).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        med = volume.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=20).median()
        gate = ((volume > med) & med.notna() & volume.notna()).astype(float)
        g = gate.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        a = asym.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        e_num = decay_linear(g * a, self._win)
        e_den = decay_linear(g, self._win)
        chan_e = (e_num / (e_den + self._shrink)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        chan_e = chan_e.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        d_sum = ts_sum(resid.fillna(0.0), self._win) / q
        d_sum = d_sum.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-25.0, 25.0)
        x_sum = ts_sum((wick * g).fillna(0.0), self._win) / q
        x_sum = x_sum.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        c = (d_sum.abs() / (d_sum.abs() + x_sum + self._c_prior)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        chan_d = np.tanh(d_sum / self._d_scale)
        advb = volume.rolling(self._adv_window, min_periods=60).mean()
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_rel = ts_sum(volume.fillna(0.0), self._win) / (float(self._win) * advb)
        a_rel = a_rel.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 100.0)
        gate_abs = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._absorb_scale)
        raw = gate_abs * ((1.0 - c) * chan_e - c * chan_d)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Both parents measure the same 100-second path but different components of it, and their realized (sign-flipped) evidence is only apparently contradictory: heavy-volume wick asymmetry — excursion that was NOT converted into net displacement — precedes continuation toward the probed side (the endpoint mid is a stale sample of where aggression actually reached), while beta-residual net displacement that WAS realised through a level is transient impact and snaps back. The child computes a single scale-free conversion ratio c = |residual net displacement| / (|residual net displacement| + probed excursion path), both in units of the name's own robust grid quantum, and uses it to switch continuously between the two polarities: low c (probe absorbed, no net move) loads long the excursion side, high c (clean sweep, path fully converted) loads against the displacement. The whole thing is scaled by a saturating absorption gate in window volume relative to ADV, because both mechanisms require real traded size to have probed the book. Neither parent can flip sign — each applies one polarity everywhere and therefore averages a continuation regime against a reversion regime, which is exactly why both showed |IC| of only a few basis points with contradicted signs; c is the state variable that separates the two and is only computable from both parents' quantities jointly.
programs.description: Over a trailing 10-bar window: probe-gated, range-normalised wick asymmetry (continuation channel) and beta-residual net displacement in grid-quantum units (snapback channel) are blended with weights (1-c) and -c, where c is the fraction of the probed path converted into net residual displacement, and the blend is scaled by a saturating absorbed-volume gate, then cross-sectionally ranked.

programs.code:
"""Paid/unpaid displacement split, activity-clock wedge, cessation timing.

Mechanism
---------
1. Impact split (parent A machinery).  For each bar, the square-root impact law
   predicts a paid magnitude lambda * sqrt(volume), with lambda estimated per
   name by a trailing through-origin regression of |ret| on sqrt(volume).  The
   paid magnitude is capped at |ret| so that
       ret = paid + unpaid,   sign(paid) = sign(unpaid) = sign(ret),
   i.e. every bar's move is cleanly partitioned into the displacement the flow
   paid for and the mid-price revision it did not pay for.

2. Placement inside the window (parent B machinery), applied to the UNPAID leg.
   The volume-clock minus calendar-clock wedge of the unpaid increments,
       wedge = sum(u * a) / sum(a) - mean(u),
   with a = exp(z-score of log(1+volume)), algebraically cancels the plain
   6-bar unpaid level and isolates WHERE the unpaid displacement was produced
   relative to liquidity demand.  Unpaid displacement created in the busiest
   bars is immediacy overshoot beyond what the impact law justifies (it is given
   back once demand stops); unpaid displacement created in quiet bars is patient
   quote repricing and is retained.  Neither parent can separate these: A's
   residual mixes overshoot with repricing, B's wedge mixes paid impact with
   unpaid overshoot.

3. Timing.  Two trailing state variables set the clock: an extinction gate
   (recent-2-bar activity weight versus the window average, cross-sectionally
   ranked) amplifies the wedge fade, and a burst-cessation clock (recent
   sqrt-volume versus the burst's own prior peak) flips the paid component:
   while one-sided flow still runs the transient over-push is still to be given
   back (fade), once the burst has ceased the transient has already relaxed
   inside the trailing window and only permanent impact remains (continue).

All statistics are trailing rolling windows and non-negative shifts, so the
value at bar t uses only bars <= t.

Falsifiable: if the unpaid-increment wedge carries no forward IC once gated by
extinction, the overshoot-attribution claim is wrong; if the paid leg does not
switch sign with the cessation clock, the relaxation-timing claim is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_max, ts_mean, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sqrt_law_lambda(absret: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing through-origin regression slope of |ret| on sqrt(volume).

    lambda_t = sum(|ret| * w) / sum(w^2) over the trailing n bars.  Causal.
    """
    n = int(n)
    mp = max(20, n // 4)
    num = (absret * w).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum()
    den = (w * w).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _cessation_clock(w: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """1 = the recent volume burst has faded, 0 = flow is still running.

    Compares mean sqrt-volume of the last 2 bars with the max sqrt-volume of
    bars t-2 .. t-(k-1).  Causal (positive shifts / trailing windows only).
    """
    k = int(k)
    recent = ts_mean(w, 2)
    prior = ts_max(w.shift(2), max(2, k - 2))
    denom = prior.where(prior > 0.0, np.nan)
    ratio = (recent / denom).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cess = (1.0 - ratio).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    fallback = (recent <= 0.0).astype(float)
    return cess.where(denom.notna(), fallback)


def _activity_weight(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strictly positive volume-clock weight: exp(trailing z of log1p(volume))."""
    v = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0))
    z = ts_zscore(v, int(n)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-cap, cap)
    return np.exp(z)


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank centred on zero (NaNs propagate)."""
    return rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)) - 0.5


@register_factor
class PaidUnpaidSplitActivityClockWedgeCessation(BaseFactor):
    """Unpaid-overshoot wedge in volume time, timed by flow extinction."""

    factor_id = "paid_unpaid_split_activity_clock_wedge_cessation"
    name = "Paid/unpaid displacement split with activity-clock wedge and cessation timing"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Splits each bar's log return into a capped square-root-law paid part "
        "(per-name lambda from a trailing through-origin regression of |ret| on "
        "sqrt(volume)) and an unpaid residual; combines minus the volume-clock "
        "minus calendar-clock wedge of unpaid increments (amplified when excess "
        "activity just collapsed), minus the unpaid displacement level, and the "
        "paid displacement level signed by a burst-cessation clock."
    )
    window_length = 340
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _lam_win = 240      # trailing window for the per-name sqrt-law slope
    _vol_win = 240      # trailing window for return volatility
    _vol_min = 60
    _act_win = 60       # trailing window for the activity z-score
    _act_cap = 3.0
    _z_clip = 8.0
    _tanh_a = 0.7
    _w_wedge = 1.0
    _w_level = 0.6
    _w_paid = 0.5

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        volume = (
            data["volume"].astype(float)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .abs()
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .fillna(0.0)
            .clip(lower=0.0)
        )

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        p = np.log(px.abs()).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret = p.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        sigma = ret.rolling(self._vol_win, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)

        # ---- square-root-law paid / unpaid split -------------------------
        w = np.sqrt(volume)
        absret = ret.abs()
        lam = _sqrt_law_lambda(absret, w, self._lam_win)
        pred = (lam * w).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        paid_mag = np.minimum(pred, absret)          # cap: paid cannot exceed the move
        paid = np.sign(ret) * paid_mag
        unpaid = ret - paid                          # same sign as ret, >= 0 fraction

        en = (paid / sigma).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-self._z_clip, self._z_clip)
        rn = (unpaid / sigma).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-self._z_clip, self._z_clip)

        # ---- volume-clock weights ---------------------------------------
        a_w = _activity_weight(volume, self._act_win, self._act_cap)
        a_w = a_w.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        valid = rn.notna() & en.notna() & a_w.notna()
        rz = rn.where(valid)
        ez = en.where(valid)
        u = a_w.where(valid)

        cnt = valid.astype(float).rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        full = cnt >= float(h)

        den = ts_sum(u.fillna(0.0), h)
        den_ok = den.where(den > 1e-12)
        cnt_ok = cnt.where(cnt > 0.0)

        # ---- unpaid-increment wedge: volume clock minus calendar clock ----
        num_r = ts_sum((rz * u).fillna(0.0), h)
        r_vol = (num_r / den_ok).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        r_sum = ts_sum(rz.fillna(0.0), h)
        r_time = (r_sum / cnt_ok).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        wedge_unpaid = (r_vol - r_time).where(full)

        # ---- levels -------------------------------------------------------
        scale = math.sqrt(float(h))
        r_level = np.tanh(self._tanh_a * (r_sum / scale)).where(full)
        e_level = np.tanh(self._tanh_a * (ts_sum(ez.fillna(0.0), h) / scale)).where(full)

        # ---- timing states ------------------------------------------------
        recent = ts_sum(u.fillna(0.0), 2) / 2.0
        window_avg = den_ok / float(h)
        share = (recent / window_avg).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(full)
        ext = rank(share * -1.0)                     # 1 = demand just died
        gate = (0.5 + ext).clip(0.0, 1.5)

        cess = _cessation_clock(w, h)
        flip = (2.0 * cess - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)     # +1 ceased, -1 flow running

        # ---- three legs, each cross-sectionally ranked --------------------
        leg_wedge = _centred_rank((wedge_unpaid * -1.0) * gate)
        leg_level = _centred_rank(r_level * -1.0)
        leg_paid = _centred_rank(flip.where(full) * e_level)

        raw = (
            self._w_wedge * leg_wedge.fillna(0.0)
            + self._w_level * leg_level.fillna(0.0)
            + self._w_paid * leg_paid.fillna(0.0)
        )
        any_leg = leg_wedge.notna() | leg_level.notna() | leg_paid.notna()
        raw = raw.where(any_leg)

        sig = rank(raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)) - 0.5
        return (
            sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Paid/unpaid displacement split with activity-clock wedge and cessation timing
programs.trading_idea: Parent A splits each bar's move into the part the square-root impact law says the flow paid for and an unpaid (quote-revision) remainder but only knows WHEN the transient relaxes; parent B knows nothing about how much of a move was paid for but precisely locates WHERE inside the window displacement was produced relative to liquidity demand (a level-cancelling volume-clock minus calendar-clock wedge). The child applies B's wedge to A's *unpaid* increments only: unpaid displacement produced in the name's busiest bars is immediacy overshoot beyond what the impact law justifies and is given back once demand dies, whereas unpaid displacement produced in quiet bars is genuine limit-order repricing and is retained — a distinction neither parent can make, since A's residual leg mixes both and B's wedge mixes paid impact with unpaid overshoot. A's realized (sign-corrected) evidence supplies the two conditioning legs: the unpaid displacement *level* reverts, and the paid (sqrt-law) component reverts while one-sided flow is still running but continues once the burst has ceased, because by then the transient depth-refill has already relaxed inside the trailing window and only permanent impact remains. The interaction — overshoot attribution (paid vs unpaid) × placement in volume-time × flow-cessation clock — times the give-back inside the 6-bar horizon rather than betting on an unconditional reversal.

programs.code:
"""Quiet-Bar Quote Repricing vs Traded-Bar Impact Split.

Trading idea (verbatim): Price changes accumulated in bars with (near-)zero
traded volume are quote-driven repricing: market makers shading their quotes
because of inventory or adverse-selection beliefs that no one has yet traded
against. Price changes accumulated in high-volume bars already contain
temporary impact that mechanically decays. Therefore the same 60-second drift
should be *continued* when it was produced silently and *reverted* when it was
paid for with aggressive volume; the persistence of this split is protected by
the fact that trading the quiet component requires paying spread on thin names.
Falsified if quiet-bar drift is simply stale-mid noise, in which case it reverts
just like traded drift and the two components carry the same sign.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import stddev, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# causal helpers (trailing windows / positive lags only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _rolling_quantile(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, q: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing q-quantile over the last n bars (per name).  Causal by
    construction: pandas rolling windows end at the current bar."""
    mp = max(int(n * 0.5), 10)
    return df.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).quantile(q)


def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row (cross-sectional) robust standardisation: median / MAD, with a
    std fallback when the MAD collapses.  Winsorised at +/-4 sigma so a single
    stale-print name cannot dominate the spread."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    z = dev.div(scale, axis=0)
    return z.clip(-4.0, 4.0)


@register_factor
class QuietQuoteRepricingVsTradedImpactSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Long the drift printed in (near-)zero-volume bars, short the drift paid for with volume."""

    factor_id = "quiet_quote_repricing_vs_traded_impact_split"
    name = "Quiet-Bar Quote Repricing vs Traded-Bar Impact Split"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Splits the last ~30 bars of log returns into quiet bars (volume below "
        "the name's rolling 25th percentile) and active bars, cross-sectionally "
        "standardises each cumulative component, and returns (quiet drift) "
        "minus (active drift) as the score."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # --- parameters ------------------------------------------------------
    _SPLIT_WIN = 30      # bars of drift being decomposed (~5 minutes of 10s bars)
    _VOL_WIN = 150       # trailing window defining each name's own volume regime
    _SIGMA_WIN = 120     # trailing window for per-name return scaling
    _QUANTILE = 0.25     # "quiet" = volume at or below own 25th percentile

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # ---- inputs ------------------------------------------------------
        vol = volume.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = _log_returns(close)

        # per-name return scale so that thin and thick names are comparable
        sigma = stddev(ret.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN)
        sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        r = (ret / sigma).clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- quiet / active bar classification ---------------------------
        thr = _rolling_quantile(vol, self._VOL_WIN, self._QUANTILE)
        # a name with an all-zero trailing volume history gets a zero threshold,
        # which still (correctly) tags its zero-volume bars as quiet
        thr = thr.fillna(0.0)
        quiet = vol <= thr
        active = ~quiet

        r_quiet = r.where(quiet, 0.0)
        r_active = r.where(active, 0.0)

        # ---- cumulative components over the split window -----------------
        n = self._SPLIT_WIN
        quiet_drift = ts_sum(r_quiet, n)
        active_drift = ts_sum(r_active, n)

        # participation counts: normalise each component by sqrt(#bars) so the
        # drift is a per-bar-intensity estimate rather than a count artefact
        q_cnt = ts_sum(quiet.astype(float), n)
        a_cnt = ts_sum(active.astype(float), n)
        quiet_drift = quiet_drift / np.sqrt(q_cnt.clip(lower=1.0))
        active_drift = active_drift / np.sqrt(a_cnt.clip(lower=1.0))

        # a name must actually show both regimes for the split to mean anything
        valid = (q_cnt >= 3.0) & (a_cnt >= 3.0) & sigma.notna()
        quiet_drift = quiet_drift.where(valid)
        active_drift = active_drift.where(valid)

        # ---- cross-sectional standardisation of each leg ------------------
        zq = _cs_robust_z(quiet_drift)
        za = _cs_robust_z(active_drift)

        score = zq - za
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # keep the panel de-meaned cross-sectionally (dollar-neutral-ish score)
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.code:
"""Occupation-density mode pull: drift from the shape of the volume-at-price profile.

Mechanism
---------
For a time-homogeneous one-dimensional diffusion dX = mu(x)dt + sigma(x)dW the
stationary density satisfies

    mu(x) = (sigma^2 / 2) * d ln p(x) / dx      (+ a sigma-gradient term),

so the *local* drift can be estimated non-parametrically from the shape of the
trailing occupation measure of the price, evaluated at the current price.  Here
the occupation measure is built from log prices visited over the last 60 bars,
each weighted by the volume traded in that bar (where resting inventory and
limit-order mass have accumulated) and by an exponential memory decay.  With a
Gaussian kernel K, K'(u) = -u K(u), hence

    d ln p / dx = -(1/h) * sum_k w_k u_k K(u_k) / sum_k w_k K(u_k),
    u_k = (x_t - x_{t-k}) / h,

which is a *saturating* restoring force toward the nearest visited price cluster
rather than a linear pull toward the window mean.  Since the linear
distance-to-VWAP reversal is heavily mined, the kernel drift is regressed per
name on the volume-weighted linear deviation from the same profile over a
trailing 240-bar window and only the residual is kept: the drift content of the
*skew / multimodality* of the occupation profile.  Names whose current price
sits in a low-occupancy void (where the density estimate is unreliable and a
liquidity vacuum may instead produce continuation) are shrunk toward zero.

All estimation is trailing-only: the value at t uses bars <= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_residual, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _occupation_moments(
    x: pd.DataFrame,
    w: pd.DataFrame,
    hband: pd.DataFrame,
    nlag: int,
    tau: float,
):
    """Trailing kernel moments of the volume-weighted occupation measure.

    Returns (num_kernel, den_kernel, den_total, num_linear, count) where
      num_kernel = sum_k w_k K(u_k) u_k,   den_kernel = sum_k w_k K(u_k),
      den_total  = sum_k w_k,              num_linear = sum_k w_k (x_t - x_{t-k}).
    Every term uses positive lags only, so the value at t sees only bars <= t.
    """
    idx, cols = x.index, x.columns
    num_k = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den_k = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den_a = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    num_l = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

    for k in range(1, int(nlag) + 1):
        decay = float(np.exp(-float(k) / float(tau)))
        d = x - x.shift(k)
        wk = w.shift(k) * decay
        u = (d / hband).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        kern = wk * np.exp(-0.5 * u * u)
        valid = d.notna() & wk.notna() & hband.notna()
        num_k = num_k.add((kern * u).where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        den_k = den_k.add(kern.where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        den_a = den_a.add(wk.where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        num_l = num_l.add((wk * d).where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        cnt = cnt.add(valid.astype(float))

    return num_k, den_k, den_a, num_l, cnt


@register_factor
class OccupationDensityModePullProfileSkewWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Fokker-Planck drift read off the volume-at-price occupation density."""

    factor_id = "occupation_density_mode_pull_profile_skew_wedge"
    name = "Occupation-density mode pull (profile skew wedge)"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Gaussian-kernel estimate of the log-gradient of the volume-weighted, "
        "exponentially-decayed occupation density of log price at the current price "
        "(stationary Fokker-Planck drift), volatility-normalised, orthogonalised per "
        "name against the volume-weighted linear deviation from the same profile, and "
        "shrunk where local occupancy is thin."
    )
    window_length = 320
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _nlag = 60          # occupation window (bars) ~ 10 minutes
    _tau = 45.0         # memory decay of the occupation measure (bars)
    _min_obs = 30       # minimum valid lags before the density is trusted
    _vol_window = 240   # trailing window for bar volatility / volume norm
    _vol_min = 60
    _orth_window = 240  # trailing OLS window for the mean-pull orthogonalisation

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        x = np.log(px)
        ret = x.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        # ---- per-bar volatility (units of log return) -------------------
        bar_vol = ret.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        bar_vol = bar_vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- volume weights: relative volume plus a time-occupation floor
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            w = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vol = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            base = ts_mean(vol, self._vol_window).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            rel = (vol / base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 10.0)
            w = rel.fillna(1.0) * 0.75 + 0.25
        w = w.where(px.notna(), 0.25)

        # ---- kernel bandwidth: Silverman-style on trailing price spread --
        px_sd = x.rolling(self._nlag, min_periods=self._min_obs).std()
        h_raw = 1.06 * px_sd * float(self._nlag) ** (-0.2)
        floor = 1.0 * bar_vol
        hband = h_raw.where(h_raw > floor, floor)
        hband = hband.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hband = hband.where(hband > _EPS)

        num_k, den_k, den_a, num_l, cnt = _occupation_moments(
            x, w, hband, self._nlag, self._tau
        )

        enough = cnt >= float(self._min_obs)

        # ---- kernel drift: mu ~ (sigma^2/2) d ln p/dx --------------------
        ratio = (num_k / den_k.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(enough)
        ratio = ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        # H-bar forecast, normalised by sqrt(H)*sigma_bar -> dimensionless
        h_fc = float(self.prediction_horizon)
        scale_const = 0.5 * h_fc / float(np.sqrt(h_fc))
        drift_z = -(scale_const) * (bar_vol / hband) * ratio
        drift_z = drift_z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- linear (mean) pull from the SAME occupation profile ---------
        dev = (num_l / den_a.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(enough)
        lin_z = -dev / (bar_vol * float(np.sqrt(h_fc)))
        lin_z = lin_z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- orthogonalise: keep the profile-SHAPE (skew) component ------
        y = drift_z.where(lin_z.notna())
        xx = lin_z.where(drift_z.notna())
        resid = rolling_residual(y, xx, self._orth_window)
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- confidence gate: local occupancy mass at the current price --
        local_mass = (den_k / den_a.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(enough)
        local_mass = local_mass.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        gate = 0.25 + 1.0 * rank(local_mass).fillna(0.5)

        alive = px.notna() & ret.notna().rolling(6, min_periods=1).sum().gt(0)

        sig = (rank(resid) - 0.5).where(resid.notna())
        sig = (sig * gate).where(alive)
        return (
            sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Occupation-density mode pull (volume-at-price profile skew wedge)
programs.trading_idea: For a one-dimensional diffusion the stationary Fokker-Planck solution implies mu(x) ~ (sigma^2/2) * d ln p(x)/dx, so the local drift of a price can be read off the *shape* of its recent occupation measure rather than from its distance to a mean: price is pulled toward the nearest peak of the trailing volume-at-price density, where resting inventory and limit-order mass have accumulated. I estimate that log-density gradient non-parametrically with a Gaussian kernel over the last 60 bars, weighting each visited price by the volume traded there and by an exponential memory decay, which yields a *saturating* restoring force toward the nearest liquidity cluster instead of a linear pull toward the window mean. Because the linear distance-to-VWAP reversal is heavily mined, I regress the kernel drift on the volume-weighted linear deviation over a trailing 240-bar window and keep only the residual — i.e. the drift information contained in the *skew/multimodality* of the occupation profile — and shrink names whose current price sits in a low-occupancy void, where the density estimate is unreliable. The edge should persist because extracting higher moments of a per-name occupation measure every 10 seconds is computationally awkward relative to the trivial VWAP-gap trade, and the mispricing is of the order of a fraction of the spread, so capacity is small; it is falsified if the residual carries no IC once distance-to-VWAP is removed, or if the low-occupancy gate fails to discriminate.
programs.description: Kernel estimate of the log-gradient of the volume-weighted, exponentially-decayed occupation density of log price at the current price (a drift forecast via the stationary Fokker-Planck relation), volatility-normalised, orthogonalised per name against the volume-weighted linear deviation from the same profile, and shrunk where local occupancy is thin.

programs.code:
"""Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating short-run path efficiency.

Mechanism
---------
At 10-second resolution two very different processes create directional price
paths.  (1) A parent order worked by a VWAP/POV scheduler spreads its child
fills nearly evenly across consecutive bars: the *entropy of the bar-volume
shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level, and
the unfinished remainder of the parent implies the grind continues.  (2) A
one-off liquidity-consuming burst / news print concentrates volume mass in one
or two bars (entropy drops) and the displacement it leaves is mostly transient
impact that decays as depth refills, so it should be faded.

The factor is the product of two *bounded, scale-free* quantities, with no
z-scores, clips or squashing functions:

    * path efficiency  E = net log displacement / total absolute path over the
      same window, in [-1, 1] (Kaufman ratio).  It is large only when the move
      was directional rather than noise, so it self-attenuates on noisy paths.
    * evenness innovation  G = H_norm(30) - mean_120(H_norm(30)), where H_norm
      is the Shannon entropy of the volume shares divided by log(n), in [0, 1].
      Subtracting its own trailing mean centres the gate per name exactly, so
      the gate flips sign across the cross-section and the unconditional
      momentum loading is purged.

Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns do not depend on the interaction between
directional path efficiency and innovations in volume evenness, the
cross-sectional IC of this product is zero.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows: the value at bar t uses only bars
<= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delta, rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_price(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal log mid-price, robust to zero / bad prints."""
    lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return np.log(lvl).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _path_efficiency(logp: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed Kaufman efficiency ratio over a trailing n-bar window.

    net n-bar log displacement divided by the total absolute path travelled.
    Bounded in [-1, 1]: +-1 is a monotone grind, ~0 is a round trip / noise.
    Scale-free and volatility-free, so no variance estimate is needed.
    """
    step = logp.diff()
    net = delta(logp, n)
    path = step.abs().rolling(n, min_periods=n).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = net / path
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

def _normalized_volume_entropy(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shannon entropy of the trailing n-bar volume shares, divided by log(n).

    With p_i = v_i / S and S = sum(v_i):
        H = -sum p_i log p_i = log(S) - (1 / S) * sum(v_i log v_i)
    computed from two trailing rolling sums (v_i log v_i is taken as 0 when
    v_i == 0, the usual 0*log0 convention).  Result lies in [0, 1]: 1 means
    perfectly even participation (scheduler fingerprint), low values mean the
    window's volume was dominated by a few bursty bars.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    tot = ts_sum(v, n)
    vlogv = (v * np.log(v.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)
    s_vlogv = ts_sum(vlogv, n)
    tot_safe = tot.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ent = np.log(tot_safe) - s_vlogv / tot_safe
    ent = ent.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / float(np.log(n))
    return ent.clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class VolumeEvennessEntropyInnovationGatedPathEfficiency(BaseFactor):
    """Grind continued when participation turns even, faded when it bursts."""
    factor_id = 'volume_evenness_entropy_innovation_gated_path_ef'
    name = 'Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = "Cross-sectional rank of (30-bar signed path-efficiency ratio) x (normalized Shannon entropy of the last 30 bars' volume shares minus its own 120-bar mean): extrapolate the drift when participation just turned unusually even, fade it when volume mass just concentrated."
    window_length = 160
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _span = 30
    _norm = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        logp = _log_price(close)
        eff = _path_efficiency(logp, self._span)
        ent = _normalized_volume_entropy(volume, self._span)
        gate = ent - ts_mean(ent, self._norm)
        raw = (eff * gate).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency
programs.trading_idea: A metaorder worked by a scheduler spreads its child fills almost evenly across consecutive 10-second bars, so the *entropy of the bar-volume shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level while price grinds directionally; the unfinished remainder of that parent order makes the grind continue over the next minute. A liquidity-consuming burst or news print does the opposite: volume mass concentrates in one or two bars (entropy drops) and the accompanying displacement is mostly transient impact that decays as depth refills, so the same displacement should be faded. The child keeps the parent's schedule-vs-burst split but expresses both legs with *bounded, scale-free* statistics — normalized Shannon entropy of volume shares (in [0,1]) minus its own trailing mean, times the Kaufman path-efficiency ratio (in [-1,1]) — eliminating the parent's fragile ratio-of-rolling-moments z-scores, clips and tanh that produced the in-sample/out-of-sample collapse. The edge survives arbitrage because detecting a schedule requires per-name conditioning on the *shape* of participation rather than its level, execution algos deliberately randomise size so the residual regularity is small and unrewarding to slow capital, and front-running the remaining children does not eliminate them — each new metaorder regenerates the signal.

programs.code:
"""Conversion-gated activity-attribution polarity switch.

Mechanism
---------
Two state variables, one from each parent, interact:

1. CONVERSION RATIO (parent B).  Over the last 6 bars (horizon-matched to the
   6-bar forecast offset) decompose the path into (i) beta-residual NET
   displacement that was actually realised through the book and (ii) probed
   excursion (wicks beyond the bar endpoints, printed on bars that traded real
   size) that was NOT converted into net displacement.  Both are expressed in
   units of the name's own slowly-varying grid quantum (a low quantile of
   non-zero absolute returns).  c = |D| / (|D| + X + prior) is the fraction of
   the probed path that was converted, i.e. the degree to which the move was
   *paid for* by sweeping levels.

2. ACTIVITY ATTRIBUTION (parent A).  Trailing z-scores of log(1+volume) give a
   per-name busyness innovation; its contemporaneous cross-sectional mean is the
   COMMON component (index / ETF / macro basket sweeps) and the name's excess
   over it is the IDIOSYNCRATIC component.  Residual increments are averaged
   with each of these non-negative weights, yielding a common-funded and an
   idio-funded displacement channel, plus an idiosyncratic activity share.

The polarity switch: when c is HIGH the path was converted into a genuine net
move, so the attribution decides its fate -- idio-funded displacement is the
transient impact of one participant's metaorder slice consuming depth and
relaxes at second scales (short it), while common-funded displacement is
staggered adjustment to information the whole cross-section is trading and
continues (long it).  When c is LOW there is no realised impact to relax; the
relevant object is B's confirmed leg -- continuation toward the side that was
probed but absorbed -- and it is only informative when the probing was
idiosyncratic, so it is scaled by the idio activity share.  Everything is
multiplied by a saturating gate in window volume relative to average bar volume,
since neither mechanism exists without traded size.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows / positive lags, hence causal.

Falsifiable: if the high-c attribution contrast (common minus idio) carries no
IC, or if the low-c excursion leg does not need the idio-share gate, the
conversion-state routing of the commonality attribution is wrong.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_TINY = 1e-12

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar series across all tickers (contemporaneous, causal)."""
    arr = np.repeat(s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)

@register_factor
class ConversionGatedActivityAttributionPolarityH6(BaseFactor):
    """Conversion state routes the idio/common activity attribution polarity."""
    factor_id = 'conversion_gated_activity_attribution_polarity_h'
    name = 'Conversion-gated activity-attribution polarity switch'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of an absorbed-volume-gated blend of c*(common-activity-weighted minus idiosyncratic-activity-weighted residual displacement) and (1-c)*idio-share*volume-gated wick asymmetry, where c is the fraction of the 6-bar probed path converted into net beta-residual displacement in grid-quantum units.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _win = 6
    _q_window = 240
    _q_min = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _act_window = 60
    _vol_window = 60
    _adv_window = 240
    _adv_min = 60
    _absorb_scale = 1.5
    _weight_prior = 1.5
    _c_prior = 0.5
    _d_scale = 2.0
    _shrink = 0.25
    _cap = 6.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        absr = ret.abs()
        nz = absr.where(absr > _TINY)
        q = nz.rolling(self._q_window, min_periods=self._q_min).quantile(0.2)
        q = q.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        mkt_bd = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt_bd, self._beta_window)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (ret - beta * mkt_bd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        dxn = (resid / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-20.0, 20.0)
        valid = dxn.notna()
        dxn0 = dxn.fillna(0.0)
        v = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0))
        z = ts_zscore(v, self._act_window).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        z = z.clip(-self._cap, self._cap)
        mact = z.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
        mact_bd = _broadcast(mact.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        common_w = mact_bd.clip(lower=0.0).where(z.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        idio_w = (z - mact_bd).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        w = int(self._win)
        s_i = ts_sum(idio_w, w)
        s_c = ts_sum(common_w, w)
        prior = float(self._weight_prior)
        d_idio = (ts_sum(dxn0 * idio_w, w) / (s_i + prior)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        d_comm = (ts_sum(dxn0 * common_w, w) / (s_c + prior)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        chan_i = np.tanh(d_idio / self._d_scale)
        chan_c = np.tanh(d_comm / self._d_scale)
        share = ((s_i + 0.5 * prior) / (s_i + s_c + prior)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        u = (2.0 * share - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        hi_end = _pair_max(open_, close)
        lo_end = _pair_min(open_, close)
        hi = _pair_max(high, hi_end)
        lo = _pair_min(low, lo_end)
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        up_w = (hi - hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_w = (lo_end - lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        asym = ((up_w - dn_w) / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        wick = ((up_w + dn_w) / px).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        med = volume.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=20).median()
        gate = ((volume > med) & med.notna() & volume.notna()).astype(float)
        g = gate.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        a = asym.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        e_num = decay_linear(g * a, w)
        e_den = decay_linear(g, w)
        chan_e = (e_num / (e_den + self._shrink)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        chan_e = chan_e.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        d_sum = (ts_sum(resid.fillna(0.0), w) / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        d_sum = d_sum.clip(-25.0, 25.0)
        x_sum = (ts_sum((wick * g).fillna(0.0), w) / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        x_sum = x_sum.clip(0.0, 50.0)
        c = (d_sum.abs() / (d_sum.abs() + x_sum + self._c_prior)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        advb = volume.rolling(self._adv_window, min_periods=self._adv_min).mean()
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_rel = (ts_sum(volume.fillna(0.0), w) / (float(w) * advb)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        a_rel = a_rel.clip(0.0, 100.0)
        gate_abs = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._absorb_scale)
        swept = c * (chan_c - chan_i)
        absorbed = (1.0 - c) * u.clip(lower=0.0) * chan_e
        raw = gate_abs * (swept + absorbed)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        support = valid.rolling(w, min_periods=w).sum()
        raw = raw.where((support >= float(w)) & q.notna() & z.notna() & c.notna())
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Conversion-gated activity-attribution polarity switch
programs.trading_idea: Parent A showed that at 10-second scale a name's displacement funded by its OWN excess trading relaxes (transient Bouchaud impact of a metaorder slice consuming depth), while displacement that arrived on market-wide synchronous bursts persists (staggered adjustment to common information — the Epps effect means slow names are still catching up), which is exactly why A's declared idio-continuation sign was contradicted. Parent B showed that this only matters when the path was actually CONVERTED into net displacement (high conversion ratio c = paid-for sweep); when c is low the probed excursion was absorbed and the endpoint mid is a stale sample, so the mechanism is continuation toward the probed side instead. The child therefore uses B's conversion ratio as the state variable that switches A's attribution machinery on and off: in high-c (swept) states it goes SHORT the idio-activity-weighted residual displacement and LONG the common-activity-weighted residual displacement; in low-c (absorbed) states it drops the attribution contrast entirely and loads the volume-gated wick-asymmetry continuation, but only for names whose probing was idiosyncratic (a market-wide synchronous probe carries no relative-value information). The interaction is the edge: A diluted its attribution contrast across absorbed states where there is no impact to relax, and B applied a single displacement polarity everywhere because it cannot see who funded the sweep.
programs.description: Over a horizon-matched 6-bar window, computes the conversion ratio c = |beta-residual net displacement| / (|displacement| + probed unconverted excursion) in grid-quantum units, and the idiosyncratic- vs common-activity-weighted mean residual increments (weights from trailing volume z-scores and their cross-sectional mean); the signal is an absorbed-volume-gated blend of c*(common-weighted minus idio-weighted displacement) and (1-c)*idio-share*wick asymmetry, ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Activity-commonality split displacement contrast.

Mechanism
---------
At 10-second resolution a mid-price increment can be produced by two very
different kinds of trading:

1. COMMON liquidity demand -- the whole cross-section is busy at the same
   instant (index / ETF / macro-driven basket sweeps).  The displacement such
   flow produces is, in relative-value terms, mechanical: it is transient
   under the Bouchaud propagator (depth refills, the basket trade ends) and
   the induced relative-price distortion overshoots and relaxes.

2. IDIOSYNCRATIC liquidity demand -- only this name is unusually busy while
   the panel is quiet.  That is the signature of a name-specific metaorder or
   of name-specific news being traded; order-flow imbalance is strongly
   autocorrelated (Lillo-Farmer), so the flow is unfinished and the
   displacement continues.

The parent factor lumped both sources together and its realized IC was
negative at the 6-bar horizon -- i.e. the common/transient component
dominated the *level* of fresh volume-weighted displacement.  This child does
not flip a sign: it attributes each increment to a source and takes the
CONTRAST between the idio-weighted and the common-weighted mean increment.
Because both averages are weighted means of the SAME normalised increments,
the aggregate displacement level (the heavily mined reversal carrier) largely
cancels, and what remains is the attribution itself.  Both legs push the
signal the same way: idio-funded displacement should continue (+), and
common-funded displacement should relax (so subtracting it is also +).

Estimation is fully causal: activity innovations are trailing z-scores of
log(1+volume); the common component at bar t is the cross-sectional mean of
those innovations at bar t (contemporaneous across names, never forward in
time); the idiosyncratic component is the name's excess over it.

Falsifiable: if the idio-weighted and common-weighted legs carry the same IC
sign, or the contrast has zero IC at 6 bars, the common-vs-idiosyncratic
attribution of fast repricing is wrong.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, stddev, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _normalised_increments(close: pd.DataFrame, n: int, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing-vol-normalised log price increments, winsorised at +-cap.

    Normalisation makes increments comparable across names so a weighted mean
    of them can be ranked cross-sectionally.  Causal: only trailing stddev.
    """
    lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    dx = np.log(lvl).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    sd = stddev(dx, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = (dx / sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return out.clip(-cap, cap)

def _activity_innovation(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing z-score of log(1+volume): how busy a name is versus its norm."""
    v = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0))
    z = ts_zscore(v, n).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return z.clip(-cap, cap)

def _weighted_mean_increment(dx: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Weighted mean of dx over the trailing n bars with non-negative weights.

    Returns NaN when no weight accumulated (no evidence of that activity type),
    which the caller maps to zero contribution.
    """
    num = ts_sum(dx * w, n)
    den = ts_sum(w, n)
    den = den.where(den > 1e-08)
    return (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

@register_factor
class ActivityCommonalitySplitDisplacementContrastH6(BaseFactor):
    """Idio-activity-funded minus common-activity-funded fresh displacement."""
    factor_id = 'activity_commonality_split_displacement_contrast'
    name = 'Activity-commonality split displacement contrast'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of the difference between the idiosyncratic-activity-weighted and the common-activity-weighted mean normalised log increment over the last 6 bars: long names whose fresh move was funded by their own excess trading, short names whose fresh move arrived on market-wide bursts.'
    window_length = 66
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _fast = 6
    _base = 60
    _cap = 6.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        dxn = _normalised_increments(close, self._base, self._cap)
        valid = dxn.notna()
        dxn_f = dxn.fillna(0.0)
        za = _activity_innovation(volume, self._base, self._cap)
        mkt = za.mean(axis=1)
        common = za.notna().astype(float).mul(mkt, axis=0)
        common = common.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        idio = za.sub(mkt, axis=0).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        idio_disp = _weighted_mean_increment(dxn_f, idio, self._fast)
        comm_disp = _weighted_mean_increment(dxn_f, common, self._fast)
        raw = idio_disp.fillna(0.0) - comm_disp.fillna(0.0)
        support = valid.rolling(self._fast, min_periods=self._fast).sum()
        raw = raw.where((support >= float(self._fast)) & za.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Activity-commonality split displacement contrast
programs.trading_idea: The parent showed that *total* fresh volume-weighted displacement reverses at the 6-bar horizon, which is exactly what you expect if a large share of fast repricing is mechanical basket/liquidity-demand pressure rather than name-specific information. I therefore split each name's recent displacement by the *contemporaneous source of the activity that produced it*: increments that arrived while the whole cross-section was simultaneously busy (common liquidity demand — index/ETF/macro sweeps) are largely transient under the Bouchaud propagator and overshoot in relative-value terms, whereas increments that arrived while only this name was unusually busy reflect an idiosyncratic metaorder whose order flow is strongly autocorrelated at second scales and keeps arriving. The factor is the contrast between the idio-activity-weighted and the common-activity-weighted mean normalised increment over the last 6 bars, so the level of aggregate displacement (the already-mined reversal carrier) largely cancels and only the attribution survives. Falsifiable: if the two legs have the same IC sign, or the contrast has zero IC, the common-vs-idiosyncratic attribution of fast repricing is wrong; the edge survives arbitrage because deciding in real time whether a 10-second move was funded by basket flow requires panel-wide synchronisation and its correction offers only one-minute, spread-limited capacity.
programs.description: For each name, normalised log-price increments over the last 6 bars are averaged twice: once weighted by the cross-sectionally common part of contemporaneous volume-activity innovation, once by the name's idiosyncratic excess activity; the signal is the cross-sectional rank of (idiosyncratic-weighted minus common-weighted) mean increment.
