"""Out-of-sample hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation.

Mechanism
---------
A short-run single-name move splits into a peer-common part (the leave-one-out
industry basket move, scaled by a trailing beta) and a peer-idiosyncratic
residual.  Liquidity providers can only warehouse -- and therefore repair --
the residual when the peer basket genuinely replicates the name; the honest
measure of that is the *out-of-sample* replication quality of the hedge,
i.e. one minus the ratio of lagged-beta residual mean square to own return
mean square, estimated on a window that ends before the impulse.

Two statistical choices follow directly from the mechanism:

  * The beta used to build the residual is computed from data ending H=6 bars
    before the impulse window, so the 6-bar residual is a genuine out-of-sample
    dislocation rather than an in-sample residual that is mechanically
    orthogonal to the basket and whose persistence is biased downwards.
  * The impulse is HORIZON-SYMMETRIC: the residual is cumulated over exactly
    H=6 bars, matching the fixed 6-bar forecast offset.

The loading is a pure interaction: the centred cross-sectional rank of hedge
precision multiplies the (negated) residual, so high-precision names are
forecast to mean-revert and high-basis-risk names to continue.  This makes the
factor close to orthogonal to plain reversal and falsifiable in both halves of
the cross-section.

Causality: all cross-sectional statistics are taken within one timestamp; all
time-series statistics are trailing rolling windows or positive lags.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker peer-group key: industry when present, else sector."""
    labels = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _loo_mean(a: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-group mean of ``a`` EXCLUDING the name itself (leave-one-out)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in a.columns]
        if not cols:
            continue
        sub = a[cols]
        present = sub.notna().to_numpy().astype(float)
        vals = sub.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        tot = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        cnt = present.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        excl_sum = tot - vals
        excl_cnt = cnt - present
        ok = excl_cnt >= float(min_peers)
        safe = np.where(excl_cnt > 0.0, excl_cnt, 1.0)
        res = np.where(ok, excl_sum / safe, np.nan)
        out[cols] = pd.DataFrame(res, index=a.index, columns=cols)
    return out


@register_factor
class OosHedgePrecisionSignFlipPeerResidual(BaseFactor):
    """Peer-residual dislocation whose loading flips with out-of-sample hedge precision."""

    factor_id = "oos_hedge_precision_signflip_peer_residual_h6"
    name = "OOS hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Minus the 6-bar cumulative leave-one-out industry-basket residual return "
        "(beta from data ending 6 bars earlier) times the centred cross-sectional "
        "rank of trailing out-of-sample hedge precision, so well-replicated names "
        "are forecast to revert and high-basis-risk names to continue."
    )
    window_length = 600
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6
    _MIN_PEERS = 3
    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _Q_WIN = 180
    _Q_MIN = 60
    _SD_WIN = 360
    _SD_MIN = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        H = self._H

        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"))

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # Peer-common channel: leave-one-out industry basket return.
        rp = _loo_mean(r, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        rp = rp.where(np.isfinite(rp))

        # Beta estimated on a window ending H bars before now => residual is OOS.
        beta = rolling_beta(r, rp, self._BETA_WIN)
        beta = beta.where(np.isfinite(beta)).clip(-4.0, 4.0).shift(H)

        u = r - beta * rp                    # out-of-sample one-bar residual
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u))

        # Horizon-symmetric impulse: H-bar cumulative residual, vol standardised.
        e = u.rolling(H, min_periods=H).sum()
        sd = e.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = e / sd
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # Hedge precision = trailing out-of-sample predictive R^2 of the basket,
        # measured strictly before the impulse window (shifted by H bars).
        ms_u = (u * u).rolling(self._Q_WIN, min_periods=self._Q_MIN).mean().shift(H)
        ms_r = (r * r).rolling(self._Q_WIN, min_periods=self._Q_MIN).mean().shift(H)
        q = 1.0 - ms_u / ms_r.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        q = q.where(np.isfinite(q)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # Hedge legs must be tradable right now: peer basket traded in last H bars.
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            live = pd.DataFrame(True, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0), 0.0)
            v6 = ts_sum(v, H)
            peer_v = _loo_mean(v6, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
            live = peer_v.fillna(0.0) > 0.0

        valid = z.notna() & q.notna() & live
        if valid.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        gate = rank(q.where(valid)) - 0.5      # in [-0.5, 0.5], sign-flexible loading
        sig = (-z.where(valid)) * (2.0 * gate)
        sig = sig.where(np.isfinite(sig))

        out = rank(sig) - 0.5
        out = out.where(sig.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: OOS hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation
programs.trading_idea: A dealer will only absorb (and therefore repair) a single-name dislocation if the peer basket actually replicates that name, and the honest measure of replication is *out-of-sample* basis risk, not in-sample fit: residuals taken with a beta estimated on data ending before the impulse retain the true dislocation, whereas in-sample residuals are mechanically orthogonalised and their persistence is biased away. So the child conditions on trailing predictive R-squared of the leave-one-out industry basket for the name (1 - MSE of lagged-beta residuals / own return variance), measured strictly before the impulse window: where hedge precision is high the 6-bar idiosyncratic residual is cheap inventory and snaps back within the same 6-bar clock, where basis risk is large the same residual is unhedgeable information and continues. The factor is therefore a pure interaction (signed by the cross-sectional rank of hedge precision), which makes it nearly orthogonal to plain reversal and falsifiable in two directions at once: if the interaction is noise, both halves of the cross-section should show the same sign. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a basis-risk/capital constraint on the liquidity provider, not a mispricing: nobody can warehouse a residual whose hedge does not track it, and that condition is measured, not assumed.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of minus the 6-bar cumulative leave-one-out-industry-basket residual return (beta estimated from data ending 6 bars earlier, so the residual is out-of-sample), multiplied by the centred cross-sectional rank of trailing out-of-sample hedge precision (1 - residual MSE / return MSE, lagged 6 bars), so reversal is expressed for well-replicated names and continuation for high-basis-risk names; restricted to names whose peer basket actually traded in the last 6 bars.

programs.code:
"""Valuation-peer propagator split: quiet repricing vs traded impact.

Mechanism
---------
The parent (valuation-tier peer impulse x trade-confirmation) realised an IC of
the opposite sign to its declared direction, and the honest reading of that
result is the *propagator* one, not the information one:

1. Comparability is kept from the parent: names are grouped by sector x half of
   a slow log-multiple level built from close over point-in-time per-share
   fundamentals (book / revenue / operating cash flow per share).  Peer-median
   subtraction removes common factor and sector-wide moves so that what is left
   is idiosyncratic mid displacement.

2. Each *bar's* peer-residual log return is attributed between liquidity demand
   and quote revision by the bar's participation share
   g = v / (v + trailing mean v):  g -> 0 for a bar in which nothing printed,
   g -> 1 for a burst bar.  a = u * g is the trade-attributable displacement
   (transient impact in the Obizhaeva-Wang / Bouchaud propagator sense);
   b = u * (1 - g) is the quiet quote-driven displacement (permanent).

3. For an exponentially decaying transient impact with timescale tau, the amount
   of impact from s bars ago that is still *left to relax* over the next h bars
   is proportional to exp(-s/tau).  Both legs are therefore accumulated with an
   exponential kernel of halflife 3 bars, which concentrates the signal on
   impact whose relaxation lands inside the fixed 6-bar forecast offset (the
   parent's 6-bar block sums peaked at 12 bars instead).

4. Each leg is z-scored by its own trailing volatility (so the wedge is not
   dominated by whichever leg carries more variance) and the signal is
   quiet_leg - traded_leg: long quiet up-displacement (continues), short
   trade-driven up-displacement (relaxes).

All statistics are causal: cross-sectional operations act within a single
timestamp; time-series operations use trailing windows and positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None, industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker coarse peer label: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _log_multiple(px: pd.DataFrame, per_share: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """log(price / per-share fundamental), masked to strictly positive inputs."""
    denom = per_share.where(np.isfinite(per_share) & (per_share > 0.0))
    ratio = px / denom
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)


def _masked_row_median(x: np.ndarray, mask: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    vals = np.where(mask, x, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        med = np.nanmedian(vals, axis=1)
    return med


def _group_median_and_count(x: pd.DataFrame, key_arr: np.ndarray) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-group median and live count for a time-varying grouping."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    med = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros(arr.shape)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    for k in np.unique(key_arr):
        m = key_arr == k
        if not m.any():
            continue
        sel = m & finite
        row_med = _masked_row_median(arr, sel)
        row_cnt = sel.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        med_b = np.broadcast_to(row_med[:, None], arr.shape)
        cnt_b = np.broadcast_to(row_cnt[:, None], arr.shape)
        med[m] = med_b[m]
        cnt[m] = cnt_b[m]
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)
    return (med_df, cnt_df)


@register_factor
class ValuationPeerPropagatorSplitRelaxationWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Quiet-vs-traded split of peer-residual displacement, propagator weighted."""

    factor_id = 'valuation_peer_propagator_split_relaxation_wedge'
    name = 'Valuation-peer propagator split relaxation wedge'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Splits each bar of peer-residual log return (peers = sector x valuation '
        'half from point-in-time per-share multiples) into a trade-attributable '
        'part (bar participation share v/(v+trailing mean v)) and a quiet part, '
        'accumulates both with an exponential propagator-decay kernel (halflife 3 '
        'bars), z-scores each leg by its own trailing volatility, and ranks '
        'quiet-leg minus traded-leg: quiet displacement is permanent and extends, '
        'trade-driven displacement is transient impact and relaxes.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare',
              'operatingCashFlowPerShare', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _LEVEL_HALFLIFE = 240.0
    _LEVEL_MIN = 30
    _N_TIERS = 2
    _VOL_BASE_WINDOW = 120
    _VOL_BASE_MIN = 30
    _KERNEL_HALFLIFE = 3.0
    _KERNEL_MIN = 6
    _SD_WINDOW = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _MIN_PEERS = 3

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            return zero
        volume = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))

        # ---- comparability: sector x valuation half -------------------------
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        lvl_sum = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        lvl_cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for field in ('bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'operatingCashFlowPerShare'):
            raw = data.get(field)
            if raw is None:
                continue
            per_share = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            if per_share.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            lm = _log_multiple(px, per_share)
            lvl_sum = lvl_sum.add(lm.fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
            lvl_cnt = lvl_cnt.add(lm.notna().astype(float), fill_value=0.0)
        level = lvl_sum / lvl_cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        level_sm = level.ewm(halflife=self._LEVEL_HALFLIFE,
                            min_periods=self._LEVEL_MIN, adjust=False).mean()

        sec_codes, uniques = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(cols).values)
        n_tiers = int(self._N_TIERS)
        tier = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for s in range(len(uniques)):
            colmask = np.asarray(sec_codes) == s
            sub_cols = cols[colmask]
            if len(sub_cols) == 0:
                continue
            sub = level_sm[sub_cols]
            if len(sub_cols) < 2 * n_tiers:
                t = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=sub_cols)
                t = t.where(sub.notna(), 0.0)
            else:
                rk = sub.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
                t = np.ceil(rk * float(n_tiers)).clip(1.0, float(n_tiers))
                t = t.fillna(0.0)
            tier.loc[:, sub_cols] = t.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        key_arr = (np.asarray(sec_codes, dtype=np.int64)[None, :] * (n_tiers + 1)
                   + tier.to_numpy(dtype=np.int64))

        # ---- bar-level peer-residual displacement --------------------------
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))
        med_r, cnt_r = _group_median_and_count(r, key_arr)
        u = r - med_r

        # ---- participation share: how much of the bar was actually traded ---
        vol = volume.where(np.isfinite(volume) & (volume >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        base = vol.rolling(self._VOL_BASE_WINDOW, min_periods=self._VOL_BASE_MIN).mean()
        base = base.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g = vol / (vol + base)
        g = g.where(np.isfinite(g)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        traded = u * g
        quiet = u * (1.0 - g)

        # ---- propagator remaining-decay kernel -----------------------------
        a = traded.ewm(halflife=self._KERNEL_HALFLIFE,
                       min_periods=self._KERNEL_MIN, adjust=True).mean()
        b = quiet.ewm(halflife=self._KERNEL_HALFLIFE,
                      min_periods=self._KERNEL_MIN, adjust=True).mean()

        sd_a = a.rolling(self._SD_WINDOW, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sd_b = b.rolling(self._SD_WINDOW, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_z = (a / sd_a).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        b_z = (b / sd_b).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        signal = b_z - a_z
        signal = signal.where(cnt_r >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Valuation-peer propagator split: quiet-repricing vs traded-impact relaxation wedge
programs.trading_idea: The parent's evaluation showed a robust interaction but the *opposite* sign to the one declared, and the correct reading is the propagator (Obizhaeva-Wang / Bouchaud) one rather than the information one: bar-level mid displacement that arrives together with abnormal trade volume is mostly *transient* price impact from liquidity demand (metaorder slices, inventory offloading) and mechanically relaxes as the book refills, whereas displacement that arrives with little or no trade is pure quote-driven revision of the market-maker's belief, which is permanent and tends to be extended by the follow-on latent flow. So the correct object is not a product of two noisy ranks but a *decomposition*: split each bar's peer-residual return into a trade-attributable and a quiet part using the bar's participation share v/(v+trailing mean v), then weight past bars by the propagator's remaining-decay kernel (exponential, halflife 3 bars) so the signal is dominated by impact that still has most of its relaxation ahead of it inside the next ~60 seconds — this is what moves the peak IC from 12 bars to the fixed 6-bar offset. The edge persists because harvesting it means supplying liquidity against possibly-informed bursts (you are paid the impact-decay premium for bearing that adverse-selection risk), and because it requires joining point-in-time per-share fundamentals (to build valuation-tier comparability groups that strip common factor moves) with bar-level trade attribution — microstructure desks never build the fundamental peer map and fundamental relative-value desks cannot act in a minute. Falsified if the trade-attributable and quiet components of the same peer-residual displacement carry the same forward coefficient at 6 bars, or if the wedge disappears once peers are formed by sector text alone.
programs.description: Within sector x valuation-half peer groups (valuation level = slow mean of log price-to-per-share multiples), each bar's peer-residual log return is split into a trade-attributable part (weighted by the bar's volume participation share v/(v+trailing mean v)) and a quiet part (the complement), each accumulated with an exponential propagator-decay kernel (halflife 3 bars) and z-scored by its own trailing volatility; the factor is the cross-sectional rank of quiet-leg minus traded-leg, i.e. long names whose recent displacement was quiet (permanent) and short names whose recent displacement was trade-driven (transient).

programs.code:
"""Depth-gated fresh wick asymmetry: absorbed probes drift toward the untested side.

Mechanism
---------
Hidden resting liquidity (icebergs, rapidly refreshed passive size) is revealed by
*volume per unit displacement*, not volume alone.  A bar that trades unusually heavy
size while covering an unusually small range had a deep, mostly invisible queue in it.
The bar's failed-excursion asymmetry -- upper wick minus lower wick, divided by the bar
range so the statistic is scale-free and needs no estimated diffusion scale -- says which
side hosted that queue.  Gating the asymmetry by relative depth separates genuine
absorption from mid-quote flicker, and because the surviving queue only lives for a few
bars the aggregation is deliberately fresh (exponential halflife of 2 bars) so the signal
is informative at the fixed ~1-minute (6-bar) offset rather than smeared over minutes.

Simplifications relative to the parent (which overfit in-sample): no rolling MAD/std
diffusion estimator, no price-unit conversion, no volume-share fallback branch, no
winsorising ladder -- one bounded shape statistic, one bounded gate, one fast average.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _emax(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _emin(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


@register_factor
class AbsorptionDepthGatedWickAsymmetryFresh(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh, depth-gated wick asymmetry: short recently absorbed upside probes."""

    factor_id = "absorption_depth_gated_wick_asymmetry_fresh"
    name = "Depth-gated fresh wick asymmetry (absorption imbalance)"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Range-normalised wick asymmetry per bar, multiplied by a relative-depth gate "
        "(relative volume divided by relative range vs each name's 60-bar norm), "
        "exponentially weighted with a 2-bar halflife, then cross-sectionally ranked "
        "with a negative sign: absorbed upside probes score low."
    )
    window_length = 80
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _norm_window = 60   # bars used to normalise volume and range per name
    _halflife = 2.0     # bars; keeps the reading fresh for a 6-bar forecast
    _depth_cap = 4.0    # bound on the depth gate

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).abs().reindex_like(close)

        # geometrically consistent bar: high >= endpoints >= low
        hi_end = _emax(open_, close)
        lo_end = _emin(open_, close)
        hi = _emax(high, hi_end)
        lo = _emin(low, lo_end)

        rng = (hi - lo).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # bounded shape statistic in [-1, 1]: +1 => all of the range was a failed
        # upside probe, -1 => all of it was a failed downside probe
        wedge = ((hi - hi_end) - (lo_end - lo)) / rng

        # relative depth = (volume vs own norm) / (range vs own norm)
        lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rng_rel = rng / lvl
        n = self._norm_window
        rel_v = volume / ts_mean(volume, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rel_r = rng_rel / ts_mean(rng_rel, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        depth = (rel_v / rel_r.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        depth = depth.clip(0.0, self._depth_cap).fillna(1.0)

        x = (wedge * depth).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fresh = x.ewm(halflife=self._halflife, min_periods=3).mean()

        signal = rank(-fresh)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Depth-gated fresh wick asymmetry (absorption imbalance)
programs.trading_idea: Hidden resting liquidity is identified not by volume alone but by volume traded per unit of price displacement: a bar that absorbs unusually heavy flow while travelling an unusually small range is a bar in which a deep, largely invisible queue sat in the book. Conditioning the bar's failed-excursion asymmetry (upper wick minus lower wick, expressed as a fraction of the bar range, so it is a scale-free shape statistic needing no diffusion-scale estimate) on this Kyle-inverse depth measure isolates probes that were genuinely absorbed rather than mid-quote flicker; the surviving iceberg keeps capping the probed side for the next few bars, so price drifts toward the untested side. Because the effect lives in the residual life of a specific hidden queue, it decays in seconds, so the child weights only the freshest bars (exponential halflife of 2 bars) instead of smearing 18 bars — which is why the parent's edge leaked out to 24 bars and was weak at the fixed 6-bar offset. It persists against arbitrage because the size being inferred is never quoted: exploiting it requires crossing the spread against concealed depth, a cost that quote-only statistical arbitrageurs will not pay. Falsified if depth-gated wick asymmetry carries no more forward sign than raw volume-weighted wick asymmetry, i.e. if the interaction with volume-per-range is flat.
programs.description: Per bar computes range-normalised wick asymmetry ((high-max(open,close)) - (min(open,close)-low)) / (high-low), multiplies it by a relative-depth gate (bar volume relative to its 60-bar norm divided by relative bar range), exponentially weights the last few bars (halflife 2), and returns the cross-sectional rank of the negative: rejected, absorbed upside probes score low.

programs.code:
"""Square-root-law weighted flow-pressure freshness wedge.

Mechanism
---------
Two well-documented microstructure regularities are combined:

1. Square-root impact law: the price displacement attributable to executed
   volume Q scales like sqrt(Q).  Hence a bar's *informational weight* about
   directional pressure is sqrt(volume) -- linear volume weighting lets one
   giant print dominate, equal weighting throws the volume information away.

2. Transient-impact propagator (Bouchaud et al.): impact from volume executed
   several bars ago decays as depth refills, whereas order-flow imbalance
   itself is strongly autocorrelated (Lillo-Farmer), i.e. flow arriving in the
   last few bars is mostly *unfinished* and keeps arriving.

So the informative object is not the level of one-sided pressure but its
freshness: the sqrt-volume-weighted directional consistency over a fast window
matched to the forecast horizon MINUS the same statistic over a slow window.
The fast term captures unfinished flow that should continue; subtracting the
slow term purges displacement that has already been impacted and is relaxing
(and which reverses at longer horizons).

Both components are bounded in [-1, 1] and scale-free, so no per-name
volatility or volume normalisation, no z-scores of z-scores, and no tuned
gates are needed.  All statistics are trailing rolling sums: the value at bar
t uses only bars <= t.

Falsifiable: if the cross-sectional IC of (fast - slow) sqrt-weighted flow
pressure is zero at the 6-bar horizon, or if the fast and slow components
carry the same IC sign, the propagator reading is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _bar_return_sign(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal sign of the bar-to-bar log price change.

    Flat bars (mid unchanged) get weight zero -- no repricing, no evidence.
    """
    lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    chg = np.log(lvl).diff()
    chg = chg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return np.sign(chg).fillna(0.0)


def _sqrt_law_pressure(sgn: pd.DataFrame, wgt: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """sqrt(volume)-weighted mean of return signs over a trailing n-bar window.

    Bounded in [-1, 1]: +1 = every traded bar repriced upward, -1 = downward,
    0 = balanced.  The sqrt weighting implements the square-root impact law,
    damping single-print dominance without discarding size information.
    """
    num = ts_sum(sgn * wgt, n)
    den = ts_sum(wgt, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = num / den
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class SqrtLawWeightedFlowPressureFreshnessWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh minus stale sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure."""

    factor_id = "sqrt_law_weighted_flow_pressure_freshness_wedge"
    name = "Square-root-law weighted flow pressure freshness wedge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of the sqrt(volume)-weighted mean bar-return sign "
        "over the last 6 bars minus the same statistic over the last 60 bars: "
        "long names whose freshest volume-weighted directional pressure exceeds "
        "the pressure they have already impacted."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _fast = 6    # matched to the forecast horizon: unfinished flow
    _slow = 60   # ~10 minutes: pressure already impacted and relaxing

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        sgn = _bar_return_sign(close)
        wgt = np.sqrt(volume)

        fresh = _sqrt_law_pressure(sgn, wgt, self._fast)
        stale = _sqrt_law_pressure(sgn, wgt, self._slow)

        raw = (fresh - stale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Square-root-law weighted flow pressure freshness wedge
programs.trading_idea: Under the square-root impact law a bar's contribution to repricing scales with the square root of its executed volume, and under Bouchaud's propagator the impact of volume executed several bars ago is largely transient and relaxes, while flow arriving in the last few bars is mostly unfinished and keeps arriving (order-flow imbalance is strongly autocorrelated at second scales). The child therefore measures a name's sqrt-volume-weighted directional consistency over a fast window matched to the forecast horizon and subtracts the same statistic over a slow window: what remains is *fresh* one-sided pressure net of pressure that has already been impacted and is decaying. This replaces the parent's noisy volume-CV 'metronome' gate (a fragile z-score of a z-score) with a single scale-free statistic that is bounded in [-1,1], robust to single giant prints (sqrt weighting, not linear), and needs no per-name normalisation. Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns do not load positively on fresh-minus-stale sqrt-weighted flow pressure — in particular if the fast and slow components carry the same IC sign — the propagator/unfinished-order interpretation is wrong; the edge survives arbitrage because it lives inside a one-minute window where net-of-spread capacity is tiny and its exploitation does not cancel the child orders still to come.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of (sqrt-volume-weighted mean of bar-return signs over the last 6 bars) minus (the same sqrt-volume-weighted mean over the last 60 bars): long names whose newest volume-weighted directional pressure exceeds their already-established pressure.

programs.code:
"""Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating short-run path efficiency.

Mechanism
---------
At 10-second resolution two very different processes create directional price
paths.  (1) A parent order worked by a VWAP/POV scheduler spreads its child
fills nearly evenly across consecutive bars: the *entropy of the bar-volume
shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level, and
the unfinished remainder of the parent implies the grind continues.  (2) A
one-off liquidity-consuming burst / news print concentrates volume mass in one
or two bars (entropy drops) and the displacement it leaves is mostly transient
impact that decays as depth refills, so it should be faded.

The factor is the product of two *bounded, scale-free* quantities, with no
z-scores, clips or squashing functions:

    * path efficiency  E = net log displacement / total absolute path over the
      same window, in [-1, 1] (Kaufman ratio).  It is large only when the move
      was directional rather than noise, so it self-attenuates on noisy paths.
    * evenness innovation  G = H_norm(30) - mean_120(H_norm(30)), where H_norm
      is the Shannon entropy of the volume shares divided by log(n), in [0, 1].
      Subtracting its own trailing mean centres the gate per name exactly, so
      the gate flips sign across the cross-section and the unconditional
      momentum loading is purged.

Falsifiable: if forward 6-bar returns do not depend on the interaction between
directional path efficiency and innovations in volume evenness, the
cross-sectional IC of this product is zero.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows: the value at bar t uses only bars
<= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delta, rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_price(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal log mid-price, robust to zero / bad prints."""
    lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return np.log(lvl).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _path_efficiency(logp: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Signed Kaufman efficiency ratio over a trailing n-bar window.

    net n-bar log displacement divided by the total absolute path travelled.
    Bounded in [-1, 1]: +-1 is a monotone grind, ~0 is a round trip / noise.
    Scale-free and volatility-free, so no variance estimate is needed.
    """
    step = logp.diff()
    net = delta(logp, n)
    path = step.abs().rolling(n, min_periods=n).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = net / path
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

def _normalized_volume_entropy(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shannon entropy of the trailing n-bar volume shares, divided by log(n).

    With p_i = v_i / S and S = sum(v_i):
        H = -sum p_i log p_i = log(S) - (1 / S) * sum(v_i log v_i)
    computed from two trailing rolling sums (v_i log v_i is taken as 0 when
    v_i == 0, the usual 0*log0 convention).  Result lies in [0, 1]: 1 means
    perfectly even participation (scheduler fingerprint), low values mean the
    window's volume was dominated by a few bursty bars.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    tot = ts_sum(v, n)
    vlogv = (v * np.log(v.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)
    s_vlogv = ts_sum(vlogv, n)
    tot_safe = tot.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ent = np.log(tot_safe) - s_vlogv / tot_safe
    ent = ent.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / float(np.log(n))
    return ent.clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class VolumeEvennessEntropyInnovationGatedPathEfficiency(BaseFactor):
    """Grind continued when participation turns even, faded when it bursts."""
    factor_id = 'volume_evenness_entropy_innovation_gated_path_ef'
    name = 'Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = "Cross-sectional rank of (30-bar signed path-efficiency ratio) x (normalized Shannon entropy of the last 30 bars' volume shares minus its own 120-bar mean): extrapolate the drift when participation just turned unusually even, fade it when volume mass just concentrated."
    window_length = 160
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _span = 30
    _norm = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        logp = _log_price(close)
        eff = _path_efficiency(logp, self._span)
        ent = _normalized_volume_entropy(volume, self._span)
        gate = ent - ts_mean(ent, self._norm)
        raw = (eff * gate).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Volume-evenness entropy innovation gating path efficiency
programs.trading_idea: A metaorder worked by a scheduler spreads its child fills almost evenly across consecutive 10-second bars, so the *entropy of the bar-volume shares* over the last few minutes rises above the name's own recent level while price grinds directionally; the unfinished remainder of that parent order makes the grind continue over the next minute. A liquidity-consuming burst or news print does the opposite: volume mass concentrates in one or two bars (entropy drops) and the accompanying displacement is mostly transient impact that decays as depth refills, so the same displacement should be faded. The child keeps the parent's schedule-vs-burst split but expresses both legs with *bounded, scale-free* statistics — normalized Shannon entropy of volume shares (in [0,1]) minus its own trailing mean, times the Kaufman path-efficiency ratio (in [-1,1]) — eliminating the parent's fragile ratio-of-rolling-moments z-scores, clips and tanh that produced the in-sample/out-of-sample collapse. The edge survives arbitrage because detecting a schedule requires per-name conditioning on the *shape* of participation rather than its level, execution algos deliberately randomise size so the residual regularity is small and unrewarding to slow capital, and front-running the remaining children does not eliminate them — each new metaorder regenerates the signal.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of (30-bar signed path-efficiency ratio) x (normalized Shannon entropy of the last 30 bars' volume shares minus its own 120-bar mean): extrapolate the drift when participation just turned unusually even, fade it when volume mass just concentrated into a burst.

"""Wilcoxon drift x Mood compression: metaorder grind versus overshoot.

Mechanism
---------
The parent measured fresh sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure and found a
*negative* IC at six bars.  The natural reading is that pressure magnitude does
not separate the two ways a short-run displacement is produced:

1.  A sliced metaorder.  Execution algorithms deliberately trade so that each
    child order moves price as little as possible, so the resulting drift is
    built from many *compressed* increments -- small relative to the name's own
    recent increment distribution -- and it continues while the parent order is
    unfinished (order-flow autocorrelation, Lillo-Farmer).

2.  A liquidity-withdrawal overshoot.  Here the same net displacement comes
    from a few increments in the tails of the own-name distribution; under the
    transient-impact propagator that displacement largely relaxes as depth
    refills, i.e. it reverts at the sixty-second scale.

So the informative object is the INTERACTION of a location shift with an
increment-scale state, both estimated nonparametrically:

*   Location: uniformize every bar return by its percentile inside the trailing
    120-bar own-name distribution (u in [0,1]); the mean of the last 6 values
    minus 1/2 is exactly a Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic for "recent increments
    are unusually positive".  Being rank-based it is automatically volatility-
    normalised per name -- no z-scores, no beta, no tuned scaling.
*   Scale: the trailing 18-bar *variance* of u (centred on its own rolling mean,
    hence location-free) compared with the uniform benchmark 1/12 -- a Mood /
    Fligner-type dispersion statistic.  Values below 1/12 mean the recent path
    is built from compressed increments (grind); above 1/12 means tail-heavy,
    violent increments (overshoot).

Signal = (cross-sectionally rank-centred location shift) x (compression gate),
where the gate is +1 for the most compressed names and -1 for the most
dispersed ones.  Long steady up-grinds, short violent up-moves, and vice versa.

Falsifiable: if the cross-sectional IC of this product is zero at six bars, or
negative -- meaning violent tail-driven moves continue while compressed drifts
revert -- the metaorder-slicing / transient-impact reading is wrong.  Uses no
volume at all, by construction independent of the flow-imbalance family.
Every statistic is a trailing rolling window: the value at bar t uses only
bars <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_increments(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar-to-bar log price increments, sanitised."""
    lvl = close.astype(float).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inc = np.log(lvl).diff()
    return inc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _uniformize(inc: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Probability-integral transform of each increment against its own trailing
    n-bar empirical distribution (percentile in [0, 1]).  Causal: ts_rank uses
    the last n bars only."""
    u = ts_rank(inc, n)
    u = u.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return u.clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _wilcoxon_location(u: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last k increments versus the
    trailing reference distribution.  Zero under the null of no shift."""
    return ts_mean(u, k) - 0.5


def _mood_dispersion(u: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Centred Mood-type scale statistic: trailing k-bar sample variance of the
    uniformized increments minus the uniform benchmark 1/12.  Negative = the
    recent path is built from compressed increments, positive = tail-heavy."""
    var = u.rolling(k, min_periods=k).var()
    return (var - (1.0 / 12.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class WilcoxonDriftMoodCompressionMetaorderWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Rank-drift conditioned on increment-scale compression."""

    factor_id = "wilcoxon_drift_mood_compression_metaorder_wedge"
    name = "Rank-drift x increment-compression metaorder wedge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of (rank-centred Wilcoxon location shift of the "
        "last 6 log-increments against the trailing 120-bar own-name increment "
        "distribution) times (1 - 2*rank of the 18-bar Mood scale statistic of "
        "the uniformized increments): long compressed steady up-drifts, short "
        "tail-heavy violent up-moves."
    )
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _ref = 120    # ~20 minutes: own-name reference increment distribution
    _fast = 6     # matched to the forecast horizon: location shift
    _state = 18   # ~3 minutes: slower-moving increment-scale regime

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)

        inc = _log_increments(close)
        u = _uniformize(inc, self._ref)

        loc = _wilcoxon_location(u, self._fast)          # directional rank drift
        disp = _mood_dispersion(u, self._state)          # increment-scale state

        # Cross-sectional centring to [-1, 1] keeps the product bounded and free
        # of per-name scale, and makes the interaction a clean sign switch.
        loc_c = 2.0 * rank(loc) - 1.0
        gate = 1.0 - 2.0 * rank(disp)                    # +1 compressed, -1 dispersed

        raw = loc_c * gate
        raw = raw.where(loc.notna() & disp.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Rank-drift × increment-compression metaorder wedge
programs.trading_idea: A net price displacement can be produced two ways with opposite futures: (a) by many small, unusually *compressed* increments — the signature of an execution algorithm slicing a large metaorder, which keeps arriving and therefore keeps repricing; or (b) by a few violent increments drawn from the tails of the name's own recent increment distribution — a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot whose impact is largely transient and relaxes as depth refills. The parent measured only the magnitude/direction of fresh pressure, so it loaded mainly on regime (b) and its IC came out negative; the child separates the two regimes with a purely nonparametric two-sample construction: a Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last 6 increments against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution, multiplied by a centred Mood-type *scale-compression* state (rolling variance of the uniformized increments below its uniform benchmark 1/12). The edge survives arbitrage because identifying an in-progress sliced order requires conditioning on the *shape* of the increment distribution rather than the size of the move, and the agent whose child orders create the drift cannot profit from front-running itself; net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is tiny.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of (rank-normalised Wilcoxon location shift of the last 6 log-increments versus the trailing 120-bar own-name distribution) × (increment-dispersion compression gate = 1 − 2·rank of the 18-bar variance of uniformized increments minus 1/12): long steady low-dispersion up-drifts, short violent high-dispersion up-moves.

programs.code:
"""Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback.

Mechanism
---------
Two objects live in a 10-second bar panel.

1. UNPAID TRANSIENT DISPLACEMENT (within-bar geometry).  Aggressive size walks
   visible depth and the mid ends far from the extreme the bar printed.  The
   participation-weighted close-location value (CLV) inside the bar range,
   aggregated with recency weights over 6 bars and purged of its sector mean,
   isolates the name-specific part of that displacement, which is the temporary
   cost of immediacy and reverts as passive depth replenishes.

2. OWED SYSTEMATIC DELIVERY.  Let m_t be the cross-sectional median log return
   and z_t its trailing z-score.  A name's total response to common shocks is
   identified on large-|z| bars (news transmission dominates bounce noise) via
   trailing shock-selected projections summed over lags 0..2, ridge-stabilised
   and shrunk toward the cross-section.  The horizon-matched gap
   D = theta * sum(z, 6) - sum(own vol-scaled return, 6) is the systematic move
   the name still owes (D > 0) or has over-delivered (D < 0).

SYNTHESIS.  A low close inside a heavy range may simply be the mechanical
delivery of an owed negative beta move, in which case there is nothing to fade.
So the displacement is first orthogonalised against D with a trailing per-name
OLS residual: only the *un-owed* displacement is faded.  The router is the
participation-weighted WICK share (range minus body, over range) of the last 6
bars -- a within-bar absorption meter neither parent uses.  High wick share =
aggressive size was absorbed and retraced, so the un-owed displacement is pure
liquidity provision and snaps back; body-dominated bars mean the move was
accepted, and there the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign.

Causal throughout: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only; sector
labels are static metadata from each name's earliest valid observation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    decay_linear,
    rank,
    rolling_residual,
    ts_mean,
    ts_sum,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    r = rank(clean)
    return ((r - 0.5) * 2.0).where(clean.notna())


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int = 3):
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = "__POOL__"
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else "__POOL__"
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), "__POOL__")
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab


def _group_purge(df: pd.DataFrame, lab) -> pd.DataFrame:
    fallback = _broadcast(df.mean(axis=1), df)
    if lab is None:
        return df - fallback
    gmean = df.T.groupby(lab).transform("mean").T
    gmean = gmean.reindex(index=df.index, columns=df.columns)
    gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
    return df - gmean


def _shock_theta(
    y0: pd.DataFrame,
    xs: pd.Series,
    n: int,
    nmin: int,
    lags: int,
    ridge: float,
    shrink: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Total shock-selected distributed-lag response, trailing and ridge-stabilised."""
    base = (xs * xs).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
    theta = None
    for j in range(lags + 1):
        xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
        den = (xl * xl).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
        num = y0.mul(xl, axis=0).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
        denom = (den + ridge * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), shrink).fillna(0.0)
        theta = th if theta is None else theta.add(th)
    return theta


@register_factor
class AbsorbedWickRoutedUnowedTransientSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade only the displacement a name was not owed; route by within-bar absorption."""

    factor_id = "absorbed_wick_routed_unowed_transient_snapback"
    name = "Absorption-wick routed un-owed transient snapback"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-purged, participation-weighted within-bar close-location "
        "displacement is orthogonalised against a shock-identified owed "
        "systematic-delivery gap and faded, then blended with that gap using "
        "the cross-sectional rank of the participation-weighted wick "
        "(absorption) share of the last 6 bars as the router."
    )
    window_length = 240
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # displacement / absorption channel
    _vol_window = 60
    _agg = 6
    _part_cap = 4.0
    _shrink_den = 0.5
    # owed-delivery channel
    _lags = 2
    _n = 180
    _nmin = 90
    _thresh = 1.0
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.30
    _k = 6
    # orthogonalisation window
    _orth = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        T, N = len(idx), len(cols)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._nmin) + int(self._agg) + 5 or N < 3:
            return zero

        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()
        volume = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- channel 1: participation-weighted within-bar displacement ----------
        clv = ((close - lo) - (hi - close)) / rng
        clv = clv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        vbase = ts_mean(volume, int(self._vol_window)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        part = (volume / vbase).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, float(self._part_cap))

        ok = clv.notna() & part.notna()
        c = clv.where(ok, 0.0)
        w = part.where(ok, 0.0)
        num = decay_linear(w * c, int(self._agg))
        den = decay_linear(w, int(self._agg))
        disp = (num / (den + float(self._shrink_den))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get("sector"), cols)
        idio_disp = _group_purge(disp, lab)

        # ---- channel 2: shock-identified owed systematic delivery ---------------
        px = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lr = np.log(px).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sig = (lr.rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (lr / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)

        mkt = lr.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))
        xs = z.where(z.abs() > float(self._thresh), 0.0)

        theta = _shock_theta(y0, xs, int(self._n), int(self._nmin),
                            int(self._lags), float(self._ridge), float(self._shrink))

        z_df = _broadcast(z, close)
        implied = theta * ts_sum(z_df, int(self._k))
        delivered = ts_sum(y0, int(self._k))
        owed = ((implied - delivered) / np.sqrt(float(self._k)))
        owed = owed.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        alive = y.notna().rolling(int(self._k), min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        owed = owed.where(alive)

        # ---- interaction: purge displacement of the part it was OWED -----------
        d_for_orth = owed.fillna(0.0)
        resid = rolling_residual(idio_disp.fillna(0.0), d_for_orth, int(self._orth))
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        unowed = resid.where(resid.notna(), idio_disp)   # fall back before window fills
        unowed = unowed.where(idio_disp.notna())

        # ---- router: participation-weighted within-bar wick (absorption) share --
        body = (close - open_).abs()
        wick = (rng - body).clip(lower=0.0)
        wshare = (wick / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        ok2 = wshare.notna() & part.notna()
        wnum = decay_linear(wshare.where(ok2, 0.0) * w, int(self._agg))
        absorb = (wnum / (den + float(self._shrink_den))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        s = rank(absorb)
        s = s.where(s.notna(), 0.5)

        # ---- blend --------------------------------------------------------------
        a = _centred_rank(-unowed)      # fade the un-owed transient displacement
        b = _centred_rank(owed)         # ride the owed systematic catch-up
        a_ok, b_ok = a.notna(), b.notna()
        s_eff = s.where(b_ok, 1.0).where(a_ok, 0.0)
        raw = s_eff * a.fillna(0.0) + (1.0 - s_eff) * b.fillna(0.0)

        valid = a_ok | b_ok
        raw = raw.where(valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback
programs.trading_idea: Parent B's participation-weighted range-position displacement measures where inside a heavy-volume bar the mid ended up, i.e. the unpaid cost of immediacy that relaxes as depth refills; Parent A's shock-selected distributed-lag kernel measures how much systematic move the name still OWES the market impulse. The child first *purges* the displacement of the part that is mechanically explained by the owed-delivery gap (trailing per-name OLS residual of displacement on the gap), so the fade is applied only to displacement nobody was entitled to, and then routes between the two channels with a state variable neither parent uses: the participation-weighted wick share of the last 6 bars (range minus body over range), which distinguishes bars where aggressive size was absorbed and retraced from clean directional body moves. Where absorption is high the un-owed displacement is pure liquidity provision and snaps back; where bars are body-dominated the displacement is beta delivery in progress and the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign. The interaction is the edge: B cannot tell a low close inside a heavy range from legitimate downside beta delivery, and A has no within-bar geometry to know whether the push was absorbed or accepted.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of a blend between (i) the negated, sector-purged, participation-weighted close-location displacement after removing its trailing regression on the shock-identified owed systematic-delivery gap, and (ii) that owed gap itself, routed by the rank of the participation-weighted within-bar wick (absorption) share of the last 6 bars.

programs.code:
"""Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback.

Mechanism: basket / program executions (index rebalances, ETF create-redeem
arbitrage, cash-flow programs) spread dollars across names in proportion to
capitalisation weight, not in proportion to fundamental beta.  The displacement
they cause in name i therefore scales with weight_i / depth_i, i.e. with
kappa_i = marketCap_i / trailing dollar volume = the inverse of dollar turnover.

The parent factor *assumed* the mechanical push equalled kappa times the
cap-weighted market return, so all of its cross-sectional dispersion came from a
nearly static characteristic timed by one common market scalar.  Here the push is
MEASURED.  Each bar:

  1. build cross-sectionally standardised exposures z_kappa and z_beta;
  2. project z_kappa onto z_beta cross-sectionally and keep the residual e_t --
     the impact-elasticity exposure that is orthogonal to the information
     (beta) channel, a principled replacement for a rank difference;
  3. read the realised *mechanical factor return*
         g_t = sum_i e_it r_it / sum_i e_it^2,
     the per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on e -- the actual
     displacement per unit of impact elasticity;
  4. gate g_t by a basket-program detector G_t (cross-sectional correlation
     between each name's dollar-volume-share deviation from its trailing norm
     and the direction of the cap-weight vector, scaled by aggregate relative
     activity), then accumulate G_t g_t with an exponential memory and lag it
     one bar so only past information is used;
  5. signal = -(e_it) x standardised accumulation: fade the mechanical push.

Everything is trailing or contemporaneous; no forward shifts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, returns, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar Series across all tickers."""
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.reindex(index), dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)


def _xs_corr(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional Pearson correlation between two aligned frames."""
    mask = a.notna() & b.notna()
    aa = a.where(mask)
    bb = b.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    ac = aa.sub(aa.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    bc = bb.sub(bb.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (ac * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = np.sqrt((ac * ac).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) * (bc * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1))
    out = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return out.where(n >= min_names)


def _xs_standardise(df: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional z-score (robust to a few missing names)."""
    n = df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sd = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    z = z.where(_row_broadcast(n, df.index, df.columns) >= float(min_names))
    return z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _xs_orthogonalise(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional residual of y on x (both already demeaned-ish).

    slope_t = sum_i y_it x_it / sum_i x_it^2 over names where both exist.
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    yc = yy.sub(yy.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    xc = xx.sub(xx.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (yc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (xc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    slope = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    resid = yc.sub(xc.mul(slope, axis=0))
    resid = resid.sub(resid.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _xs_factor_return(exposure: pd.DataFrame, ret: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on an exposure."""
    mask = exposure.notna() & ret.notna()
    e = exposure.where(mask)
    r = ret.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    e = e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    r = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (e * r).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (e * e).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    g = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return g.where(n >= min_names)


@register_factor
class ProgramGatedElasticityFactorReturnSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade the measured mechanical (weight-per-depth) cross-sectional push."""

    factor_id = "program_gated_elasticity_factor_return_snapback"
    name = "Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity exposure times minus an "
        "exponentially accumulated, program-gated cross-sectional factor return "
        "measured on that same exposure."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        L = 120           # trailing estimation window (20 minutes on 10s bars)
        mp = max(20, L // 2)
        hl = 4.0          # exponential memory of the accumulated push (bars)
        min_names = 8

        # ---------------- returns ----------------
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)

        # ---------------- capitalisation weights ----------------
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
        med_cap = mcap.median(axis=1)
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).ffill()
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        cap = mcap.where(mcap.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_cap, idx, cols))

        cap_tot = cap.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        w = cap.div(cap_tot, axis=0)

        # cap-weighted market return over names quoting this bar (beta reference)
        w_av = w.where(ret.notna())
        denom = w_av.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        m = (w_av * ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / denom
        m = m.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---------------- basket-program detector ----------------
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dv = (close.abs() * vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        tot_dv = dv.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        share = dv.div(tot_dv, axis=0)
        share_bar = ts_mean(share, L)

        dev_share = share - share_bar          # allocation anomaly this bar
        dev_w = w - share_bar                  # direction of the cap-weight vector
        tilt = _xs_corr(dev_share, dev_w, min_names)

        act = tot_dv / tot_dv.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        act = act.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.25, 6.0)

        G = 0.10 + tilt.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0) * np.sqrt(act)
        G = G.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.10)

        # ---------------- exposures: elasticity and beta ----------------
        advdv = adv(dv, L).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        turnover = (advdv / cap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        turnover = turnover.where(turnover > 0.0)
        kappa = -np.log(turnover)              # weight-per-depth fragility

        m_df = _row_broadcast(m.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret.fillna(0.0), m_df, L)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 5.0)

        z_kappa = _xs_standardise(kappa, min_names)
        z_beta = _xs_standardise(beta, min_names)

        # beta-orthogonal mechanical exposure
        e = _xs_orthogonalise(z_kappa, z_beta)

        # ---------------- measured mechanical factor return ----------------
        g = _xs_factor_return(e, ret, min_names)
        sig_g = g.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g_std = (g / sig_g).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        push = (G * g_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        P = push.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        P = P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        P_df = _row_broadcast(P, idx, cols)

        # ---------------- signal ----------------
        valid = e.notna() & ret.notna()
        raw = (-e) * P_df
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)

        out = raw.sub(raw.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback
programs.trading_idea: Basket/program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight rather than by fundamental beta, so their price displacement loads on a name's weight-per-unit-depth elasticity kappa = marketCap / dollar-volume, a characteristic that is orthogonal to beta only after explicit projection. Rather than *assuming* the mechanical push equals kappa times the cap-weighted market return (the parent's single common scalar, which makes every cross-sectional bet a static pattern timed by a beta-like market signal), I *measure* it: each bar I run a cross-sectional regression of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity exposure and read off the realised 'mechanical factor return' g_t — the actual displacement per unit of impact elasticity, cleanly separated from the information (beta) channel. Accumulating g_t with an exponential memory only over bars whose cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector (the basket footprint) isolates uncompensated liquidity demand, which must relax; the signal is minus the name's orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulation. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the depth-heterogeneous mechanical component un-hedged, and capturing it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
programs.description: Per bar, cross-sectionally regress returns on the beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity (-log dollar turnover) to extract a mechanical factor return; accumulate it with an exponential kernel gated by a basket-program detector (alignment of dollar-volume-share deviations with the cap-weight vector), and short names in proportion to their orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulated push.

"""Corporate Net-Demand Hinge: asymmetric intraday dislocation repair.

Mechanism: corporations are price-insensitive, direction-known participants.
An active repurchaser runs a standing algorithmic bid (10b-18 style VWAP
slicing, participation capped as a share of contemporaneous volume), so its
idiosyncratic dips are absorbed and repair quickly; a net issuer supplies
stock into strength, so its rallies are capped.  The reversal coefficient is
therefore a HINGE: it acts on the negative part of the dislocation for net
repurchasers and on the positive part for net issuers.  Falsified if the
sign-asymmetry vanishes (identical reversion for issuers and repurchasers).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import stddev, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _frame(data: dict, key: str, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Defensively fetch a panel field, aligned and numeric (NaN if absent)."""
    df = data.get(key)
    if df is None:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    out = df.reindex(index=index, columns=columns)
    out = out.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors='coerce')
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _corporate_net_demand(data: dict, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time net corporate demand for own stock, as a fraction of cap.

    Positive  = firm is a net buyer of its own shares (repurchase programme).
    Negative  = firm is a net supplier (issuance, ATM, secondary).
    Quarterly step function; missing names are left NaN and neutralised later.
    """
    mcap = _frame(data, 'marketCap', index, columns)
    mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
    nsi = _frame(data, 'netStockIssuance', index, columns)
    rep = _frame(data, 'shareRepurchase', index, columns)
    sgr = _frame(data, 'sharesGrowth', index, columns)
    d1 = -nsi / mcap
    d2 = -rep / mcap
    d3 = (-sgr).clip(-0.25, 0.25)
    demand = d1.where(d1.notna(), d2)
    demand = demand.where(demand.notna(), d3)
    return demand.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _signed_robust_scale(df: pd.DataFrame, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise scaling by the cross-sectional median absolute value.

    Unlike a z-score this PRESERVES the economic sign (net buyer vs net
    seller): only the magnitude is put on a comparable cross-sectional scale.
    """
    med_abs = df.abs().median(axis=1)
    med_abs = med_abs.where(med_abs > 0.0, np.nan)
    out = df.div(med_abs, axis=0)
    return out.clip(-cap, cap)

@register_factor
class CorporateNetDemandHingeAsymmetricDislocation(BaseFactor):
    """Hinge interaction of dislocation sign with corporate net share demand."""
    factor_id = 'corporate_net_demand_hinge_asymmetric_dislocatio'
    name = 'Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Volatility-scaled 12-bar market-neutral dislocation split into its negative and positive parts and interacted, hinge-style, with point-in-time corporate net share demand (repurchases vs issuance), scaled by current relative volume and cross-sectionally demeaned.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'netStockIssuance', 'shareRepurchase', 'sharesGrowth']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _DISLOC_WIN = 12
    _SIGMA_WIN = 240
    _VOL_FAST = 6
    _VOL_SLOW = 240
    _DEMAND_CAP = 3.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        index, columns = (close.index, close.columns)
        ret = _log_returns(close)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1)
        idio = ret.sub(mkt, axis=0)
        sigma = stddev(idio.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN)
        sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cum = ts_sum(idio.fillna(0.0), self._DISLOC_WIN)
        disloc = cum / (sigma * np.sqrt(float(self._DISLOC_WIN)))
        disloc = disloc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        disloc = disloc.where(sigma.notna() & ret.notna())
        dip = (-disloc).clip(lower=0.0)
        pop = disloc.clip(lower=0.0)
        demand = _corporate_net_demand(data, index, columns)
        b = _signed_robust_scale(demand, self._DEMAND_CAP)
        b = b.fillna(0.0)
        buyer = b.clip(lower=0.0)
        seller = (-b).clip(lower=0.0)
        vol = _frame(data, 'volume', index, columns).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        base = ts_mean(vol, self._VOL_SLOW).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        v_rel = ts_mean(vol, self._VOL_FAST) / base
        gate = np.sqrt(v_rel.clip(0.2, 5.0))
        gate = gate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(1.0)
        score = (buyer * dip - seller * pop) * gate
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.where(disloc.notna())
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return score.reindex(index=index, columns=columns)
programs.name: Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)
programs.trading_idea: Firms are the one class of participant whose trading direction is known in advance and is price-insensitive: an active repurchaser has a standing algorithmic *bid* working the tape all day (Rule 10b-18 VWAP slicing), while a net issuer (ATM/secondary/option-driven supply) is a standing *offer*. This makes short-horizon liquidity provision asymmetric at the firm level: an idiosyncratic dip in a heavy repurchaser is absorbed by corporate demand and snaps back within a minute, whereas a rally in a net issuer is capped by corporate supply — so the reversal coefficient should be a hinge in the sign of the dislocation interacted with the sign of net corporate share issuance, not a symmetric linear reversal. Because participation is capped as a fraction of contemporaneous volume, the support strength scales with current relative volume. The edge survives arbitrage because intraday buyback schedules are never disclosed (only quarterly totals), so an arbitrageur cannot distinguish a corporate-supported dip from genuine adverse information ex ante and must warehouse inventory risk; it is falsified if downside reversion at 6 bars is identical for repurchasers and issuers, i.e. if the hinge interaction adds nothing over symmetric reversal.
programs.description: Piecewise (hinge) interaction between a volatility-scaled 12-bar market-neutral price dislocation and point-in-time corporate net share demand: long the dip in net repurchasers, short the rally in net issuers, with the magnitude scaled by current relative volume and the cross-section demeaned.
