programs.code:
"""Wilcoxon drift x Mood compression: metaorder grind versus overshoot.

Mechanism
---------
The parent measured fresh sqrt-volume-weighted directional pressure and found a
*negative* IC at six bars.  The natural reading is that pressure magnitude does
not separate the two ways a short-run displacement is produced:

1.  A sliced metaorder.  Execution algorithms deliberately trade so that each
    child order moves price as little as possible, so the resulting drift is
    built from many *compressed* increments -- small relative to the name's own
    recent increment distribution -- and it continues while the parent order is
    unfinished (order-flow autocorrelation, Lillo-Farmer).

2.  A liquidity-withdrawal overshoot.  Here the same net displacement comes
    from a few increments in the tails of the own-name distribution; under the
    transient-impact propagator that displacement largely relaxes as depth
    refills, i.e. it reverts at the sixty-second scale.

So the informative object is the INTERACTION of a location shift with an
increment-scale state, both estimated nonparametrically:

*   Location: uniformize every bar return by its percentile inside the trailing
    120-bar own-name distribution (u in [0,1]); the mean of the last 6 values
    minus 1/2 is exactly a Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic for "recent increments
    are unusually positive".  Being rank-based it is automatically volatility-
    normalised per name -- no z-scores, no beta, no tuned scaling.
*   Scale: the trailing 18-bar *variance* of u (centred on its own rolling mean,
    hence location-free) compared with the uniform benchmark 1/12 -- a Mood /
    Fligner-type dispersion statistic.  Values below 1/12 mean the recent path
    is built from compressed increments (grind); above 1/12 means tail-heavy,
    violent increments (overshoot).

Signal = (cross-sectionally rank-centred location shift) x (compression gate),
where the gate is +1 for the most compressed names and -1 for the most
dispersed ones.  Long steady up-grinds, short violent up-moves, and vice versa.

Falsifiable: if the cross-sectional IC of this product is zero at six bars, or
negative -- meaning violent tail-driven moves continue while compressed drifts
revert -- the metaorder-slicing / transient-impact reading is wrong.  Uses no
volume at all, by construction independent of the flow-imbalance family.
Every statistic is a trailing rolling window: the value at bar t uses only
bars <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_increments(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar-to-bar log price increments, sanitised."""
    lvl = close.astype(float).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inc = np.log(lvl).diff()
    return inc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _uniformize(inc: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Probability-integral transform of each increment against its own trailing
    n-bar empirical distribution (percentile in [0, 1]).  Causal: ts_rank uses
    the last n bars only."""
    u = ts_rank(inc, n)
    u = u.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return u.clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _wilcoxon_location(u: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last k increments versus the
    trailing reference distribution.  Zero under the null of no shift."""
    return ts_mean(u, k) - 0.5


def _mood_dispersion(u: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Centred Mood-type scale statistic: trailing k-bar sample variance of the
    uniformized increments minus the uniform benchmark 1/12.  Negative = the
    recent path is built from compressed increments, positive = tail-heavy."""
    var = u.rolling(k, min_periods=k).var()
    return (var - (1.0 / 12.0)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class WilcoxonDriftMoodCompressionMetaorderWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Rank-drift conditioned on increment-scale compression."""

    factor_id = "wilcoxon_drift_mood_compression_metaorder_wedge"
    name = "Rank-drift x increment-compression metaorder wedge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of (rank-centred Wilcoxon location shift of the "
        "last 6 log-increments against the trailing 120-bar own-name increment "
        "distribution) times (1 - 2*rank of the 18-bar Mood scale statistic of "
        "the uniformized increments): long compressed steady up-drifts, short "
        "tail-heavy violent up-moves."
    )
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _ref = 120    # ~20 minutes: own-name reference increment distribution
    _fast = 6     # matched to the forecast horizon: location shift
    _state = 18   # ~3 minutes: slower-moving increment-scale regime

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)

        inc = _log_increments(close)
        u = _uniformize(inc, self._ref)

        loc = _wilcoxon_location(u, self._fast)          # directional rank drift
        disp = _mood_dispersion(u, self._state)          # increment-scale state

        # Cross-sectional centring to [-1, 1] keeps the product bounded and free
        # of per-name scale, and makes the interaction a clean sign switch.
        loc_c = 2.0 * rank(loc) - 1.0
        gate = 1.0 - 2.0 * rank(disp)                    # +1 compressed, -1 dispersed

        raw = loc_c * gate
        raw = raw.where(loc.notna() & disp.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Rank-drift × increment-compression metaorder wedge
programs.trading_idea: A net price displacement can be produced two ways with opposite futures: (a) by many small, unusually *compressed* increments — the signature of an execution algorithm slicing a large metaorder, which keeps arriving and therefore keeps repricing; or (b) by a few violent increments drawn from the tails of the name's own recent increment distribution — a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot whose impact is largely transient and relaxes as depth refills. The parent measured only the magnitude/direction of fresh pressure, so it loaded mainly on regime (b) and its IC came out negative; the child separates the two regimes with a purely nonparametric two-sample construction: a Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift of the last 6 increments against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution, multiplied by a centred Mood-type *scale-compression* state (rolling variance of the uniformized increments below its uniform benchmark 1/12). The edge survives arbitrage because identifying an in-progress sliced order requires conditioning on the *shape* of the increment distribution rather than the size of the move, and the agent whose child orders create the drift cannot profit from front-running itself; net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is tiny.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of (rank-normalised Wilcoxon location shift of the last 6 log-increments versus the trailing 120-bar own-name distribution) × (increment-dispersion compression gate = 1 − 2·rank of the 18-bar variance of uniformized increments minus 1/12): long steady low-dispersion up-drifts, short violent high-dispersion up-moves.

programs.code:
"""Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback.

Mechanism
---------
Two objects live in a 10-second bar panel.

1. UNPAID TRANSIENT DISPLACEMENT (within-bar geometry).  Aggressive size walks
   visible depth and the mid ends far from the extreme the bar printed.  The
   participation-weighted close-location value (CLV) inside the bar range,
   aggregated with recency weights over 6 bars and purged of its sector mean,
   isolates the name-specific part of that displacement, which is the temporary
   cost of immediacy and reverts as passive depth replenishes.

2. OWED SYSTEMATIC DELIVERY.  Let m_t be the cross-sectional median log return
   and z_t its trailing z-score.  A name's total response to common shocks is
   identified on large-|z| bars (news transmission dominates bounce noise) via
   trailing shock-selected projections summed over lags 0..2, ridge-stabilised
   and shrunk toward the cross-section.  The horizon-matched gap
   D = theta * sum(z, 6) - sum(own vol-scaled return, 6) is the systematic move
   the name still owes (D > 0) or has over-delivered (D < 0).

SYNTHESIS.  A low close inside a heavy range may simply be the mechanical
delivery of an owed negative beta move, in which case there is nothing to fade.
So the displacement is first orthogonalised against D with a trailing per-name
OLS residual: only the *un-owed* displacement is faded.  The router is the
participation-weighted WICK share (range minus body, over range) of the last 6
bars -- a within-bar absorption meter neither parent uses.  High wick share =
aggressive size was absorbed and retraced, so the un-owed displacement is pure
liquidity provision and snaps back; body-dominated bars mean the move was
accepted, and there the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign.

Causal throughout: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only; sector
labels are static metadata from each name's earliest valid observation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    decay_linear,
    rank,
    rolling_residual,
    ts_mean,
    ts_sum,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    clean = df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    r = rank(clean)
    return ((r - 0.5) * 2.0).where(clean.notna())


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int = 3):
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = "__POOL__"
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else "__POOL__"
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), "__POOL__")
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab


def _group_purge(df: pd.DataFrame, lab) -> pd.DataFrame:
    fallback = _broadcast(df.mean(axis=1), df)
    if lab is None:
        return df - fallback
    gmean = df.T.groupby(lab).transform("mean").T
    gmean = gmean.reindex(index=df.index, columns=df.columns)
    gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
    return df - gmean


def _shock_theta(
    y0: pd.DataFrame,
    xs: pd.Series,
    n: int,
    nmin: int,
    lags: int,
    ridge: float,
    shrink: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Total shock-selected distributed-lag response, trailing and ridge-stabilised."""
    base = (xs * xs).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
    theta = None
    for j in range(lags + 1):
        xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
        den = (xl * xl).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
        num = y0.mul(xl, axis=0).rolling(n, min_periods=nmin).mean()
        denom = (den + ridge * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), shrink).fillna(0.0)
        theta = th if theta is None else theta.add(th)
    return theta


@register_factor
class AbsorbedWickRoutedUnowedTransientSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade only the displacement a name was not owed; route by within-bar absorption."""

    factor_id = "absorbed_wick_routed_unowed_transient_snapback"
    name = "Absorption-wick routed un-owed transient snapback"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Sector-purged, participation-weighted within-bar close-location "
        "displacement is orthogonalised against a shock-identified owed "
        "systematic-delivery gap and faded, then blended with that gap using "
        "the cross-sectional rank of the participation-weighted wick "
        "(absorption) share of the last 6 bars as the router."
    )
    window_length = 240
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # displacement / absorption channel
    _vol_window = 60
    _agg = 6
    _part_cap = 4.0
    _shrink_den = 0.5
    # owed-delivery channel
    _lags = 2
    _n = 180
    _nmin = 90
    _thresh = 1.0
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.30
    _k = 6
    # orthogonalisation window
    _orth = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        T, N = len(idx), len(cols)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._nmin) + int(self._agg) + 5 or N < 3:
            return zero

        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()
        volume = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- channel 1: participation-weighted within-bar displacement ----------
        clv = ((close - lo) - (hi - close)) / rng
        clv = clv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        vbase = ts_mean(volume, int(self._vol_window)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        part = (volume / vbase).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, float(self._part_cap))

        ok = clv.notna() & part.notna()
        c = clv.where(ok, 0.0)
        w = part.where(ok, 0.0)
        num = decay_linear(w * c, int(self._agg))
        den = decay_linear(w, int(self._agg))
        disp = (num / (den + float(self._shrink_den))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get("sector"), cols)
        idio_disp = _group_purge(disp, lab)

        # ---- channel 2: shock-identified owed systematic delivery ---------------
        px = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lr = np.log(px).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sig = (lr.rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (lr / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)

        mkt = lr.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))
        xs = z.where(z.abs() > float(self._thresh), 0.0)

        theta = _shock_theta(y0, xs, int(self._n), int(self._nmin),
                            int(self._lags), float(self._ridge), float(self._shrink))

        z_df = _broadcast(z, close)
        implied = theta * ts_sum(z_df, int(self._k))
        delivered = ts_sum(y0, int(self._k))
        owed = ((implied - delivered) / np.sqrt(float(self._k)))
        owed = owed.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        alive = y.notna().rolling(int(self._k), min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        owed = owed.where(alive)

        # ---- interaction: purge displacement of the part it was OWED -----------
        d_for_orth = owed.fillna(0.0)
        resid = rolling_residual(idio_disp.fillna(0.0), d_for_orth, int(self._orth))
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        unowed = resid.where(resid.notna(), idio_disp)   # fall back before window fills
        unowed = unowed.where(idio_disp.notna())

        # ---- router: participation-weighted within-bar wick (absorption) share --
        body = (close - open_).abs()
        wick = (rng - body).clip(lower=0.0)
        wshare = (wick / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        ok2 = wshare.notna() & part.notna()
        wnum = decay_linear(wshare.where(ok2, 0.0) * w, int(self._agg))
        absorb = (wnum / (den + float(self._shrink_den))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        s = rank(absorb)
        s = s.where(s.notna(), 0.5)

        # ---- blend --------------------------------------------------------------
        a = _centred_rank(-unowed)      # fade the un-owed transient displacement
        b = _centred_rank(owed)         # ride the owed systematic catch-up
        a_ok, b_ok = a.notna(), b.notna()
        s_eff = s.where(b_ok, 1.0).where(a_ok, 0.0)
        raw = s_eff * a.fillna(0.0) + (1.0 - s_eff) * b.fillna(0.0)

        valid = a_ok | b_ok
        raw = raw.where(valid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Absorption-wick routed, un-owed transient snapback
programs.trading_idea: Parent B's participation-weighted range-position displacement measures where inside a heavy-volume bar the mid ended up, i.e. the unpaid cost of immediacy that relaxes as depth refills; Parent A's shock-selected distributed-lag kernel measures how much systematic move the name still OWES the market impulse. The child first *purges* the displacement of the part that is mechanically explained by the owed-delivery gap (trailing per-name OLS residual of displacement on the gap), so the fade is applied only to displacement nobody was entitled to, and then routes between the two channels with a state variable neither parent uses: the participation-weighted wick share of the last 6 bars (range minus body over range), which distinguishes bars where aggressive size was absorbed and retraced from clean directional body moves. Where absorption is high the un-owed displacement is pure liquidity provision and snaps back; where bars are body-dominated the displacement is beta delivery in progress and the owed-catch-up direction carries the sign. The interaction is the edge: B cannot tell a low close inside a heavy range from legitimate downside beta delivery, and A has no within-bar geometry to know whether the push was absorbed or accepted.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of a blend between (i) the negated, sector-purged, participation-weighted close-location displacement after removing its trailing regression on the shock-identified owed systematic-delivery gap, and (ii) that owed gap itself, routed by the rank of the participation-weighted within-bar wick (absorption) share of the last 6 bars.

programs.code:
"""Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback.

Mechanism: basket / program executions (index rebalances, ETF create-redeem
arbitrage, cash-flow programs) spread dollars across names in proportion to
capitalisation weight, not in proportion to fundamental beta.  The displacement
they cause in name i therefore scales with weight_i / depth_i, i.e. with
kappa_i = marketCap_i / trailing dollar volume = the inverse of dollar turnover.

The parent factor *assumed* the mechanical push equalled kappa times the
cap-weighted market return, so all of its cross-sectional dispersion came from a
nearly static characteristic timed by one common market scalar.  Here the push is
MEASURED.  Each bar:

  1. build cross-sectionally standardised exposures z_kappa and z_beta;
  2. project z_kappa onto z_beta cross-sectionally and keep the residual e_t --
     the impact-elasticity exposure that is orthogonal to the information
     (beta) channel, a principled replacement for a rank difference;
  3. read the realised *mechanical factor return*
         g_t = sum_i e_it r_it / sum_i e_it^2,
     the per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on e -- the actual
     displacement per unit of impact elasticity;
  4. gate g_t by a basket-program detector G_t (cross-sectional correlation
     between each name's dollar-volume-share deviation from its trailing norm
     and the direction of the cap-weight vector, scaled by aggregate relative
     activity), then accumulate G_t g_t with an exponential memory and lag it
     one bar so only past information is used;
  5. signal = -(e_it) x standardised accumulation: fade the mechanical push.

Everything is trailing or contemporaneous; no forward shifts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, returns, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar Series across all tickers."""
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.reindex(index), dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)


def _xs_corr(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional Pearson correlation between two aligned frames."""
    mask = a.notna() & b.notna()
    aa = a.where(mask)
    bb = b.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    ac = aa.sub(aa.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    bc = bb.sub(bb.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (ac * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = np.sqrt((ac * ac).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) * (bc * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1))
    out = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return out.where(n >= min_names)


def _xs_standardise(df: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional z-score (robust to a few missing names)."""
    n = df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sd = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    z = z.where(_row_broadcast(n, df.index, df.columns) >= float(min_names))
    return z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _xs_orthogonalise(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional residual of y on x (both already demeaned-ish).

    slope_t = sum_i y_it x_it / sum_i x_it^2 over names where both exist.
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    yc = yy.sub(yy.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    xc = xx.sub(xx.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (yc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (xc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    slope = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    resid = yc.sub(xc.mul(slope, axis=0))
    resid = resid.sub(resid.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _xs_factor_return(exposure: pd.DataFrame, ret: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on an exposure."""
    mask = exposure.notna() & ret.notna()
    e = exposure.where(mask)
    r = ret.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    e = e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    r = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (e * r).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (e * e).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    g = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return g.where(n >= min_names)


@register_factor
class ProgramGatedElasticityFactorReturnSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade the measured mechanical (weight-per-depth) cross-sectional push."""

    factor_id = "program_gated_elasticity_factor_return_snapback"
    name = "Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity exposure times minus an "
        "exponentially accumulated, program-gated cross-sectional factor return "
        "measured on that same exposure."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        L = 120           # trailing estimation window (20 minutes on 10s bars)
        mp = max(20, L // 2)
        hl = 4.0          # exponential memory of the accumulated push (bars)
        min_names = 8

        # ---------------- returns ----------------
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)

        # ---------------- capitalisation weights ----------------
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
        med_cap = mcap.median(axis=1)
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).ffill()
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        cap = mcap.where(mcap.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_cap, idx, cols))

        cap_tot = cap.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        w = cap.div(cap_tot, axis=0)

        # cap-weighted market return over names quoting this bar (beta reference)
        w_av = w.where(ret.notna())
        denom = w_av.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        m = (w_av * ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / denom
        m = m.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---------------- basket-program detector ----------------
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dv = (close.abs() * vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        tot_dv = dv.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        share = dv.div(tot_dv, axis=0)
        share_bar = ts_mean(share, L)

        dev_share = share - share_bar          # allocation anomaly this bar
        dev_w = w - share_bar                  # direction of the cap-weight vector
        tilt = _xs_corr(dev_share, dev_w, min_names)

        act = tot_dv / tot_dv.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        act = act.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.25, 6.0)

        G = 0.10 + tilt.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0) * np.sqrt(act)
        G = G.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.10)

        # ---------------- exposures: elasticity and beta ----------------
        advdv = adv(dv, L).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        turnover = (advdv / cap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        turnover = turnover.where(turnover > 0.0)
        kappa = -np.log(turnover)              # weight-per-depth fragility

        m_df = _row_broadcast(m.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret.fillna(0.0), m_df, L)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 5.0)

        z_kappa = _xs_standardise(kappa, min_names)
        z_beta = _xs_standardise(beta, min_names)

        # beta-orthogonal mechanical exposure
        e = _xs_orthogonalise(z_kappa, z_beta)

        # ---------------- measured mechanical factor return ----------------
        g = _xs_factor_return(e, ret, min_names)
        sig_g = g.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g_std = (g / sig_g).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        push = (G * g_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        P = push.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        P = P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        P_df = _row_broadcast(P, idx, cols)

        # ---------------- signal ----------------
        valid = e.notna() & ret.notna()
        raw = (-e) * P_df
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)

        out = raw.sub(raw.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback
programs.trading_idea: Basket/program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight rather than by fundamental beta, so their price displacement loads on a name's weight-per-unit-depth elasticity kappa = marketCap / dollar-volume, a characteristic that is orthogonal to beta only after explicit projection. Rather than *assuming* the mechanical push equals kappa times the cap-weighted market return (the parent's single common scalar, which makes every cross-sectional bet a static pattern timed by a beta-like market signal), I *measure* it: each bar I run a cross-sectional regression of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity exposure and read off the realised 'mechanical factor return' g_t — the actual displacement per unit of impact elasticity, cleanly separated from the information (beta) channel. Accumulating g_t with an exponential memory only over bars whose cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector (the basket footprint) isolates uncompensated liquidity demand, which must relax; the signal is minus the name's orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulation. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the depth-heterogeneous mechanical component un-hedged, and capturing it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
programs.description: Per bar, cross-sectionally regress returns on the beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity (-log dollar turnover) to extract a mechanical factor return; accumulate it with an exponential kernel gated by a basket-program detector (alignment of dollar-volume-share deviations with the cap-weight vector), and short names in proportion to their orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulated push.

programs.code:
"""Corporate Net-Demand Hinge: asymmetric intraday dislocation repair.

Mechanism: corporations are price-insensitive, direction-known participants.
An active repurchaser runs a standing algorithmic bid (10b-18 style VWAP
slicing, participation capped as a share of contemporaneous volume), so its
idiosyncratic dips are absorbed and repair quickly; a net issuer supplies
stock into strength, so its rallies are capped.  The reversal coefficient is
therefore a HINGE: it acts on the negative part of the dislocation for net
repurchasers and on the positive part for net issuers.  Falsified if the
sign-asymmetry vanishes (identical reversion for issuers and repurchasers).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import stddev, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _frame(data: dict, key: str, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Defensively fetch a panel field, aligned and numeric (NaN if absent)."""
    df = data.get(key)
    if df is None:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=index, columns=columns)
    out = df.reindex(index=index, columns=columns)
    out = out.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors='coerce')
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _corporate_net_demand(data: dict, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Point-in-time net corporate demand for own stock, as a fraction of cap.

    Positive  = firm is a net buyer of its own shares (repurchase programme).
    Negative  = firm is a net supplier (issuance, ATM, secondary).
    Quarterly step function; missing names are left NaN and neutralised later.
    """
    mcap = _frame(data, 'marketCap', index, columns)
    mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
    nsi = _frame(data, 'netStockIssuance', index, columns)
    rep = _frame(data, 'shareRepurchase', index, columns)
    sgr = _frame(data, 'sharesGrowth', index, columns)
    d1 = -nsi / mcap
    d2 = -rep / mcap
    d3 = (-sgr).clip(-0.25, 0.25)
    demand = d1.where(d1.notna(), d2)
    demand = demand.where(demand.notna(), d3)
    return demand.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _signed_robust_scale(df: pd.DataFrame, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise scaling by the cross-sectional median absolute value.

    Unlike a z-score this PRESERVES the economic sign (net buyer vs net
    seller): only the magnitude is put on a comparable cross-sectional scale.
    """
    med_abs = df.abs().median(axis=1)
    med_abs = med_abs.where(med_abs > 0.0, np.nan)
    out = df.div(med_abs, axis=0)
    return out.clip(-cap, cap)

@register_factor
class CorporateNetDemandHingeAsymmetricDislocation(BaseFactor):
    """Hinge interaction of dislocation sign with corporate net share demand."""
    factor_id = 'corporate_net_demand_hinge_asymmetric_dislocatio'
    name = 'Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)'
    category = 'mean_reversion'
    description = 'Volatility-scaled 12-bar market-neutral dislocation split into its negative and positive parts and interacted, hinge-style, with point-in-time corporate net share demand (repurchases vs issuance), scaled by current relative volume and cross-sectionally demeaned.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'netStockIssuance', 'shareRepurchase', 'sharesGrowth']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _DISLOC_WIN = 12
    _SIGMA_WIN = 240
    _VOL_FAST = 6
    _VOL_SLOW = 240
    _DEMAND_CAP = 3.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        index, columns = (close.index, close.columns)
        ret = _log_returns(close)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1)
        idio = ret.sub(mkt, axis=0)
        sigma = stddev(idio.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN)
        sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cum = ts_sum(idio.fillna(0.0), self._DISLOC_WIN)
        disloc = cum / (sigma * np.sqrt(float(self._DISLOC_WIN)))
        disloc = disloc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        disloc = disloc.where(sigma.notna() & ret.notna())
        dip = (-disloc).clip(lower=0.0)
        pop = disloc.clip(lower=0.0)
        demand = _corporate_net_demand(data, index, columns)
        b = _signed_robust_scale(demand, self._DEMAND_CAP)
        b = b.fillna(0.0)
        buyer = b.clip(lower=0.0)
        seller = (-b).clip(lower=0.0)
        vol = _frame(data, 'volume', index, columns).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        base = ts_mean(vol, self._VOL_SLOW).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        v_rel = ts_mean(vol, self._VOL_FAST) / base
        gate = np.sqrt(v_rel.clip(0.2, 5.0))
        gate = gate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(1.0)
        score = (buyer * dip - seller * pop) * gate
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.where(disloc.notna())
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return score.reindex(index=index, columns=columns)
programs.name: Corporate Net-Demand Hinge (asymmetric intraday dislocation)
programs.trading_idea: Firms are the one class of participant whose trading direction is known in advance and is price-insensitive: an active repurchaser has a standing algorithmic *bid* working the tape all day (Rule 10b-18 VWAP slicing), while a net issuer (ATM/secondary/option-driven supply) is a standing *offer*. This makes short-horizon liquidity provision asymmetric at the firm level: an idiosyncratic dip in a heavy repurchaser is absorbed by corporate demand and snaps back within a minute, whereas a rally in a net issuer is capped by corporate supply — so the reversal coefficient should be a hinge in the sign of the dislocation interacted with the sign of net corporate share issuance, not a symmetric linear reversal. Because participation is capped as a fraction of contemporaneous volume, the support strength scales with current relative volume. The edge survives arbitrage because intraday buyback schedules are never disclosed (only quarterly totals), so an arbitrageur cannot distinguish a corporate-supported dip from genuine adverse information ex ante and must warehouse inventory risk; it is falsified if downside reversion at 6 bars is identical for repurchasers and issuers, i.e. if the hinge interaction adds nothing over symmetric reversal.
programs.description: Piecewise (hinge) interaction between a volatility-scaled 12-bar market-neutral price dislocation and point-in-time corporate net share demand: long the dip in net repurchasers, short the rally in net issuers, with the magnitude scaled by current relative volume and the cross-section demeaned.

programs.code:
"""Comparable-basket dislocation repaired on a peer-activity clock.

Mechanism
---------
Dealers who absorb an idiosyncratic dislocation hedge it with the name's
*valuation comparables*: same industry AND similar market cap (so the hedge legs
have comparable liquidity and factor loadings).  The dislocation therefore decays
at a rate that (a) differs per name -- some names have a repair half-life of
seconds, others of many minutes -- and (b) is proportional to how much hedging
capacity is live in the comparable basket right now.

Design choices that follow from the mechanism
---------------------------------------------
  * Peer set = static industry (or sector) label refined by a size split, using
    the FIRST observed marketCap per name (no look-ahead in the grouping key).
  * Dislocation = log price minus the leave-one-out comparable-basket log price,
    demeaned by its own 600-bar level (removes each name's permanent premium)
    and standardised by trailing dispersion.  It is averaged over 3 bars because
    a single bar-close contains Roll bid-ask noise, which would bias a
    level-on-change regression toward spurious reversal.
  * The loading is HORIZON-MATCHED and PER NAME: a trailing OLS beta of the
    realised 6-bar comparable-relative return on the dislocation observed 6 bars
    earlier.  It is shrunk toward the cross-sectional median loading with weight
    R^2 / (R^2 + 0.02), so poorly identified names inherit the pooled repair
    rate instead of noise.  This is what makes the signal live at the fixed
    6-bar offset rather than at 24 bars: names whose measured repair clock is
    slower than a minute simply get a small loading.
  * Repair capacity gate (strictly positive, never flips the sign):
    (1 - exp(-3 * peer activity, leave-one-out)) * (0.3 + 0.7 * hedge quality),
    where hedge quality is the trailing correlation between the name's 1-bar
    return and its basket's return -- a basket that does not track the name is
    not a usable hedge.

Causality: every cross-sectional statistic is taken inside one timestamp; every
time-series statistic is a trailing rolling window or a positive lag; the fit
pairs the 6-bar return ending at t with a regressor observed at t-6.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    correlation,
    rank,
    rolling_beta,
    stddev,
    ts_mean,
    ts_rank,
    ts_sum,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _first_valid(df: pd.DataFrame | None, col: str) -> float | None:
    """Earliest non-NaN value of a column -- used so grouping keys are
    determined by information available at (or before) the start of the sample."""
    if df is None or col not in df.columns:
        return None
    ser = df[col].dropna()
    if len(ser) == 0:
        return None
    try:
        return float(ser.iloc[0])
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _comparable_labels(
    columns: pd.Index,
    sector: pd.DataFrame | None,
    industry: pd.DataFrame | None,
    mcap: pd.DataFrame | None,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Static comparable-basket key: industry (else sector) x size half."""
    base = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[0]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    base[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                base[col] = str(val)

    caps: dict[str, float] = {}
    for col in columns:
        v = _first_valid(mcap, col)
        if v is not None and np.isfinite(v) and v > 0.0:
            caps[col] = v
    if len(caps) < 6:
        return base

    cap = pd.Series(caps, dtype=float)
    out = base.copy()
    for key, members in base.groupby(base).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in cap.index]
        if len(cols) < 6:
            continue
        med = float(cap[cols].median())
        for c in cols:
            out[c] = "%s|%s" % (key, "H" if cap[c] >= med else "L")
    return out


def _loo_mean(a: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-group mean EXCLUDING the name itself (leave-one-out)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in a.columns]
        if not cols:
            continue
        sub = a[cols]
        present = sub.notna().to_numpy().astype(float)
        vals = sub.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        tot = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        cnt = present.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        excl_sum = tot - vals
        excl_cnt = cnt - present
        ok = excl_cnt >= float(min_peers)
        safe = np.where(excl_cnt > 0.0, excl_cnt, 1.0)
        res = np.where(ok, excl_sum / safe, np.nan)
        out[cols] = pd.DataFrame(res, index=a.index, columns=cols)
    return out


@register_factor
class ComparableBasketRepairRateActivityClock(BaseFactor):
    """Per-name horizon-matched repair of a comparable-basket dislocation,
    scaled by live hedging capacity in that basket."""

    factor_id = "comparable_basket_repair_rate_activity_clock_h6"
    name = "Comparable-basket repair rate on a peer-activity clock"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Noise-averaged deviation of log price from its leave-one-out "
        "valuation-comparable basket (industry x size half), multiplied by a "
        "trailing per-name horizon-matched OLS loading (shrunk toward the "
        "cross-sectional median by fit R^2) and by a positive repair-capacity "
        "gate from leave-one-out peer activity and rolling basket hedge quality."
    )
    window_length = 1400
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6
    _L = 600      # own-level baseline (~100 minutes at 10s bars)
    _SD = 300     # trailing dispersion window (~50 minutes)
    _FIT = 600    # trailing per-name loading window
    _ACT = 300    # activity / hedge-quality window
    _MIN_PEERS = 2
    _SHRINK_C = 0.02
    _CAP_B = 2.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)

        labels = _comparable_labels(
            cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"), data.get("marketCap")
        )

        # ---- comparable-basket dislocation -----------------------------------
        bp = _loo_mean(lp, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        sp = (lp - bp).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d))
        if sp.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        d_raw = sp - ts_mean(sp, self._L)
        sd_d = stddev(d_raw, self._SD).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dz = (d_raw / sd_d).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        ds = ts_mean(dz, 3)                      # Roll-noise averaged regressor

        # ---- horizon-matched target: 6-bar comparable-relative return --------
        ry = sp - sp.shift(self._H)
        sd_y = stddev(ry, self._SD).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        yz = (ry / sd_y).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        xl = ds.shift(self._H)
        b = rolling_beta(yz, xl, self._FIT)
        r = correlation(yz, xl, self._FIT)
        r2 = (r * r).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d))
        w = (r2 / (r2 + self._SHRINK_C)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        b_cs = b.median(axis=1)
        b_cs_df = pd.DataFrame({c: b_cs for c in cols}, index=idx).reindex(columns=cols)
        b_eff = b.sub(b_cs, axis=0).mul(w).add(b_cs, axis=0)
        b_eff = b_eff.where(np.isfinite(b_eff))
        b_eff = b_eff.where(b_eff.notna(), b_cs_df).clip(-self._CAP_B, self._CAP_B)

        # ---- repair-capacity gate (strictly positive) ------------------------
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            a_peer = pd.DataFrame(0.5, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0), 0.0)
            live = ts_sum(v, self._ACT) > 0.0
            a_own = ts_rank(ts_sum(v, self._H), self._ACT).where(live)
            a_peer = _loo_mean(a_own, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        a_peer = a_peer.where(np.isfinite(a_peer)).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)

        r1 = lp - lp.shift(1)
        br1 = _loo_mean(r1, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        h = correlation(r1, br1, self._ACT)
        h_pos = h.where(np.isfinite(h)).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.3)

        gate = (1.0 - np.exp(-3.0 * a_peer)) * (0.3 + 0.7 * h_pos)
        gate = gate.where(np.isfinite(gate)).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- forecast of the 6-bar comparable-relative return ----------------
        pred = b_eff * ds * gate
        signal = pred.where(np.isfinite(pred) & ds.notna() & b_eff.notna())

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Comparable-basket dislocation with per-name repair rate on a peer-activity clock
programs.trading_idea: A name's deviation from its *valuation-comparable* basket (same industry AND same size half, because dealers hedge inventory with similar-cap same-industry names) is repaired at a speed that differs per name and is proportional to how much hedging capacity is live in that basket right now. The parent measured the dislocation and gated it with coarse 2x2 activity cells but fitted a single pooled loading, so names whose natural repair half-life is far from 60 seconds diluted the 6-bar signal (its IC peaked at 24 bars); the child instead estimates each name's own horizon-matched repair loading by a trailing OLS of the realised 6-bar comparable-relative return on the lagged, noise-averaged dislocation, and scales it by a continuous repair-capacity clock = (peer leave-one-out activity) x (statistical hedge quality of the basket for that name). Falsifiable predictions: (i) names with an empirically fast, well-identified 6-bar repair loading carry essentially all of the 6-bar edge and names with weak/slow loadings carry none; (ii) the same dislocation predicts a strictly smaller repair when its comparables are quiet or poorly correlated with it. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a capacity constraint, not a mispricing: closing an idiosyncratic dislocation consumes hedging capital and simultaneous comparable-basket liquidity, and in the states where that liquidity is absent nobody can force the repair inside a minute.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of a per-name 6-bar return forecast: the noise-averaged deviation of log price from its valuation-comparable basket (industry x size-half, leave-one-out) relative to its own 600-bar level, multiplied by a trailing per-name horizon-matched OLS loading (shrunk empirical-Bayes style toward the cross-sectional median loading by fit R-squared) and by a positive repair-capacity gate built from leave-one-out peer activity and the name's rolling correlation with its basket.

programs.code:
"""Round-number lattice barrier asymmetry on a volatility-matched grid.

Mechanism: retail and algorithmic limit orders cluster on round price nodes
(x.05 / x.10 / x.25 / x.50 / x.00).  The economically relevant node spacing for a
given forecast horizon is the one comparable to the distance the mid actually
travels over that horizon, so the lattice is selected per name so that its
spacing ~ 2 x (trailing dollar sigma of 6-bar price changes).  Inside a lattice
cell the excess resting depth sits at the two boundaries: a mid travelling
*toward* the near boundary meets abnormally thick liquidity and stalls / retreats,
while a mid that has just *crossed* a boundary has consumed that depth and faces
a thinner book ahead, so it continues.  Both effects are one antisymmetric
function of the position inside the cell, signed by the direction of travel; its
unconditional (uniform-in-cell) mean is zero, so the score carries almost no
plain short-term-reversal loading.  A per-name empirical gate (excess frequency
of the mid sitting within +/-12.5% of a cell width of a node, versus the 25%
uniform benchmark) amplifies names where the clustering is actually observed and
damps names where it is not.

Everything is trailing (rolling windows, positive lags) and the final step is a
same-bar cross-sectional rank, hence causal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, sign, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_TINY = 1e-12
_GRIDS = (0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 1.00)


def _select_grid(sigma: pd.DataFrame, c: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar, per-name round-number grid whose spacing is closest (in log) to
    ``c * sigma``.  Deterministic, elementwise, uses only the passed trailing
    sigma, so it is causal."""
    target = np.log(np.maximum(c * sigma.to_numpy(dtype=float), _TINY))
    grid = None
    best = None
    for cand in _GRIDS:
        cost = np.abs(np.log(cand) - target)
        if grid is None:
            grid = np.full(cost.shape, float(cand))
            best = cost
        else:
            upd = cost < best
            grid = np.where(upd, float(cand), grid)
            best = np.where(upd, cost, best)
    out = pd.DataFrame(grid, index=sigma.index, columns=sigma.columns)
    return out.where(sigma.notna())


@register_factor
class RoundNumberLatticeBarrierAsymmetryH6(BaseFactor):
    """Resistance before a round node, continuation just after it."""

    factor_id = "roundnumber_lattice_barrier_breach_asymmetry_h6"
    name = "Volatility-matched round-number lattice barrier asymmetry"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Antisymmetric within-cell barrier score on a per-name round-price lattice "
        "matched to the 6-bar dollar volatility: -sign(drift) x [exp(-d_ahead/sigma) "
        "- exp(-d_behind/sigma)], amplified by measured excess occupancy of node "
        "neighbourhoods, ranked cross-sectionally."
    )
    window_length = 520
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _sig_window = 240
    _sig_min = 60
    _grid_c = 2.0
    _drift_window = 12
    _occ_window = 480
    _occ_min = 120
    _node_band = 0.125
    _k_lo = 0.75
    _k_hi = 10.0

    def calc(self, data: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- horizon-matched dollar volatility of a 6-bar move -------------
        d6 = (px - px.shift(self.prediction_horizon)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        sigma = d6.rolling(self._sig_window, min_periods=self._sig_min).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- pick the round-number lattice for this name -------------------
        grid = _select_grid(sigma, self._grid_c)
        k = (grid / sigma).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)   # cell width in sigmas
        usable = (k >= self._k_lo) & (k <= self._k_hi)

        # ---- position inside the lattice cell -----------------------------
        q = (px / grid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        u = q - np.floor(q)                                     # in [0, 1)

        # ---- direction of travel toward / away from a node ----------------
        dev = (px - ts_mean(px, self._drift_window)).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        d = sign(dev)

        # ---- distances (in sigma units) to node ahead / behind ------------
        a_up = k * (1.0 - u)
        a_dn = k * u
        ahead = a_up.where(d > 0.0, a_dn)
        behind = (k - ahead)

        barrier = np.exp(-ahead.clip(0.0, 50.0)) - np.exp(-behind.clip(0.0, 50.0))

        # ---- empirical node-clustering gate -------------------------------
        m = pd.DataFrame(
            np.minimum(u.to_numpy(dtype=float), 1.0 - u.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=idx,
            columns=cols,
        )
        near = (m < self._node_band).astype(float).where(u.notna())
        occ = near.rolling(self._occ_window, min_periods=self._occ_min).mean()
        excess = occ - 0.25                                     # uniform benchmark
        gate = (1.0 + 4.0 * excess).clip(0.25, 3.0)

        # ---- signed score --------------------------------------------------
        score = (-d * barrier * gate).where(usable)
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        active = score.notna() & (score.abs() > 1e-9) & px.notna()
        out = rank(score.where(active)) - 0.5

        return (
            out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Volatility-matched round-number lattice barrier asymmetry
programs.trading_idea: Human limit-order placement clusters on round price nodes (…x.00, x.50, x.25, x.10, x.05), so the book carries excess resting depth exactly at those levels; the relevant node spacing is the one comparable to the distance price actually travels over the forecast horizon. A mid drifting *into* the nearest node therefore meets an abnormally thick wall and stalls/retreats, while a mid that has just *passed* a node has consumed that depth and faces a thinner book on the far side, so it continues. The child expresses this as a single antisymmetric function of the price's position inside its volatility-matched lattice cell, signed by the direction of travel — so it is resistance and post-breach continuation in one term whose time-series mean loading on plain reversal is ~zero (position within a cell is nearly uniform), which is why it is not another reversal clone. The edge survives arbitrage because each event is worth a fraction of a tick, it lives in the price *level modulo a lattice* — a non-scale-invariant feature that virtually every return-based model normalises away — and crossing the spread to harvest it costs more than the drift for anyone not already resting in the queue.
programs.description: Chooses per name the round-price grid (0.05…1.00) whose spacing best matches ~2x the trailing dollar sigma of 6-bar moves, then scores -sign(recent drift) x [exp(-distance to the node ahead / sigma) - exp(-distance to the node behind / sigma)], amplified by the name's measured excess occupancy of node neighbourhoods, ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Kalman-gain transient deviation with noise-purged path memory.

Mechanism: the observed mid price is p_t = M_t + eps_t, where M is the efficient
(fractional-Gaussian) price and eps is a transient microstructure deviation from
quote bounce, discreteness and unwinding impact.  Over a 6-bar (60-second)
horizon the expected observed change is

    E[p_{t+6} - p_t] = -eps_t + rho_eff * (M_t - M_{t-6}),

i.e. the transient deviation is fully repaid while the efficient path carries
its own signed block memory rho_eff = 2^(2H-1) - 1.  The parent factor purged
2*Var(eps) out of its displacement scales and then forecast only the second
term; because at 10-second sampling the first term dominates the forecastable
variation, its realized IC came out with the opposite sign.  This child keeps
the noise identification but *uses* the noise instead of discarding it.

Noise identification is exact under the fGn-plus-iid-noise model when scales are
geometric: with Var(D_k) = A k^{2H} + s (s = 2 Var(eps)) and k = 1, 4, 16,

    s = (V_4^2 - V_1 V_16) / (2 V_4 - V_1 - V_16),

which holds for every H (the roughness cancels).  Scale is measured with mean
absolute displacement (q = 1) mapped through the Gaussian constant pi/2, which
is far more robust to jumps than a second moment.  Given s, the per-bar
efficient variance is A = V_1 - s, the signal-to-noise ratio is q = A / (s/2),
and the steady-state local-level (Kalman) gain solving K^2 + qK - q = 0 gives
the *optimal per-name filter bandwidth*: eps_hat_t = p_t - EWMA_K(p)_t.  The
filtered path also supplies the efficient displacement used with rho_eff.

Falsifiable: if the tradable object at 60 seconds were efficient-price memory
rather than the repayment of a name-specific transient deviation, the -eps_hat
term would carry no information and the factor's IC would be zero or negative.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices (causal)."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _mad_var(disp: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Variance implied by a trailing mean-absolute-displacement scale (q = 1)."""
    a = ts_mean(disp.abs(), n)
    return (math.pi / 2.0) * a.pow(2.0)


def _elem_clip(x: pd.DataFrame, lo: pd.DataFrame, hi: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Element-wise clip with DataFrame bounds (NaNs propagate)."""
    v = np.minimum(np.maximum(x.to_numpy(), lo.to_numpy()), hi.to_numpy())
    return pd.DataFrame(v, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)


def _gain_lattice_ewma(
    path: pd.DataFrame,
    gain: pd.DataFrame,
    alphas: tuple,
    default_j: int,
    min_p: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """EWMA of `path` whose smoothing constant is chosen, per name and bar, as the
    lattice point nearest (in log space) to the estimated Kalman gain.

    Fully causal: every candidate EWMA is a trailing exponential average and the
    lattice choice at t uses only trailing-window estimates of the gain.
    """
    logk = np.log(gain.where(gain > 0.0))
    chosen = pd.DataFrame(
        float(default_j), index=path.index, columns=path.columns
    )
    best = None
    for j, a in enumerate(alphas):
        d = (logk - math.log(a)).abs()
        if best is None:
            best = d
            chosen = chosen.where(d.isna(), float(j))
        else:
            better = (d < best).fillna(False)
            chosen = chosen.where(~better, float(j))
            best = best.where(~better, d)
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=path.index, columns=path.columns)
    for j, a in enumerate(alphas):
        m = path.ewm(alpha=float(a), adjust=True, min_periods=int(min_p)).mean()
        out = out.where(chosen != float(j), m)
    return out


@register_factor
class TsrvKalmanGainTransientDeviationMemory(BaseFactor):
    """Fade the per-name Kalman-filtered transient deviation, follow purged memory."""

    factor_id = "tsrv_kalman_gain_transient_deviation_memory_h6"
    name = "Kalman-gain transient deviation with noise-purged path memory"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Negative of the log-price deviation from a per-name Kalman-gain EWMA of "
        "the idiosyncratic log-price path, plus the fractional-Gaussian block "
        "autocorrelation applied to the filtered 6-bar efficient displacement, "
        "both scaled by the name's 6-bar efficient volatility; noise variance, "
        "Hurst exponent and gain are identified from mean-absolute displacements "
        "at 1, 4 and 16 bars."
    )
    window_length = 560
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K1 = 1
    _K2 = 4
    _K3 = 16
    _EST_WIN = 480
    _H_BLOCK = 6
    _PRIOR = 8.0
    _ALPHAS = (0.04, 0.09, 0.18, 0.35, 0.65)
    _DEFAULT_J = 2

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        ret = _log_returns(close)
        # market (cross-sectional median) removed: forecast the idiosyncratic path
        rres = ret.sub(ret.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        rf = rres.fillna(0.0)

        k1, k2, k3 = int(self._K1), int(self._K2), int(self._K3)
        n = int(self._EST_WIN)
        h = int(self._H_BLOCK)

        d1 = rf if k1 == 1 else ts_sum(rf, k1)
        d2 = ts_sum(rf, k2)
        d3 = ts_sum(rf, k3)

        v1 = _mad_var(d1, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        v2 = _mad_var(d2, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        v3 = _mad_var(d3, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # --- exact three-scale noise identification (s = 2 Var(eps)) ---------
        num = v2 * v2 - v1 * v3
        den = 2.0 * v2 - v1 - v3
        s3 = (num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # random-walk fallback if the second difference is ill-conditioned
        a_fb = (v3 - v1) / float(k3 - k1)
        s_fb = v1 - a_fb

        lo = 0.02 * v1
        hi = 0.90 * v1
        ok = (den < 0.0) & s3.notna() & (s3 > lo) & (s3 < hi)
        s = s3.where(ok, s_fb)
        s = _elem_clip(s, lo, hi)

        # --- roughness exponent from the noise-purged scale ratio ------------
        ratio = ((v3 - s) / (v1 - s)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ratio = ratio.clip(1e-06, 1000000.0)
        hurst = (np.log(ratio) / (2.0 * math.log(float(k3)))).clip(0.10, 0.90)

        a_eff = (v1 - s)                      # per-bar efficient variance scale
        var_h = a_eff * np.exp(2.0 * hurst * math.log(float(h)))
        sd_h = np.sqrt(var_h.clip(lower=0.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # --- steady-state local-level Kalman gain from signal-to-noise -------
        sig_eps2 = (s / 2.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        q = (a_eff / sig_eps2).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        q = q.clip(1e-06, 1000000.0)
        gain = ((np.sqrt(q * q + 4.0 * q) - q) / 2.0).clip(0.02, 0.95)

        # --- filter the idiosyncratic log-price path with that gain ----------
        lp = rf.cumsum()
        mfilt = _gain_lattice_ewma(
            lp, gain, self._ALPHAS, int(self._DEFAULT_J), 60
        )
        eps_hat = lp - mfilt                  # estimated transient deviation
        d_eff = mfilt - mfilt.shift(h)        # filtered efficient displacement

        # --- fGn block memory of the efficient path, shrunk by sample size --
        rho = (np.exp((2.0 * hurst - 1.0) * math.log(2.0)) - 1.0).clip(-0.5, 0.6)
        cnt = ret.notna().astype(float).rolling(n, min_periods=int(n // 2)).sum()
        n_eff = cnt / float(k3)
        rho = rho * (n_eff / (n_eff + float(self._PRIOR)))

        e_std = (eps_hat / sd_h).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        d_std = (d_eff / sd_h).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        fc = (-e_std + rho * d_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        fc = fc.where(cnt >= 0.6 * float(n))

        out = fc.sub(fc.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Kalman-gain transient deviation with noise-purged path memory
programs.trading_idea: Observed mid = efficient price + a transient deviation (quote bounce, discreteness, unwinding impact); over a 60-second horizon the *only* reliably forecastable part of the observed mid change is the reversal of that deviation, which is exactly the term the parent subtracted out — hence its declared sign was contradicted. This child identifies the noise variance exactly (invariantly to how rough the efficient price is) from mean-absolute displacements at three geometrically spaced scales (1/4/16 bars), since Var(D_k)=A·k^(2H)+2σ²_ε implies the closed form 2σ²_ε=(V₄²−V₁V₁₆)/(2V₄−V₁−V₁₆); the resulting noise-to-signal ratio q fixes each name's steady-state local-level Kalman gain K=(√(q²+4q)−q)/2, so the transient deviation is measured as the price minus a per-name-bandwidth EWMA rather than a common-lookback deviation. The forecast is −ε̂ (fade the estimated transient) plus the fractional-Gaussian block memory ρ=2^(2H−1)−1 applied to the *filtered* efficient displacement (follow genuinely persistent efficient paths), all in units of the name's 6-bar efficient volatility. The edge persists because reversion desks apply one common filter bandwidth and one common reversion coefficient to the whole book: the residual is the cross-sectional dispersion of the optimal bandwidth and of the noise-purged roughness, worth only a few basis points per name and requiring continuous per-name re-estimation.
