    """Repurchase-capacity x idiosyncratic-dip interaction, main effects purged."""

    factor_id = "buyback_capacity_gated_dip_absorption"
    name = "Buyback-capacity-gated dip absorption"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Interaction of a firm's repurchase-capacity rank (buyback dollars vs "
        "market cap and vs trailing dollar volume, share-count shrinkage, net "
        "issuance, scaled by distance below the 65-minute VWAP anchor) with the "
        "size of its beta-adjusted 6-bar idiosyncratic DOWN push, cross-"
        "sectionally orthogonalised against every main effect and rank-demeaned."
    )
    window_length = 400
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "shareRepurchase",
        "sharesGrowth",
        "netStockIssuance",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    W_LONG = 390      # ~65 minutes: VWAP anchor / traded-dollar capacity window
    W_BETA = 360      # trailing beta and idiosyncratic-vol window
    K_PUSH = 6        # dislocation window == forecast horizon (1 minute)

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        n_cols = len(cols)

        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs().fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        wl, wb, kp = self.W_LONG, self.W_BETA, self.K_PUSH

        # ---- idiosyncratic short-run dislocation -------------------------
        mkt_s = ret.median(axis=1)
        mkt = pd.DataFrame(
            np.tile(mkt_s.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1), (1, n_cols)),
            index=idx,
            columns=cols,
        )
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt, wb)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0).fillna(1.0)
        idio = ret - beta * mkt

        push = idio.rolling(kp, min_periods=kp).sum()
        sd = idio.rolling(wb, min_periods=wb // 2).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (push / (sd * float(np.sqrt(kp)))).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        dn = (-z).clip(lower=0.0)          # size of the idiosyncratic dip
        up = z.clip(lower=0.0)             # size of the idiosyncratic pop

        # ---- VWAP anchor: where a benchmarked desk leans hardest ---------
        pv = (close * vol).rolling(wl, min_periods=wl // 3).sum()
        vv = vol.rolling(wl, min_periods=wl // 3).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        anchor = pv / vv
        anchor = anchor.where(anchor > 0.0)
        gap = (anchor - close) / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gapr = rank(gap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)).fillna(0.5)

        # ---- repurchase capacity (point-in-time quarterly fields) --------
        mcap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        rep = data["shareRepurchase"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        rep = rep.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        bb = (-rep).clip(lower=0.0)                     # dollars actually repurchased

        byield = (bb / mcap).clip(0.0, 1.0)             # buyback yield per quarter

        dvol = (close.abs() * vol).rolling(wl, min_periods=wl // 3).sum()
        dvol = dvol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        # quarter ~ 63 sessions, each ~6 windows of 65 minutes -> per-window dollars
        capacity = ((bb / 378.0) / dvol).clip(0.0, 50.0)

        sg = data["sharesGrowth"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        shrink = (-sg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).clip(-0.5, 0.5)

        nsi = data["netStockIssuance"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        net_buy = (-nsi.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / mcap).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        g0 = _rank_mean([byield, capacity, shrink, net_buy])   # in [0, 1]
        g = g0 * (0.5 + gapr)                                  # cheap-vs-anchor tilt

        # ---- the interaction, purged of all main effects -----------------
        inter = _xs_demean(g) * _xs_demean(dn)

        controls: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for c in (dn, up, g0, gapr, g):
            cc = c
            for prev in controls:
                cc = _xs_deflate(cc, prev)
            controls.append(cc)

        resid = inter
        for c in controls:
            resid = _xs_deflate(resid, c)
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = rank(resid)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Buyback-capacity-gated dip absorption
programs.trading_idea: Firms running large actual repurchase programs have a mechanical, price-contingent, anonymous buyer standing in their own book: Rule 10b-18's safe harbour forces the desk to bid passively at or below the last independent bid, caps it near 25% of ADV, and most programs are VWAP-benchmarked, so the desk absorbs weakness and mechanically steps aside on rallies (Hong-Wang-Yu 'firms as buyers of last resort'; Busch-Obernberger RFS 2017 find repurchase flow supplies liquidity and pulls prices back toward value precisely on down-moves). The falsifiable claim is therefore an INTERACTION, not a level: after an idiosyncratic 1-minute dip, names whose quarterly repurchase dollars are large relative to their own realised dollar volume (i.e. the program has capacity to matter) should snap back more than equally-dipped names with no program, and the differential should be absent for equal-sized upward pushes and stronger when the stock is already below its trailing volume-weighted anchor (where VWAP-benchmarked desks buy hardest). We therefore compute the gated dip and Gram-Schmidt out every main effect (dip size, pop size, buyback intensity, VWAP gap), so only the pure interaction survives — this is what decorrelates it from the book's semivariance/reversal family. The edge persists because it requires joining a quarterly cash-flow-statement item to 10-second dislocations, buyback flow is untagged on the tape, and the absorption capacity itself is finite and non-arbitrageable (no instrument pays for it).
programs.description: Cross-sectional interaction between a firm's repurchase-capacity rank (buyback dollars vs market cap, vs trailing dollar volume, share-count shrinkage, net issuance — scaled by how far price sits below its 65-minute VWAP anchor) and the size of its beta-adjusted idiosyncratic 6-bar downward push, orthogonalised cross-sectionally against all main effects and rank-demeaned.

programs.code:
"""Participant-mix adaptive shock response (empirical Bayes).

Mechanism
---------
A 10-second price path is generated by a persistent mixture of two agents:

  * execution algorithms slicing a parent order -> long-memory child order flow
    -> POSITIVE autocorrelation of minute-scale returns (order-splitting memory,
    Bouchaud et al.);
  * liquidity providers recycling inventory -> transient impact decay and quote
    bounce -> NEGATIVE autocorrelation.

Which agent dominates a given name is a *state* that persists for tens of
minutes (a parent order lives that long).  So instead of imposing reversal or
momentum, we estimate the name's own lag-6 return-response coefficient on a
trailing window, shrink it toward a prior by its statistical reliability
(empirical Bayes), and apply it to the live shock.  The prior centre is not
zero but the sign implied by *volume* memory: autocorrelated deseasonalised
bar volume means a parent order is still being worked, which argues for
continuation; choppy volume argues for inventory recycling and reversal.

All statistics are trailing rolling moments or positive lags -> causal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _roll_moments(
    x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, n: int, minp: int
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing covariance and variances of x and y over an n-bar window.

    Implemented from raw rolling means so that min_periods is under our
    control and no pandas pairwise-cov ambiguity can arise.  Purely trailing.
    """
    mx = x.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).mean()
    my = y.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).mean()
    mxx = (x * x).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).mean()
    myy = (y * y).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).mean()
    mxy = (x * y).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).mean()
    cov = mxy - mx * my
    vx = (mxx - mx * mx).clip(lower=0.0)
    vy = (myy - my * my).clip(lower=0.0)
    return cov, vx, vy


def _beta_and_corr(
    y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, minp: int
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing OLS slope of y on x and the corresponding correlation."""
    cov, vx, vy = _roll_moments(x, y, n, minp)
    beta = cov / vx.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    denom = np.sqrt(vx * vy).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    rho = (cov / denom).clip(-0.99, 0.99)
    return beta, rho


def _safe_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return r.fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class ParticipantMixAdaptiveShockResponseEB(BaseFactor):
    """Sign-adaptive shock response: measured, shrunk, and applied."""

    factor_id = "participant_mix_adaptive_shock_response_eb"
    name = "Empirical-Bayes adaptive shock-response state"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Trailing 180-bar OLS response of the 6-bar return to the previous "
        "6-bar return, shrunk by its own reliability toward a prior whose sign "
        "comes from volume-flow persistence, then multiplied by the current "
        "volatility-standardised 6-bar shock; ranked and demeaned cross-"
        "sectionally."
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    H = 6            # shock / response horizon in bars (matches forecast horizon)
    W = 180          # estimation window for the response state (~30 min)
    SEAS = 60        # window used to deseasonalise bar volume
    RHO0 = 0.18      # prior scale: rho0^2 ~ 1 / effective independent obs (W/H)
    PRIOR_AMP = 0.06 # amplitude of the volume-memory prior on the response beta

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        h, w_n = self.H, self.W
        minp = max(60, w_n // 2)

        # ---- horizon-matched shocks -------------------------------------
        r_h = ret.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()          # last h-bar return
        x_prev = delay(r_h, h)                             # the preceding block

        sd_h = r_h.rolling(w_n, min_periods=minp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # winsorise both regression channels at 3 trailing sd so that single
        # jumps do not dictate the estimated response state
        y_w = np.sign(r_h) * np.minimum(r_h.abs(), 3.0 * sd_h)
        x_w = np.sign(x_prev) * np.minimum(x_prev.abs(), 3.0 * delay(sd_h, h))

        beta, rho = _beta_and_corr(y_w, x_w, w_n, minp)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.5, 0.5)

        # ---- empirical-Bayes reliability weight -------------------------
        rho2 = (rho ** 2).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        weight = rho2 / (rho2 + self.RHO0 ** 2)
        weight = weight.fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # ---- mechanism prior: persistence of deseasonalised bar volume ---
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.where(vol > 0.0, 0.0)
        lv = np.log1p(vol)
        lv_norm = lv - lv.rolling(self.SEAS, min_periods=self.SEAS // 2).mean()
        _, vac = _beta_and_corr(lv_norm, delay(lv_norm, 1), w_n, minp)
        prior = self.PRIOR_AMP * (2.0 * _safe_rank(vac) - 1.0)

        beta_eff = weight * beta.fillna(0.0) + (1.0 - weight) * prior

        # ---- apply the state to the live standardised shock -------------
        shock = (r_h / sd_h).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        forecast = beta_eff * shock

        sig = rank(forecast.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Empirical-Bayes adaptive shock-response state (order-splitting memory vs inventory recycling)
programs.trading_idea: At 10-second granularity a price path is produced by a mixture of two agents whose identity persists for tens of minutes: (i) parent orders being sliced by execution algorithms, whose long-memory child-order flow imprints POSITIVE minute-scale return autocorrelation, and (ii) liquidity providers recycling inventory, whose transient impact and quote bounce imprint NEGATIVE autocorrelation. Rather than assuming reversal or continuation, the child *measures* which agent currently dominates each name — a causal trailing OLS of the 6-bar return on the previous 6-bar return — shrinks that estimate toward a mechanism-driven prior by its own statistical reliability (empirical Bayes with weight rho^2/(rho^2+rho0^2)), where the prior centre is set by the persistence of the name's deseasonalised bar volume (autocorrelated volume = a parent order still being worked = continuation prior), and then applies the shrunken response coefficient to the live standardised shock. The edge is falsifiable: if the participant mix were not persistent, this interaction would earn zero IC even though both plain momentum and plain reversal are non-degenerate; it survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires per-name, per-episode state estimation and takes the *opposite* side in different names at the same instant, so it cannot be crowded by a single directional reversal or momentum book.
programs.description: Signal = shrunken trailing lag-6 return-response coefficient (empirical-Bayes blend of a 180-bar rolling OLS beta of the 6-bar return on the prior 6-bar return with a volume-persistence prior) multiplied by the current volatility-standardised 6-bar shock, ranked and demeaned cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Unscheduled-flow impact: diurnal volume surprise x intra-bar price impact.

Mechanism
---------
Intraday volume is dominated by a deterministic calendar schedule (VWAP / TWAP
execution programmes, index and open/close driven flow, the classic U-shape).
The *informative* part of activity is therefore the residual of volume against
its own same-clock-time norm on previous sessions -- NOT against a rolling
trailing average, which is what essentially every short-horizon volume gate in
the literature (and in our book) uses.

Given that decomposition:
  * a within-bar mid move that happens while volume is ABOVE its calendar
    schedule is information-driven -> its impact persists;
  * the same move on BELOW-schedule volume is inventory / quote displacement by
    a fee-insensitive scheduled trader -> it reverts.

Both legs are captured by one signed statistic: the recency-weighted trailing
covariance between the diurnally standardized log-volume surprise and the
volatility-standardized *intra-bar* return (close - open) / open, i.e. the mid
displacement that was actually paid for by that bar's volume.  The signal is
then mildly scaled by market-cap rank, because scheduled algorithmic flow is a
larger share of volume in big names, which makes the schedule residual a
sharper information proxy there.

Causality
---------
The diurnal baseline is built with ``groupby(clock-time).shift(k)`` for k >= 1,
which can only reference *earlier* rows of the panel (the same clock time on a
previous session).  Everything else is a trailing rolling statistic or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional rank, so the value at bar t uses only
information available at or before t.  If the sample contains too few prior
sessions the baseline falls back to a lagged trailing mean of log-volume.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, delay, rank, stddev, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _seconds_of_day(index) -> np.ndarray:
    """Integer seconds since midnight for each bar timestamp (clock-time key)."""
    idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(index)
    secs = idx.hour.values.astype(np.int64) * 3600
    secs = secs + idx.minute.values.astype(np.int64) * 60
    secs = secs + idx.second.values.astype(np.int64)
    return secs


def _diurnal_mean(df: pd.DataFrame, key: np.ndarray, lags) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mean of the values observed at the SAME clock time on previous sessions.

    ``groupby(key).shift(k)`` with k >= 1 walks back k occurrences of the same
    clock time, i.e. k sessions back -- strictly past information.  NaNs are
    skipped by accumulating a sum and a count.
    """
    grouped = df.groupby(key)
    total = None
    count = None
    for k in lags:
        shifted = grouped.shift(k)
        val = shifted.fillna(0.0)
        cnt = shifted.notna().astype(float)
        total = val if total is None else total + val
        count = cnt if count is None else count + cnt
    if total is None or count is None:
        return df * np.nan
    return total / count.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _safe_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return r.fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class UnscheduledFlowDiurnalSurpriseImpact(BaseFactor):
    """Covariance of calendar-conditional volume surprise with intra-bar impact."""

    factor_id = "unscheduled_flow_diurnal_surprise_impact"
    name = "Unscheduled-flow impact (diurnal volume surprise x intra-bar impact)"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Recency-weighted 6-bar covariance between the diurnally standardized "
        "log-volume surprise (volume versus its same-clock-time norm on previous "
        "sessions) and the volatility-standardized intra-bar mid return "
        "(close-open)/open, mildly scaled by market-cap rank and ranked "
        "cross-sectionally: long moves paid for by unscheduled volume, short "
        "moves that happened on below-schedule volume."
    )
    window_length = 6800          # ~3 sessions of 10s bars: needed for the diurnal baseline
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # ---- few, interpretable constants ----
    _fast = 6                     # covariance window, matched to the 6-bar horizon
    _norm = 240                   # trailing window for per-name standardisation
    _sessions = (1, 2, 3)         # previous sessions used for the clock-time norm

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        op = data["open"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        cl = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # --- intra-bar mid displacement: the impact actually paid in this bar ---
        rb = ((cl - op) / op).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        sig_rb = stddev(rb, self._norm).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rtil = (rb / sig_rb).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # --- volume surprise versus the CALENDAR schedule (not a trailing mean) ---
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        lv = np.log1p(vol)

        key = _seconds_of_day(idx)
        base_diurnal = _diurnal_mean(lv, key, self._sessions)
        base_trail = ts_mean(delay(lv, 1), self._norm)      # fallback, strictly lagged
        base = base_diurnal.where(base_diurnal.notna(), base_trail)

        u = (lv - base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        su = stddev(u, self._norm).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        uz = (u / su).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        # --- recency-weighted trailing covariance of surprise with impact ---
        valid = rtil.notna() & uz.notna()
        prod = (uz * rtil).where(valid, 0.0)
        cov = decay_linear(prod, self._fast)
        enough = valid.astype(float).rolling(self._fast, min_periods=self._fast).sum()
        cov = cov.where(enough >= 3.0)

        # --- size scaling: scheduled flow share rises with market cap ---
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            gate = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mc = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            mc = mc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            mc = mc.where(mc > 0.0)
            gate = 0.6 + 0.8 * _safe_rank(np.log1p(mc))
            gate = gate.fillna(1.0)

        raw = cov * gate
        sig = rank(raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Unscheduled-flow impact (diurnal volume surprise × intra-bar impact)
programs.trading_idea: Intraday volume is largely a deterministic calendar schedule (VWAP/TWAP algos, index and open/close-driven flow follow a U-shape), so the informative part of trading activity is the residual of volume against its own same-clock-time norm on previous sessions, not against a rolling trailing average as almost every short-horizon factor assumes. Price moves produced *during* bars with above-schedule (unscheduled) volume are information-motivated and their impact persists, whereas identical moves occurring on below-schedule volume are pure inventory/quote displacement by a fee-insensitive scheduled trader and mean-revert; the recency-weighted trailing covariance between diurnally-standardized volume surprise and the *within-bar* mid change (close−open, the impact actually paid) therefore predicts the next minute of returns with a single signed statistic. The mechanism is falsifiable in two ways: replacing the diurnal baseline with a plain trailing-ADV baseline should kill the incremental edge, and the effect should be strongest in large caps where scheduled algorithmic flow is the biggest share of volume (hence the mild size scaling). It survives arbitrage because latency-driven liquidity providers condition on rolling recent depth/volume and on spread, not on per-name cross-day calendar-conditional volume profiles, and because harvesting it requires holding ~1 minute — longer than queue-position strategies and shorter than typical stat-arb rebalancing.
programs.description: Recency-weighted 6-bar covariance between (a) each name's log-volume surprise relative to the mean log-volume at the same clock time on the previous three sessions and (b) its volatility-standardized intra-bar mid return (close−open), mildly scaled by market-cap rank and ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Drift-burst t-statistic with a noise-regime flip.

Mechanism: a locally explosive drift (Christensen-Oomen-Reno 'drift burst') is
estimated as an exponential-kernel weighted sum of returns divided by a
Newey-West / Bartlett HAC volatility computed with a longer bandwidth.  The very
autocovariance terms that enter the HAC correction also classify the burst: a
Bartlett-weighted autocovariance that is unusually POSITIVE for the name (versus
its own slow baseline) means the move was assembled by persistent, order-splitting
flow -> continuation; unusually NEGATIVE means the move was assembled out of
bounce / quote-flicker noise against thin depth -> snapback.  The factor is
therefore the interaction (signed burst magnitude) x (noise-regime excess), a
state-conditioned directional signal rather than a plain drift or reversal bet.

All estimators are trailing exponentially-weighted moments and positive lags, so
the value at bar t uses only information available at or before t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _ew(df: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float, min_p: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially-weighted mean (adjust=True ignores leading NaNs)."""
    return df.ewm(halflife=float(halflife), min_periods=int(min_p), adjust=True).mean()


def _hac_moments(r: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float, min_p: int, lags: int):
    """Exponentially-weighted per-bar variance g0 and Bartlett-weighted
    autocovariance sum  c = sum_{l=1..L} (1 - l/(L+1)) * gamma_l.

    Only positive lags (r_t * r_{t-l}) are used -> strictly causal.
    """
    g0 = _ew(r * r, halflife, min_p)
    c = None
    for l in range(1, int(lags) + 1):
        w = 1.0 - l / (float(lags) + 1.0)
        gl = _ew(r * r.shift(l), halflife, min_p) * w
        c = gl if c is None else c + gl
    return g0, c


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank mapped to [-1, +1]; missing -> 0."""
    rk = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return (2.0 * rk - 1.0).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class DriftBurstTstatNoiseRegimeFlip(BaseFactor):
    """Kernel drift-burst t-stat, sign-flipped by the burst's autocovariance regime."""

    factor_id = 'drift_burst_tstat_noise_regime_flip'
    name = 'Drift-burst t-stat flipped by noise-regime excess'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        "Exponential-kernel drift-burst t-statistic (drift halflife 6 bars over a "
        "Newey-West HAC volatility, halflife 30 bars, 3 Bartlett lags) multiplied by "
        "the centred cross-sectional rank of the burst-window Bartlett autocorrelation "
        "in excess of the name's own slow (halflife 150 bars) autocorrelation level."
    )
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ['close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # kernel bandwidths (bars)
    H_MU = 6.0
    H_SIG = 30.0
    H_SLOW = 150.0
    LAGS = 3

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        r = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        r = r.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        # ---- kernel drift (numerator of the drift-burst statistic) ----
        mu_bar = _ew(r, self.H_MU, 5)

        # ---- HAC volatility at the (longer) volatility bandwidth ----
        g0_f, c_f = _hac_moments(r, self.H_SIG, 20, self.LAGS)
        sig2 = g0_f + 2.0 * c_f
        floor = 0.2 * g0_f
        sig2 = sig2.where(sig2 > floor, floor)
        sig2 = sig2.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig2 = sig2.where(sig2 > 0.0, np.nan)

        lam = 0.5 ** (1.0 / self.H_MU)
        c_mu = float(np.sqrt(1.0 - lam ** 2) / (1.0 - lam))
        tstat = c_mu * mu_bar / np.sqrt(sig2)
        tstat = tstat.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        amp = np.tanh(tstat / 2.0)          # saturating, monotone in burst size

        # ---- noise regime: Bartlett autocorrelation, fast minus own slow level ----
        g0_s, c_s = _hac_moments(r, self.H_SLOW, 120, self.LAGS)
        denom_f = g0_f.where(g0_f > 0.0, np.nan)
        denom_s = g0_s.where(g0_s > 0.0, np.nan)
        ns_fast = (c_f / denom_f).clip(-1.5, 1.5)
        ns_slow = (c_s / denom_s).clip(-1.5, 1.5)
        ns_exc = (ns_fast - ns_slow).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        cond = _centred_rank(ns_exc)        # +1 = trending texture, -1 = bounce texture

        raw = (amp * cond).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = rank(raw)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Drift-burst t-stat flipped by noise-regime excess
programs.trading_idea: Christensen-Oomen-Renò show that locally explosive drift ('drift bursts') can be measured as a kernel-weighted drift over a HAC (Newey-West) volatility, and that some bursts are news-driven (they persist) while others are pure liquidity gaps (they snap back). The discriminator I use is the *texture of the path that produced the burst*, taken directly from the HAC correction term: when the Bartlett-weighted return autocovariance of the burst window is unusually positive relative to the name's own recent norm, the move was built by persistent, order-splitting (informed) flow and should continue; when it is unusually negative, the move was built out of bounce/quote-flicker noise against thin depth and should revert. Because the same autocovariance object both corrects the variance estimate and classifies the burst, the signal is an interaction (burst size x noise-regime excess) rather than a directional drift bet, which is why it should act as a state/conditioning variable in a book. It survives arbitrage because market makers condition on inventory, spread and order-flow imbalance, not on a kernel drift t-stat multiplied by its own HAC-correction anomaly; falsification is direct — if drift bursts revert (or persist) irrespective of the sign of the autocovariance excess, the interaction IC collapses to zero.
programs.description: Exponential-kernel drift-burst t-statistic (halflife 6 bars) divided by a Newey-West/Bartlett HAC volatility (halflife 30 bars, 3 lags), multiplied by the cross-sectional rank (mapped to [-1,1]) of the burst-window Bartlett autocorrelation in excess of the name's own slow (halflife 150) autocorrelation level.

programs.code:
"""Opacity-conditioned volume-return permanence wedge.

Mechanism (Llorente / Michaely / Saar / Wang 2002, taken to 10-second bars):
the volume-conditioned autocorrelation of returns flips sign with information
asymmetry.  A price move accompanied by abnormal volume is more likely
information-driven -- and therefore permanent / continuing -- in opaque,
hard-to-value names, whereas the same volume-backed move in a transparent,
cash-generative, tangible-asset name is far more likely to be liquidity
demand and mean-reverts.  Accounting opacity (asset intangibility, goodwill,
R&D intensity, weak cash-backing of earnings, small size) is used as the
point-in-time information-asymmetry prior; the tradable object is the *triple*
interaction (scaled fresh move) x (volume surprise) x (opacity), residualised
cross-sectionally against plain reversal, volume-conditioned reversal and the
static opacity tilt so that only the mechanism's differential loading is left.

All inputs are trailing / contemporaneous: rolling windows only, positive lags
only, and the fundamental fields are already point-in-time step functions.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import log, rank, stddev, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _xs_ols_residual(y: pd.DataFrame, regressors: list[pd.DataFrame], min_obs: int=12, ridge: float=1e-08) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional OLS residual of y on [1, regressors].

    Closed-form batched normal equations solved independently for every bar,
    so only contemporaneous cross-sectional information is used (no temporal
    leakage).  Names with any missing input at bar t are dropped from that
    bar's fit and returned as NaN.
    """
    ya = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n_rows, n_cols = ya.shape
    k = len(regressors) + 1
    xa = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols, k), dtype=float)
    xa[:, :, 0] = 1.0
    for i, xr in enumerate(regressors):
        xa[:, :, i + 1] = xr.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(ya) & np.isfinite(xa).all(axis=2)
    xw = np.where(valid[:, :, None], xa, 0.0)
    yw = np.where(valid, ya, 0.0)
    xtx = np.einsum('tnk,tnl->tkl', xw, xw)
    xty = np.einsum('tnk,tn->tk', xw, yw)
    counts = valid.sum(axis=1)
    eye = np.eye(k)
    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(np.trace(xtx, axis1=1, axis2=2)) / float(k), 1.0)
    xtx = xtx + (ridge * scale)[:, None, None] * eye[None, :, :]
    beta = np.full((n_rows, k), np.nan, dtype=float)
    ok = counts >= max(min_obs, k + 2)
    if ok.any():
        inv = np.linalg.pinv(xtx[ok])
        beta[ok] = np.einsum('tkl,tl->tk', inv, xty[ok])
    fitted = np.einsum('tnk,tk->tn', xa, beta)
    resid = np.where(valid, ya - fitted, np.nan)
    return pd.DataFrame(resid, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)

def _rank_composite(frames: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-aware average of cross-sectional percentile ranks."""
    tot = None
    cnt = None
    for f in frames:
        r = rank(f.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        add = r.fillna(0.0)
        msk = r.notna().astype(float)
        tot = add if tot is None else tot + add
        cnt = msk if cnt is None else cnt + msk
    if tot is None or cnt is None:
        raise ValueError('empty composite')
    return tot / cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)

def _centered_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank mapped to [-1, +1]; missing -> 0 (neutral)."""
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return (2.0 * (r - 0.5)).fillna(0.0)

def _sector_demean(x: pd.DataFrame, sector: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract the per-sector cross-sectional mean (fallback: panel mean).

    Sector labels are static text; the earliest observed label per name is used
    so no future label revision can influence an earlier bar.
    """
    out = x.sub(x.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    if sector is None:
        return out
    labels: dict[object, str] = {}
    for c in x.columns:
        if c not in sector.columns:
            continue
        s = sector[c].dropna()
        if len(s) > 0:
            labels[c] = str(s.iloc[0])
    buckets: dict[str, list] = {}
    for c, lab in labels.items():
        buckets.setdefault(lab, []).append(c)
    for lab, gcols in buckets.items():
        if len(gcols) >= 4:
            sub = x[gcols]
            out[gcols] = sub.sub(sub.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return out

@register_factor
class OpacityConditionedVolumeReturnPermanenceWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Volume-conditioned reversal / continuation split by accounting opacity."""
    factor_id = 'opacity_conditioned_volume_return_permanence_wed'
    name = 'Opacity-conditioned volume-return permanence wedge'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Triple interaction of a vol-scaled sector-neutral 6-bar move, a trailing z-scored 6-bar volume surprise, and a centred accounting-opacity composite, residualised cross-sectionally against plain reversal, volume-conditioned reversal and the opacity tilt, then ranked.'
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector', 'marketCap', 'intangiblesToAssets', 'rdToRevenue', 'incomeQuality', 'goodwill', 'totalAssets']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        logp = log(close.where(close > 0.0))
        r6 = logp.diff(6)
        r1 = logp.diff(1)
        r_idio = _sector_demean(r6, data.get('sector'))
        scale = (stddev(r1, 120) * np.sqrt(6.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rtil = (r_idio / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        turn = ts_sum(vol, 6)
        vsurp = ts_zscore(log(turn + 1.0), 120)
        vsurp = vsurp.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-2.0, 3.0)
        intang = data['intangiblesToAssets'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        assets = data['totalAssets'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        assets_pos = assets.where(assets > 0.0)
        gw = (data['goodwill'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).clip(lower=0.0) / assets_pos).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        rd = data['rdToRevenue'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 2.0)
        iq = data['incomeQuality'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-10.0, 10.0)
        mcap = data['marketCap'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        log_mcap = log(mcap.where(mcap > 0.0))
        opacity_raw = _rank_composite([intang, gw, rd, -iq, -log_mcap])
        opac_c = _centered_rank(opacity_raw)
        y = rtil * vsurp * opac_c
        resid = _xs_ols_residual(y, [rtil, rtil * vsurp, opac_c])
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(resid)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Opacity-conditioned volume-return permanence wedge
programs.trading_idea: Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang show that the sign of the volume-conditioned return autocorrelation is governed by information asymmetry: when a price move is accompanied by abnormal volume it continues in names where trading is likely informed, and reverses in names where volume mostly reflects liquidity/hedging demand. The parent's edge came from a slow balance-sheet-conditioned variance state whose information only accrues over minutes; here the fundamentals instead set the *prior on impact permanence* (accounting opacity: intangibility, goodwill, R&D intensity, weak cash-backing of earnings, small size), while the fast trigger is a fresh 6-bar sector-neutral move scaled by its own volatility and interacted with a 6-bar volume surprise — an object whose predictive content lives exactly on the one-minute clock, matching the fixed horizon. To make the test sharp, the triple interaction return x volume-surprise x opacity is cross-sectionally residualised against plain reversal, volume-conditioned reversal, and the static opacity tilt, so only the differential loading predicted by the mechanism survives. It persists because market makers condition on spread, queue and volume, not on point-in-time accrual quality or asset intangibility, so the cross-name variation in how much of a one-minute impact is permanent is not arbitraged away; it is falsified if the residual interaction carries no IC at 6 bars while the plain reversal leg does.
programs.description: Sector-neutral 6-bar return scaled by trailing volatility, multiplied by a trailing z-scored 6-bar volume surprise and by a centred cross-sectional accounting-opacity composite (intangibles/assets, goodwill/assets, R&D intensity, negative income quality, negative log size), then cross-sectionally residualised against plain reversal, volume-conditioned reversal and the opacity tilt, and ranked.

programs.code:
"""Roll-vs-Corwin-Schultz bounce pervasiveness, flipped by information opacity.

Mechanism: Roll's (1984) effective spread from window-level lag-1 return
autocovariance measures reversal noise that is PERVASIVE over the trailing
window (mid oscillating around a stable anchor: inventory / tick noise).  The
Corwin-Schultz (2012) high-low estimator averages positive-part LOCAL two-bar
estimates and is therefore driven by EPISODIC range expansion.  The normalised
wedge between the two separates 'oscillation about an anchor' (recent
displacement snaps back over the next minute) from 'episodic directional
demand' (displacement continues).  Glosten-Milgrom adverse selection implies
the continuation branch is stronger for information-opaque firms, so ranked
intangible intensity and R&D intensity tilt the same displacement toward
continuation.  All estimators are trailing-window closed forms; no learned
model, no negative lags.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    covariance,
    delay,
    rank,
    returns,
    ts_mean,
    ts_sum,
    ts_zscore,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_K1 = 3.0 - 2.0 * np.sqrt(2.0)


def _corwin_schultz(high: pd.DataFrame, low: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Corwin-Schultz proportional spread, averaged over a trailing n-bar window.

    beta_t  = ln(H_t/L_t)^2 + ln(H_{t-1}/L_{t-1})^2      (pair of consecutive bars)
    gamma_t = ln(max(H_t,H_{t-1}) / min(L_t,L_{t-1}))^2
    alpha_t = (sqrt(2 beta) - sqrt(beta))/k1 - sqrt(gamma/k1)
    S_t     = 2 (e^alpha - 1) / (1 + e^alpha), negative values clipped to zero.

    Positive-part clipping makes this estimator sensitive to *episodic* local
    reversals; only trailing bars are used, so it is causal.
    """
    h = high.where(high > 0.0)
    l = low.where(low > 0.0)
    lr = (np.log(h) - np.log(l)).clip(lower=0.0)
    hl2 = lr ** 2
    beta = (hl2 + hl2.shift(1)).clip(lower=0.0)
    h2 = h.rolling(2, min_periods=2).max()
    l2 = l.rolling(2, min_periods=2).min()
    gamma = ((np.log(h2) - np.log(l2)).clip(lower=0.0)) ** 2
    alpha = (np.sqrt(2.0 * beta) - np.sqrt(beta)) / _K1 - np.sqrt(gamma / _K1)
    alpha = alpha.clip(-20.0, 20.0)
    ea = np.exp(alpha)
    s = 2.0 * (ea - 1.0) / (1.0 + ea)
    s = s.clip(lower=0.0)
    return ts_mean(s, n)


def _roll_spread(ret: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Roll (1984) implied proportional spread: 2*sqrt(max(-cov(r_t, r_{t-1}), 0))
    from a trailing n-bar covariance (window-level, i.e. pervasive bounce)."""
    cov = covariance(ret, delay(ret, 1), n)
    return 2.0 * np.sqrt((-cov).clip(lower=0.0))


def _centered_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank in [-0.5, +0.5]; missing pinned to median."""
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return r.fillna(0.5) - 0.5


@register_factor
class RollCorwinBouncePervasivenessOpacityFlip(BaseFactor):
    """Displacement continuation/reversal gated by the Roll-vs-Corwin bounce wedge."""

    factor_id = "roll_corwin_bounce_pervasiveness_opacity_flip"
    name = "Roll-vs-Corwin bounce pervasiveness with opacity flip"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Vol-normalised 6-bar displacement multiplied by a gate that is negative "
        "when Roll-implied (pervasive) bounce dominates Corwin-Schultz high-low "
        "(episodic) bounce and positive when episodic structure or firm "
        "information opacity dominates; cross-sectionally ranked and demeaned."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "intangiblesToAssets",
        "rdToRevenue",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        nan_frame = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)

        def _get(field: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
            df = data.get(field)
            if df is None:
                return nan_frame.copy()
            return df.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

        high = _get("high")
        low = _get("low")
        ret = (
            returns(data)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        )

        # --- two spread estimators over the same trailing window -------------
        s_cs = _corwin_schultz(high, low, 60)
        s_roll = _roll_spread(ret, 60)
        den = (s_cs.abs() + s_roll.abs()).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        wedge = (s_roll - s_cs) / den            # +1 = pervasive bounce dominates
        wedge = wedge.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # --- information opacity (point-in-time quarterly step functions) ----
        intang = _get("intangiblesToAssets").replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        rdint = _get("rdToRevenue").replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        opacity = 0.5 * (_centered_rank(intang) + _centered_rank(rdint))

        # --- directional carrier: recent displacement, vol-normalised --------
        disp = ts_zscore(ts_sum(ret, 6), 120)
        disp = disp.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # gate: pervasive bounce -> reversal, opacity/episodic -> continuation
        gate = opacity - _centered_rank(wedge)
        gate = gate.where(wedge.notna())

        raw = gate * disp
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = rank(raw)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Roll-vs-Corwin bounce pervasiveness with opacity flip
programs.trading_idea: Two classic spread estimators disagree in an informative way: Roll's signed lag-1 autocovariance measures reversal noise that is *pervasive* across the whole trailing window (a mid oscillating around a stable anchor, i.e. inventory/tick noise), whereas the Corwin-Schultz high-low estimator averages positive-part *local two-bar* estimates and is therefore driven by episodic range expansions. When the pervasive component dominates, a name's last-minute displacement is oscillation about an anchor and snaps back within the next minute; when the episodic component dominates, the displacement is directional demand impounding information and continues. Adverse selection (Glosten-Milgrom) makes the continuation side stronger for information-opaque firms (high intangible intensity, high R&D/revenue), so opacity tilts the same displacement toward continuation, and transparent asset-heavy firms toward reversal. The edge persists because market makers screen on quoted spread and volume level, not on the *ratio* of window-level to pair-level bounce, and they never condition inventory pricing on balance-sheet intangibility.
programs.description: Signal = recent 6-bar displacement (vol-normalised) multiplied by a gate that is negative when Roll-implied bounce dominates Corwin-Schultz high-low-implied bounce (reversal) and positive when the Corwin-Schultz side or firm information opacity (intangiblesToAssets, rdToRevenue ranks) dominates (continuation); the product is cross-sectionally ranked and demeaned.

programs.code:
"""Intrinsic-time overshoot velocity anomaly.

Mechanism: represent each name's price path in intrinsic (event) time via the
directional-change algorithm with a volatility-scaled threshold delta.  Each run
is characterised by (i) its overshoot -- the extension of the extreme beyond the
last directional-change confirmation price, in units of delta -- and (ii) its
duration in bars.  Both are self-normalised by exponentially-weighted averages of
the name's OWN realised overshoots and durations, giving two dimensionless state
variables: price-stretch ps and time-stretch ts.

ps > ts means the price has extended further than its typical overshoot in less
time than its typical run lasts: a fast, mechanically-driven displacement, which
reverts.  ts > ps means a slow grind that has not gone anywhere in price: absorbed,
informed flow, which continues.  The signal is therefore -direction * (ps - ts),
confirmed by how far the price has already retraced from the run's extreme.

All state is updated in a single forward pass over bars, so the value at bar t is
built only from information available at or before t (trailing rolling volatility
and a causal event recursion).  No look-ahead anywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _dc_scan(x: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, hl_events: float, warm: float):
    """Causal directional-change scan, vectorised across names, looped over bars.

    Returns per-bar arrays of (run direction, price-stretch, time-stretch,
    retracement fraction).  Values are NaN until a name has completed ``warm``
    directional-change events, so the arbitrary initial state washes out.
    """
    T, N = x.shape
    alpha = 1.0 - 0.5 ** (1.0 / float(hl_events))

    m = np.ones(N, dtype=float)          # current run direction (+1 up, -1 down)
    ext = np.full(N, np.nan)             # running extreme of the current run
    pdc = np.full(N, np.nan)             # log price at last DC confirmation
    tdc = np.zeros(N, dtype=float)       # bar index of last DC confirmation
    obar = np.full(N, np.nan)            # EWMA of realised overshoot (units of delta)
    dbar = np.full(N, np.nan)            # EWMA of realised run duration (bars)
    nev = np.zeros(N, dtype=float)       # completed events per name

    o_m = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
    o_ps = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
    o_ts = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
    o_r = np.full((T, N), np.nan)

    for t in range(T):
        xt = x[t]
        d = delta[t]
        ok = np.isfinite(xt) & np.isfinite(d) & (d > 0.0)
        if not ok.any():
            continue
        ds = np.where(ok, d, np.nan)

        need = ok & ~np.isfinite(ext)
        if need.any():
            ext[need] = xt[need]
            pdc[need] = xt[need]
            tdc[need] = float(t)

        up = ok & (m > 0.0)
        gt = up & (xt > ext)
        if gt.any():
            ext[gt] = xt[gt]
        dn = ok & (m < 0.0)
        lt = dn & (xt < ext)
        if lt.any():
            ext[lt] = xt[lt]

        ev = (up & (xt <= ext - ds)) | (dn & (xt >= ext + ds))
        if ev.any():
            om = np.abs(ext[ev] - pdc[ev]) / ds[ev]
            dur = float(t) - tdc[ev]
            ob = obar[ev]
            db = dbar[ev]
            obar[ev] = np.where(np.isfinite(ob), ob + alpha * (om - ob), om)
            dbar[ev] = np.where(np.isfinite(db), db + alpha * (dur - db), dur)
            nev[ev] = nev[ev] + 1.0
            m[ev] = -m[ev]
            pdc[ev] = xt[ev]
            ext[ev] = xt[ev]
            tdc[ev] = float(t)

        cur_o = np.abs(ext - pdc) / ds
        age = float(t) - tdc
        ps = cur_o / np.maximum(obar, 0.05)
        ts = (age + 1.0) / np.maximum(dbar + 1.0, 1.0)
        rr = np.abs(ext - xt) / ds
        ready = ok & (nev >= warm) & np.isfinite(obar) & np.isfinite(dbar)

        o_m[t] = np.where(ready, m, np.nan)
        o_ps[t] = np.where(ready, ps, np.nan)
        o_ts[t] = np.where(ready, ts, np.nan)
        o_r[t] = np.where(ready, np.clip(rr, 0.0, 1.0), np.nan)

    return o_m, o_ps, o_ts, o_r


def _group_demean(y: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, min_count: int = 4) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional demeaning inside static text groups (sector).

    Purely contemporaneous.  Groups with too few valid names on a bar fall back
    to that bar's global mean.
    """
    ya = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(ya)
    lab = labels.to_numpy(dtype=object)

    cnt_all = valid.sum(axis=1)
    sum_all = np.where(valid, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    gmean = np.where(cnt_all > 0, sum_all / np.maximum(cnt_all, 1), 0.0)

    out = np.full_like(ya, np.nan)
    uniq = pd.unique(pd.Series(lab.ravel()).dropna())
    for g in uniq:
        mask = valid & (lab == g)
        if not mask.any():
            continue
        c = mask.sum(axis=1)
        s = np.where(mask, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mu = np.where(c >= min_count, s / np.maximum(c, 1), gmean)
        out = np.where(mask, ya - mu[:, None], out)
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)


@register_factor
class IntrinsicTimeOvershootVelocityReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade runs whose price extension outran their event-time duration."""

    factor_id = "intrinsic_time_overshoot_velocity_reversal"
    name = "Intrinsic-time overshoot velocity anomaly"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Directional-change scan with a volatility-scaled threshold; the current "
        "overshoot and its age are normalised by the name's own EWMA realised "
        "overshoot and duration, and the signal is minus the run direction times "
        "the (price-stretch - time-stretch) residual, retracement-weighted and "
        "sector-demeaned."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.where(close > 0.0)
        x = np.log(px)
        x = x.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        ret = x.diff()
        sigma = ret.rolling(120, min_periods=60).std()
        delta = (3.0 * sigma).clip(lower=1e-5)
        delta = delta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        xa = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        da = delta.to_numpy(dtype=float)

        m_a, ps_a, ts_a, r_a = _dc_scan(xa, da, 10.0, 5.0)

        m = pd.DataFrame(m_a, index=idx, columns=cols)
        ps = pd.DataFrame(ps_a, index=idx, columns=cols)
        ts = pd.DataFrame(ts_a, index=idx, columns=cols)
        rr = pd.DataFrame(r_a, index=idx, columns=cols)

        # velocity residual: extension in price vs extension in event time
        d = (ps - ts).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        d_pos = d.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)     # stretched-fast run -> fade
        d_neg = (-d).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)  # slow grind -> follow

        w_rev = 0.5 + rr        # reversal is more imminent once retracement began
        w_con = 1.5 - rr        # a grind still pinned at its extreme is cleanest
        core = d_pos * w_rev - d_neg * w_con
        raw = (-m) * core
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sec = data["sector"]
        if isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame):
            sec = sec.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:  # defensive: a Series of static labels
            sec = pd.DataFrame(
                np.repeat(np.asarray(sec.reindex(cols), dtype=object)[None, :], len(idx), axis=0),
                index=idx,
                columns=cols,
            )
        sec = sec.astype(object).where(sec.notna(), "__NA__")

        z = _group_demean(raw, sec, 4)

        scale_row = z.abs().mean(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sig = z.div(scale_row, axis=0).clip(lower=-4.0, upper=4.0)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Intrinsic-time overshoot velocity anomaly
programs.trading_idea: In the directional-change (intrinsic-time) representation of a price path, each run is described by two quantities that obey their own scaling laws: the overshoot beyond the confirmation threshold and the duration of that overshoot. Self-calibrating both to the name's own realised event-time distributions gives a dimensionless velocity residual: a run whose normalised price extension has outrun its normalised duration is a fast, mechanically-driven displacement (inventory unloading into thin depth) and snaps back, whereas a run whose duration exceeds its extension is a slow grind — informed accumulation being absorbed — and continues. The edge persists because the state variable lives in event time and is path-dependent: it requires maintaining per-name overshoot and duration distributions across directional-change events, whereas HFT liquidity provision and standard alpha libraries gate on calendar-time volatility, spread and depth, so nobody is bidding away the specific fast-vs-slow asymmetry. It is falsifiable: if extension speed carries no information, the signed residual (ps − ts) should be uncorrelated with 6-bar forward returns, and the reversal branch should not separate from the grind branch.
programs.description: Runs a causal directional-change scan (threshold = 3x trailing 120-bar return volatility) per name, self-normalises the current unrealised overshoot and its age by EWMAs of the name's own realised overshoots and run durations, and trades minus the run direction times the clipped (price-stretch − time-stretch) residual, weighted by the retracement already achieved and demeaned within sector.

programs.code:
"""BVC toxicity / float-turnover permanence switch.

Mechanism: volume on this feed is unsigned, so we recover a probabilistic
buy/sell split with bulk-volume classification (Easley, Lopez de Prado &
O'Hara 2012): the buy share of a bar's volume is the Student-t CDF of the
bar's return standardized by trailing volatility.  Summing the signed volume
over a 12-bar window and dividing by gross volume gives a VPIN-style
toxicity ratio -- how concentrated (one-sided) the flow that produced the
last displacement was.  Combined with how much of the *float* traded in that
window (gross volume / point-in-time shares outstanding), this discriminates
permanent, information-driven displacement from transitory market-maker
inventory pressure.  The factor is therefore a permanence switch: fade the
displacement when flow was diffuse and small relative to float, extrapolate
it when flow was concentrated and large relative to float.  All statistics
are trailing rolling windows or positive lags, so the value at bar t uses
only information available at or before t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, rank, returns, stddev
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _bvc_signed_volume(ret: pd.DataFrame, vol: pd.DataFrame, n_sig: int, nu: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bulk-volume-classified signed volume.

    buy_share_t = T_nu(ret_t / sigma_t), signed volume = vol_t * (2*buy_share - 1).
    sigma_t is a trailing rolling standard deviation -> causal.
    """
    sig = ret.rolling(n_sig, min_periods=max(10, n_sig // 3)).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-20.0, 20.0)
    arr = np.asarray(z, dtype=float)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan, dtype=float)
    mask = np.isfinite(arr)
    if mask.any():
        out[mask] = stats.t.cdf(arr[mask], nu)
    buy_share = pd.DataFrame(out, index=ret.index, columns=ret.columns)
    return vol * (2.0 * buy_share - 1.0)


def _safe_rank_mid(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank with missing values pinned to the median."""
    return rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class BvcToxicityFloatTurnoverPermanenceSwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Forecast the permanence of recent displacement, not its direction."""

    factor_id = "bvc_toxicity_float_turnover_permanence_switch"
    name = "BVC toxicity / float-turnover permanence switch"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Standardized 12-bar displacement times a permanence weight built from "
        "cross-sectional ranks of BVC order-flow toxicity (|net signed volume| / "
        "gross volume) and the share of float traded in the same window: fade "
        "diffuse/small-flow moves, extrapolate concentrated/large-flow moves."
    )
    window_length = 260
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sharesOutstanding", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- (1) BVC toxicity of the flow behind the last 12 bars -------------
        sv = _bvc_signed_volume(ret, vol, 60, 2.0)
        net = sv.rolling(12, min_periods=8).sum()
        gross = vol.rolling(12, min_periods=8).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        tox = (net.abs() / gross).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # ---- (2) share of float traded in the same window --------------------
        shares = data["sharesOutstanding"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        shares = shares.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        shares_alt = mcap / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        shares = shares.where(shares > 0.0, shares_alt)
        shares = shares.where(shares > 0.0, np.nan)
        float_turn = (gross / shares).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        float_turn = np.log1p(float_turn.clip(lower=0.0))

        # ---- (3) standardized recent displacement ----------------------------
        r12 = (close / delay(close, 12).replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
        bar_sig = stddev(ret, 120).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        disp = (r12 / (bar_sig * np.sqrt(12.0))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        disp = disp.clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        # ---- (4) permanence weight in [-1, +1] -------------------------------
        # +1 = concentrated, float-heavy flow -> permanent -> extrapolate
        # -1 = diffuse, float-light flow      -> transitory -> fade
        w = _safe_rank_mid(tox) + _safe_rank_mid(float_turn) - 1.0

        raw = (disp * w).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        # only express a view where the flow window is actually populated
        raw = raw.where(gross.notna() & disp.notna())

        sig = rank(raw)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: BVC toxicity / float-turnover permanence switch
programs.trading_idea: With unsigned trade volume, Easley-Lopez de Prado-O'Hara's bulk-volume classification (BVC) recovers a probabilistic buy/sell split from standardized bar returns, and the resulting imbalance concentration (a VPIN-style toxicity ratio) tells us whether a recent price displacement was paid for by one-sided informed flow or by transient two-sided inventory pressure. Whether the impact is permanent also depends on how much of the *float* changed hands: consuming a large share of outstanding equity in a minute is repositioning, consuming a trivial slice is market-maker inventory that gets recycled. The child therefore does not forecast reversal or continuation, it forecasts the *permanence* of the last 12 bars of displacement: displacement is faded when BVC imbalance is diffuse and float turnover low, and extrapolated when imbalance is concentrated and float turnover high. It survives arbitrage because the switch is a sign-flipping interaction that a linear reversal book cannot represent (the conditioning weight is cross-sectionally centred, so the factor has almost no unconditional loading on plain reversal), and because float-normalised turnover requires point-in-time share counts rather than the raw volume market makers already condition on.
programs.description: Standardized 12-bar price displacement multiplied by a permanence weight in [-1,+1] built from the cross-sectional ranks of (a) BVC-implied order-flow toxicity |net signed volume| / gross volume over 12 bars and (b) the fraction of shares outstanding traded in those 12 bars; ranked cross-sectionally and demeaned.

programs.code:
"""De-levered implied asset shock, split into reversal vs continuation by participation.

Mechanism:
  1. Equity is a levered claim on assets (Merton), so the elasticity of an equity
     return to the underlying asset-value shock is approximately assets/equity.
     A given 6-bar (~60 s) idiosyncratic equity impulse therefore implies a much
     LARGER asset shock in a low-leverage firm than in a highly levered one.
  2. Over a minute, asset values cannot plausibly move by tens of basis points,
     so a large *implied asset shock* needs an information story to be credible.
  3. Volume supplies (or denies) that story.  Below-normal participation means no
     trade-borne information arrived: the implied asset shock is a liquidity
     vacuum (quote withdrawal, one-sided pressure) and reverts.  Above-normal
     participation means the low-leverage asset repricing was actually executed
     and keeps diffusing, so the same signal should be traded with, not against.
     The gate therefore FLIPS the sign of the de-levered impulse instead of only
     scaling its magnitude.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows or contemporaneous cross-sectional
operations, so the value at bar t uses only information available at or before t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    adv,
    rank,
    returns,
    signed_power,
    ts_mean,
    ts_sum,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rank_centered(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank shifted to [-0.5, +0.5]; missing -> 0."""
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return (r - 0.5).fillna(0.0)


def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)


@register_factor
class DeleveredAssetShockParticipationSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Reversal or continuation of de-levered asset shocks, decided by participation."""

    factor_id = "delevered_asset_shock_participation_split"
    name = "De-levered asset-shock reversal/continuation split by participation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Six-bar signed realised-semivariance imbalance of idiosyncratic returns, "
        "standardised by trailing 120-bar quadratic variation and divided by "
        "capital-structure elasticity (financial leverage), multiplied by a signed "
        "participation gate: reversal when 6-bar volume is below its 120-bar norm, "
        "continuation when above."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "financialLeverage", "debtToAssets"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        k = 6      # impulse window == forecast horizon (~60 s on 10 s bars)
        L = 120    # trailing normalisation window

        # ---- idiosyncratic bar returns (strip the equal-weight market move) ----
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        r_id = ret.sub(ret.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        # ---- signed realised-semivariance imbalance (RS+ - RS-) over k bars ----
        imbalance = ts_sum(signed_power(r_id, 2.0), k)
        qv_k = (ts_mean(r_id * r_id, L) * float(k)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        equity_shock = (imbalance / qv_k).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # ---- Merton equity-to-asset elasticity from the balance sheet ----
        flev = data.get("financialLeverage")
        if flev is None:
            flev = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        flev = flev.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        d2a = data.get("debtToAssets")
        if d2a is None:
            d2a = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        d2a = d2a.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        alt_lev = 1.0 / (1.0 - d2a.clip(0.0, 0.9))

        lev = flev.where(flev >= 1.0, alt_lev)
        lev = lev.where(lev >= 1.0).clip(1.0, 12.0)

        med_lev = lev.median(axis=1)
        med_lev = med_lev.where(med_lev > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        lev = lev.where(lev.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_lev, idx, cols))
        elasticity = lev.div(med_lev, axis=0).clip(0.3, 3.0).fillna(1.0)

        # implied asset shock: same equity move => bigger asset shock if unlevered
        asset_shock = (equity_shock / elasticity).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- signed participation gate: +1 vacuum (revert), -1 confirmed (follow) ----
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(vol >= 0.0)
        base_vol = (adv(vol, L) * float(k)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        participation = (ts_sum(vol, k) / base_vol).clip(0.05, 20.0)
        gate = -2.0 * _rank_centered(participation)

        raw = (-asset_shock) * gate
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = rank(raw)
        sig = sig.where(raw.notna())
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: De-levered asset-shock reversal/continuation split by participation
programs.trading_idea: Parent A showed that a short-run equity impulse which de-levers (via Merton elasticity ≈ assets/equity) into an implausibly large *implied asset shock* is prima facie non-fundamental and reverts; parent B showed that whether one-sided pressure reverts or continues depends on volume confirmation, but applied that gate to a slow variance-asymmetry level with no 6-bar edge. The child conditions A's proven de-levered impulse on B's signed participation gate: the leverage de-levering measures *how much fundamental news the move would require*, while participation measures *whether any news actually arrived*. A large implied asset shock on below-normal volume is arithmetically impossible as information — pure quote withdrawal / one-sided liquidity demand — and snaps back within a minute, whereas the same large implied asset shock on above-normal volume is a genuine, low-leverage asset repricing that keeps diffusing, so the gate flips sign rather than merely amplifying magnitude (A's gate could only scale, never flip). The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A pays the same reversal to informed low-leverage repricings it should be trading with, and B's gate had no impulse worth splitting.
programs.description: Six-bar signed realised-semivariance imbalance of idiosyncratic (market-demeaned) returns, standardised by the name's own 120-bar quadratic variation and divided by its capital-structure elasticity (financial leverage, 1/(1−debtToAssets) fallback, row-normalised), then multiplied by a signed participation gate (+1 when 6-bar volume is below its 120-bar norm → reversal, −1 when above → continuation), cross-sectionally ranked and demeaned.

programs.code:
"""Multiple-space band-pass dislocation scaled by measured reversion elasticity.

Mechanism
---------
A peer spread in multiple space is a superposition of frequency bands, each
with its own relaxation time.  A 'deviation from a 5-minute EWMA' statistic is
dominated by low-frequency content that unwinds over many minutes, so its
predictive power peaks far beyond a 60-second forecast offset.  To forecast a
fixed 6-bar horizon we therefore:

  1. build live log multiples m = log(close / X_per_share) for X in
     {bookValuePerShare, revenuePerShare, operatingCashFlowPerShare} (the
     denominators are point-in-time quarterly step functions);
  2. subtract the within-industry (sector fallback) cross-sectional median and
     combine channels with GLS-style precision weights 1 / dispersion, so tight
     comparables dominate the spread and business-mix-heavy groups are damped;
  3. extract the band matched to the forecast horizon with a difference of
     EWMAs (half-lives 1.5 and 6 bars) -- a causal high-pass whose
     autocorrelation decays on ~6 bars -- and standardise it by its own
     trailing volatility;
  4. estimate, causally, each name's band-level reversion elasticity: the
     trailing OLS slope of the realised 6-bar spread change s_t - s_{t-6} on
     the band value B_{t-6}.  A negative slope means displacement in that band
     historically unwound over exactly the forecast offset;
  5. signal = -(band z-score) * clipped magnitude of the negative elasticity,
     ranked cross-sectionally.

All windows are trailing and all lags positive, so the value at t uses only
information available at t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import covariance, rank, stddev
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None, industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker peer-group key: industry when present, else sector."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _group_stats(x: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-row within-group median, MAD and live count, broadcast to members.

    Purely cross-sectional at each timestamp: no time-series leakage.
    """
    med_parts: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    mad_parts: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    cnt_parts: dict[str, pd.Series] = {}
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in x.columns]
        if not cols:
            continue
        sub = x[cols]
        med = sub.median(axis=1)
        mad = sub.sub(med, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1)
        cnt = sub.notna().sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        for c in cols:
            med_parts[c] = med
            mad_parts[c] = mad
            cnt_parts[c] = cnt
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med_parts, index=x.index).reindex(columns=x.columns)
    mad_df = pd.DataFrame(mad_parts, index=x.index).reindex(columns=x.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt_parts, index=x.index).reindex(columns=x.columns)
    return (med_df, mad_df, cnt_df)

def _log_multiple(close: pd.DataFrame, per_share: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """log(price / per-share fundamental), masked to strictly positive inputs."""
    denom = per_share.reindex_like(close)
    denom = denom.where(np.isfinite(denom) & (denom > 0.0))
    px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
    ratio = px / denom
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)

def _bandpass(spread: pd.DataFrame, hl_fast: float, hl_slow: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Difference-of-EWMAs high-pass: keeps fluctuations near the fast scale."""
    fast = spread.ewm(halflife=hl_fast, min_periods=4, adjust=False).mean()
    slow = spread.ewm(halflife=hl_slow, min_periods=10, adjust=False).mean()
    return fast - slow

def _reversion_elasticity(spread: pd.DataFrame, band: pd.DataFrame, lag: int, win: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS slope of the realised lag-bar spread change on the band
    value observed `lag` bars ago.  Both regressand and regressor are known at
    t (positive lags only), so the estimate is causal.  Negative slope => the
    band historically decayed over exactly `lag` bars.
    """
    y = spread - spread.shift(lag)
    x = band.shift(lag)
    cov = covariance(y, x, win)
    sd = stddev(x, win)
    var = (sd * sd).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = cov / var
    return beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

@register_factor
class MultipleSpaceBandpassDislocationReversionElasticity(BaseFactor):
    """Horizon-matched band-pass of comparability-weighted multiple spreads."""
    factor_id = 'multiple_space_bandpass_dislocation_reversion_el'
    name = 'Multiple-Space Band-Pass Dislocation x Measured Reversion Elasticity'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Precision-weighted industry-median-demeaned log multiples (close over point-in-time per-share book / revenue / operating cash flow), high-pass filtered with a 1.5-vs-6-bar EWMA difference so the retained band relaxes on the 6-bar forecast offset, standardised and multiplied by the negated trailing-estimated reversion elasticity of that band at lag 6.'
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ['close', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'operatingCashFlowPerShare', 'industry', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _HL_FAST = 1.5
    _HL_SLOW = 6.0
    _VOL_WINDOW = 120
    _VOL_MIN = 40
    _LAG = 6
    _BETA_WINDOW = 300
    _DISP_HALFLIFE = 60.0
    _MIN_PEERS = 4

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        channels = ['bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'operatingCashFlowPerShare']
        num = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        den = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        cnt_max = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for field in channels:
            raw = data.get(field)
            if raw is None:
                continue
            per_share = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            if per_share.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            lm = _log_multiple(close, per_share)
            if lm.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            med, mad, cnt = _group_stats(lm, labels)
            spread_k = lm - med
            disp = mad.where(np.isfinite(mad) & (mad >= 0.0))
            disp = disp.ewm(halflife=self._DISP_HALFLIFE, min_periods=1, adjust=False).mean()
            scale = disp.median(axis=1)
            scale = scale.where(np.isfinite(scale) & (scale > 0.0)).ffill()
            rel = disp.div(scale, axis=0).clip(0.0, 10.0)
            prec = 1.0 / (0.25 + rel)
            prec = prec.where(np.isfinite(prec) & spread_k.notna())
            prec = prec.where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
            num = num.add((spread_k * prec).fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
            den = den.add(prec.fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
            cnt_max = np.maximum(cnt_max, cnt.fillna(0.0))
        den_pos = den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        spread = num / den_pos
        if spread.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
            lm = np.log(px)
            med, _mad, cnt = _group_stats(lm, labels)
            spread = (lm - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
            cnt_max = cnt.fillna(0.0)
        band = _bandpass(spread, self._HL_FAST, self._HL_SLOW)
        sd = band.rolling(self._VOL_WINDOW, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).std()
        sd = sd.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (band / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        beta = _reversion_elasticity(spread, band, self._LAG, self._BETA_WINDOW)
        rev = (-beta).clip(0.0, 1.5) / 1.5
        rev = rev.where(np.isfinite(rev), 0.0)
        signal = -(z * rev)
        signal = signal.where(cnt_max >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))
        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Multiple-Space Band-Pass Dislocation × Measured Reversion Elasticity
