    (thin downside book), -1 the opposite.
    """
    m_dn = _cond_ew_mean(cost, dn, hl, min_p)
    m_up = _cond_ew_mean(cost, up, hl, min_p)
    tot = (m_dn + m_up).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (m_dn - m_up) / tot

def _group_demean(x: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame, min_members: int=4) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar demeaning of ``x`` inside the groups given by ``labels``.

    Nonparametric conditioning: instead of a linear projection on leverage we
    subtract the contemporaneous mean of the name's own sector x leverage bucket.
    Buckets with fewer than ``min_members`` valid names fall back to the whole
    cross-section mean of that bar.  Only same-bar information is used.
    """
    xv = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t_n, n_n = xv.shape
    lab = labels.to_numpy(dtype=object).ravel()
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(lab)
    k = int(len(uniq))
    if k == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame(np.full_like(xv, np.nan), index=x.index, columns=x.columns)
    codes = codes.reshape(t_n, n_n)
    valid = np.isfinite(xv) & (codes >= 0)
    flat = np.arange(t_n)[:, None] * k + np.clip(codes, 0, k - 1)
    sums = np.zeros(t_n * k, dtype=float)
    cnts = np.zeros(t_n * k, dtype=float)
    np.add.at(sums, flat[valid], xv[valid])
    np.add.at(cnts, flat[valid], 1.0)
    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
        gmean = np.where(cnts >= float(min_members), sums / np.maximum(cnts, 1.0), np.nan).reshape(t_n, k)
    cell = np.take_along_axis(gmean, np.clip(codes, 0, k - 1), axis=1)
    row_sum = np.where(valid, xv, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    row_cnt = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
        row_mean = np.where(row_cnt > 0.0, row_sum / np.maximum(row_cnt, 1.0), 0.0)
    ref = np.where(np.isfinite(cell), cell, row_mean[:, None])
    out = np.where(valid, xv - ref, np.nan)
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)

@register_factor
class AsymImpactCostVacuumLeverageBucketSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh, leverage-unjustified downside impact-cost vacuum -> snapback."""
    factor_id = 'asym_impact_cost_vacuum_leverage_bucket_snapback_1'
    name = 'Leverage-bucketed asymmetric impact-cost vacuum snapback'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Exponentially weighted asymmetry between downside and upside price-move cost per unit sqrt(normalised volume), taken as fast-minus-slow innovation, z-scored, demeaned inside sector x leverage-tercile buckets, and scaled by alignment with the latest 3-bar move.'
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector', 'debtToAssets', 'netDebtToEbitda']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        advv = adv(vol, 121).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vnorm = (vol / advv).clip(0.0, 50.0).fillna(0.0)
        cost = ret.abs() / np.sqrt(1.0 + vnorm)
        valid = ret.notna()
        rv = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        dn = pd.DataFrame(np.where(rv < 0.0, 1.0, 0.0), index=idx, columns=cols).where(valid)
        up = pd.DataFrame(np.where(rv > 0.0, 1.0, 0.0), index=idx, columns=cols).where(valid)
        a_fast = _cost_asymmetry(cost, dn, up, 6.0, 24)
        a_slow = _cost_asymmetry(cost, dn, up, 48.0, 96)
        innov = (a_fast - a_slow).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sd = stddev(innov, 126).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (innov / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        d2a = data['debtToAssets'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 3.0)
        nde = data['netDebtToEbitda'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-30.0, 30.0)
        r1 = rank(d2a)
        r2 = rank(nde)
        cnt = r1.notna().astype(float) + r2.notna().astype(float)
        lev = (r1.fillna(0.0) + r2.fillna(0.0)) / cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lv = lev.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        lev_lab = np.where(np.isfinite(lv), np.where(lv < 1.0 / 3.0, 'L', np.where(lv < 2.0 / 3.0, 'M', 'H')), 'U')
        sec_raw = data['sector'].reindex(columns=cols).reindex(index=idx)
        sec_raw = sec_raw.ffill()
        sec_lab = sec_raw.where(sec_raw.notna(), 'UNK').astype(str).to_numpy()
        gstr = np.char.add(np.char.add(sec_lab.astype(str), '|'), lev_lab.astype(str))
        groups = pd.DataFrame(gstr, index=idx, columns=cols)
        z_resid = _group_demean(z, groups)
        ret3 = close.pct_change(3).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig_r = stddev(ret, 65).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        align = -np.tanh(ret3 / (sig_r * np.sqrt(3.0)))
        align = align.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        raw = z_resid + 0.5 * z_resid.abs() * align
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Leverage-bucketed asymmetric impact-cost vacuum snapback (jitter)
programs.trading_idea: Split the sqrt-impact law by trade direction: for each bar measure the price move achieved per unit of sqrt(normalised traded volume), then take its exponentially-weighted conditional mean separately on down bars and up bars. When down-moves suddenly become much *cheaper* in volume terms than up-moves (a fresh one-sided liquidity vacuum), the fall was produced by depth withdrawal rather than by information, so it is mechanically reversed as depth refills; volume-backed one-sided moves are informative and are not. Because genuinely distressed capital structures (high debtToAssets / netDebtToEbitda) have structurally cheaper downside liquidity — equity is a call on assets, so credit-sensitive names legitimately gap on thin books — the innovation is demeaned nonparametrically inside sector x leverage-tercile buckets, leaving only the transient, unjustified component. Freshness matters at a 60-second horizon, so the residual is amplified when the last three bars actually moved in the vacuum's direction and damped when the move has already been absorbed. The edge persists because direction-split impact cost conditioned on balance-sheet distress buckets is not a screen short-horizon liquidity providers run; their reversion coefficients are direction-symmetric and leverage-blind.
programs.description: Exponentially-weighted asymmetry between downside and upside price-move cost per unit sqrt(normalised volume), taken as a fast-minus-slow innovation, z-scored, demeaned within sector x leverage-tercile buckets, and scaled by alignment with the most recent 3-bar move.

programs.code:
"""Precision-whitened low-variance dislocation snapback.

Mechanism:
Let x_t be the vector of vol-standardized 10-second returns and Sigma the
trailing covariance of x estimated on a strictly past window.  The whitened
(Mahalanobis / Kritzman-Li turbulence) coordinate y_t = Sigma^{-1} x_t weights a
move by the INVERSE variance of the eigen-direction it lives in, so it is
dominated by the historically tightest (lowest-variance) linear combinations -
precisely the relative-value spreads that market makers and stat-arb desks
normally keep pinned.  A large positive y_i therefore means "this name has moved
in a way the recent correlation structure says should not happen", which at a
10-second granularity is the fingerprint of basket-inconsistent, size-driven
liquidity demand rather than news.  Inventory-constrained liquidity providers and
spread arbitrageurs push such dislocations back over the next ~minute, so -y
should forecast the 6-bar forward return.

To make sure this is NOT a relabelled univariate reversal factor, the whitened
deviation is orthogonalized, row by row (cross-sectionally), against the raw
6-bar standardized move itself.  What remains is the component of the dislocation
that exists only in the precision metric.

Regularization (deterministic, self-implemented): the window covariance of
standardized returns is diagonally shrunk and its eigenvalues are floored at a
fraction of the mean eigenvalue (an RMT-style clip), so the inverse is stable
even when the number of names is comparable to the window length.

Causality: the precision matrix used for bars [a, a+S) is estimated only from
rows [a-W, a); every rolling statistic is trailing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _shrunk_precision(x_win: np.ndarray, eig_floor: float, shrink: float):
    """Eigenvalue-floored, diagonally shrunk inverse covariance of a window.

    x_win : (m, n) array of standardized returns, rows strictly in the past.
    Returns an (n, n) symmetric positive-definite precision matrix, or None if
    the window is degenerate.
    """
    if x_win.ndim != 2:
        return None
    m, n = x_win.shape
    if m < 20 or n < 3:
        return None
    xw = np.nan_to_num(x_win, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    xc = xw - xw.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    cov = (xc.T @ xc) / float(max(m - 1, 1))
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(cov)):
        return None
    d = np.diag(cov)
    avg = float(np.mean(d))
    if not np.isfinite(avg) or avg <= 1e-12:
        return None
    cov = (1.0 - shrink) * cov + shrink * avg * np.eye(n)
    cov = 0.5 * (cov + cov.T)
    try:
        w, v = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return None
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(w)) and np.all(np.isfinite(v))):
        return None
    mean_w = float(np.mean(w))
    if not np.isfinite(mean_w) or mean_w <= 1e-14:
        return None
    w = np.maximum(w, eig_floor * mean_w)
    prec = (v / w) @ v.T          # V diag(1/w) V^T
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(prec)):
        return None
    return prec


@register_factor
class PrecisionWhitenedLowVarianceDislocationSnap(BaseFactor):
    """Reversal of the correlation-structure-inconsistent part of a short move."""

    factor_id = "precision_whitened_lowvariance_dislocation_snap"
    name = "Precision-whitened low-variance dislocation snapback"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Minus the cross-sectional rank of the eigenvalue-floored precision-weighted "
        "(Sigma^{-1}) trailing 6-bar standardized return, after removing its "
        "cross-sectional projection on the raw 6-bar standardized return."
    )
    window_length = 520
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 6            # horizon-matched trailing aggregation (= prediction_horizon)
    _VOL_WIN = 120    # trailing window for per-name return standardization
    _COV_WIN = 360    # trailing window for the covariance / precision estimate
    _REFIT = 60       # refit cadence of the precision matrix (bars)
    _SHRINK = 0.30    # diagonal shrinkage intensity
    _EIG_FLOOR = 0.20 # eigenvalues floored at 20% of the mean eigenvalue

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff()

        vol = ret.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=int(self._VOL_WIN // 2)).std()
        vol = vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (ret / vol).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        agg = x.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum()
        valid = agg.notna() & vol.notna()

        xf = x.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        aggf = agg.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        n_rows, n_cols = xf.shape

        y = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        w_cov = int(self._COV_WIN)
        step = int(self._REFIT)
        start = max(w_cov, self._VOL_WIN + self._K)

        a = start
        while a < n_rows:
            prec = _shrunk_precision(
                xf[a - w_cov:a, :], self._EIG_FLOOR, self._SHRINK
            )
            if prec is not None:
                end = min(a + step, n_rows)
                y[a:end, :] = aggf[a:end, :] @ prec
            a += step

        ydf = pd.DataFrame(y, index=idx, columns=cols)
        ydf = ydf.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
        xdf = agg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)

        # cross-sectional orthogonalization of the whitened deviation against the
        # plain standardized move (row-wise OLS through the cross-section)
        ym = ydf.sub(ydf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        xm = xdf.sub(xdf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        denom = (xm * xm).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = (xm * ym).sum(axis=1) / denom
        res = ym.sub(xm.mul(beta.fillna(0.0), axis=0))
        res = res.where(ydf.notna() & xdf.notna())

        sig = 0.5 - rank(res)          # fade the precision-metric dislocation
        sig = sig.where(res.notna())
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Precision-whitened low-variance dislocation snapback
programs.trading_idea: Instead of the parent's occupancy geometry (67% correlated with the book, and with the wrong declared sign), the child measures dislocation in the *precision metric* of the trailing return covariance: y = Sigma^{-1} x, the Mahalanobis / Kritzman-Li whitening of the last 6 bars of vol-standardized returns. Inverting Sigma up-weights moves along historically low-variance eigen-directions - i.e. tight relative-value spreads inside industries/baskets - so a large |y| flags a move that is inconsistent with the recent correlation structure, the signature of size-driven, basket-inconsistent liquidity demand rather than information; market-maker inventory limits and stat-arb capital close such spreads on a ~1-minute clock, so the whitened deviation should predict its own reversal. Crucially, the whitened deviation is orthogonalized cross-sectionally against the plain 6-bar standardized move, so what survives is only the correlation-structure-inconsistent piece: if the information were carried by the univariate move alone, the residual would have zero IC (that is the falsification test). The edge persists because each episode is worth a few ticks along a low-variance direction, requires simultaneous multi-name execution and a stable, regularized rolling precision matrix (eigenvalue-floored, diagonally shrunk), and is invisible to univariate reversal / momentum screens which we explicitly project out.
programs.description: Cross-sectional signal equal to minus the rank of the eigenvalue-floored precision-weighted (Sigma^{-1}) 6-bar standardized return vector, after removing its cross-sectional projection on the raw 6-bar standardized return, using a strictly trailing 360-bar covariance refit every 60 bars.

programs.code:
"""Absorption-side-conditioned sign kernel, iterated to the fixed 6-bar horizon.

Mechanism
---------
At 10-second resolution an idiosyncratic price change mixes transient
liquidity-provision noise (quote flicker / inventory bounce) that recoils within
seconds with informed order-splitting that persists.  Parent B estimated the
mixture weight per name with a *sign-symmetric* volume regime; Parent A showed
that the informative state is *directional*: a sign-split square-root impact
coefficient

    lam_side = mean |idio return| / sqrt(dollar volume / trailing dollar volume)

estimated separately over up bars and down bars reveals which side of the book
is being persistently absorbed (cheap impact) and which pays full impact.

This child fuses the two: the lag-1 sign-persistence kernel is estimated
separately on conditioning bars whose move pointed into the *cheaply absorbed*
side and on bars that pushed into the *expensive* side, each empirical-Bayes
shrunk toward the name's pooled kernel, arcsine-inverted to a return AR(1)
coefficient (rho = sin(pi/2 rho_sign)) and iterated exactly six steps
(S = sum_{k=1..6} lam^k), then applied to the current winsorised idiosyncratic
innovation.  Moves into an absorbing side should recoil (negative kernel);
moves into an expensive side are information and travel (positive kernel).
A small bounded buyback-yield tilt preserves Parent A's economics -- persistent
one-sided absorption is often a Rule 10b-18 repurchase -- without letting a
stale quarterly field drive the sign.

Every statistic is a trailing rolling window, a positive lag or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional operation -> causal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, rolling_residual
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _sign_df(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Elementwise sign preserving index/columns (NaN -> NaN)."""
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.sign(df.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=df.index, columns=df.columns
    )


def _arcsine_invert(rho_sign: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Gaussian arcsine law inversion: rho = sin(pi/2 * rho_sign)."""
    s = rho_sign.clip(-0.95, 0.95)
    vals = np.sin(0.5 * np.pi * s.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(vals, index=rho_sign.index, columns=rho_sign.columns)


def _geometric_horizon_sum(lam: pd.DataFrame, h: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """sum_{k=1..h} lam^k -- AR(1) impulse response truncated at h bars."""
    l = lam.clip(-0.85, 0.85)
    return (l * (1.0 - l ** h)) / (1.0 - l)


def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame, clip: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional median/MAD standardisation."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = dev.div(1.4826 * mad, axis=0)
    return z.clip(-clip, clip)


@register_factor
class AbsorptionSideConditionedSignKernelRecoil(BaseFactor):
    """Sign kernel split by which side of the book is cheaply absorbed."""

    factor_id = "absorption_side_conditioned_sign_kernel_recoil"
    name = "Absorption-side-conditioned sign-kernel recoil"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Lag-1 sign-persistence kernel of market-residualised returns estimated "
        "separately on conditioning bars pushing into the cheaply-absorbed side "
        "versus the expensive side of a trailing sign-split square-root impact "
        "coefficient, EB-shrunk, arcsine-inverted and iterated six steps against "
        "the current winsorised innovation, with a bounded buyback-yield tilt."
    )
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "shareRepurchase"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    W_BETA = 90
    W_DV = 390
    W_IMP = 180
    W_KER = 300
    MIN_KER = 120
    K_SHRINK = 60.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        n_cols = len(cols)

        ret = (
            returns(data)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        )
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).abs().fillna(0.0)

        # ---- strip the systematic component (Parent B) ----------------------
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1)
        mkt_df = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(mkt.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], n_cols, axis=1),
            index=idx,
            columns=cols,
        )
        idio = rolling_residual(ret, mkt_df, self.W_BETA).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        # ---- Parent A: sign-split square-root impact coefficient ------------
        dv = close.abs() * vol
        dvbar = (
            dv.rolling(self.W_DV, min_periods=self.W_DV // 3)
            .mean()
            .replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        vn = (dv / dvbar).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        vn = vn.where(dv > 0.0)
        lam = idio.abs() / np.sqrt(vn.clip(lower=0.05))
        lam = lam.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        mp_imp = max(self.W_IMP // 6, 20)
        lam_up = (
            lam.where(idio > 0.0)
            .rolling(self.W_IMP, min_periods=mp_imp)
            .mean()
        )
        lam_dn = (
            lam.where(idio < 0.0)
            .rolling(self.W_IMP, min_periods=mp_imp)
            .mean()
        )
        denom = (lam_up + lam_dn).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        asym = ((lam_up - lam_dn) / denom).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # cheap (absorbed) direction: -1 when up bars pay MORE impact than
        # down bars (asym > 0 => the downside is being absorbed cheaply).
        cheap_dir = _sign_df(-asym).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- Parent B: sign kernel, now split by absorption side ------------
        x = _sign_df(idio)
        xl = x.shift(1)
        cheap_lag = cheap_dir.shift(1).fillna(0.0)

        align = (xl * cheap_lag).fillna(0.0)
        m_cheap = (align > 0.0).astype(float)   # lagged move into absorbed side
        m_exp = (align < 0.0).astype(float)     # lagged move into costly side

        prod = (x * xl).fillna(0.0)
        axl = xl.abs().fillna(0.0)

        nw, mp = self.W_KER, self.MIN_KER
        num_p = prod.rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()
        den_p = axl.rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()
        num_c = (prod * m_cheap).rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()
        den_c = (axl * m_cheap).rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()
        num_e = (prod * m_exp).rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()
        den_e = (axl * m_exp).rolling(nw, min_periods=mp).sum()

        k = self.K_SHRINK
        rho_pool = num_p / (den_p + k)
        rho_cheap = (num_c + k * rho_pool) / (den_c + k)
        rho_exp = (num_e + k * rho_pool) / (den_e + k)

        # ---- select the kernel by the CURRENT bar's absorption side ---------
        cur = (x * cheap_dir).fillna(0.0)
        rho_sign = rho_pool.copy()
        rho_sign = rho_sign.where(cur <= 0.0, rho_cheap)
        rho_sign = rho_sign.where(cur >= 0.0, rho_exp)
        rho_sign = rho_sign.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        lam_ar = _arcsine_invert(rho_sign)
        s_h = _geometric_horizon_sum(lam_ar, self.prediction_horizon)

        # ---- current innovation, winsorised in own-volatility units ---------
        sigma = (
            idio.rolling(self.W_BETA, min_periods=self.W_BETA // 2)
            .std()
            .replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        u = (idio / sigma).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        innov = (u * sigma).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- bounded repurchase-capacity amplitude tilt (Parent A economics)
        mcap = data["marketCap"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rep = data["shareRepurchase"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        bb = (-rep.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).clip(lower=0.0)
        byield = (bb / mcap).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        cap_r = rank(byield).fillna(0.5)
        tilt = 1.0 + 0.4 * (cap_r - 0.5)

        f = (s_h * innov * tilt).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        z = _cs_robust_z(f, 4.0)
        z = z.sub(z.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return z.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Absorption-side-conditioned sign-kernel recoil
programs.trading_idea: Parent B showed that each name's 6-bar impulse response is a mixture of quote-noise (negative lag-1 kernel) and informed order-splitting (positive kernel), with the mixture weight switching on a crude volume regime; Parent A showed that the true state variable is directional — one side of the book can be persistently absorbed (small square-root impact per unit dollar traded) while the other pays full impact. The child conditions B's per-name sign-persistence kernel on A's *signed* absorption state: bars whose move points into the cheaply-absorbed side are liquidity-provision noise and should recoil, while bars pushing into the expensive side are information that keeps travelling, so the kernel is estimated separately for cheap-side and expensive-side conditioning bars, EB-shrunk to the pooled kernel, arcsine-inverted and geometrically summed over exactly six steps. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: A's asymmetry was only a slow level (and was crippled by a stale quarterly gate, hence its sign flip), B's regime was sign-symmetric and therefore averaged the absorbed and unabsorbed directions together; a small bounded buyback-yield tilt keeps A's economic story that persistent one-sided absorption is often a real repurchase program, without letting a quarterly field drive the signal.
programs.description: Lag-1 sign-persistence kernel of market-residualised 10-second returns, estimated separately on conditioning bars that pushed into the cheaply-absorbed side versus the expensive side of the trailing sign-split square-root impact coefficient, empirical-Bayes shrunk, arcsine-inverted to an AR coefficient, summed over six steps and applied to the current winsorised idiosyncratic innovation with a bounded buyback-yield amplitude tilt.

programs.code:
"""Side-resolved impact vacuum x exhaustion switch.

Mechanism
---------
Liquidity is asymmetric and slow-moving: a sign-split square-root impact
coefficient  lam = |idio return| / sqrt(dollar volume / trailing dollar volume)
averaged separately over up bars and down bars of a trailing 30-minute window
identifies which side of the book is currently expensive (thin) to trade
through.  That is a *state*, not a trigger.  The trigger is an exhaustion clock:
a side-aligned Hawkes-style exponentially-decayed flow intensity that has fallen
off its own 30-bar peak while price has lifted off the excursion extreme.

A fresh 12-bar displacement is then classified by the interaction of the two:
  * it travelled into the EXPENSIVE side (little volume needed to move price)
    and the side-aligned flow has finished  -> mechanical vacuum move, snap back;
  * it travelled into the CHEAP / absorbing side (price moved even though impact
    per unit traded is low there) and the flow is still at its peak
    -> informational metaorder, continue; amplified in high-leverage names where
    a down move carries genuine asset-value news (Merton / Christie).

Every statistic is a trailing rolling / exponentially-weighted window or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional operation, so the value at bar t uses only
information available at or before t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_max, ts_min
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rank_mid(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank in [0, 1]; missing pinned to the median."""
    return rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)


def _side_impact(lam: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, w: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing mean of the impact coefficient restricted to one bar sign."""
    return lam.where(mask).rolling(w, min_periods=max(w // 6, 5)).mean()


def _intensity(flow: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float, minp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Hawkes-style exponentially-decayed event intensity (causal EWMA)."""
    return flow.ewm(halflife=halflife, min_periods=minp, adjust=True).mean()


def _exhaustion(lam_i: pd.DataFrame, w: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fractional decay of an intensity from its own trailing w-bar peak."""
    peak = ts_max(lam_i, w).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = 1.0 - lam_i / peak
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class SideResolvedImpactVacuumExhaustionSwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Sign-split impact asymmetry (which side is thin) x side-aligned flow exhaustion."""

    factor_id = 'side_resolved_impact_vacuum_exhaustion_switch'
    name = 'Side-resolved impact vacuum x exhaustion switch'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Signed 12-bar idiosyncratic displacement, magnitude-ranked, multiplied by a '
        'switch between continuation (move travelled into the cheap-impact side with '
        'side-aligned flow intensity still at its 30-bar peak, levered names amplified) '
        'and reversal (move travelled into the expensive-impact side, intensity decayed '
        'off its peak, price lifted off the excursion extreme).'
    )
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume', 'debtToAssets']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    W_IMP = 180        # 30 min : sign-split impact estimation window
    W_LONG = 390       # 65 min : dollar-volume / return-vol normaliser
    W_DISP = 12        # 2 min  : fresh displacement window
    W_PEAK = 30        # 5 min  : flow-intensity peak window
    HL_FLOW = 6.0      # intensity halflife in bars

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        high = data['high'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).abs().fillna(0.0)

        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        rel = ret.sub(ret.median(axis=1), axis=0)          # idiosyncratic increment

        wi, wl, wd, wp = self.W_IMP, self.W_LONG, self.W_DISP, self.W_PEAK

        # ---- sign-split square-root impact coefficient (which side is thin) ----
        dv = close.abs() * vol
        dvbar = dv.rolling(wl, min_periods=wl // 3).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vn = (dv / dvbar).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        lam = rel.abs() / np.sqrt(vn.clip(lower=0.01))
        lam = lam.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lam_up = _side_impact(lam, rel > 0.0, wi)
        lam_dn = _side_impact(lam, rel < 0.0, wi)
        denom = (lam_up + lam_dn).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        asym = ((lam_up - lam_dn) / denom).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # ---- fresh signed displacement, vol-normalised ----
        disp = rel.rolling(wd, min_periods=max(wd - 4, 4)).sum()
        sig_r = rel.rolling(wl, min_periods=wl // 3).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        zd = (disp / (sig_r * np.sqrt(float(wd)))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        zd = zd.clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        up_side = zd > 0.0
        s = np.sign(zd)

        # ---- side-resolved vacuum: did the move travel into the expensive side? ----
        vac_raw = (asym * s).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        vac = _rank_mid(vac_raw.where(zd.notna()))

        # ---- side-aligned exhaustion clock ----
        flow_up = (vol * rel.clip(lower=0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        flow_dn = (vol * (-rel.clip(upper=0.0))).fillna(0.0)
        ex_up = _exhaustion(_intensity(flow_up, self.HL_FLOW, 12), wp)
        ex_dn = _exhaustion(_intensity(flow_dn, self.HL_FLOW, 12), wp)
        ex_flow = ex_up.where(up_side, ex_dn)

        hi = ts_max(high, wp)
        lo = ts_min(low, wp)
        span = (hi - lo).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lift_up = ((hi - close) / span).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        lift_dn = ((close - lo) / span).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        liftoff = lift_up.where(up_side, lift_dn)

        exh = np.sqrt(ex_flow.fillna(0.0) * liftoff.fillna(0.0)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # ---- leverage tilt: down moves in levered names carry asset-value news ----
        d2a = data['debtToAssets'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        d2a = d2a.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 3.0)
        r_lev = _rank_mid(d2a)
        lev_amp = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols).where(up_side, 0.6 + 0.8 * r_lev)

        # ---- two-sided switch ----
        w_cont = (1.0 - vac) * (1.0 - exh) * lev_amp
        w_rev = vac * exh
        switch = (w_cont - w_rev).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        mag = _rank_mid(zd.abs().where(zd.notna()))
        signed_mag = (s * mag).where(zd.notna())

        sig = (signed_mag * switch).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Side-resolved impact vacuum × exhaustion switch
programs.trading_idea: Parent B shows that liquidity is asymmetric and persistent: a sign-split square-root impact coefficient (|idio return| per sqrt(normalised dollar volume) on up bars vs down bars) tells you which side of the book is thin, but B fires on the state alone with no timing. Parent A supplies the clock — a pressure-driven displacement only pays back after the side-aligned Hawkes-style flow intensity has decayed off its own peak and price has lifted off the excursion extreme — but A's 'purity' (variance per unit participation) is direction-blind, so half of its supposedly mechanical bursts actually travelled into the *deep* side and kept going, which is the most likely reason its realized IC contradicted its declared reversal direction. The child fixes exactly that by making the vacuum measure side-resolved: a 12-bar displacement that travelled into the expensive/thin side (mechanical impact) AND whose side-aligned flow intensity has already decayed off its 30-bar peak is traded as a snapback, whereas a displacement that moved price *despite* paying cheap impact into a deep, absorbing side while its flow is still peaking is genuine information and is traded as continuation (amplified for levered names, where a down-move carries asset-value news). Neither parent can express this sign flip: A cannot tell which side was thin, B cannot tell whether the pressure has finished.
programs.description: Signed 12-bar idiosyncratic displacement, magnitude-ranked, multiplied by a switch between continuation weight (displacement travelled into the cheap-impact/deep side while the side-aligned exponentially-decayed flow intensity is still at its 30-bar peak, levered names amplified) and reversal weight (displacement travelled into the expensive-impact/thin side and the side-aligned intensity has decayed off its peak with price lifted off the excursion extreme).

programs.code:
"""Symbolic mutual-information gated flow propagation.

Mechanism: an execution algorithm working a metaorder leaves a low-entropy,
repeating (direction x size) footprint on consecutive bars; uncoordinated
two-sided competition leaves a near-maximal-entropy footprint.  For each name we
estimate, from trailing data only:

  * MI  -- the Miller-Madow bias-corrected mutual information between the
           consecutive symbols s_t, s_{t-1} of a 4-letter alphabet
           {up, down} x {heavy volume, light volume}.  This is a model-free,
           nonlinear measure of how much of the next bar's symbol is already
           determined by the current one.
  * lam -- a volume-weighted lag-1 sign-propagation coefficient: are
           heavy-volume moves followed by same-signed moves (unfinished informed
           metaorder, lam > 0) or by opposite-signed moves (transient impact of
           a liquidity-demanding print, lam < 0)?

Recent volume-weighted directional pressure is then FOLLOWED where lam > 0 and
FADED where lam < 0, with position size scaled by MI (conviction).  Every
statistic is a trailing rolling window or a contemporaneous cross-sectional
operation, so the value at bar t uses only information available at or before t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_N = 120
_MINP = 60

def _rolling_entropy(codes: pd.DataFrame, k_max: int, n: int, minp: int):
    """Trailing plug-in Shannon entropy (nats) of an integer symbol frame.

    ``codes`` holds symbol indices 0..k_max-1, with -1 marking invalid bars.
    Returns (entropy, number of occupied cells, valid count) -- the occupancy
    count feeds the Miller-Madow bias correction.  Causal: only trailing
    rolling sums are used.
    """
    valid = (codes >= 0).astype(float)
    cnt = valid.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
    cnt_safe = cnt.where(cnt > 0.0)
    ent = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=codes.index, columns=codes.columns)
    occ = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=codes.index, columns=codes.columns)
    for k in range(k_max):
        c = (codes == k).astype(float).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
        p = c / cnt_safe
        term = -(p * np.log(p.where(p > 0.0)))
        ent = ent + term.fillna(0.0)
        occ = occ + (c > 0.0).astype(float)
    keep = cnt >= float(minp)
    return (ent.where(keep), occ.where(keep), cnt.where(keep))

@register_factor
class SymbolicMutualInformationGatedFlowPropagation(BaseFactor):
    """Follow pressure when the symbol stream is predictable and propagating."""
    factor_id = 'symbolic_mutual_information_gated_flow_propagati'
    name = 'Symbolic mutual-information gated flow propagation'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Decay-weighted volume-weighted signed pressure over the last 6 bars, multiplied by tanh of a trailing volume-weighted lag-1 sign-propagation coefficient (continuation vs bounce switch) and weighted by the bias-corrected mutual information between consecutive (sign x volume regime) symbols.'
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        ret_idio = ret.sub(ret.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        advv = vol.rolling(_N, min_periods=_MINP).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        omega = (vol / advv).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0, upper=10.0)
        med = vol.rolling(_N, min_periods=_MINP).median()
        sgn_df = np.sign(ret_idio)
        sgn = sgn_df.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        volA = vol.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        medA = med.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        ok = np.isfinite(sgn) & (sgn != 0.0) & np.isfinite(volA) & np.isfinite(medA)
        heavy = np.where(np.isfinite(volA) & np.isfinite(medA), volA > medA, False)
        up = sgn > 0.0
        sym = np.where(ok, up.astype(np.int64) + 2 * heavy.astype(np.int64), -1).astype(np.int64)
        prev = np.full_like(sym, -1)
        prev[1:, :] = sym[:-1, :]
        pair_ok = (sym >= 0) & (prev >= 0)
        x_codes = pd.DataFrame(np.where(pair_ok, sym, -1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        y_codes = pd.DataFrame(np.where(pair_ok, prev, -1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        xy_codes = pd.DataFrame(np.where(pair_ok, sym * 4 + prev, -1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        h_x, occ_x, cnt = _rolling_entropy(x_codes, 4, _N, _MINP)
        h_y, occ_y, _ = _rolling_entropy(y_codes, 4, _N, _MINP)
        h_xy, occ_xy, _ = _rolling_entropy(xy_codes, 16, _N, _MINP)
        mi_plug = h_x + h_y - h_xy
        bias = (occ_xy - occ_x - occ_y + 1.0) / (2.0 * cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        mi = ((mi_plug - bias) / np.log(4.0)).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        mi = mi.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        s_prev = sgn_df.shift(1)
        w_prev = omega.shift(1)
        conc = sgn_df * s_prev
        num = (conc * w_prev).rolling(_N, min_periods=_MINP).mean()
        den = (conc.abs() * w_prev).rolling(_N, min_periods=_MINP).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lam = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0)
        flow = sgn_df * np.sqrt(omega.clip(lower=0.0))
        flow = flow.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        press = decay_linear(flow.fillna(0.0), 6)
        press = press.where(ret.notna())
        switch = np.tanh(2.5 * lam)
        conviction = 0.3 + rank(mi).fillna(0.5)
        sig = (rank(press) - 0.5) * switch * conviction
        valid = press.notna() & lam.notna() & mi.notna()
        sig = sig.where(valid)
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Symbolic mutual-information gated flow propagation
programs.trading_idea: A schedule-constrained execution algorithm imprints a low-entropy, repeating (direction x size) pattern on consecutive bars, while genuinely competitive two-sided flow produces a near-maximal-entropy symbol stream; so the *predictability* of a name's own recent symbol sequence tells you whether its current directional pressure is the visible tail of an unfinished metaorder or just noise. I therefore estimate per name, on trailing data only, (a) the Miller-Madow-corrected mutual information between consecutive symbols drawn from {up,down} x {heavy,light volume} — a model-free, nonlinear measure of how much of the next bar is already determined — and (b) a volume-weighted sign-propagation coefficient lambda that says whether heavy-volume moves are followed by same-signed moves (unfinished informed metaorder) or opposite-signed moves (transient impact of a liquidity-demanding print). The signal follows the last minute's volume-weighted directional pressure when lambda > 0 and fades it when lambda < 0, with conviction scaled by the symbolic mutual information; it is falsified if pressure alone carries the IC, if the mutual-information weighting adds nothing, or if lambda < 0 names show the same pressure-return sign as lambda > 0 names. The edge should persist because the pattern is manufactured by participation-constrained execution algos that cannot conceal their regularity, while liquidity providers gate on spread and depth and the standard alpha stack measures order flow with linear autocorrelations and imbalance sums — a plug-in, bias-corrected mutual information on a discretised joint (sign, size) alphabet is nonlinear and non-differentiable, hence invisible to those estimators.
programs.description: Cross-sectional interaction of (i) decay-weighted volume-weighted signed pressure over the last 6 bars with (ii) a trailing volume-weighted lag-1 sign-propagation coefficient (continuation vs. bounce switch) and (iii) the bias-corrected mutual information between consecutive (return-sign x volume-regime) symbols over 120 bars used as a conviction weight.

programs.code:
"""Depth-asymmetry diffusivity gradient drift.

Mechanism: if a unit of traded volume displaces the mid further upward than
downward around the current price (an asymmetric impact map / diffusivity
landscape), then even unbiased order flow generates a positive expected mid
displacement, E[dP] ~ (lambda_up - lambda_down) / 2 * flow.  This is a pure
convexity effect and is *not* a martingale, so it is falsifiable: measure the
Kyle-style impact coefficient per unit volume separately for bars whose
pre-bar state was above vs below a fast EWMA price anchor, and take the log
ratio.  The per-volume normalisation removes the 'one side is simply busier'
confound, and the fast anchor makes the two regimes interleave in time so slow
volatility trends cancel in the ratio.  The edge persists because harvesting it
requires crossing the spread on the thin, adverse-selection-prone side, and
because depth asymmetry is continuously regenerated by inventory management.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# causal helpers (trailing windows / positive lags only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _log_price(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Log mid price, robust to zero / negative / missing prints."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    return np.log(c)


def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row robust standardisation (median / MAD with std fallback)."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    z = dev.div(scale, axis=0)
    return z.clip(-4.0, 4.0)


@register_factor
class DepthAsymmetryDiffusivityGradientDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Long names whose impact-per-volume is higher above their local anchor."""

    factor_id = "depth_asymmetry_diffusivity_gradient_drift"
    name = "Depth-asymmetry diffusivity gradient drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Two-sided Kyle impact coefficient (sum of variance-normalised squared "
        "returns / sum of baseline-normalised volume) estimated separately for "
        "bars starting above vs below a fast EWMA price anchor; the signal is "
        "the cross-sectionally standardised log ratio (upper / lower), scaled by "
        "recent flow intensity."
    )
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # --- parameters ------------------------------------------------------
    _EST_WIN = 240        # trailing bars used to estimate each side's impact (~40 min)
    _ANCHOR_HL = 30.0     # EWMA halflife of the price anchor (~5 min)
    _SIG_WIN = 180        # trailing window for per-name return scaling
    _DEV_MIN = 120        # min_periods for the state-dispersion estimate
    _BAND = 0.4           # dead-band (in state sigmas) around the anchor
    _MIN_CNT = 15.0       # minimum bars required on each side
    _FLOW_WIN = 6         # recent-flow window (matches the forecast horizon)

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        # ---- returns and per-name scaling --------------------------------
        p = _log_price(close)
        r = (p - p.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = r.rolling(self._SIG_WIN, min_periods=self._SIG_WIN // 2).std()
        sig = sig.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rr = (r / sig) ** 2                      # dimensionless squared return
        rr = rr.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(upper=100.0)

        base_v = ts_mean(vol, self._EST_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vn = (vol / base_v).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        vn = vn.clip(lower=0.0, upper=50.0)      # dimensionless flow

        # ---- local state: signed distance from a fast price anchor --------
        anchor = p.ewm(halflife=self._ANCHOR_HL, min_periods=int(self._ANCHOR_HL)).mean()
        dev = p - anchor
        sdev = dev.rolling(self._EST_WIN, min_periods=self._DEV_MIN).std()
        sdev = sdev.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        state = (dev / sdev).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        state_prev = state.shift(1)              # pre-bar state -> strictly causal

        # ---- side masks (dead-band excludes the ambiguous middle) ---------
        good = rr.notna() & vn.notna() & state_prev.notna()
        up = good & (state_prev > self._BAND)
        dn = good & (state_prev < -self._BAND)

        rrf = rr.fillna(0.0)
        vnf = vn.fillna(0.0)
        n = self._EST_WIN

        cnt_up = ts_sum(up.astype(float), n)
        cnt_dn = ts_sum(dn.astype(float), n)
        s_up = ts_sum(rrf.where(up, 0.0), n)
        s_dn = ts_sum(rrf.where(dn, 0.0), n)
        v_up = ts_sum(vnf.where(up, 0.0), n)
        v_dn = ts_sum(vnf.where(dn, 0.0), n)

        # ratio-of-sums Kyle coefficient per side (floors keep it well posed)
        lam_up = (s_up + 0.05 * cnt_up) / (v_up + 0.10 * cnt_up)
        lam_dn = (s_dn + 0.05 * cnt_dn) / (v_dn + 0.10 * cnt_dn)
        lam_up = lam_up.where((cnt_up >= self._MIN_CNT) & (lam_up > 0.0))
        lam_dn = lam_dn.where((cnt_dn >= self._MIN_CNT) & (lam_dn > 0.0))

        grad = (np.log(lam_up) - np.log(lam_dn))
        grad = grad.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        # ---- the drift needs flow to materialise -------------------------
        flow = ts_mean(vnf, self._FLOW_WIN).clip(lower=0.05, upper=4.0)
        weight = np.sqrt(flow)

        raw = grad * weight
        score = _cs_robust_z(raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Depth-asymmetry diffusivity gradient drift
programs.trading_idea: If the price-impact map around a name's current price is asymmetric — a unit of traded volume moves the mid further upward than downward — then even perfectly unbiased order flow produces a positive expected mid displacement, because E[dP] = (lambda_up - lambda_down)/2 * flow: a purely convexity-driven, non-martingale drift toward the thin side of the book. I estimate the local diffusivity landscape as a two-sided Kyle coefficient (sum of normalised squared returns divided by sum of normalised traded volume) computed separately over bars whose *pre-bar* state was above versus below a fast 5-minute EWMA price anchor, so slow volatility trends and the symmetric 'extremes are volatile' effect cancel in the log-ratio, and the per-volume normalisation removes the possibility that one side is merely busier. Prediction: the log-ratio of upper-side to lower-side impact per unit volume predicts positive 60-second returns, and the effect must be concentrated where current flow is non-trivial (hence the flow-intensity scaling) — it is falsified if the drift is absent, or reverses, once impact asymmetry is measured per unit volume rather than per bar. It survives arbitrage because it is a conditional *second*-moment-per-unit-flow statistic invisible to first-moment flow/momentum signals, harvesting it means crossing the spread exactly on the thin (expensive, adverse-selection-prone) side so the sub-spread drift is unprofitable for latency players, and the depth asymmetry it exploits is continuously regenerated by market-maker inventory management rather than being permanently arbitraged away.
programs.description: Per name, estimates the price-impact coefficient (sum of variance-normalised squared returns / sum of baseline-normalised volume) separately for bars starting above vs below a fast EWMA price anchor, and returns the cross-sectionally robust z-score of the log ratio (upper impact / lower impact), scaled by recent flow intensity.

programs.code:
"""Side-conditional flow-deficit reversal.

Mechanism
---------
A price change is permanent only if flow paid for it.  Campbell-Grossman-Wang
(1993) / Kyle logic: bar returns accompanied by unusual traded volume are
information-driven and persist, whereas returns produced with little or no
traded volume are inventory / quote-repricing driven and are unwound as the
intermediary restores its position.

The parent factor of this child measured the *persistent level* of up-bar vs
down-bar square-root impact and gated it on quarterly buyback capacity; that
level is a slow illiquidity characteristic and carried no stable direction out
of sample.  Here the sign-split elasticity is demoted to a *baseline*: each
bar's move-per-unit-flow

    e_t = |idio return_t| / sqrt(dollar volume_t / trailing dollar volume)

is compared with the trailing 30-minute mean of e over bars of the SAME return
sign (lagged one bar).  The excess, z_t = e_t / lambda_side - 1, is the bar's
'flow deficit': z_t > 0 means the price travelled further than this stock
normally travels per unit of flow in that direction (unsupported move),
z_t < 0 means the move was volume-confirmed.  The forecast is the negative of
the deficit-weighted signed return summed over the last 6 bars, so unsupported
moves are faded and volume-confirmed moves are (mildly) extrapolated.

Everything is a trailing rolling statistic or a contemporaneous cross-sectional
operation -> causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, rank, returns, stddev
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _side_baseline(e: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing mean of ``e`` restricted to bars where ``mask`` is True, lagged
    one bar so the current observation never enters its own baseline."""
    m = max(8, n // 6)
    return delay(e.where(mask).rolling(n, min_periods=m).mean(), 1)


@register_factor
class SideConditionalFlowDeficitReversal(BaseFactor):
    """Fade recent price moves that were not paid for by flow."""

    factor_id = 'side_conditional_flow_deficit_reversal'
    name = 'Side-conditional flow-deficit reversal'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Negative cross-sectional rank of the 6-bar sum of signed idiosyncratic '
        'returns weighted by each bar\u2019s excess move-per-unit-flow relative to the '
        'stock\u2019s own trailing 30-minute elasticity for bars of the same sign, '
        'scaled by trailing return volatility.'
    )
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    W_SIDE = 180   # ~30 min: side-conditional elasticity baseline
    W_NORM = 390   # ~65 min: dollar-volume and volatility normalisers
    K = 6          # bars of deficit-weighted move to fade (= horizon)

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs().fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.1, 0.1)

        # idiosyncratic (market-neutral) bar return
        r = ret.sub(ret.median(axis=1), axis=0)

        # normalised dollar volume; a floor keeps zero-volume repricing bars as
        # the extreme 'unsupported move' case rather than dropping them
        dv = close.abs() * vol
        dvbar = dv.rolling(self.W_NORM, min_periods=self.W_NORM // 3).mean()
        dvbar = dvbar.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vn = (dv / dvbar).clip(0.02, 50.0)

        # move per unit of flow (square-root impact metric)
        e = (r.abs() / np.sqrt(vn)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        up = r > 0.0
        dn = r < 0.0
        lam_up = _side_baseline(e, up, self.W_SIDE)
        lam_dn = _side_baseline(e, dn, self.W_SIDE)
        lam = lam_up.where(up, lam_dn).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # flow deficit: >0 unsupported move, <0 volume-confirmed move
        z = (e / lam - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 4.0)
        contrib = (r * z).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        s = contrib.rolling(self.K, min_periods=1).sum()
        sigma = stddev(r, self.W_NORM).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        s_n = (s / (sigma * np.sqrt(float(self.K)))).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        s_n = s_n.clip(-10.0, 10.0)

        sig = rank(-s_n)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Side-conditional flow-deficit reversal
programs.trading_idea: A price change is only permanent if flow paid for it: Campbell-Grossman-Wang / Kyle logic says moves backed by unusual volume carry information and persist, while moves achieved with little or no traded volume are inventory- or quote-driven and are unwound as the intermediary re-establishes its position. The parent measured only the *persistent level* of up-vs-down impact asymmetry — a slow illiquidity characteristic that carried no stable direction out of sample (its interaction even scored with the opposite sign) — so the child keeps the sign-split elasticity estimate but uses it merely as the *baseline*: each bar's move-per-unit-flow is judged against that stock's own trailing elasticity for bars of that same direction, and the resulting excess ('flow deficit') weights the signed return before it is reversed. Side-conditioning matters because in a persistently asymmetric book an ordinary up-tick in a thin-ask name would otherwise be mislabelled as a vacuum move; conditioning on the side removes that static characteristic and leaves only the transient inventory shock. The edge survives arbitrage because each reversal is a few basis points — below single-name round-trip cost — and is only harvestable as a diversified cross-sectional overlay built from side-conditional 10-second elasticity baselines, while the structural cause (dealers absorbing uninformed liquidity demand and unwinding within a minute) recurs continuously.
programs.description: For each 10-second bar, computes move-per-unit-flow e = |idiosyncratic return| / sqrt(normalised dollar volume), divides it by the stock's trailing 30-minute mean of e over bars of the *same* return sign to get an excess-elasticity ('flow deficit') score, weights the signed return by that score, sums over the last 6 bars, scales by trailing return volatility and takes the negative cross-sectional rank: long names whose recent moves were volume-unsupported downticks, short those whose recent moves were volume-unsupported upticks.

programs.code:
"""Online RLS estimate of 6-bar move permanence, split by flow confirmation.

Mechanism
---------
1.  Idiosyncratic return: r is de-marketed with a trailing OLS beta on the
    equal-weighted cross-sectional return, giving eps.
2.  State at bar t (both observable at t):
        x1 = 6-bar cumulated eps, standardised by trailing eps volatility
        x2 = x1 * u, where u is the trailing z-score of log 6-bar volume
    x1 is the raw displacement channel; x2 is the flow-confirmation channel
    (was the displacement backed by abnormal traded volume?).
3.  HORIZON-MATCHED ONLINE REGRESSION.  The realised standardised 6-bar
    forward return seen from bar u is exactly x1 at bar u+6, so the causal
    training pair available at time t is (x1_{t-6}, x2_{t-6}) -> x1_t.
    Exponentially-weighted cross-moments of those pairs give a recursive
    least-squares (forgetting-factor) estimate of the two coefficients per
    name; a scale-relative ridge stabilises the 2x2 solve and the estimates
    are precision-shrunk toward the panel-mean coefficients.
4.  Signal = b1 * x1 + b2 * x2, the name's own live estimate of its expected
    next-6-bar idiosyncratic return.  Sign and amplitude are measured, not
    assumed.

Everything is causal: trailing rolling / EW windows, positive lags only, and
the moment matrices are additionally shifted by one bar so the current bar's
target never influences the coefficients used on it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast(series: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar series across every ticker column."""
    arr = np.tile(series.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1), (1, len(cols)))
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)


def _ew_moment(df: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Exponentially-weighted (forgetting-factor) mean of a cross-product term.

    Trailing and causal; an extra one-bar shift is applied by the caller.
    """
    return df.ewm(halflife=halflife, min_periods=min_obs, adjust=False).mean()


def _solve_2x2(
    a11: pd.DataFrame,
    a12: pd.DataFrame,
    a22: pd.DataFrame,
    b1: pd.DataFrame,
    b2: pd.DataFrame,
    ridge: float,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Ridge-regularised closed-form solution of the 2x2 normal equations."""
    scale = (0.5 * (a11.abs() + a22.abs())).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    lam = ridge * scale
    d11 = a11 + lam
    d22 = a22 + lam
    det = d11 * d22 - a12 * a12
    det = det.where(det.abs() > 1e-10)
    beta1 = (d22 * b1 - a12 * b2) / det
    beta2 = (d11 * b2 - a12 * b1) / det
    return beta1, beta2


def _precision_shrink(
    beta: pd.DataFrame, precision: pd.DataFrame, frac: float
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Blend each name's coefficient toward the same-bar panel mean.

    Weight on the own estimate rises with the EW design precision of that
    name relative to the panel median precision (empirical-Bayes flavour).
    """
    med = precision.median(axis=1)
    tau = (frac * med).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    w = precision.div(precision.add(tau, axis=0).replace(0.0, np.nan))
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w), 0.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    panel = beta.mean(axis=1)
    own = beta.fillna(0.0)
    blended = w * own + (1.0 - w) * (_broadcast(panel, beta.index, beta.columns).fillna(0.0))
    return blended.where(beta.notna() | panel.notna().reindex(beta.index).to_numpy()[:, None])


@register_factor
class RlsOnlineMovePermanenceFlowSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Per-name online RLS forecast of 6-bar residual return, flow-split."""

    factor_id = "rls_online_move_permanence_flow_split"
    name = "Online RLS move-permanence coefficient (flow-split)"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Per-name exponentially-weighted recursive-least-squares forecast of the "
        "next 6-bar market-residual return, fitted at exactly the 6-bar lag on the "
        "prior 6-bar residual return and its interaction with the volume z-score, "
        "ridge-regularised and precision-shrunk toward the panel-mean coefficients."
    )
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # constants (1 bar = 10 seconds)
    _LAG = 6            # == prediction_horizon; the regression is fitted at this lag
    _BETA_WIN = 360     # ~1 hour trailing market beta
    _VOL_WIN = 180      # ~30 min volatility / volume normalisation
    _VOL_MIN = 60
    _HL = 600.0         # RLS forgetting half-life (~100 min)
    _MIN_OBS = 300
    _RIDGE = 0.10
    _SHRINK_FRAC = 0.5
    _X_CLIP = 5.0
    _U_CLIP = 3.0
    _B_CLIP = 2.0
    _F_CLIP = 6.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        if px.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        logp = np.log(px)
        r = logp.diff()
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # ---- 1) idiosyncratic (market-residual) return -------------------- #
        mkt = r.mean(axis=1)
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta_m = rolling_beta(r, mkt_df, self._BETA_WIN)
        beta_m = beta_m.where(np.isfinite(beta_m)).clip(-3.0, 3.0).fillna(1.0)
        eps = r - beta_m * mkt_df
        eps = eps.where(np.isfinite(eps))

        # ---- 2) state variables ------------------------------------------ #
        e6 = eps.rolling(self._LAG, min_periods=self._LAG).sum()
        sd = eps.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).std()
        sd = sd.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x1 = (e6 / (sd * np.sqrt(float(self._LAG)))).clip(-self._X_CLIP, self._X_CLIP)

        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            return zero
        vol = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0))
        v6 = vol.rolling(self._LAG, min_periods=self._LAG).sum()
        lv = np.log1p(v6)
        mu = lv.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).mean()
        sv = lv.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        u = ((lv - mu) / sv).clip(-self._U_CLIP, self._U_CLIP)
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u))

        x2 = x1 * u

        # ---- 3) horizon-matched online RLS -------------------------------- #
        big_x1 = x1.shift(self._LAG)
        big_x2 = x2.shift(self._LAG)
        y = x1  # realised standardised 6-bar return following big_x*

        ok = big_x1.notna() & big_x2.notna() & y.notna()
        gx1 = big_x1.where(ok)
        gx2 = big_x2.where(ok)
        gy = y.where(ok)

        a11 = _ew_moment(gx1 * gx1, self._HL, self._MIN_OBS).shift(1)
        a12 = _ew_moment(gx1 * gx2, self._HL, self._MIN_OBS).shift(1)
        a22 = _ew_moment(gx2 * gx2, self._HL, self._MIN_OBS).shift(1)
        b1m = _ew_moment(gx1 * gy, self._HL, self._MIN_OBS).shift(1)
        b2m = _ew_moment(gx2 * gy, self._HL, self._MIN_OBS).shift(1)

        beta1, beta2 = _solve_2x2(a11, a12, a22, b1m, b2m, self._RIDGE)
        beta1 = beta1.where(np.isfinite(beta1)).clip(-self._B_CLIP, self._B_CLIP)
        beta2 = beta2.where(np.isfinite(beta2)).clip(-self._B_CLIP, self._B_CLIP)

        prec = a11.abs().where(np.isfinite(a11))
        beta1s = _precision_shrink(beta1, prec, self._SHRINK_FRAC)
        beta2s = _precision_shrink(beta2, prec, self._SHRINK_FRAC)

        # ---- 4) fitted 6-bar-ahead expected residual return --------------- #
        pred = beta1s * x1 + beta2s * x2
        pred = pred.where(np.isfinite(pred)).clip(-self._F_CLIP, self._F_CLIP)
        pred = pred.where(x1.notna() & u.notna())

        if pred.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero

        out = rank(pred) - 0.5
        out = out.where(pred.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Online RLS move-permanence coefficient (flow-split)
programs.trading_idea: At 10-second frequency the fraction of a price move that is permanent rather than transient is a name-specific, slowly drifting quantity set by queue depth, tick-size binding and the inventory horizon of whoever is making that name's market: the identical 60-second move continues in one stock and snaps back in another, and within a stock it tends to continue when it arrives with abnormal trade volume (informed flow, permanent impact) and to revert when it does not (inventory pressure or liquidity withdrawal). Instead of imposing a sign or a heuristic gate, the child estimates each name's two permanence coefficients ONLINE by exponentially-weighted recursive least squares fitted at exactly the 6-bar forecast lag — regressing each realised 6-bar idiosyncratic (market-beta-residual) return on the preceding 6-bar idiosyncratic return and on its interaction with the contemporaneous volume z-score — ridge-regularised and precision-shrunk toward the panel-mean coefficient vector, and emits the fitted 6-bar-ahead expected return. The edge survives arbitrage because the coefficient flips sign across names and across regimes, so the aggregate signal carries almost no unconditional momentum or reversal loading and looks like noise to any fixed-sign relative-value trader; it is falsified if replacing the per-name coefficients with their panel means (or with a constant negative loading) costs no information content.
programs.description: Per-name, exponentially-weighted recursive-least-squares forecast of the next 6-bar market-residual return, regressed at exactly the 6-bar lag on the prior 6-bar residual return and its interaction with the trade-volume z-score, ridge-regularised and precision-shrunk toward the panel-mean coefficients; output is the cross-sectional rank of the fitted forecast.

programs.code:
"""Tail-Volume-Concentration Gated Characteristic Factor Relay.

Mechanism
---------
At the 10-second scale the cross-sectional return attached to a fundamental
characteristic (its "factor return") is a mixture of two things:

  (a) sliced execution of a basket / factor-tilt programme, which keeps pushing
      the same characteristic the same way for tens of seconds, and
  (b) quote-bounce noise, which reverses within a couple of bars.

Unconditionally these cancel near a 6-bar horizon.  What separates them is
WHERE the traded volume sits along the characteristic axis: a long-short
programme trades BOTH tails of the characteristic, so abnormal volume loads on
|characteristic loading| (a magnitude-only, non-tautological detector that does
not reuse the return sign).  Bounce noise leaves volume unrelated to the axis.

Implementation (all causal, trailing windows / positive lags only):
  1. Live loadings from point-in-time fundamentals over the live price
     (book/price, sales/price, FCF/price), plus log size and ROE, each turned
     into a cross-sectionally centred rank in [-1, 1].
  2. Per-bar ridge cross-sectional regression of the bar return on
     [intercept | loadings] -> characteristic factor returns F_t.
  3. Per-bar, per-characteristic cross-sectional slope of trailing-z-scored
     abnormal volume on cross-sectionally demeaned |loading| -> A_kt
     ("tail-volume concentration" of characteristic k).
  4. Gate g_kt = tanh(trailing z-score of the 6-bar-smoothed A_kt): positive
     when a programme is demonstrably trading the axis, negative when quiet.
  5. pred_kt = g_kt * z(sum of last 6 bars of F_k)  -> continuation when gated
     on, reversal when gated off; relayed onto names via their loadings.
  6. Cross-sectional rank, centred at zero.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, returns, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _centered_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank mapped to [-1, 1]; NaN stays NaN."""
    r = df.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    return (r - 0.5) * 2.0

def _pos_log_ratio(num: pd.DataFrame, den: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """log(num / den) restricted to strictly positive, finite inputs."""
    d = den.where(np.isfinite(den) & (den != 0.0))
    ratio = num / d
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)

def _ratio(num: pd.DataFrame, den: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    d = den.where(np.isfinite(den) & (den != 0.0))
    ratio = num / d
    return ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio))

def _robust_clip_rows(r: pd.DataFrame, k: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Winsorise each bar's cross-section at k robust sigmas (median / MAD)."""
    med = r.median(axis=1)
    mad = r.sub(med, axis=0).abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    lim = (k * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    lim = lim.where(np.isfinite(lim), 1.0)
    dev = r.sub(med, axis=0)
    dev = dev.clip(lower=-lim, upper=lim, axis=0)
    return dev.add(med, axis=0)

def _cs_factor_returns(loadings: list[pd.DataFrame], ret: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int, ridge_rel: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar ridge cross-sectional regression of ret on [1 | loadings].

    Purely contemporaneous in the cross-section: the coefficient at bar t uses
    only bar-t returns and bar-t loadings (no time-series leakage).
    """
    idx = ret.index
    ones = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=ret.columns)
    cols = [ones] + loadings
    cols = [c.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0) for c in cols]
    rv = ret.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    kk = len(cols)
    t = len(idx)
    xtx = np.zeros((t, kk, kk), dtype=float)
    xtr = np.zeros((t, kk), dtype=float)
    for a in range(kk):
        xtr[:, a] = (cols[a] * rv).sum(axis=1).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        for b in range(a, kk):
            v = (cols[a] * cols[b]).sum(axis=1).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            xtx[:, a, b] = v
            xtx[:, b, a] = v
    tr = np.trace(xtx, axis1=1, axis2=2)
    lam = np.maximum(1e-10, ridge_rel * tr / float(kk))
    xtx = xtx + lam[:, None, None] * np.eye(kk)[None, :, :]
    fac = np.linalg.solve(xtx, xtr[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]
    cnt = mask.sum(axis=1).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    fac[cnt < float(min_names)] = 0.0
    fac = np.nan_to_num(fac, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    fac = np.clip(fac, -0.05, 0.05)
    return pd.DataFrame(fac, index=idx, columns=list(range(kk)))

def _tail_volume_slope(loading: pd.DataFrame, uc: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Cross-sectional slope of abnormal volume on |loading| (both demeaned).

    Magnitude-only: it measures whether abnormal trading concentrates at BOTH
    tails of the characteristic, i.e. the footprint of a long-short programme
    working that axis.  Uses only bar-t information.
    """
    w = loading.abs().where(mask)
    wc = w.sub(w.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    wc = wc.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    num = (wc * uc).sum(axis=1)
    den = (wc * wc).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return num / den

@register_factor
class TailVolumeConcentrationGatedCharacteristicRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Sign characteristic-factor continuation by tail-volume concentration."""
    factor_id = 'characteristic_tail_volume_concentration_gated_f'
    name = 'Tail-Volume-Concentration Gated Characteristic Factor Relay'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Per-bar ridge cross-sectional regression of 10-second returns on live point-in-time characteristic loadings (book/price, sales/price, FCF/price, log size, ROE) gives characteristic factor returns; each characteristic's trailing-normalised cross-sectional slope of abnormal volume on |loading| signs the relay of its last-6-bar factor return back onto names' loadings (continuation when tail-volume concentration is high, reversal when low), then cross-sectionally ranked."
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'freeCashFlowPerShare', 'marketCap', 'sharesOutstanding', 'roe']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _SUM_WIN = 6
    _SMOOTH = 6
    _NORM_WIN = 240
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _MIN_NAMES = 10
    _RIDGE_REL = 0.005
    _RET_CLIP_SIGMA = 6.0
    _Z_CLIP = 4.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))

        def _get(field: str) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
            raw = data.get(field)
            if raw is None:
                return None
            out = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            try:
                out = out.astype(float)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
            if out.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                return None
            return out
        bvps = _get('bookValuePerShare')
        rps = _get('revenuePerShare')
        fcfps = _get('freeCashFlowPerShare')
        mcap = _get('marketCap')
        shares = _get('sharesOutstanding')
        roe = _get('roe')
        raw_chars: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        if bvps is not None:
            raw_chars.append(_pos_log_ratio(bvps, px))
        if rps is not None:
            raw_chars.append(_pos_log_ratio(rps, px))
        if fcfps is not None:
            raw_chars.append(_ratio(fcfps, px))
        size_src = None
        if mcap is not None:
            size_src = mcap.where(np.isfinite(mcap) & (mcap > 0.0))
        elif shares is not None:
            cand = px * shares.where(np.isfinite(shares) & (shares > 0.0))
            size_src = cand.where(np.isfinite(cand) & (cand > 0.0))
        if size_src is not None:
            raw_chars.append(np.log(size_src))
        if roe is not None:
            raw_chars.append(roe.where(np.isfinite(roe)))
        if not raw_chars:
            return zero
        loadings = [_centered_rank(c) for c in raw_chars]
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.where(np.isfinite(ret))
        ret = _robust_clip_rows(ret, self._RET_CLIP_SIGMA)
        have_char = None
        for ld in loadings:
            flag = ld.notna()
            have_char = flag if have_char is None else have_char | flag
        mask = ret.notna() & px.notna() & have_char
        if mask.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        fac = _cs_factor_returns(loadings, ret, mask, self._MIN_NAMES, self._RIDGE_REL)
        vol = data.get('volume')
        if vol is None:
            return zero
        vol = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        try:
            vol = vol.astype(float)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return zero
        vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0))
        lv = np.log1p(vol)
        uz = ts_zscore(lv, self._VOL_WIN)
        uz = uz.where(np.isfinite(uz)).clip(-self._Z_CLIP, self._Z_CLIP)
        uz = uz.where(mask)
        uc = uz.sub(uz.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        uc = uc.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        n_ok = mask.sum(axis=1)
        slope_cols: dict[int, pd.Series] = {}
        for k, ld in enumerate(loadings, start=1):
            s = _tail_volume_slope(ld, uc, mask)
            s = s.where(n_ok >= self._MIN_NAMES)
            slope_cols[k] = s
        a_df = pd.DataFrame(slope_cols, index=idx)
        a_df = a_df.where(np.isfinite(a_df))
        a_s = decay_linear(a_df.fillna(0.0), self._SMOOTH)
        a_z = ts_zscore(a_s, self._NORM_WIN)
        a_z = a_z.where(np.isfinite(a_z)).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        gate = np.tanh(a_z).fillna(0.0)
        f6 = ts_sum(fac, self._SUM_WIN)
        f6z = ts_zscore(f6, self._NORM_WIN)
        f6z = f6z.where(np.isfinite(f6z)).clip(-self._Z_CLIP, self._Z_CLIP)
        f6z = f6z.fillna(0.0)
        sig = None
        for k, ld in enumerate(loadings, start=1):
            if k not in f6z.columns or k not in gate.columns:
                continue
            p = gate[k] * f6z[k]
            if p.abs().sum() == 0.0:
                continue
            contrib = ld.fillna(0.0).mul(p, axis=0)
            contrib = contrib.where(np.isfinite(contrib), 0.0)
            sig = contrib if sig is None else sig.add(contrib, fill_value=0.0)
        if sig is None:
            return zero
        sig = sig.where(mask)
        sig = sig.where(np.isfinite(sig))
        out = rank(sig) - 0.5
        out = out.where(sig.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
