programs.trading_idea: The parent showed that 10-second characteristic factor returns reverse at 1-3 bars and continue at 12-24 bars, so at the pinned 6-bar horizon the unconditional relay sits exactly on its zero crossing: it is a mixture of two opposite populations. The separating state variable is *where the traded volume sits along the characteristic axis*: a genuine sliced basket/factor-tilt programme buys one tail of a characteristic and sells the other, so abnormal volume concentrates at BOTH extremes of that characteristic's loading (positive cross-sectional slope of abnormal volume on |loading|), whereas quote-bounce noise leaves volume unrelated to the characteristic. The child therefore measures, per bar and per characteristic, the ridge cross-sectional factor return AND this magnitude-only tail-volume concentration slope, and relays the recent 6-bar factor return onto names with a sign given by whether tail-volume concentration is above or below its own trailing norm — continuation when a programme is demonstrably trading the axis, reversal when it is not. It is falsifiable: if replacing the tanh(z) tail-concentration gate by a fixed constant (+1 or -1) reproduces the IC, or if the gate's slope is statistically zero, the execution-footprint mechanism is wrong and this is repackaged characteristic momentum. The edge persists because it needs real-time point-in-time loadings, per-bar cross-sectional estimation of both a return and a volume-shape moment, and high turnover on a capacity-limited execution footprint rather than a mispricing anyone can hold.

programs.code:
"""Vacuum-concordant semivariance gate on peer-comparable displacement.

Mechanism
---------
A peer-relative displacement tells you the size and the sign of a possible
mispricing but not whether it was produced by information (continuation) or by
mechanical price impact from a fee-insensitive liquidator (fast reversion).  The
discriminator is microstructural and is dated to the last two minutes: a fresh
one-sided (down vs up) realised-semivariance innovation whose *direction agrees
with the displacement*, produced on abnormally little participation (high
variance-burst per unit volume-burst = thin-book vacuum), is impact, and its
relaxation is front-loaded into the next minute.  The child therefore trades the
negated, vol-standardised peer displacement multiplied by (a) a reversion-onset
velocity gate, (b) a semivariance-asymmetry concordance gate, and (c) a vacuum
weight, and finally demeans the composite inside leverage-tercile x size-half
buckets so the slow Merton / Christie structural component of semivariance
asymmetry cannot masquerade as a dislocation.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows, positive lags, or contemporaneous
cross-sectional operations, so the value at bar t uses only information at <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index,
                   sector: pd.DataFrame | None,
                   industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _safe_log_pos(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    x = df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    x = x.where(x > 0.0)
    return np.log(x)


def _blend_log_multiples(data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
                         idx: pd.Index,
                         cols: pd.Index,
                         fields: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Average of available log valuation multiples (point-in-time step fields)."""
    num = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    for field in fields:
        raw = data.get(field)
        if raw is None:
            continue
        ser = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        lm = _safe_log_pos(ser)
        good = lm.notna()
        if good.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            continue
        num = num.add(lm.fillna(0.0))
        den = den.add(good.astype(float))
    den = den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return num / den


def _within_group_tercile(vs: pd.DataFrame, sec_arr: np.ndarray, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-coarse-group bucket (0..k-1) of a slow valuation coordinate."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vs.index, columns=vs.columns)
    for code in np.unique(sec_arr):
        sel = vs.columns[sec_arr == code]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        sub = vs[sel]
        r = sub.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        b = np.ceil(r * float(k)) - 1.0
        out[sel] = b.clip(0.0, float(k - 1))
    return out


def _group_median_count(vals: pd.DataFrame,
                        codes: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-group median and live count, broadcast back to members."""
    V = vals.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    C = codes.reindex_like(vals).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    med = np.full(V.shape, np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros(V.shape)
    finite_codes = C[np.isfinite(C)]
    uniq = np.unique(finite_codes) if finite_codes.size else np.array([])
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for c in uniq:
            mask = C == c
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            sub = np.where(mask, V, np.nan)
            gm = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1)
            gc = np.isfinite(sub).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            med[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gm[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
            cnt[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gc[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    return med_df, cnt_df


def _semivariances(ret: pd.DataFrame, n: int, minp: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing realised down / up semivariances (Barndorff-Nielsen et al.)."""
    down = ret.clip(upper=0.0) ** 2
    up = ret.clip(lower=0.0) ** 2
    return (down.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum(),
            up.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum())


def _asymmetry(rs_minus: pd.DataFrame, rs_plus: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    total = (rs_minus + rs_plus).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (rs_minus - rs_plus) / total


def _bin_ranks(r: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map a cross-sectional percentile rank frame to integer bins 0..k-1."""
    a = r.fillna(0.5).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    b = np.floor(a * float(k))
    b = np.clip(b, 0.0, float(k - 1))
    return b.astype(np.int64)


def _group_demean(y: pd.DataFrame, lab: np.ndarray, n_groups: int,
                  min_count: int = 5) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional demeaning inside integer groups (contemporaneous)."""
    ya = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(ya)
    cnt_all = valid.sum(axis=1)
    sum_all = np.where(valid, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    gmean = np.where(cnt_all > 0, sum_all / np.maximum(cnt_all, 1), np.nan)
    resid = np.full_like(ya, np.nan)
    for g in range(n_groups):
        m = valid & (lab == g)
        c = m.sum(axis=1)
        s = np.where(m, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mu = np.where(c >= min_count, s / np.maximum(c, 1), gmean)
        resid = np.where(m, ya - mu[:, None], resid)
    return pd.DataFrame(resid, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)


def _expit_df(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = special.expit(df.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)


@register_factor
class VacuumConcordantSemivarPeerDisplacement(BaseFactor):
    """Peer displacement traded only when a vacuum-made one-sided burst made it."""

    factor_id = "vacuum_concordant_semivar_peer_displacement"
    name = "Vacuum-concordant semivariance-gated peer displacement"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Negated vol-standardised displacement of log price from its sector x "
        "valuation-tercile peer median and its own 60-bar anchor, gated by 3-bar "
        "reversion-onset velocity, by sign concordance with the 12-vs-120-bar "
        "realised semivariance asymmetry innovation, and by the rank of variance "
        "burst per unit volume burst; demeaned in leverage x size buckets."
    )
    window_length = 360
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "industry",
        "pbRatio",
        "psRatio",
        "debtToAssets",
        "marketCap",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 3
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _ANCHOR_HL = 60.0
    _VAL_HL = 600.0
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _VEL_LAG = 3
    _ONSET_SLOPE = 1.5
    _CONC_SLOPE = 1.0
    _FAST = 12
    _FAST_MIN = 8
    _SLOW = 120
    _SLOW_MIN = 60

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero

        # ---- coarse and fine valuation-comparable peer groups -----------------
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"))
        uniq_lab = list(pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()))
        code_map = {lab: float(i) for i, lab in enumerate(uniq_lab)}
        sec_arr = np.array([code_map[labels[c]] for c in cols], dtype=float)
        sec_frame = pd.DataFrame(
            np.repeat(sec_arr[None, :], len(idx), axis=0), index=idx, columns=cols
        )

        val = _blend_log_multiples(data, idx, cols, ["pbRatio", "psRatio"])
        if val.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            ter = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vs = val.ewm(halflife=self._VAL_HL, min_periods=1, adjust=False).mean()
            ter = _within_group_tercile(vs, sec_arr, self._K)

        codes_fine = sec_frame * 10.0 + ter.fillna(9.0)
        med_f, cnt_f = _group_median_count(p, codes_fine)
        med_c, cnt_c = _group_median_count(p, sec_frame)
        fine_ok = cnt_f.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS)
        med = med_f.where(fine_ok, med_c)
        cnt = cnt_f.where(fine_ok, cnt_c)

        q = (p - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))

        # ---- displacement from own peer-relative anchor -----------------------
        anchor = q.ewm(halflife=self._ANCHOR_HL, min_periods=20, adjust=False).mean()
        dis = q - anchor
        sd = dis.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (dis / sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # ---- reversion-onset velocity gate -----------------------------------
        vel = z - z.shift(self._VEL_LAG)
        sv = vel.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        conv = ((-np.sign(z)) * vel) / sv
        conv = conv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        onset = _expit_df((self._ONSET_SLOPE * conv).fillna(0.0))

        # ---- fresh one-sided semivariance innovation --------------------------
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rsm_s, rsp_s = _semivariances(ret, self._FAST, self._FAST_MIN)
        rsm_l, rsp_l = _semivariances(ret, self._SLOW, self._SLOW_MIN)
        asym_s = _asymmetry(rsm_s, rsp_s)
        asym_l = _asymmetry(rsm_l, rsp_l)
        sa = (asym_s - asym_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sa_sd = sa.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sa_z = (sa / sa_sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # concordance: displacement direction agrees with the one-sided burst
        conc = ((-np.sign(z)) * sa_z).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        conc_gate = _expit_df((self._CONC_SLOPE * conc).fillna(0.0))

        # ---- thin-book vacuum weight: variance burst per unit volume burst ----
        rv_s = (rsm_s + rsp_s) / float(self._FAST)
        rv_l = ((rsm_l + rsp_l) / float(self._SLOW)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        var_burst = (rv_s / rv_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 25.0)

        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            thin = pd.DataFrame(0.5, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            v = v.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            v_s = v.rolling(self._FAST, min_periods=self._FAST_MIN).mean()
            v_l = v.rolling(self._SLOW, min_periods=self._SLOW_MIN).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
            part = (v_s / v_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            impact = var_burst / part.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            impact = impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(1e-9, 1e9)
            thin = rank(np.log(impact)).fillna(0.5)
        vac_w = 0.25 + thin  # in [0.25, 1.25]

        # ---- composite -------------------------------------------------------
        raw = -(z * onset * conc_gate * vac_w)
        raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(z) & np.isfinite(raw))

        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())

        # ---- structural (leverage x size) conditioning ------------------------
        d2a = data.get("debtToAssets")
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if d2a is None:
            lev_bin = np.zeros(sig.shape, dtype=np.int64)
        else:
            d = d2a.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            d = d.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-2.0, 5.0)
            lev_bin = _bin_ranks(rank(d), 3)
        if mcap is None:
            size_bin = np.zeros(sig.shape, dtype=np.int64)
        else:
            m = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            m = m.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            size_bin = _bin_ranks(rank(m.where(m > 0.0)), 2)
        lab = lev_bin * 2 + size_bin

        resid = _group_demean(sig, lab, 6, 5)
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        out = resid.sub(resid.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Parent B knows *where* a name is relative to its valuation-comparable peers but not *how* it got there, which is why its edge only matures at 12-24 bars; Parent A knows that a fresh one-sided variance burst produced on abnormally little volume (high variance-per-participation, a thin-book vacuum) is mechanical inventory/impact and snaps back inside a minute, but it throws away the direction and the relative-value anchor. The child trades the negated peer-relative displacement only when that displacement is *directionally concordant* with a fresh 12-bar downside-vs-upside semivariance innovation created in a vacuum: a name pushed below its peer anchor by a downside-heavy variance burst that no volume justifies is a liquidator's footprint, so its relaxation is front-loaded and lands at the fixed 6-bar offset, whereas the same displacement accompanied by commensurate volume is news and is left alone. The interaction is the edge: displacement supplies the size and sign of the mispricing (A cannot), while the vacuum/asymmetry concordance supplies the clock that tells you the relaxation is happening now rather than over the next four minutes (B cannot); the composite is demeaned within leverage-tercile x size-half buckets so the slow Merton/Christie structural part of semivariance asymmetry is not mistaken for a dislocation.

programs.code:
"""Semivariance-sourced, vacuum-gated peer displacement snapback.

Mechanism
---------
Two complementary states are combined.  (1) A peer-relative displacement from a
leverage-matched sector basket gives a *signed, sized* relative-value target but
says nothing about whether the push that created it has ended.  (2) A fresh
12-bar realised-semivariance asymmetry innovation, measured against the name's
own 120-bar asymmetry and demeaned inside sector x leverage buckets (so the
Merton / Christie structural part is removed), is an event dated to the last two
minutes, and the ratio of its variance burst to its volume burst says whether
the displacement was manufactured mechanically in a thin book or by informed
flow.

The child fades the displacement only when the *side* of the fresh one-sided
variance burst matches the side of the displacement (down-heavy variance under a
below-peer price, up-heavy variance above it) -- i.e. the burst plausibly
*sourced* the gap -- and only when that burst came with little participation.
This attributes the gap to transient impact and stamps it with a recent event
date, so the front-loaded relaxation falls inside a 6-bar (60 second) window.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows or contemporaneous cross-sectional
operations; the value at bar t uses only information available at or before t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None, industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker (sector preferred, else industry)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[0]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _within_group_tercile(vs: pd.DataFrame, sec_arr: np.ndarray, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-coarse-group bucket (0..k-1) of a slow conditioning coordinate."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vs.index, columns=vs.columns)
    for code in np.unique(sec_arr):
        sel = vs.columns[sec_arr == code]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        r = vs[sel].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        b = np.ceil(r * float(k)) - 1.0
        out[sel] = b.clip(0.0, float(k - 1))
    return out

def _group_median_count(vals: pd.DataFrame, codes: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-group median and live count, broadcast back to members."""
    V = vals.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    C = codes.reindex_like(vals).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    med = np.full(V.shape, np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros(V.shape)
    fin = C[np.isfinite(C)]
    uniq = np.unique(fin) if fin.size else np.array([])
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for c in uniq:
            mask = C == c
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            sub = np.where(mask, V, np.nan)
            gm = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1)
            gc = np.isfinite(sub).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            med[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gm[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
            cnt[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gc[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
    return (pd.DataFrame(med, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns), pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns))

def _group_demean_codes(y: pd.DataFrame, codes: pd.DataFrame, min_count: int=5) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Contemporaneous cross-sectional demeaning of y inside code groups.

    Removes the conditional level of y given (sector, leverage tercile) without
    assuming linearity; thin groups fall back to that bar's global mean.
    """
    ya = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    ca = codes.reindex_like(y).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(ya)
    cnt_all = valid.sum(axis=1)
    sum_all = np.where(valid, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    gmean = np.where(cnt_all > 0, sum_all / np.maximum(cnt_all, 1), np.nan)
    resid = np.full(ya.shape, np.nan)
    fin = ca[np.isfinite(ca)]
    uniq = np.unique(fin) if fin.size else np.array([])
    for c in uniq:
        m = valid & (ca == c)
        if not m.any():
            continue
        cn = m.sum(axis=1)
        s = np.where(m, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mu = np.where(cn >= min_count, s / np.maximum(cn, 1), gmean)
        resid = np.where(m, ya - mu[:, None], resid)
    return pd.DataFrame(resid, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)

def _semivariances(ret: pd.DataFrame, n: int, minp: int) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Trailing realised down / up semivariances (Barndorff-Nielsen et al.)."""
    down = ret.clip(upper=0.0) ** 2
    up = ret.clip(lower=0.0) ** 2
    return (down.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum(), up.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum())

def _asymmetry(rs_minus: pd.DataFrame, rs_plus: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    total = (rs_minus + rs_plus).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (rs_minus - rs_plus) / total

def _expit_df(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = special.expit(df.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)

@register_factor
class SemivarSourcedVacuumGatedPeerDisplacementSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade a peer displacement only when a fresh thin-book one-sided variance
    burst of the matching side plausibly created it."""
    factor_id = 'semivar_sourced_vacuum_gated_peer_displacement_s'
    name = 'Semivariance-sourced vacuum-gated peer displacement snapback'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Negated, vol-standardised displacement of log price from a sector x leverage-tercile peer median (fast 15-bar anchor), gated by sign alignment with a bucket-demeaned 12-vs-120-bar semivariance asymmetry innovation and by the cross-sectional rank of variance-burst per unit volume-burst.'
    window_length = 360
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector', 'industry', 'debtToAssets', 'financialLeverage']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 3
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _ANCHOR_HL = 15.0
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _FAST = 12
    _FAST_MIN = 8
    _SLOW = 120
    _SLOW_MIN = 60
    _ALIGN_SLOPE = 2.5

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        uniq_lab = list(pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()))
        code_map = {lab: float(i) for i, lab in enumerate(uniq_lab)}
        sec_arr = np.array([code_map[labels[c]] for c in cols], dtype=float)
        sec_frame = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(sec_arr[None, :], len(idx), axis=0), index=idx, columns=cols)
        d2a = data.get('debtToAssets')
        flev = data.get('financialLeverage')
        if d2a is None:
            d2a = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            d2a = d2a.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        if flev is None:
            flev = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            flev = flev.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        d2a = d2a.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-2.0, 5.0)
        flev = flev.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-50.0, 50.0)
        lev_score = 0.5 * (rank(d2a).fillna(0.5) + rank(flev).fillna(0.5))
        ter = _within_group_tercile(lev_score, sec_arr, self._K)
        codes_fine = sec_frame * 10.0 + ter.fillna(9.0)
        codes_coarse = sec_frame
        med_f, cnt_f = _group_median_count(p, codes_fine)
        med_c, cnt_c = _group_median_count(p, codes_coarse)
        fine_ok = cnt_f.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS)
        med = med_f.where(fine_ok, med_c)
        cnt = cnt_f.where(fine_ok, cnt_c)
        q = (p - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        anchor = q.ewm(halflife=self._ANCHOR_HL, min_periods=10, adjust=False).mean()
        dis = q - anchor
        sd = dis.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (dis / sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rsm_s, rsp_s = _semivariances(ret, self._FAST, self._FAST_MIN)
        rsm_l, rsp_l = _semivariances(ret, self._SLOW, self._SLOW_MIN)
        asym_s = _asymmetry(rsm_s, rsp_s)
        asym_l = _asymmetry(rsm_l, rsp_l)
        rv_s = (rsm_s + rsp_s) / float(self._FAST)
        rv_l = ((rsm_l + rsp_l) / float(self._SLOW)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        var_burst = (rv_s / rv_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 25.0)
        innov = (asym_s - asym_l) * np.sqrt(var_burst)
        innov = innov.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        resid = _group_demean_codes(innov, codes_fine, 5)
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rz = 2.0 * (rank(resid) - 0.5)
        align_raw = -np.sign(z.fillna(0.0)) * rz
        align_raw = align_raw.where(np.isfinite(align_raw), 0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        gate_align = _expit_df(self._ALIGN_SLOPE * align_raw)
        vol = data.get('volume')
        if vol is None:
            gate_vac = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            v = v.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            v_s = v.rolling(self._FAST, min_periods=self._FAST_MIN).sum() / float(self._FAST)
            v_l = (v.rolling(self._SLOW, min_periods=self._SLOW_MIN).sum() / float(self._SLOW)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            participation = (v_s / v_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            impact = var_burst / participation.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            impact = impact.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(1e-09, 1000000000.0)
            thin = rank(np.log(impact)).fillna(0.5)
            gate_vac = 0.25 + thin
        signal = -(z * gate_align * gate_vac)
        signal = signal.where(z.notna() & resid.notna() & gate_vac.notna())
        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

The child trades the negated peer displacement only when that displacement is *sourced* by a fresh, structurally-unexplained semivariance burst of the matching side (down-heavy variance under a below-peer price, up-heavy above) and when that burst was produced on little volume (high variance-per-unit-participation, i.e. mechanical inventory/impact rather than news). The interaction is the edge: sign-alignment converts A's unsigned asymmetry event into an attribution of B's displacement to transient impact, and it stamps B's slow level with a two-minute-old event date, so the front-loaded Bouchaud relaxation lands inside the fixed 6-bar window rather than 24; conversely, displacements accompanied by two-sided variance with commensurate volume are informed and are down-weighted instead of faded.

programs.code:
"""Anharmonic Langevin drift: idiosyncratic restoring force from a rolling
Kramers-Moyal regression, shrunk toward the cross-sectional consensus curve.

Mechanism
---------
Let z_t be a name's displacement from its own slow (EWMA) anchor, standardized by
its trailing displacement volatility.  Model the dynamics as an overdamped
Langevin equation

    dz = -U'(z) dt + sqrt(2D) dW,

so the conditional forward drift is the first Kramers-Moyal coefficient -U'(z).
Expanding it in the (near-orthogonal, for Gaussian z) Hermite basis

    mu(z) = a * z + b * (z^3 - 3 z)

gives a harmonic restoring coefficient a and an anharmonic coefficient b:
a < 0 is a single well (liquidity providers restore price -> reversion),
a > 0 with b < 0 is a locally unstable barrier (the price escapes the centre and
is only caught in the tails -> continuation near the centre, reversion far out).

The coefficients are estimated per name by a trailing OLS of realized 6-bar log
returns on the basis evaluated 6 bars earlier (strictly causal: at t the window
only contains pairs whose target already completed by t).  Because a single
global short-horizon reversal prior is what everyone already trades, the
tradable object here is the *deviation* of each name's fitted drift curve from
the contemporaneous cross-sectional consensus curve, with empirical-Bayes
(precision-weighted) shrinkage of each deviation toward zero.  Finally the drift
is damped when the current activity (volume) energy far exceeds the estimation
window's norm, since a particle with anomalous energy is no longer described by
the fitted potential.

All statistics are trailing / positive-lag only; cross-sectional operations act
within a single timestamp.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rs(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing rolling sum (NaNs already replaced by zeros by the caller)."""
    return df.rolling(n, min_periods=1).sum()


def _rolling_ols2(
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    x1: pd.DataFrame,
    x2: pd.DataFrame,
    n: int,
    min_obs: int,
    overlap: int,
):
    """Causal rolling two-regressor OLS (with intercept) via rolling moments.

    Returns (a, b, var_a, var_b) where a, b are the slopes on x1, x2.  The
    residual variance is inflated by `overlap` as a crude correction for the
    overlapping-target autocorrelation, so the empirical-Bayes precisions are
    not overstated.
    """
    valid = y.notna() & x1.notna() & x2.notna()
    Y = y.where(valid, 0.0)
    X1 = x1.where(valid, 0.0)
    X2 = x2.where(valid, 0.0)

    cnt = _rs(valid.astype(float), n)
    nz = cnt.where(cnt > 0.0)

    S1 = _rs(X1, n)
    S2 = _rs(X2, n)
    Sy = _rs(Y, n)

    m11 = _rs(X1 * X1, n) - S1 * S1 / nz
    m22 = _rs(X2 * X2, n) - S2 * S2 / nz
    m12 = _rs(X1 * X2, n) - S1 * S2 / nz
    m1y = _rs(X1 * Y, n) - S1 * Sy / nz
    m2y = _rs(X2 * Y, n) - S2 * Sy / nz
    myy = _rs(Y * Y, n) - Sy * Sy / nz

    det = m11 * m22 - m12 * m12
    ok = (cnt >= float(min_obs)) & (det > 0.0) & (m11 > 0.0) & (m22 > 0.0)
    detf = det.where(ok)

    a = (m22 * m1y - m12 * m2y) / detf
    b = (m11 * m2y - m12 * m1y) / detf

    rss = (myy - (a * m1y + b * m2y)).clip(lower=0.0)
    dof = (cnt - 3.0).clip(lower=1.0)
    s2 = float(overlap) * rss / dof

    var_a = (s2 * m22 / detf).clip(lower=1e-24)
    var_b = (s2 * m11 / detf).clip(lower=1e-24)

    return a.where(ok), b.where(ok), var_a.where(ok), var_b.where(ok)


def _eb_dev(coef: pd.DataFrame, var: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Precision-weighted deviation of each name's coefficient from the
    per-bar cross-sectional mean (empirical Bayes / James-Stein shrinkage)."""
    c = coef.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = var.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    v = np.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v > 0.0), v, np.nan)
    c = np.where(np.isfinite(c) & np.isfinite(v), c, np.nan)

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        cnt = np.sum(np.isfinite(c), axis=1)
        mu = np.nanmean(c, axis=1)
        vcs = np.nanvar(c, axis=1, ddof=1)
        mv = np.nanmean(v, axis=1)
        tau2 = np.clip(vcs - mv, 0.0, None)          # true dispersion of coefs
        lam = tau2[:, None] / (tau2[:, None] + v)     # shrinkage weight in [0,1]
        dev = lam * (c - mu[:, None])
        dev = np.where(cnt[:, None] >= int(min_names), dev, np.nan)

    return pd.DataFrame(dev, index=coef.index, columns=coef.columns)


@register_factor
class AnharmonicLangevinIdioRestoringForceDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Predicted idiosyncratic Langevin drift at the current displacement."""

    factor_id = 'anharmonic_langevin_idio_restoring_force_drift'
    name = 'Anharmonic Langevin drift (idiosyncratic restoring force)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Rolling causal OLS of 6-bar log returns on the lagged Hermite basis (z, z^3-3z) of each '
        'name\u2019s standardized deviation from its own EWMA anchor; the empirical-Bayes-shrunk '
        'deviations of the fitted harmonic / anharmonic coefficients from the cross-sectional '
        'consensus are re-evaluated at the current z to give a predicted idiosyncratic drift, '
        'damped when current volume energy exceeds the estimation-window norm, then ranked.'
    )
    window_length = 1100
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6              # forecast / target horizon in bars
    _HL = 30.0          # EWMA anchor halflife (bars)
    _HL_MIN = 60        # min observations before the anchor is usable
    _Z_WIN = 300        # window for displacement volatility
    _Z_MIN = 120
    _N = 720            # regression window (~2 hours of 10s bars)
    _MIN_OBS = 300      # min usable pairs in the regression window
    _MIN_NAMES = 5      # min cross-sectional names for the EB prior

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)

        # --- slow anchor and standardized displacement (dimensionless z) -------
        ema = lp.ewm(halflife=self._HL, min_periods=self._HL_MIN).mean()
        dev = lp - ema
        sd = dev.rolling(self._Z_WIN, min_periods=self._Z_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (dev / sd)
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        h3 = z ** 3 - 3.0 * z                     # third Hermite polynomial

        h = int(self._H)

        # --- Kramers-Moyal drift regression: r_{t-h->t} ~ a z_{t-h} + b h3_{t-h}
        y = lp - lp.shift(h)
        y = y.where(np.isfinite(y))
        a, b, var_a, var_b = _rolling_ols2(
            y, z.shift(h), h3.shift(h), self._N, self._MIN_OBS, h
        )

        # --- empirical-Bayes deviations from the consensus drift curve ----------
        da = _eb_dev(a, var_a, self._MIN_NAMES)
        db = _eb_dev(b, var_b, self._MIN_NAMES)

        raw = da * z + db * h3
        raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw))

        # --- energy damping: fitted potential is off-calibration when the
        #     current activity level far exceeds the estimation-window norm ------
        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is not None:
            vol = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0))
            v_short = vol.rolling(h, min_periods=h).mean()
            v_long = vol.rolling(self._N, min_periods=self._MIN_OBS).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
            energy = v_short / v_long
            w = 1.0 / (1.0 + (energy - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0))
            w = w.where(np.isfinite(w)).fillna(1.0).clip(0.2, 1.0)
            raw = raw * w
            raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw))

        out = rank(raw) - 0.5
        out = out.where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Anharmonic Langevin drift (idiosyncratic restoring force)
programs.trading_idea: Treat each name's standardized displacement z from its own slow anchor as a particle in a potential U(z): the conditional 6-bar drift is the Kramers-Moyal first coefficient -U'(z), which I estimate per name by a trailing OLS of realized 6-bar log returns on the Hermite basis {z, z^3-3z} evaluated 6 bars earlier — so the *sign and curvature* of the local drift are learned from that name's own dynamics rather than imposed (a<0 = single restoring well, a>0 with b<0 = locally unstable barrier that lets the price escape before being caught in the tails). The tradable object is the precision-weighted *deviation* of each name's fitted drift curve from the contemporaneous cross-sectional consensus curve (empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the pooled coefficients), i.e. how much faster or slower this book's liquidity providers restore price than the average book at the same displacement; the signal is that idiosyncratic drift function evaluated at the current z, damped when the current activity level (volume energy) is far above the estimation window's norm and the fitted potential is therefore off-calibration. The edge should persist because everyone applies a single, homogeneous short-horizon reversal prior, whereas the heterogeneity and anharmonicity of per-name resiliency is a second-order slope difference that requires noisy nonlinear conditional-mean estimation per name, is worth only a fraction of the spread per trade, and is therefore capacity-limited rather than arbitraged. It is falsified if the shrunk coefficient deviations carry no forward information (IC ~ 0), or if the anharmonic term adds nothing over the linear one, meaning the potential is universally harmonic and the factor collapses to plain reversal (which would also show up as redundancy with the book).
programs.description: Rolling two-regressor causal OLS of 6-bar log returns on the lagged Hermite basis (z, z^3-3z) of each name's standardized deviation from its own EWMA anchor; the empirical-Bayes-shrunk deviations of the fitted coefficients from the cross-sectional consensus are re-evaluated at the current z to give a predicted idiosyncratic drift, activity-damped and cross-sectionally ranked.
