"""Volume-at-price shelf occupancy decides whether dealer inventory pressure
reverts or extends over the next 60 seconds.

Mechanism
---------
1. Inventory state (from the dealer-inventory parent).  Tick-rule signed volume,
   ADV-normalised and cross-sectionally demeaned, is accumulated with an
   exponential memory kernel:  Q_t = sum_j kappa^j f_{t-j}.  A trailing OLS of
   the same-kernel cumulative idio return on Q gives an impact elasticity
   lambda (return per ADV unit of accumulated net flow), shrunk toward the
   cross-sectional median.  D_t = lambda_i * Q_t is the flow-implied
   displacement currently embedded in the mid, in return units.

2. Local liquidity state (from the local-time / recurrence parent, upgraded from
   a pure occupancy count to a *volume*-at-price occupancy).  With bandwidth
   eps_t = 1.5 * same-window one-bar sigma,

       share_t = sum_{k=1..N} v_{t-k} 1{|log p_{t-k} - log p_t| <= eps_t}
                 / sum_{k=1..N} v_{t-k}

   is the fraction of the last N bars' traded volume that printed within one
   band of where the mid stands *now* — a scale-free market-profile measure of
   how much real two-sided size exists at the current level.  Its own trailing
   z-score (with a small positive neutral point, encoding the prior that impact
   is transient more often than permanent) is passed through tanh to give a
   signed state s_t in (-1, 1).

3. The interaction.  On a heavy shelf (s > 0) a liquidity provider can shed the
   inventory into standing size with almost no quote skew, so the displacement
   is predominantly *permanent* (a queue is being consumed by a metaorder) and
   it extends.  In a volume vacuum (s < 0) the same absorbed flow required a
   large quote skew, so the displacement is predominantly *transitory* dealer
   inventory overshoot and it snaps back as counterparty volume arrives — which
   is why the trade-clock clearing fraction  clear = Vhat / (Vhat + |Q|)  is
   retained as a saturating magnitude damper (reversion needs volume, not
   calendar time).

       signal = lambda_i * Q_t * clear_t * tanh(z(share_t) - offset)

   Positive signal => higher forward 6-bar return.  Because the state variable
   is centred in the name's own time, the average loading on the plain
   inventory-reversal term is small: the factor lives in the interaction and is
   therefore not spanned by either parent.  Every statistic is a trailing
   rolling moment, a causal exponential recursion or a positive lag, so the
   value at bar t uses only data <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _ew_sum(df: pd.DataFrame, halflife: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal exponentially-weighted *sum* sum_j kappa^j x_{t-j} (a 'stock')."""
    kappa = 0.5 ** (1.0 / float(halflife))
    alpha = 1.0 - kappa
    return df.ewm(halflife=float(halflife), adjust=False, min_periods=1).mean() / alpha


def _volume_at_price_share(
    lp: pd.DataFrame, vol: pd.DataFrame, eps: pd.DataFrame, n: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Share of the last n bars' volume that printed within eps of the current log price.

    Causal: only strictly positive lags of ``lp`` / ``vol`` are compared with the
    current row.  NaN comparisons evaluate to False and contribute zero volume;
    rows without a full window are masked out.
    """
    num = None
    for k in range(1, int(n) + 1):
        hit = (lp - lp.shift(k)).abs().le(eps)
        contrib = vol.shift(k).where(hit, 0.0)
        num = contrib if num is None else num + contrib
    den = ts_sum(vol, int(n)).shift(1)
    den = den.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    share = num / den
    ok = lp.notna() & eps.notna() & lp.shift(int(n)).notna()
    return share.where(ok)


@register_factor
class ShelfOccupancyGatedInventoryPermanenceSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Flow-implied displacement: extends on a volume shelf, reverts in a vacuum."""

    factor_id = "shelf_occupancy_gated_inventory_permanence_split"
    name = "Shelf-occupancy gated inventory permanence split"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Shrunk trailing impact elasticity times exponentially accumulated tick-rule "
        "signed flow, damped by a saturating 6-bar volume clearing fraction and "
        "multiplied by a tanh switch on the trailing z-score of the share of recent "
        "traded volume printed within 1.5 window-sigma of the current mid."
    )
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ["open", "close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _HL = 18.0    # inventory memory half-life in bars (~3 minutes)
    _ADV = 360    # ~1h volume normaliser
    _BETA = 480   # impact-elasticity estimation window
    _VSH = 30     # short volume window used to forecast the next 60 seconds
    _H = 6        # pinned forecast offset in bars
    _N = 90       # volume-at-price occupancy window (15 minutes)
    _BAND = 1.5   # occupancy bandwidth in units of same-window one-bar sigma
    _ZWIN = 240   # window normalising occupancy against the name's own norm
    _OFF = 0.4    # neutral point of the permanence switch (transient-impact prior)

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float)
        vol = data["volume"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        opx = open_.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        opx = opx.where(opx > 0.0)

        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # --- winsorise returns at 4 trailing sigma (jumps must not drive lambda) ---
        sd = r.rolling(240, min_periods=60).std()
        limv = (4.0 * sd).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        limv = np.where(np.isfinite(limv) & (limv > 0.0), limv, np.inf)
        r = pd.DataFrame(
            np.clip(r.to_numpy(dtype=float), -limv, limv), index=idx, columns=cols
        )

        v = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        v = v.where(v > 0.0, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---------------- 1. inventory state, in return units ------------------
        d1 = np.sign((px - opx).to_numpy(dtype=float))
        d2 = np.sign(px.diff().to_numpy(dtype=float))
        d = np.where(np.isfinite(d1) & (np.abs(d1) > 0.0), d1, d2)
        d = np.where(np.isfinite(d), d, 0.0)

        advol = adv(v, int(self._ADV)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        f = pd.DataFrame(d, index=idx, columns=cols) * v / advol
        f = f.clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        vn = (v / advol).clip(upper=5.0)

        fi = f.sub(f.mean(axis=1), axis=0).fillna(0.0)
        ri = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0).fillna(0.0)

        Q = _ew_sum(fi, self._HL)     # dealer inventory proxy, ADV units
        P = _ew_sum(ri, self._HL)     # same-kernel cumulative idio return

        beta = rolling_beta(P, Q, int(self._BETA))
        beta_p = beta.clip(lower=0.0)
        med = beta_p.median(axis=1)
        medv = med.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1)
        medf = pd.DataFrame(np.tile(medv, (1, len(cols))), index=idx, columns=cols)
        lam = 0.5 * beta_p.fillna(medf) + 0.5 * medf
        lam = lam.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---------------- 2. trade-clock clearing capacity --------------------
        vhat = float(self._H) * ts_mean(vn, int(self._VSH))
        clear = vhat / (vhat + Q.abs() + 1e-9)

        # ---------------- 3. volume-at-price shelf occupancy ------------------
        n = int(self._N)
        sig_w = r.rolling(n, min_periods=int(n * 3 // 4)).std()
        sig_w = sig_w.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eps = self._BAND * sig_w

        share = _volume_at_price_share(lp, v, eps, n)
        z = ts_zscore(share, int(self._ZWIN))
        z = z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        state = np.tanh(z - float(self._OFF))

        # ---------------- 4. permanence split --------------------------------
        raw = lam * Q * clear * state

        valid = (
            np.isfinite(lam.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(Q.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(clear.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(state.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(advol.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(raw.to_numpy(dtype=float))
        )
        sig = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(valid, raw.to_numpy(dtype=float), np.nan), index=idx, columns=cols
        )

        out = rank(sig) - 0.5
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Parent B shows that exponentially-accumulated signed flow, converted to return units by a trailing Kyle-lambda and damped by the volume that can clear it, is on average a transitory dealer-inventory overshoot that snaps back; Parent A shows (in its realized, sign-contradicted direction) that what happens next depends on whether the mid is sitting on a level the path has repeatedly revisited or in a recurrence vacuum. The child fuses them: I replace Parent A's pure local-time count with a volume-at-price *shelf occupancy* — the share of the last 90 bars' traded volume that printed within ~1.5 window-sigma of the current mid — and use its own trailing z-score to switch the sign of Parent B's flow-implied dislocation. On a heavy shelf the maker can offload inventory into standing two-sided size at almost no quote skew, so whatever displacement the flow produced is mostly *information* about a queue being consumed and it extends; in a volume vacuum the maker had to skew quotes hard to absorb the same flow, so the displacement is mostly *transitory* inventory overshoot and it reverts once counterparty volume arrives (hence Parent B's trade-clock saturation is retained as a magnitude damper). The interaction carries edge neither parent has alone: Parent B applies one unconditional reversion sign to permanent and transitory impact alike (which is why it is 68% redundant with the book), and Parent A gates a raw price move that contains no information about who pushed it or whether the pusher still holds inventory — only flow-implied displacement times local volume-at-price tells you whether an overshoot has a book to lean on.

"""GLS basket-projected precision dislocation split.

Mechanism
---------
Let x_t be vol-standardised 10-second log returns, agg_t the trailing 6-bar sum
of x, and Sigma the trailing covariance of x estimated strictly in the past.  The
precision-metric coordinate u_t = Sigma^{-1} agg_t up-weights motion along
historically low-variance eigen-directions (tight relative-value spreads inside
baskets).  Parent B traded -u unconditionally and its sign was contradicted: at a
10-second clock the pooled object is dominated by slow information diffusion
(Epps / staleness catch-up), which CONTINUES.  Only the weight-proportional,
basket-driven slice of u is mechanical liquidity demand that must relax.

So we split u using the capitalisation-weight vector w inside the SAME metric:

    a_t = (w' Sigma^{-1} agg_t) / (w' Sigma^{-1} w)          (GLS basket coordinate)
    basket displacement (return space) : a_t * w_i
    basket-orthogonal whitened residual: u_t - a_t * (Sigma^{-1} w)

The residual is additionally orthogonalised cross-sectionally against the plain
6-bar standardised move (Parent B's falsification design), so what survives lives
only in the precision metric and is not univariate reversal/momentum.

Trading rule (opposite signs for the two pieces):
  * basket-orthogonal residual  -> CONTINUATION, amplified when the name is
    mechanically fragile (rank(-log dollar turnover) - rank(beta) high, i.e. slow
    diffusion) and when the name is NOT currently receiving basket flow;
  * basket-attributed weight-proportional displacement -> REVERSAL, amplified by
    the name-level program footprint (its own contribution to the cross-sectional
    correlation between dollar-volume-share anomaly and the index-weight
    direction, scaled by the market-wide program regime) times the same
    elasticity wedge.

Causality: the precision matrix applied on bars [a, a+step) is estimated only
from rows [a-W, a); every other statistic is a trailing rolling window or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional operation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar Series across all tickers."""
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.reindex(index), dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)


def _xs_z(df: pd.DataFrame, clip: float = 4.0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional z-score, clipped."""
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sd = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-clip, clip)


def _shrunk_precision(x_win: np.ndarray, eig_floor: float, shrink: float):
    """Eigenvalue-floored, diagonally shrunk inverse covariance of a past window."""
    if x_win.ndim != 2:
        return None
    m, n = x_win.shape
    if m < 20 or n < 3:
        return None
    xw = np.nan_to_num(x_win, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    xc = xw - xw.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    cov = xc.T @ xc / float(max(m - 1, 1))
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(cov)):
        return None
    avg = float(np.mean(np.diag(cov)))
    if not np.isfinite(avg) or avg <= 1e-12:
        return None
    cov = (1.0 - shrink) * cov + shrink * avg * np.eye(n)
    cov = 0.5 * (cov + cov.T)
    try:
        w, v = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return None
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(w)) and np.all(np.isfinite(v))):
        return None
    mean_w = float(np.mean(w))
    if not np.isfinite(mean_w) or mean_w <= 1e-14:
        return None
    w = np.maximum(w, eig_floor * mean_w)
    prec = v / w @ v.T
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(prec)):
        return None
    return prec


@register_factor
class GlsBasketProjectedPrecisionDislocationSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Split the precision-whitened dislocation into basket-mechanical and idio parts."""

    factor_id = "gls_basket_projected_precision_dislocation_split"
    name = "GLS basket-projected precision dislocation split"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Precision-whitened 6-bar dislocation with the GLS index-weight basket "
        "coordinate projected out and traded as continuation (scaled by the "
        "impact-elasticity wedge and by one minus the name-level program "
        "footprint), minus the weight-proportional basket-attributed displacement "
        "traded as reversal where program footprint and elasticity wedge are high."
    )
    window_length = 640
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 6
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _COV_WIN = 360
    _REFIT = 60
    _SHRINK = 0.30
    _EIG_FLOOR = 0.20
    _L = 120
    _PN = 240
    _CONT = 1.0
    _FADE = 1.2
    _KW = 0.8

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        L = int(self._L)
        mp = max(20, L // 2)

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)

        vol = ret.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=int(self._VOL_WIN // 2)).std()
        vol = vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (ret / vol).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        agg = x.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum()
        valid_agg = agg.notna() & vol.notna()

        # ---- capitalisation weights (defensive: quarterly step function) ----
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
        med_cap = mcap.median(axis=1)
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).ffill()
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        cap = mcap.where(mcap.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_cap, idx, cols))
        cap_tot = cap.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        wgt = cap.div(cap_tot, axis=0)

        # ---- precision whitening + GLS basket coordinate (trailing, blockwise) ----
        xf = x.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        aggf = agg.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        wf = wgt.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        n_rows, n_cols = xf.shape

        u = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        hmat = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        gcoef = np.full(n_rows, np.nan, dtype=float)

        w_cov = int(self._COV_WIN)
        step = int(self._REFIT)
        a = max(w_cov, self._VOL_WIN + self._K)
        while a < n_rows:
            prec = _shrunk_precision(xf[a - w_cov:a, :], self._EIG_FLOOR, self._SHRINK)
            if prec is not None:
                end = min(a + step, n_rows)
                blk_agg = aggf[a:end, :]
                blk_w = wf[a:end, :]
                U = blk_agg @ prec
                H = blk_w @ prec                     # prec symmetric => Sigma^{-1} w
                den = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", blk_w, H)
                num = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", blk_agg, H)
                den_safe = np.where(np.abs(den) > 1e-14, den, np.nan)
                u[a:end, :] = U
                hmat[a:end, :] = H
                gcoef[a:end] = num / den_safe
            a += step

        ydf = pd.DataFrame(u, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hdf = pd.DataFrame(hmat, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gser = pd.Series(gcoef, index=idx).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # basket-orthogonal whitened residual
        ures = ydf.sub(hdf.mul(gser, axis=0))
        ures = ures.where(valid_agg)
        xdf = agg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid_agg)

        # cross-sectional orthogonalisation against the plain 6-bar move
        ym = ures.sub(ures.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        xm = xdf.sub(xdf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        denom = (xm * xm).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta_xs = (xm * ym).sum(axis=1) / denom
        res = ym.sub(xm.mul(beta_xs.fillna(0.0), axis=0))
        res = res.where(ures.notna() & xdf.notna())
        rz = _xs_z(res, 4.0)

        # ---- basket-attributed weight-proportional displacement ----
        g_sd = gser.rolling(self._PN, min_periods=60).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ghat = (gser / g_sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        gtan = pd.Series(np.tanh(ghat.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx)
        gtan = gtan.where(ghat.notna())
        wz = 2.0 * (rank(wgt) - 0.5)
        bterm = _row_broadcast(gtan, idx, cols) * wz
        bterm = bterm.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- market-wide return (cap-weighted) for beta ----
        w_av = wgt.where(ret.notna())
        wden = w_av.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mkt = (w_av * ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / wden
        mkt = mkt.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- dollar volume, shares, program footprint ----
        volu = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volu = volu.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dv = (close.abs() * volu).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        tot_dv = dv.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        share = dv.div(tot_dv, axis=0)
        share_bar = ts_mean(share, L)
        dev_share = share - share_bar
        dev_w = wgt - share_bar

        zs = _xs_z(dev_share, 5.0)
        zw = _xs_z(dev_w, 5.0)
        contrib = (zs * zw).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        contrib_s = contrib.rolling(self._K, min_periods=max(2, self._K // 2)).mean()
        foot_name = pd.DataFrame(
            np.tanh(contrib_s.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)),
            index=idx,
            columns=cols,
        )

        tilt = contrib.mean(axis=1)
        act = tot_dv / tot_dv.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        act = act.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.25, 6.0)
        P = tilt.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=3.0) * np.sqrt(act)
        P = P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        Ps = P.rolling(self._K, min_periods=max(2, self._K // 2)).mean()
        p_mu = Ps.rolling(self._PN, min_periods=60).mean()
        p_sd = Ps.rolling(self._PN, min_periods=60).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        Pz = ((Ps - p_mu) / p_sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        Pmkt = pd.Series(special.expit(Pz.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx)
        gate = (_row_broadcast(Pmkt, idx, cols) * foot_name).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- impact-elasticity wedge (fragility in excess of beta) ----
        advdv = adv(dv, L).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        turnover = (advdv / cap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        turnover = turnover.where(turnover > 0.0)
        kappa = -np.log(turnover)
        mkt_df = _row_broadcast(mkt.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret.fillna(0.0), mkt_df, L)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 5.0)
        wedge = (rank(kappa) - rank(beta)).where(kappa.notna() & beta.notna())
        wedge = wedge.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        elast = 1.0 + float(self._KW) * wedge.fillna(0.0)

        # ---- combine: idio continuation, basket-mechanical reversal ----
        cont = float(self._CONT) * rz * (1.0 - gate) * elast
        fade = float(self._FADE) * gate * elast * bterm.fillna(0.0)
        sig = cont - fade

        valid = rz.notna() & wedge.notna()
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
        sig = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

Parent A supplied the geometry that identifies that mechanical part (cap-weight direction, volume-share tilt toward it, and the impact-elasticity wedge rank(-log turnover) − rank(beta)) but used it only as a multiplicative scalar gate on the pooled dislocation. """Concordant permanence gate on a peer-relative break.

Mechanism
---------
Two independent liquidity read-outs are required to AGREE before the recent
peer-relative move is traded as continuation:

1. PATH GEOMETRY (local time).  rho_t = fraction of the last N bars whose log
   mid sat within one window-sigma of the CURRENT mid.  High rho (relative to
   the name's own trailing norm) means the mid is standing on / has just left a
   level it revisited many times - passive quoters re-post there, so the level
   was queued and defended.  Low rho means the price has walked into territory
   with no resting inventory (a local-time vacuum).

2. FLOW (impact purity).  purity = log( 6-bar realised-variance burst /
   6-bar participation burst ): price motion per unit of traded volume, i.e. an
   effective Kyle lambda relative to the name's own norm.  Low purity = the
   move was PAID FOR with volume and absorbed by depth.  High purity = the mid
   moved on air.

The empirical law (the realised direction of both parents, read with their
signs) is that VOLUME-BACKED breaks of well-visited levels are PERMANENT
repricings and continue over the next minute, while displacements produced in a
vacuum are transient impact / mid noise and snap back.  So both gates point the
same way: g = tanh(z(rho)) > 0 (defended level) and h = -centred rank(purity) >
0 (volume-backed) both mean "permanent".  The child asserts permanence only
when they concur:

    G = sign(g) * sqrt( max(g * h, 0) )

which is zero whenever the geometry and the flow disagree - exactly the
ambiguous states in which each parent alone was diluted - and largest when a
heavy-volume move has torn away from a repeatedly-revisited level.

A side-aligned, exponentially decayed flow intensity divided by its own 6-bar
peak scales the magnitude only (never the sign), so the bet is expressed while
the flow episode is still live: this is what pulls the edge onto the fixed
6-bar offset instead of the slower 24-bar decay of both parents.

All statistics are trailing rolling / EW windows, positive lags, or purely
contemporaneous cross-sectional operations: bar t uses only data <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, ts_max, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _recurrence_density(lp: pd.DataFrame, eps: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of the last n bars whose log price lies within eps of the current one.

    Causal: only positive lags of ``lp`` are compared against the current row.
    """
    cnt = None
    for k in range(1, int(n) + 1):
        hit = (lp - lp.shift(k)).abs().le(eps).astype(float)
        cnt = hit if cnt is None else cnt + hit
    rho = cnt / float(n)
    ok = lp.notna() & eps.notna() & lp.shift(int(n)).notna()
    return rho.where(ok)


def _codes(sec: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
    """Integer-code a (mostly static) text label frame using forward fill only."""
    s = sec.astype(object).ffill()
    arr = s.to_numpy()
    flat = pd.Series(arr.ravel(), dtype=object)
    flat = flat.where(flat.notna(), "UNK").astype(str)
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(flat, sort=True)
    return codes.reshape(arr.shape).astype(np.int64), int(len(uniq))


def _group_demean(y: pd.DataFrame, lab: np.ndarray, n_groups: int, min_count: int = 4) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional demeaning inside integer groups (contemporaneous)."""
    ya = y.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    valid = np.isfinite(ya)
    cnt_all = valid.sum(axis=1)
    sum_all = np.where(valid, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    gmean = np.where(cnt_all > 0, sum_all / np.maximum(cnt_all, 1), np.nan)
    out = np.full_like(ya, np.nan)
    for g in range(int(n_groups)):
        m = valid & (lab == g)
        if not m.any():
            continue
        c = m.sum(axis=1)
        s = np.where(m, ya, 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        mu = np.where(c >= min_count, s / np.maximum(c, 1), gmean)
        out = np.where(m, ya - mu[:, None], out)
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)


def _rank_mid(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank, missing pinned to the median."""
    return rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class LocalTimeBackedImpactConcordanceBreakRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Ride volume-backed breaks of defended levels; ignore vacuum displacements."""

    factor_id = "local_time_backed_impact_concordance_break_relay"
    name = "Concordant permanence gate on peer-relative break"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Centred cross-sectional rank of the sector-demeaned decay-weighted 6-bar "
        "vol-standardised move, multiplied by a sign-shared geometric-mean concordance gate "
        "of local-time recurrence density (z-scored per name) and minus-ranked impact purity, "
        "amplitude-scaled by side-aligned flow freshness versus its 6-bar peak."
    )
    window_length = 240
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 6        # displacement / burst horizon, matched to the forecast offset
    _N = 60       # local-time recurrence window (10 minutes of 10s bars)
    _ZWIN = 120   # per-name normalisation of the recurrence density
    _LONG = 60    # burst baselines
    _BAND = 1.0   # recurrence bandwidth in same-window one-bar sigmas

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)

        K = int(self._K)
        N = int(self._N)
        L = int(self._LONG)

        # ---- 1. peer-relative, freshness-weighted displacement ------------
        sd = ret.rolling(L, min_periods=L // 2).std()
        sd = sd.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (ret / sd).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        move = decay_linear(x, K).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sec = data.get("sector")
        if isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame):
            lab, n_sec = _codes(sec.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols))
        else:
            lab, n_sec = (np.zeros((len(idx), len(cols)), dtype=np.int64), 1)
        disloc = _group_demean(move, lab, max(n_sec, 1), 4)
        disloc = disloc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- 2. path-geometry gate: local-time recurrence density ---------
        sig_w = ret.rolling(N, min_periods=(N * 3) // 4).std()
        sig_w = sig_w.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rho = _recurrence_density(lp, self._BAND * sig_w, N)
        zr = ts_zscore(rho, int(self._ZWIN))
        zr = zr.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        g = np.tanh(zr)                       # +1 defended level, -1 local-time vacuum

        # ---- 3. flow gate: minus impact purity (volume-backed = +) --------
        r2 = ret ** 2
        rv_s = r2.rolling(K, min_periods=K).mean()
        rv_l = r2.rolling(L, min_periods=L // 2).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        var_burst = (rv_s / rv_l).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 25.0)

        v_s = vol.rolling(K, min_periods=K).mean()
        v_l = vol.rolling(L, min_periods=L // 2).mean()
        part = ((v_s + 1e-9) / (v_l + 1e-9)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(1e-6, 50.0)

        purity = np.log((var_burst + 1e-9) / part).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        h = -2.0 * (_rank_mid(purity) - 0.5)  # +1 volume-backed, -1 impact vacuum

        # ---- 4. concordance AND-gate --------------------------------------
        prod = (g * h).where(g.notna() & h.notna())
        gate = np.sign(g) * np.sqrt(prod.clip(lower=0.0))
        gate = gate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- 5. side-aligned flow freshness (amplitude only) -------------
        v0 = vol.fillna(0.0)
        lam_up = (v0 * ret.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)).ewm(halflife=2.0, min_periods=K).mean()
        lam_dn = (v0 * (-ret.clip(upper=0.0)).fillna(0.0)).ewm(halflife=2.0, min_periods=K).mean()
        lam = lam_dn.where(disloc < 0.0, lam_up)
        peak = ts_max(lam, K).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        fresh = (lam / peak).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
        weight = 0.4 + 0.6 * fresh

        # ---- 6. assemble: POSITIVE loading on permanence-confirmed breaks --
        s = (2.0 * (rank(disloc) - 0.5)).where(disloc.notna())
        out = s * gate * weight
        out = out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Concordant permanence gate on peer-relative break
programs.trading_idea: Read together, both parents' realized (negative) ICs state one law from opposite sides: a displacement produced in a liquidity vacuum — high price variance per unit of traded volume, price walking into rarely-visited territory — is mostly TRANSIENT impact on a thin book and gives back within a minute, while a displacement that cost real volume and had to break away from a level the mid has repeatedly revisited (a defended, well-queued price) is PERMANENT repricing by informed size and continues. The child therefore trades the peer-relative 6-bar break with a POSITIVE (continuation) loading gated by permanence, and the synthesis is an AND-gate over two structurally different liquidity proxies neither parent combines: a path-geometry proxy (scale-free local-time recurrence density of the mid at the level it now stands on, from A) and a flow proxy (impact purity = variance burst per unit participation burst, from B). Permanence is only asserted when the two concur — geometric-mean magnitude with the shared sign, zero when they disagree — so the signal is silent exactly in the ambiguous states where each parent alone was diluted, and a short side-aligned flow-freshness weight (halflife 2 bars, 6-bar peak) concentrates the bet on live episodes so the edge lands at the fixed 6-bar offset rather than at 24 bars.
programs.description: Cross-sectionally centred rank of the sector-demeaned, decay-weighted 6-bar vol-standardised move, multiplied by a concordance gate = sign-shared geometric mean of (i) tanh z-score of local-time recurrence density at the current mid and (ii) minus the centred rank of impact purity (variance burst per unit volume burst), scaled by side-aligned exponential flow freshness relative to its 6-bar peak.

programs.code:
"""Event-clock-matched peer-hedged dislocation, fixed 6-bar horizon.

Mechanism
---------
An idiosyncratic (industry-hedged) price dislocation is absorbed by liquidity
providers only while the hedge basket is tradable, so the *repair* of that
dislocation runs on the peer basket's event (volume) clock rather than on the
calendar clock.  A calendar-fixed impulse window therefore mismatches the
repair window whenever peer trading intensity departs from its own norm: the
same 6 calendar bars contain very different amounts of hedgeable peer flow.

The child fixes exactly that.  For every name and bar we forecast the peer flow
that will arrive over the next H = 6 bars from the trailing peer arrival rate,
and then pick the *backward* lookback L(t) that contains the same amount of peer
flow (L ~ H / speed, speed = short-run peer volume rate / long-run rate).  The
hedged dislocation is measured over that adaptive lookback, vol-standardised,
and its loading on the cross-sectionally demeaned realised 6-bar return is
estimated by a trailing pooled robust sign-slope inside cells of
(peer clock speed) x (own activity).  If the mechanism is wrong, the fitted
slope in the fast-clock cell will not be more negative than in the slow-clock
cell and the signal will carry no information at the fixed offset.

Causality: every cross-sectional statistic is taken inside one timestamp; every
time-series statistic is a trailing rolling window or positive lag; the fit
pairs target y_t (t-6 -> t) with regressors observed at t-6.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None,
                   industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker peer-group key: industry when present, else sector."""
    labels = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[0]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _refine_by_size(base: pd.Series, mcap: pd.DataFrame | None,
                    min_size: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Split each peer group into two static size buckets (valuation comparables).

    Uses each ticker's FIRST available market cap (backward-looking), so the
    grouping is a static label exactly like the sector/industry text fields.
    Groups that end up too small fall back to the unrefined label.
    """
    if mcap is None:
        return base
    firsts: dict[str, float] = {}
    for c in base.index:
        if c not in mcap.columns:
            continue
        ser = mcap[c].dropna()
        if len(ser) == 0:
            continue
        try:
            val = float(ser.iloc[0])
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if np.isfinite(val) and val > 0.0:
            firsts[c] = val
    if len(firsts) < 2 * min_size:
        return base
    vals = pd.Series(firsts, dtype=float)
    med = float(vals.median())
    ref = base.copy()
    for c in base.index:
        if c in vals.index:
            tag = "|B" if float(vals[c]) >= med else "|S"
            ref[c] = str(base[c]) + tag
    counts = ref.value_counts()
    for c in ref.index:
        if int(counts.get(ref[c], 0)) < min_size:
            ref[c] = base[c]
    return ref


def _group_excl_mean(a: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-group mean of ``a`` EXCLUDING the name itself (leave-one-out)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in a.columns]
        if not cols:
            continue
        sub = a[cols]
        present = sub.notna().to_numpy().astype(float)
        vals = sub.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        tot = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        cnt = present.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        excl_sum = tot - vals
        excl_cnt = cnt - present
        ok = excl_cnt >= float(min_peers)
        safe = np.where(excl_cnt > 0.0, excl_cnt, 1.0)
        res = np.where(ok, excl_sum / safe, np.nan)
        out[cols] = pd.DataFrame(res, index=a.index, columns=cols)
    return out


def _sign_slope(x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, win: int,
                minp: int, min_obs: float, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Trailing pooled robust slope  b = sum(sign(x) * y) / sum(|x|).

    Consistent for y = b*x under symmetric noise and far less tail-sensitive
    than a normal-equation solve at 10-second sampling.  Sums are taken across
    names inside a timestamp then accumulated over a trailing window, so the
    estimate at t uses only data <= t.
    """
    valid = mask & x.notna() & y.notna()
    xs = x.where(valid)
    ys = y.where(valid)
    num_row = (np.sign(xs) * ys).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).fillna(0.0)
    den_row = xs.abs().sum(axis=1, min_count=1).fillna(0.0)
    num = num_row.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    den = den_row.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    nobs = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float).rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    b = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    b = b.where(np.isfinite(b) & (nobs >= float(min_obs)))
    return b.clip(-cap, cap)


@register_factor
class PeerEventClockMatchedHedgeDislocation(BaseFactor):
    """Hedge-clock-matched reversal of the peer-idiosyncratic price dislocation."""

    factor_id = "peer_event_clock_matched_hedge_dislocation_h6"
    name = "Peer-event-clock-matched hedged dislocation (fixed 6-bar)"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Beta-hedged peer-relative price dislocation measured over an adaptive "
        "lookback whose accumulated leave-one-out peer volume matches the peer "
        "volume expected over the next 6 bars, loaded by a trailing pooled "
        "robust sign-slope fitted inside cells of peer clock speed x own activity."
    )
    window_length = 1200
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry", "sector", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6
    _MIN_PEERS = 3
    _MIN_GROUP = 4
    _FAST_WIN = 60
    _SLOW_WIN = 900
    _BETA_WIN = 360
    _SD_WIN = 360
    _SD_MIN = 120
    _FIT_WIN = 600
    _FIT_MIN = 200
    _MIN_OBS = 400.0
    _SHRINK = 0.6
    _CAP_B = 3.0
    _CANDS = (2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, 20, 30)

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zeros = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        H = self._H

        base_labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"))
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is not None:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        labels = _refine_by_size(base_labels, mcap, self._MIN_GROUP)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r1 = (lp - lp.shift(1))
        r1 = r1.where(np.isfinite(r1))

        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            v = zeros.copy()
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0), 0.0)
        v = v.where(px.notna())

        peer_r = _group_excl_mean(r1, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        peer_v = _group_excl_mean(v, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        if peer_r.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zeros

        # --- peer event-clock speed: short-run arrival rate vs its own norm ----
        fast = ts_mean(peer_v, self._FAST_WIN)
        slow = ts_mean(peer_v, self._SLOW_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        speed = (fast / slow)
        speed = speed.where(np.isfinite(speed)).clip(0.2, 5.0)

        # lookback that contains as much peer flow as the next H bars will
        l_target = (float(H) / speed.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        l_target = l_target.where(np.isfinite(l_target)).clip(1.5, 30.0)

        cands = list(self._CANDS)
        bounds = [float(np.sqrt(cands[i] * cands[i + 1])) for i in range(len(cands) - 1)]
        kidx = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for b in bounds:
            kidx = kidx + (l_target > b).astype(float)
        kidx = kidx.where(l_target.notna())

        beta = rolling_beta(r1, peer_r, self._BETA_WIN)
        beta = beta.where(np.isfinite(beta)).clip(0.0, 2.5).fillna(1.0)

        x = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for k, L in enumerate(cands):
            own_l = lp - lp.shift(int(L))
            peer_l = ts_sum(peer_r, int(L))
            rel = own_l - beta * peer_l
            rel = rel.where(np.isfinite(rel))
            sd = rel.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std()
            sd = sd.replace(0.0, np.nan)
            z = (rel / sd)
            z = z.where(np.isfinite(z)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
            sel = (kidx == float(k))
            x = x.where(~sel, z)
        x = x.where(np.isfinite(x))
        if x.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zeros

        # --- scored quantity: cross-sectionally demeaned realised H-bar return -
        rr = lp - lp.shift(H)
        y_raw = rr.sub(rr.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        sdy = y_raw.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        y = (y_raw / sdy)
        y = y.where(np.isfinite(y)).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        # --- state variables -------------------------------------------------
        own_act = (ts_sum(v.fillna(0.0), H) > 0.0).astype(float)
        own_act = own_act.where(px.notna())
        sp = speed

        x_l = x.shift(H)
        sp_l = sp.shift(H)
        act_l = own_act.shift(H)

        base_ok = x_l.notna() & y.notna()
        state_ok = sp_l.notna() & act_l.notna()
        cur_ok = sp.notna() & own_act.notna() & x.notna()

        b_all = _sign_slope(x_l, y, base_ok, self._FIT_WIN, self._FIT_MIN,
                            self._MIN_OBS, self._CAP_B)

        cells = (
            ((sp_l > 1.0) & (act_l > 0.5), (sp > 1.0) & (own_act > 0.5)),
            ((sp_l > 1.0) & (act_l <= 0.5), (sp > 1.0) & (own_act <= 0.5)),
            ((sp_l <= 1.0) & (act_l > 0.5), (sp <= 1.0) & (own_act > 0.5)),
            ((sp_l <= 1.0) & (act_l <= 0.5), (sp <= 1.0) & (own_act <= 0.5)),
        )

        pred = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        good = pd.DataFrame(False, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for fit_mask, cur_mask in cells:
            b_c = _sign_slope(x_l, y, fit_mask & state_ok & base_ok, self._FIT_WIN,
                              self._FIT_MIN, self._MIN_OBS, self._CAP_B)
            b_c = b_c.where(b_c.notna(), b_all)
            b_u = self._SHRINK * b_c + (1.0 - self._SHRINK) * b_all
            b_u = b_u.where(np.isfinite(b_u))
            sel = (cur_mask & cur_ok).astype(float)
            contrib = sel * x.fillna(0.0).mul(b_u.fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            pred = pred + contrib.fillna(0.0)
            avail = sel.mul(b_u.notna().astype(float), axis=0)
            good = good | (avail > 0.0)

        signal = pred.where(good & x.notna())
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))
        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: A liquidity provider only absorbs a name's peer-idiosyncratic dislocation if the hedge basket can be traded, and the repair therefore completes on the *peer basket's event clock*, not the calendar clock. The parent measured the impulse over a fixed 6 calendar bars, which mismatches the repair window whenever peer trading intensity deviates from its norm — hence its edge leaked to 24 bars. The child makes the impulse event-clock-symmetric: the lookback over which the industry-hedged dislocation is measured is stretched or compressed so that the peer volume accumulated behind the impulse equals the peer volume the trailing rate predicts will arrive over the next 6 bars, so the measured dislocation is exactly the one that is repairable within the fixed forecast offset. Falsifiable: the trailing pooled sign-slope of the demeaned 6-bar forward return on this event-clock-matched impulse should be more negative (stronger reversal) than on any single calendar-matched lookback, and should be strongest in the fast-peer-clock cell; the edge survives arbitrage because it is a hedging-capacity constraint — in slow-clock states there is simply no peer liquidity to complete the round trip.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of a trailing-fitted linear forecast of the demeaned 6-bar forward return from a beta-hedged, vol-scaled peer-relative price dislocation whose lookback is chosen per name/bar so that accumulated leave-one-out peer volume matches the peer volume expected over the next 6 bars; the loading is a robust pooled sign-slope fitted inside cells of peer clock speed x own trading activity.

"""Volume-clock owed split of idiosyncratic vs basket flow impact.

Mechanism
---------
Two parents, two half-truths:

*  Parent A established the PERMANENCE law: mid displacement produced by
   name-specific (idiosyncratic) liquidity demand is information-bearing and
   continues; displacement produced by basket / sector-common flow is
   uninformed about any single name, so the differential push delivered to
   high-loading names is transitory pressure and reverts; flow-unexplained
   (quiet) displacement is quote shading / fleeting-quote flicker and reverts.
   A used a fixed 12-bar calendar box-car to accumulate the legs.

*  Parent B established the CLOCK law: how much of a past push is still 'owed'
   (un-continued or un-reverted) is set by business time - volume traded since
   that bar, measured against the volume expected to trade over the fixed
   6-bar horizon - not by wall-clock age.  B's declared direction failed
   because it never split the flow: on a 10-second grid, high-participation
   bars are disproportionately sector-wide activity bursts, so B's 'backed'
   leg was dominated by basket overpush and net-REVERTED, which is exactly
   what A's basket leg predicts.  B's evidence therefore does not refute A's
   signs; it identifies the missing conditioning variable.

The child is the synthesis: A's three-way decomposition of standardised,
peer-purged displacement is accumulated with B's horizon-matched volume-clock
kernel applied leg by leg.

    f_i(t)      = b_i * f_peer(t) + e_i(t)          (flow commonality split)
    x           = peer-purged bar return / trailing sd
    x_idio      = lambda_i * e_i / sd               (permanent, follow)
    x_basket    = lambda_i * b_i * f_peer / sd      (transitory, fade)
    x_quiet     = x - x_idio - x_basket             (quote flicker, fade)
    w(t, s)     = clip(1 - V(t-s, t] / (6 * vbar), 0, 1)   (business clock)
    A_leg(t)    = sum_s w(t,s) * x_leg(t-s) / sqrt(sum_s w^2)

    score = rank(A_idio) - rank(A_basket) - 0.5 * rank(A_quiet)

Fast-trading names forget quickly in wall-clock terms, quiet names slowly, so
the kernel keeps only the still-live part of each leg - the part whose
continuation (idiosyncratic) or reversion (basket) is still ahead of us.

All statistics are causal: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only;
cross-sectional operations act inside a single timestamp.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_codes(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Integer-coded static sector label per ticker (last observed text value)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    if sector is not None:
        for col in columns:
            if col not in sector.columns:
                continue
            ser = sector[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(columns).values)
    return np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)


def _peer_ex_self_mean(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-sector mean EXCLUDING the own column.

    Small sectors fall back to the whole cross-section (still ex-self).  Purely
    contemporaneous and cross-sectional, so no look-ahead in time.
    """
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    vals = np.where(finite, arr, 0.0)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    row_sum = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    row_cnt = finite.sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float)
    for k in np.unique(codes):
        m = codes == k
        if int(m.sum()) < int(min_peers):
            s = row_sum - vals[:, m]
            c = row_cnt - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        else:
            s = vals[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None] - vals[:, m]
            c = finite[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float) - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
            res = np.where(c > 0.0, s / np.where(c > 0.0, c, 1.0), np.nan)
        out[:, m] = res
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)


def _volume_clock_legs(
    chans: list[pd.DataFrame],
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    vol: pd.DataFrame,
    vh: pd.DataFrame,
    max_lag: int,
) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Accumulate each channel with a kernel decaying in volume since the bar.

    At lag s the weight is clip(1 - V(t-s, t] / vh, 0, 1) where V(t-s, t] is the
    volume traded strictly after bar t-s, and vh is the volume expected to trade
    over the forecast horizon.  Variance-normalised by sqrt(sum w^2).  Causal:
    only positive shifts are used.
    """
    idx, cols = valid.index, valid.columns
    nums = [pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols) for _ in chans]
    w2 = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    cum = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    v0 = vol.fillna(0.0)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for s in range(int(max_lag) + 1):
            w = (1.0 - cum / vh).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            w = w.where(np.isfinite(w)).fillna(0.0)
            wv = w * valid.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
            for j, ch in enumerate(chans):
                nums[j] = nums[j] + wv * ch.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
            w2 = w2 + wv * wv
            cum = cum + v0.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
    denom = np.sqrt(w2.where(w2 > 0.0))
    return [n / denom for n in nums]


@register_factor
class VolumeClockBasketVsIdioImpactOwedSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Follow still-live idiosyncratic impact, fade still-owed basket overpush."""

    factor_id = 'volume_clock_basket_vs_idio_impact_owed_split'
    name = 'Volume-clock owed split: idiosyncratic vs basket flow impact'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Splits normalized signed sqrt-volume flow into a within-sector ex-self basket component '
        '(trailing OLS loading on peer flow) and an idiosyncratic residual, maps each into a '
        'Kyle-lambda-implied displacement alongside the flow-unexplained (quiet) part of '
        'peer-purged volatility-standardised bar returns, accumulates the three legs with a '
        'kernel decaying in volume traded since each bar relative to 6-bar expected volume, and '
        'scores +idiosyncratic \u2212 basket \u2212 \u00bd\u00b7quiet cross-sectionally.'
    )
    window_length = 320
    inputs = ['close', 'open', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _NORM_WIN = 180
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _VOL_MIN = 30
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _MAX_LAG = 24
    _H = 6.0
    _QUIET_W = 0.5
    _SMOOTH = 3

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            return zero
        vol = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = (lp - lp.shift(1))
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # ---- trade direction: intra-bar mid change, else bar-over-bar change ----
        op = data.get('open')
        if op is not None:
            op = op.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            op = op.where(np.isfinite(op) & (op > 0.0))
            dmid = lp - np.log(op)
        else:
            dmid = r
        s_dir = np.sign(dmid.fillna(0.0))
        s_dir = s_dir.where(s_dir != 0.0, np.sign(r.fillna(0.0)))

        rv = np.sqrt(vol)
        scale_v = ts_mean(rv, self._NORM_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        f = (s_dir * rv / scale_v).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)

        codes = _static_codes(cols, data.get('sector'))

        # ---- peer-purged displacement increments --------------------------------
        r_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(r, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        u = (r - r_peer).where(np.isfinite(r) & np.isfinite(r_peer))

        # ---- flow commonality split: own flow on basket (ex-self peer) flow -----
        f_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(f, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        f_peer = f_peer.where(np.isfinite(f_peer)).fillna(0.0)
        b = rolling_beta(f, f_peer, self._BETA_WIN)
        b = b.where(np.isfinite(b)).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
        f_common = b * f_peer
        f_idio = f - f_common

        # ---- per-name trailing Kyle lambda on idio displacement -----------------
        lam = rolling_beta(u, f, self._BETA_WIN)
        lam = lam.where(np.isfinite(lam)).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        sd = u.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (u / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        x_idio = (lam * f_idio / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        x_bask = (lam * f_common / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        base_ok = x.notna() & sd.notna()
        x0 = x.where(base_ok)
        xi = x_idio.where(base_ok).fillna(0.0).where(base_ok)
        xb = x_bask.where(base_ok).fillna(0.0).where(base_ok)
        xq = (x0 - xi - xb).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        valid = base_ok.astype(float)

        # ---- business clock: volume expected over the 6-bar horizon -------------
        vbar = vol.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vh = (float(self._H) * vbar).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        legs = _volume_clock_legs(
            [xi.fillna(0.0), xb.fillna(0.0), xq.fillna(0.0)],
            valid,
            vol,
            vh,
            self._MAX_LAG,
        )
        a_idio, a_bask, a_quiet = legs
        a_idio = a_idio.where(np.isfinite(a_idio))
        a_bask = a_bask.where(np.isfinite(a_bask))
        a_quiet = a_quiet.where(np.isfinite(a_quiet))

        ok = a_idio.notna() & a_bask.notna() & a_quiet.notna()

        z_i = (rank(a_idio.where(ok)) - 0.5)
        z_b = (rank(a_bask.where(ok)) - 0.5)
        z_q = (rank(a_quiet.where(ok)) - 0.5)

        raw = z_i - z_b - float(self._QUIET_W) * z_q
        raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw) & ok)
        raw = decay_linear(raw.fillna(0.0), self._SMOOTH).where(raw.notna())

        out = rank(raw) - 0.5
        out = out.where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: Parent A showed that at 10-second resolution the *permanence* of mid displacement depends on whether the flow behind it is name-specific (informed, continues) or basket/sector-common (uninformed overpush, reverts), while Parent B showed that how much of a past push is still 'owed' is governed by business time — volume traded since the push relative to the volume expected over the horizon — not calendar time. B's declared direction failed precisely because it never split the flow: on a 10s grid high-participation bars are disproportionately sector-wide activity bursts, so B's 'backed' leg was dominated by basket overpush and therefore net-reverted, exactly as A's basket leg predicts. The child fixes this by applying B's horizon-matched volume-clock kernel *separately to each of A's legs*: only push that has not yet been worked off in business time is still live, so the idiosyncratic-impact continuation leg (metaorder splitting, still un-completed in business time) and the basket-impact reversion leg (makers have not yet reloaded because too little volume has traded) are both measured on the clock that actually governs their decay, while A's fixed 12-bar box-car diluted both with already-resolved history.
