programs.trading_idea: A 60-second industry-relative dislocation is only absorbed (and therefore only snaps back) if a liquidity provider can put on the offsetting peer leg *at the same instant*; average peer volume, the parent's gate, is the wrong state variable because peer flow can be plentiful yet arrive in bars where the name itself is untradeable. The sharper conditioning variable is the excess joint-arrival probability — the trailing frequency of bars in which the name trades AND at least half its industry peers trade, minus the product of the two marginal arrival rates — i.e. a co-arrival 'lift' that measures arrival clustering (Hawkes-style cross-excitation) rather than arrival volume. Prediction: the reversal slope on the 6-bar industry-relative return is materially more negative for names in the high co-arrival-lift state and near zero in the low-lift state, and is further damped when the dislocation was itself backed by abnormal own volume (informed, hence permanent). The edge persists because it is a capacity/executability constraint: hedging an idiosyncratic valuation gap consumes both capital and *simultaneous* peer liquidity, so in asynchronous-arrival states no one can arbitrage it away, and the compensation for immediacy in the synchronous states is a fee, not a mispricing.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of minus the volatility-scaled 6-bar industry-relative (leave-one-out) log return, multiplied by a hedge-executability gate built from the trailing co-arrival lift (joint name+peer trading frequency in excess of independent arrivals) and damped by the name's own 6-bar volume backing.

programs.code:
"""Volume-confirmed peer leader impulse vs stale-quote follower catch-up.

Mechanism
---------
The parent factor (quiet-minus-traded split of peer-residual displacement)
realised the opposite sign to its declared propagator direction.  The honest
reading is a timescale error, not noise: order flow is strongly autocorrelated
(order splitting / metaorders), so over the next ~60 seconds a mid displacement
that printed volume keeps going (permanent impact plus still-live slices),
while a displacement that printed nothing is quote flicker / inventory skew and
reverts.  Transient-impact relaxation only dominates on much longer clocks.

The child keeps the part of the parent that earned residual IC (valuation-tier
peer comparability from point-in-time per-share multiples) but re-roles the
trade attribution:

1. Cells = sector x half of a slowly smoothed log-multiple level (price over
   book- and revenue-per-share).  These are fundamentally comparable names,
   not just same-sector names.

2. Each bar's log return is attributed to liquidity/informed trade by the bar's
   participation share g = v / (v + trailing mean v).  a = r * g is the
   trade-attributable (credible, information-bearing) displacement.

3. Within each cell, a dollar-volume-weighted, LEAVE-ONE-OUT average of peers'
   trade-attributable displacement is the cell's volume-confirmed information
   impulse: price discovery concentrates in the members actually printing.
   It is accumulated with an exponential kernel (halflife 5 bars) so the impulse
   still has delivery ahead of it inside the 6-bar forecast offset.

4. The name's own accumulated move over the same kernel is the part already
   delivered.  Each leg is normalised by its own trailing volatility, and the
   gap (peer impulse - own delivered) is multiplied by a staleness weight
   1 - mean(g, 6): the claim is confined to names whose own tape has been
   silent, i.e. whose mid is quote-stale and has not repriced yet.

Falsifiable: the edge should die if the peer impulse is built from the QUIET
part r*(1-g) instead of the traded part, if the gate is inverted to favour
highly active names, or if cells are formed by sector text alone.

All statistics are causal: cross-sectional operations act within one timestamp,
time-series operations use trailing windows and positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None,
                   industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker coarse peer label: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _log_multiple(px: pd.DataFrame, per_share: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """log(price / per-share fundamental), masked to strictly positive inputs."""
    denom = per_share.where(np.isfinite(per_share) & (per_share > 0.0))
    ratio = px / denom
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)


def _group_weighted_sum(a: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, valid: np.ndarray,
                        key_arr: np.ndarray) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-cell weighted sum of a, weight sum, and live count.

    Purely within-timestamp (row-wise) aggregation: no information from t+1.
    """
    av = a.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    wv = w.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a_safe = np.where(np.isfinite(av), av, 0.0)
    w_safe = np.where(np.isfinite(wv), wv, 0.0)
    aw = np.where(valid, a_safe * w_safe, 0.0)
    ww = np.where(valid, w_safe, 0.0)

    S = np.zeros(av.shape, dtype=float)
    W = np.zeros(av.shape, dtype=float)
    C = np.zeros(av.shape, dtype=float)
    for k in np.unique(key_arr):
        m = key_arr == k
        if not m.any():
            continue
        rs = (aw * m).sum(axis=1)
        rw = (ww * m).sum(axis=1)
        rc = (valid & m).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
        S[m] = np.broadcast_to(rs[:, None], av.shape)[m]
        W[m] = np.broadcast_to(rw[:, None], av.shape)[m]
        C[m] = np.broadcast_to(rc[:, None], av.shape)[m]

    return (pd.DataFrame(S, index=a.index, columns=a.columns),
            pd.DataFrame(W, index=a.index, columns=a.columns),
            pd.DataFrame(C, index=a.index, columns=a.columns))


@register_factor
class TradedLeaderStaleFollowerCatchupWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Volume-confirmed valuation-peer impulse owed to quote-stale followers."""

    factor_id = 'traded_leader_stale_follower_catchup_wedge'
    name = 'Volume-confirmed peer leader vs stale follower catch-up'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Within sector x valuation-tier cells, accumulates a dollar-volume-weighted '
        'leave-one-out average of peers trade-attributable log returns (bar return '
        'times participation share), z-scores it against the names own accumulated '
        'move, and gates the difference on low recent own participation (stale mid): '
        'long names owed an upward catch-up to volume-confirmed peer information.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare',
              'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _LEVEL_HALFLIFE = 240.0
    _LEVEL_MIN = 30
    _N_TIERS = 2
    _VOL_BASE_WINDOW = 120
    _VOL_BASE_MIN = 30
    _ADV_WINDOW = 120
    _KERNEL_HALFLIFE = 5.0
    _KERNEL_MIN = 6
    _SD_WINDOW = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _STALE_WINDOW = 6
    _MIN_PEERS = 4

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            return zero
        volume = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))

        # ---- comparability cells: sector x valuation half -------------------
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        lvl_sum = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        lvl_cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for field in ('bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare'):
            raw = data.get(field)
            if raw is None:
                continue
            per_share = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            if per_share.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            lm = _log_multiple(px, per_share)
            lvl_sum = lvl_sum.add(lm.fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
            lvl_cnt = lvl_cnt.add(lm.notna().astype(float), fill_value=0.0)
        level = lvl_sum / lvl_cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        level_sm = level.ewm(halflife=self._LEVEL_HALFLIFE,
                             min_periods=self._LEVEL_MIN, adjust=False).mean()

        sec_codes, uniques = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(cols).values)
        n_tiers = int(self._N_TIERS)
        tier = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for s in range(len(uniques)):
            colmask = np.asarray(sec_codes) == s
            sub_cols = cols[colmask]
            if len(sub_cols) == 0:
                continue
            sub = level_sm[sub_cols]
            if len(sub_cols) < 2 * n_tiers:
                t = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=sub_cols)
                t = t.where(sub.notna(), 1.0)
            else:
                rk = sub.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
                t = np.ceil(rk * float(n_tiers)).clip(1.0, float(n_tiers))
                t = t.fillna(0.0)
            tier.loc[:, sub_cols] = t.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        key_arr = (np.asarray(sec_codes, dtype=np.int64)[None, :] * (n_tiers + 1)
                   + tier.to_numpy(dtype=np.int64))

        # ---- bar returns and participation share ---------------------------
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        vol = volume.where(np.isfinite(volume) & (volume >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        base = vol.rolling(self._VOL_BASE_WINDOW, min_periods=self._VOL_BASE_MIN).mean()
        denom = (vol + base.fillna(0.0)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g = (vol / denom).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        # trade-attributable (information-bearing) displacement
        a = r * g

        # ---- liquidity weight: trailing dollar volume ----------------------
        dollar = (px * vol).where(np.isfinite(px * vol) & (px * vol >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        w = adv(dollar, self._ADV_WINDOW)
        w = w.where(np.isfinite(w) & (w > 0.0))

        valid_df = r.notna() & w.notna()
        valid_np = valid_df.to_numpy()

        S, W, C = _group_weighted_sum(a, w, valid_np, key_arr)
        w_v = w.where(valid_df, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        a_v = a.where(valid_df, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        den = (W - w_v)
        lead = (S - w_v * a_v) / den.where(den > 0.0)
        lead = lead.where(C >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        lead = lead.where(np.isfinite(lead))

        # ---- horizon-matched accumulation kernels --------------------------
        lead_acc = lead.ewm(halflife=self._KERNEL_HALFLIFE,
                            min_periods=self._KERNEL_MIN, adjust=True).mean()
        own_acc = r.ewm(halflife=self._KERNEL_HALFLIFE,
                        min_periods=self._KERNEL_MIN, adjust=True).mean()

        sd_l = lead_acc.rolling(self._SD_WINDOW, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sd_o = own_acc.rolling(self._SD_WINDOW, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lz = (lead_acc / sd_l).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        oz = (own_acc / sd_o).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # ---- staleness gate: own tape silent relative to its own norm ------
        stale = (1.0 - ts_mean(g, self._STALE_WINDOW)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        signal = stale * (lz - oz)
        signal = signal.where(C >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)

programs.trading_idea: The parent's realized sign says the opposite of its propagator story, and the honest reading is a timescale error: metaorders and the order flow that generates impact are autocorrelated over minutes, so within the next 60 seconds a *volume-backed* mid displacement keeps going (permanent/informational component plus live slices), while a *quiet* mid displacement is quote flicker or inventory skew and mean-reverts — relaxation of transient impact only dominates far beyond 6 bars. The child therefore stops treating the traded leg as the thing that decays and instead uses it as the information carrier, but moves the claim cross-sectionally: within a valuation-comparable cell (sector x slow valuation tier from point-in-time per-share multiples), price discovery concentrates in the members that are actually printing volume, so the dollar-volume-weighted, leave-one-out accumulation of peers' *trade-attributable* residual displacement is a credible information impulse that a peer whose own tape has been silent has not yet incorporated. The signal is that undelivered gap (peer volume-confirmed impulse minus the name's own accumulated move), gated on the name's own recent participation being abnormally low, i.e. on its mid being quote-stale. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires joining point-in-time fundamentals (to build valuation-tier comparability cells, which no microstructure desk maintains) with bar-level trade attribution, and because taking the stale side means providing liquidity against possibly-informed peer flow, so the catch-up is compensation for adverse selection rather than a free lag.

programs.code:
"""Convex synthetic-twin pricing gap: simplex peer replication + snapback.

Mechanism
---------
The parent decomposed *flow* into basket vs idiosyncratic parts; the evaluation
said that idea, while independent-ish, adds almost nothing on the margin because
the book is saturated with quiet-vs-traded / basket-overpush permanence splits.
So the child changes the mechanism, not the window.

For every name we construct a SYNTHETIC TWIN: the convex combination of the
other names (weights >= 0, summing to 1, own weight forced to 0) whose trailing
standardized return path best replicates the name.  The problem

    min_{w in simplex, w_j = 0}  || z_j - Z w ||^2  =  (e_j - w)' G (e_j - w)

is solved in Gram space by exponentiated-gradient mirror descent (a batched,
deterministic, trailing-window solver written out here - no external library).
The simplex constraint makes the tracker sparse and level-matched, so the
residual is a *relative-value spread between close substitutes* rather than a
diffuse OLS residual.  Such a spread is opened by one-sided inventory demand in
a single name and is closed by the desks that watch substitute baskets, hence it
reverts over tens of seconds.

The conditioning interaction (the falsifiable part) is the gate

    gate = sqrt(tracking R2) * sqrt(Herfindahl of twin weights)

Reversal should be strong only where the twin actually tracks (high R2) AND the
twin is concentrated in a few substitutes (high HHI); a diffuse, badly-tracking
twin leaves unhedged idiosyncratic news, which should NOT revert.

Causality: weights, standardizations, beta and R2 at a refit time t0 use rows
t0-W .. t0-1 only, and are then applied forward to rows t0 .. t0+step-1.  Every
other statistic is a trailing rolling / ewm object or a within-bar cross-
sectional operation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _eg_simplex_weights(G: np.ndarray, valid: np.ndarray, iters: int, eta: float = 0.5) -> np.ndarray:
    """Batched exponentiated-gradient (simplex mirror-descent) tracking weights.

    Column j of the returned matrix holds the convex weights of the synthetic
    twin of target j (own weight = 0).  Only the trailing Gram matrix G enters,
    so the solver is deterministic and cheap.
    """
    v = np.asarray(valid, dtype=float)
    mask = np.outer(v, v)
    np.fill_diagonal(mask, 0.0)
    csum = mask.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    ok = csum > 0.5
    Wm = np.where(ok, mask / np.where(ok, csum, 1.0), 0.0)
    Gs = np.where(np.isfinite(G), G, 0.0)
    n_it = int(max(iters, 0))
    for _ in range(n_it):
        grad = Gs @ Wm - Gs                     # d/dw of (e_j - w)'G(e_j - w) / 2
        sc = np.max(np.abs(grad), axis=0, keepdims=True)
        gn = grad / np.where(sc > 1e-12, sc, 1.0)
        Wm = Wm * np.exp(np.clip(-eta * gn, -30.0, 30.0))
        Wm = Wm * mask
        s = Wm.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        Wm = np.where(s > 1e-12, Wm / np.where(s > 1e-12, s, 1.0), 0.0)
    return Wm


@register_factor
class EgSimplexSyntheticTwinGapSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade the pricing gap of a name against its convex synthetic twin."""

    factor_id = 'eg_simplex_synthetic_twin_gap_snapback'
    name = 'Convex synthetic-twin pricing gap snapback'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Fits, on trailing windows only, a simplex-constrained (non-negative, sum-to-one) peer '
        'tracking portfolio per name via exponentiated-gradient mirror descent, beta-scales it, and '
        'scores minus the recent exponentially-weighted residual drift gated by '
        'sqrt(tracking R2 x weight Herfindahl).'
    )
    window_length = 480
    inputs = ['close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _FIT_WIN = 240        # bars used to fit the synthetic twin (~40 min)
    _MIN_FRAC = 0.6       # minimum finite fraction inside the fit window
    _HL = 3.0             # halflife (bars) of the residual-drift filter
    _Z_WIN = 240          # trailing window for residual scaling
    _Z_MIN = 60

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = (lp - lp.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        arr = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        T, N = arr.shape
        Wf = int(self._FIT_WIN)
        if T < Wf + 8 or N < 4:
            return zero

        # --- work budget: keep the batched solver cheap for wide panels --------
        if N <= 80:
            iters = 60
        elif N <= 200:
            iters = 40
        elif N <= 600:
            iters = 20
        else:
            iters = 0                     # degenerate to equal-weight peer twin
        work = float(T) * float(max(iters, 1)) * (float(N) ** 3)
        step = int(np.clip(np.ceil(work / 2.0e10), 30.0, 600.0))

        E = np.full((T, N), np.nan)       # residual vs synthetic twin
        Q = np.full((T, N), np.nan)       # gate = sqrt(R2 * HHI)

        for t0 in range(Wf, T, step):
            win = arr[t0 - Wf:t0, :]                       # strictly past rows
            fin = np.isfinite(win)
            cnt = fin.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
            filled = np.where(fin, win, 0.0)
            mu = filled.sum(axis=0) / np.maximum(cnt, 1.0)
            Xc = np.where(fin, win - mu[None, :], 0.0)
            var = (Xc ** 2).sum(axis=0) / np.maximum(cnt - 1.0, 1.0)
            sd = np.sqrt(np.where(np.isfinite(var) & (var > 0.0), var, 0.0))
            valid = (cnt >= self._MIN_FRAC * Wf) & (sd > 1e-12)
            if int(valid.sum()) < 4:
                continue
            sdv = np.where(valid, np.where(sd > 1e-12, sd, 1.0), 1.0)
            Z = Xc / sdv[None, :]
            Z[:, ~valid] = 0.0
            G = (Z.T @ Z) / float(Wf)

            Wm = _eg_simplex_weights(G, valid, iters)

            GW = G @ Wm
            quad = np.sum(Wm * GW, axis=0)                 # w'Gw
            cross = np.sum(Wm * G, axis=0)                 # G_j'w
            safe_q = np.where(quad > 1e-10, quad, np.nan)
            beta = np.clip(cross / safe_q, 0.0, 4.0)
            beta = np.where(np.isfinite(beta), beta, 0.0)
            r2 = np.clip((cross ** 2) / safe_q, 0.0, 1.0)
            r2 = np.where(np.isfinite(r2), r2, 0.0)
            hhi = np.clip(np.sum(Wm ** 2, axis=0), 0.0, 1.0)
            gate = np.sqrt(r2) * np.sqrt(hhi)
            gate = np.where(valid, gate, np.nan)

            t1 = min(t0 + step, T)
            blk = arr[t0:t1, :]
            bfin = np.isfinite(blk)
            Zb = np.where(bfin, blk, 0.0) / sdv[None, :]
            Zb[:, ~valid] = 0.0
            syn = Zb @ Wm                                  # synthetic twin path
            res = Zb - beta[None, :] * syn
            res = np.where(bfin & valid[None, :], res, np.nan)
            E[t0:t1, :] = res
            Q[t0:t1, :] = np.repeat(gate[None, :], t1 - t0, axis=0)

        Edf = pd.DataFrame(E, index=idx, columns=cols)
        gap = Edf.ewm(halflife=self._HL, min_periods=3).mean()
        sde = Edf.rolling(self._Z_WIN, min_periods=self._Z_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (gap / sde).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        gatedf = pd.DataFrame(Q, index=idx, columns=cols).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        raw = -(z * gatedf)
        raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw))

        out = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Convex synthetic-twin pricing gap snapback
programs.trading_idea: Instead of splitting a name's flow (the parent's angle, which the book already spans), the child changes the mechanism: it builds each name a *synthetic twin* — the convex (non-negative, sum-to-one) combination of the other names whose 40-minute return path best replicates it — using exponentiated-gradient mirror descent on the simplex, refit on trailing windows only. The simplex constraint forces the tracker to be sparse and level-matched, so what is left over is a genuine relative-value spread between close substitutes rather than a diffuse OLS residual; such a spread is created by one-sided inventory demand in a single name and is closed by the very relative-value desks that watch substitute pairs, so it snaps back within about a minute. The falsifiable interaction is the gate: reversal strength must rise monotonically with (a) the twin's in-window tracking correlation and (b) the Herfindahl concentration of the twin's weights — a diffuse, poorly-tracking twin leaves mostly unhedged idiosyncratic news, which should show little or no reversal. The edge persists because per-name simplex tracking portfolios must be re-solved continuously across the whole cross-section and each closure earns only a fraction of the spread, making it capacity-limited rather than arbitraged away.
programs.description: For each name, fits a trailing exponentiated-gradient simplex tracking portfolio of its peers (a synthetic twin), beta-scales it, and scores the negative of the recent exponentially-weighted residual drift, multiplied by a gate equal to sqrt(in-window tracking R2 x weight Herfindahl); output is the cross-sectional rank.

programs.code:
"""Completion-clock dual-kernel split of idiosyncratic vs basket flow impact.

Mechanism
---------
The parent factor established two useful facts and one flaw.

Facts kept:
  (1) Mid displacement produced by *name-specific* liquidity demand is
      information-bearing and continues; displacement produced by
      *basket / sector-common* flow is uninformative about any single name and
      is transitory pressure that is paid back; flow-unexplained (quiet)
      displacement is quote shading / fleeting-quote flicker and reverts.
  (2) The relevant age of a past push is business time - volume traded since
      the bar, measured against the volume expected over the forecast horizon -
      not wall-clock age.

Flaw fixed:
      the parent applied the SAME fresh-weighted (low-pass) volume kernel to
      both legs.  A stock of still-owed push weighted toward the newest bars is
      a level: it is highly autocorrelated and therefore forecasts slow drift,
      which is exactly what the evaluation showed (|IC| peaked at 24 bars, not
      at the fixed 6-bar offset).

The two legs do not resolve on the same schedule:

  * IDIOSYNCRATIC leg - continuation over the next horizon requires the parent
    metaorder to STILL BE EXECUTING.  Order-splitting lifetimes are
    approximately geometric in executed volume, so the probability that the
    push at business-age V is still being extended is a survival function

        S(V) = exp(-V / (H * vbar))                      (low-pass, fast)

  * BASKET leg - a sector burst holds the price displaced while it is being
    worked (a plateau); relaxation only begins once the burst completes and
    makers reload, at a business-time scale Vc of a few horizon-volumes.  With
    a plateau-then-decay propagator

        g(V) = 1 / (1 + (V / Vc)^p),   p = 3,  Vc = 2.5 * H * vbar

    the displacement that will be repaid over the NEXT horizon is the
    horizon DIFFERENCE

        w_b(V) = g(V) - g(V + H * vbar)                  (BAND-PASS in age)

    which is ~0 for very fresh push (nothing is due yet), peaks at
    V ~ 1.5-2 horizon-volumes (due now) and dies for ancient push (already
    paid).  This band-pass, not a fresh-weighted stock, is the object whose
    resolution lands inside the fixed 6-bar window.

  * QUIET leg - quote flicker reverts almost immediately, so only the last two
    bars are used.

    score = rank(A_idio) - rank(A_basket) - 0.5 * rank(A_quiet)

Falsifiable: if displacement resolution were memoryless in business time, the
band-pass basket leg would carry no more 6-bar information than the parent's
fresh-weighted stock, and the child's IC would again peak far beyond 6 bars.

All statistics are causal: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only;
cross-sectional operations act inside a single timestamp.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_codes(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Integer-coded static sector label per ticker (last observed text value)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    if sector is not None:
        for col in columns:
            if col not in sector.columns:
                continue
            ser = sector[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(columns).values)
    return np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)


def _peer_ex_self_mean(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-sector mean EXCLUDING the own column.

    Small sectors fall back to the whole cross-section (still ex-self).  Purely
    contemporaneous and cross-sectional, so no look-ahead in time.
    """
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    vals = np.where(finite, arr, 0.0)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    row_sum = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    row_cnt = finite.sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float)
    for k in np.unique(codes):
        m = codes == k
        if int(m.sum()) < int(min_peers):
            s = row_sum - vals[:, m]
            c = row_cnt - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        else:
            s = vals[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None] - vals[:, m]
            c = finite[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float) - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
            res = np.where(c > 0.0, s / np.where(c > 0.0, c, 1.0), np.nan)
        out[:, m] = res
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)


def _clean_w(w: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return w.where(np.isfinite(w)).fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _dual_clock_legs(
    x_idio: pd.DataFrame,
    x_bask: pd.DataFrame,
    x_quiet: pd.DataFrame,
    valid: pd.DataFrame,
    vol: pd.DataFrame,
    vh: pd.DataFrame,
    surv_scale: pd.DataFrame,
    comp_scale: pd.DataFrame,
    power: float,
    max_lag: int,
    quiet_lag: int,
) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Accumulate the three legs, each on its OWN business-time kernel.

    V(t-s, t] = volume traded strictly after bar t-s (business age of that bar).
      idio  : exp(-V / surv_scale)                        survival low-pass
      basket: g(V) - g(V + vh), g(V)=1/(1+(V/comp_scale)^p)   horizon band-pass
      quiet : 1 for s <= quiet_lag, else 0                     flicker window
    Each accumulation is variance-normalised by sqrt(sum w^2).  Only positive
    shifts are used, so the value at t sees only bars <= t.
    """
    idx, cols = valid.index, valid.columns
    zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    n_i, n_b, n_q = zero.copy(), zero.copy(), zero.copy()
    d_i, d_b, d_q = zero.copy(), zero.copy(), zero.copy()
    cum = zero.copy()
    v0 = vol.fillna(0.0)

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for s in range(int(max_lag) + 1):
            vv = valid.shift(s).fillna(0.0)

            # --- idiosyncratic: still-executing survival probability ---------
            w_i = _clean_w(np.exp(-(cum / surv_scale))) * vv

            # --- basket: horizon-differenced delayed-relaxation band-pass ----
            u0 = (cum / comp_scale)
            u1 = ((cum + vh) / comp_scale)
            g0 = 1.0 / (1.0 + u0.pow(power))
            g1 = 1.0 / (1.0 + u1.pow(power))
            w_b = _clean_w(g0 - g1) * vv

            # --- quiet flicker: only the freshest bars ----------------------
            w_q = vv if s <= int(quiet_lag) else zero

            n_i = n_i + w_i * x_idio.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
            n_b = n_b + w_b * x_bask.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
            n_q = n_q + w_q * x_quiet.shift(s).fillna(0.0)
            d_i = d_i + w_i * w_i
            d_b = d_b + w_b * w_b
            d_q = d_q + w_q * w_q

            cum = cum + v0.shift(s).fillna(0.0)

    out = []
    for num, den in ((n_i, d_i), (n_b, d_b), (n_q, d_q)):
        dd = np.sqrt(den.where(den > 0.0))
        out.append(num / dd)
    return out


@register_factor
class CompletionClockDualKernelImpactSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Follow still-executing idio impact, fade basket overpush that is due now."""

    factor_id = 'completion_clock_dual_kernel_impact_split'
    name = 'Completion-clock dual-kernel idio vs basket impact split'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Splits normalised signed sqrt-volume flow into a within-sector ex-self common leg '
        '(trailing OLS loading on peer flow) and an idiosyncratic residual, maps both through a '
        'trailing Kyle lambda into volatility-standardised peer-purged displacement, then '
        'accumulates the idiosyncratic leg with an exponential survival kernel in volume traded '
        'since each bar and the basket leg with a horizon-differenced plateau-then-decay '
        '(band-pass) kernel on the same business clock, plus a 2-bar quiet-flicker leg, scoring '
        '+idiosyncratic \u2212 basket \u2212 \u00bd\u00b7quiet cross-sectionally.'
    )
    window_length = 340
    inputs = ['close', 'open', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _NORM_WIN = 180
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _VOL_MIN = 30
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _MAX_LAG = 36
    _QUIET_LAG = 1
    _H = 6.0
    _SURV_MULT = 1.0      # metaorder survival scale, in horizon-volumes
    _COMP_MULT = 2.5      # burst completion / relaxation onset scale
    _POWER = 3.0          # sharpness of the plateau shoulder
    _QUIET_W = 0.5
    _SMOOTH = 2

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            return zero
        vol = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = (lp - lp.shift(1))
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # ---- trade direction: intra-bar mid change, else bar-over-bar -------
        op = data.get('open')
        if op is not None:
            op = op.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            op = op.where(np.isfinite(op) & (op > 0.0))
            dmid = lp - np.log(op)
        else:
            dmid = r
        s_dir = np.sign(dmid.fillna(0.0))
        s_dir = s_dir.where(s_dir != 0.0, np.sign(r.fillna(0.0)))

        rv = np.sqrt(vol)
        scale_v = ts_mean(rv, self._NORM_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        f = (s_dir * rv / scale_v).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)

        codes = _static_codes(cols, data.get('sector'))

        # ---- peer-purged displacement increments ----------------------------
        r_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(r, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        u = (r - r_peer).where(np.isfinite(r) & np.isfinite(r_peer))

        # ---- flow commonality split -----------------------------------------
        f_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(f, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        f_peer = f_peer.where(np.isfinite(f_peer)).fillna(0.0)
        b = rolling_beta(f, f_peer, self._BETA_WIN)
        b = b.where(np.isfinite(b)).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
        f_common = b * f_peer
        f_idio = f - f_common

        # ---- per-name trailing Kyle lambda ----------------------------------
        lam = rolling_beta(u, f, self._BETA_WIN)
        lam = lam.where(np.isfinite(lam)).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        sd = u.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (u / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        x_idio = (lam * f_idio / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        x_bask = (lam * f_common / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        base_ok = x.notna() & sd.notna()
        x0 = x.where(base_ok)
        xi = x_idio.where(base_ok)
        xb = x_bask.where(base_ok)
        xq = (x0 - xi.fillna(0.0) - xb.fillna(0.0)).clip(-4.0, 4.0).where(base_ok)

        valid = base_ok.astype(float)

        # ---- business clock scales ------------------------------------------
        vbar = vol.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vh = (float(self._H) * vbar).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        surv = (float(self._SURV_MULT) * vh).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        comp = (float(self._COMP_MULT) * vh).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        a_idio, a_bask, a_quiet = _dual_clock_legs(
            xi.fillna(0.0),
            xb.fillna(0.0),
            xq.fillna(0.0),
            valid,
            vol,
            vh,
            surv,
            comp,
            float(self._POWER),
            self._MAX_LAG,
            self._QUIET_LAG,
        )
        a_idio = a_idio.where(np.isfinite(a_idio))
        a_bask = a_bask.where(np.isfinite(a_bask))
        a_quiet = a_quiet.where(np.isfinite(a_quiet))

        ok = a_idio.notna() & a_bask.notna() & a_quiet.notna()

        z_i = rank(a_idio.where(ok)) - 0.5
        z_b = rank(a_bask.where(ok)) - 0.5
        z_q = rank(a_quiet.where(ok)) - 0.5

        raw = z_i - z_b - float(self._QUIET_W) * z_q
        raw = raw.where(np.isfinite(raw) & ok)
        raw = decay_linear(raw.fillna(0.0), self._SMOOTH).where(raw.notna())

        out = rank(raw) - 0.5
        out = out.where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Completion-clock dual-kernel idiosyncratic vs basket impact split
programs.trading_idea: The parent showed the idio/basket flow split has real, book-orthogonal content but expressed it as a *stock* of still-owed push weighted toward the freshest bars, which is a low-pass level and therefore predicts slow drift (its IC peaked at 24 bars, not 6). The fix is that the two legs resolve on different business-time schedules: idiosyncratic (informed) push keeps accruing only while the parent metaorder is still executing, so its next-60-second continuation is governed by a *survival* low-pass in volume traded since the bar; basket/sector-common overpush stays plateaued while the burst is still being worked and only starts being paid back once execution completes, so what reverts over the *next* horizon is push whose business-time age sits near the completion scale — a *band-pass* in volume-clock age, not a fresh-weighted low-pass. Applying a survival kernel to the idio leg and a horizon-differenced delayed-relaxation kernel (g(V) − g(V+V_h), g plateau-then-decay) to the basket leg selects exactly the displacement that is due to move within 6 bars, so the edge should migrate from 24 bars to the fixed 6-bar offset. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires jointly estimating each name's flow-commonality loading, its Kyle lambda and its volume clock at 10-second resolution, and the payoff is a few basis points of maker-side timing that is uneconomic for anyone crossing the spread.
programs.description: Splits normalised signed sqrt-volume flow into a within-sector ex-self common component (trailing OLS loading on peer flow) and an idiosyncratic residual, maps both through a trailing Kyle lambda into volatility-standardised peer-purged displacement, then accumulates the idiosyncratic leg with an exponential *survival* kernel in volume traded since each bar and the basket leg with a horizon-differenced plateau-then-decay (band-pass) kernel in the same business clock, plus a 2-bar quiet-flicker leg, and scores +idio − basket − ½·quiet cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Trade-Quote Cross-Excitation Arrow Gated Displacement.

Mechanism: large mid-price revisions and large traded-volume bars are two event
streams.  If revision events statistically *excite* subsequent volume events
(quote-led / maker-led price formation), the mid moved first and flow arrives to
confirm it, so a fresh displacement continues.  If volume events excite
subsequent revision events (taker-led), the displacement is paid-for transient
impact and decays.  The excitation asymmetry is a slow structural gate; it is
cross-sectionally centred and multiplied by the fast, horizon-matched 6-bar
displacement, so the factor is a pure interaction with little unconditional
momentum / reversal exposure.

Falsified if the conditional sign of the 6-bar displacement is unrelated to the
excitation arrow (i.e. displacement reverts, or continues, regardless of which
channel leads).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, rank, stddev, ts_rank, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# causal helpers (trailing windows / positive lags only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row robust standardisation (median / MAD with std fallback)."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    return dev.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _cross_excitation_arrow(
    s_move: pd.DataFrame,
    s_act: pd.DataFrame,
    lags: tuple,
    n: int,
    min_events: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Hawkes-style cross-excitation asymmetry between two event streams.

    Counts, inside a trailing n-bar window, how many activity events are
    preceded (by 1..K bars) by a move event, minus how many move events are
    preceded by an activity event, normalised by the count expected under
    independence  K * N_move * N_act / n.  Positive => moves lead flow
    (quote/maker-led); negative => flow leads moves (taker-led impact).
    Causal: only positive lags and trailing sums.
    """
    fm = s_move.astype(float)
    fa = s_act.astype(float)

    pair_ma = None   # activity now, move earlier
    pair_am = None   # move now, activity earlier
    for k in lags:
        a_after_m = fa * delay(fm, k)
        m_after_a = fm * delay(fa, k)
        pair_ma = a_after_m if pair_ma is None else pair_ma + a_after_m
        pair_am = m_after_a if pair_am is None else pair_am + m_after_a

    c_ma = ts_sum(pair_ma, n)
    c_am = ts_sum(pair_am, n)
    n_m = ts_sum(fm, n)
    n_a = ts_sum(fa, n)

    expect = (float(len(lags)) * n_m * n_a / float(n)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    arrow = (c_ma - c_am) / expect
    arrow = arrow.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    enough = (n_m >= min_events) & (n_a >= min_events)
    return arrow.where(enough)


@register_factor
class CrossExcitationArrowGatedFastDisplacement(BaseFactor):
    """Continue the fresh move where quotes excite flow, fade it where flow excites quotes."""

    factor_id = "cross_excitation_arrow_gated_fast_displacement"
    name = "Trade-Quote Cross-Excitation Arrow Gated Displacement"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectionally centred rank of a per-name Hawkes-style cross-excitation "
        "asymmetry between large-|return| events and large-volume events (lags 1-3 "
        "bars, 240-bar trailing window), multiplied by the cross-sectional robust "
        "z-score of the volatility-normalised last-6-bar displacement."
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # --- parameters ------------------------------------------------------
    _EVENT_WIN = 240      # trailing window defining local event thresholds / counts
    _EVENT_Q = 0.80       # top-20% of own recent history counts as an "event"
    _LAGS = (1, 2, 3)     # 10-30s excitation kernel
    _MIN_EVENTS = 8.0     # minimum events per stream for a usable arrow
    _DISP_WIN = 6         # horizon-matched displacement window
    _SIGMA_WIN = 120      # trailing per-name return scale

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        vol = volume.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = _log_returns(close)

        # ---- event streams ------------------------------------------------
        # "move" events: |return| in the top tail of the name's own recent history
        mag = ret.abs().fillna(0.0)
        move_pct = ts_rank(mag, self._EVENT_WIN)
        s_move = move_pct >= self._EVENT_Q

        # "activity" events: traded volume in the top tail of its own recent history
        act_pct = ts_rank(vol, self._EVENT_WIN)
        s_act = act_pct >= self._EVENT_Q

        arrow = _cross_excitation_arrow(
            s_move, s_act, self._LAGS, self._EVENT_WIN, self._MIN_EVENTS
        )

        # slow, cross-sectionally centred, bounded gate in [-1, +1]
        gate = (rank(arrow) - 0.5) * 2.0
        gate = gate.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- fast horizon-matched displacement ----------------------------
        sigma = stddev(ret.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        r = (ret / sigma).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        disp = ts_sum(r.fillna(0.0), self._DISP_WIN) / np.sqrt(float(self._DISP_WIN))
        disp = disp.where(sigma.notna())
        disp_z = _cs_robust_z(disp)

        # ---- pure interaction --------------------------------------------
        score = disp_z.fillna(0.0) * gate
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        score = score.where(close.notna())
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Trade-Quote Cross-Excitation Arrow Gated Displacement
programs.trading_idea: The parent's insight — displacement produced by quotes moving on their own persists, displacement paid for with aggressive volume decays — is a statement about *which channel excites which*, so it should be measured as an asymmetry between two point processes rather than accumulated over 30 bars (which is why the parent's edge only matured at 24 bars). For each name I treat large |mid-return| bars and large-volume bars as two marked event streams and estimate a Hawkes-style cross-excitation arrow: how often activity spikes follow quote-revision spikes within 1-3 bars versus the reverse, normalised by the independence expectation, so the statistic is a slow, structural property of the name's price-formation regime (maker-led vs taker-led). That slow gate then multiplies the *horizon-matched* 6-bar displacement: in maker-led names the fresh move is genuine repricing that later attracts confirming flow and continues over the next minute; in taker-led names it is transient impact and snaps back. Because the gate is cross-sectionally demeaned the factor carries almost no unconditional reversal/momentum exposure — it is pure interaction — and it is falsified if the conditional sign of 6-bar displacement is unrelated to (or ordered opposite to) the excitation arrow.
programs.description: Product of (i) the cross-sectionally centred rank of a per-name Hawkes-style cross-excitation asymmetry between large-|return| events and large-volume events at lags 1-3 bars over a 240-bar trailing window, and (ii) the cross-sectionally robust z-score of the volatility-normalised last-6-bar displacement.

programs.code:
"""Excursion-age front-loaded propagator relaxation of peer displacement.

Mechanism
---------
Transient price impact relaxes along a power-law propagator
G(t) = (1 + t / t0) ** (-beta).  For a fixed forecast window h the fraction of a
standing displacement that unwinds inside the window is

    g(a) = 1 - G(a + h) / G(a),

which is a strictly decreasing function of the excursion AGE a.  A displacement
that opened a few bars ago therefore delivers most of its relaxation inside a
60-second window, while an old displacement delivers only a small slice per bar
and its predictability shows up much further out.  A level-based peer-relative
reversion signal mixes all ages together and is consequently dominated by the
slow, old excursions - which is precisely why such signals peak at long
horizons.  Re-weighting the same displacement by g(age) horizon-matches it to the
fixed 6-bar offset.

Construction (all statistics causal: trailing windows and positive lags only)
1. Comparables in valuation space: static sector label crossed with the name's
   within-sector tercile of a slow blended log multiple (log P/B, log P/S), with
   fallback to the plain sector group when the fine cell is too thin.
2. Peer-relative log price q = log(close) - group median log(close); displacement
   dis = q - EWMA_30(q), vol-standardised by a 240-bar rolling sd and clipped.
3. Excursion age a = number of bars since |z| was last inside a small band around
   the anchor (or since the name last had valid data).
4. Propagator front-loading weight g(a) = 1 - G(a+6)/G(a), t0 = 4 bars,
   beta = 0.7.
5. Self-calibrated reversion coefficient kappa = 1 - trailing OLS beta of z_t on
   z_{t-6} over 480 bars, clipped and shrunk toward the cross-sectional mean
   (empirical-Bayes); kappa < 0 means the name has been trending, and the signal
   sign flips for it.
6. Signal = rank( -(kappa * z * g(a)) ) - 0.5.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None, industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _log_multiple(close: pd.DataFrame, per_share: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    denom = per_share.reindex_like(close)
    denom = denom.where(np.isfinite(denom) & (denom > 0.0))
    px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
    ratio = px / denom
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)

def _blend_multiples(close: pd.DataFrame, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], fields: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
    num = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    for field in fields:
        raw = data.get(field)
        if raw is None:
            continue
        ps = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        if ps.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            continue
        lm = _log_multiple(close, ps)
        good = lm.notna()
        if good.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            continue
        num = num.add(lm.fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
        den = den.add(good.astype(float), fill_value=0.0)
    den = den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return num / den

def _within_group_tercile(vs: pd.DataFrame, sec_arr: np.ndarray, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-coarse-group bucket (0..k-1) of a slow valuation coordinate."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vs.index, columns=vs.columns)
    for code in np.unique(sec_arr):
        sel = vs.columns[sec_arr == code]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        sub = vs[sel]
        r = sub.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        b = np.ceil(r * float(k)) - 1.0
        out[sel] = b.clip(0.0, float(k - 1))
    return out

def _group_median_count(vals: pd.DataFrame, codes: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-group median and live member count, broadcast to members."""
    V = vals.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    C = codes.reindex_like(vals).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    T, N = V.shape
    med = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros((T, N))
    finite_codes = C[np.isfinite(C)]
    uniq = np.unique(finite_codes) if finite_codes.size else np.array([])
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for c in uniq:
            mask = C == c
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            sub = np.where(mask, V, np.nan)
            gm = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1)
            gc = np.isfinite(sub).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            med[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gm[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
            cnt[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gc[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    return (med_df, cnt_df)

def _age_since_reset(cond: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bars since ``cond`` was last True (causal running-max of reset indices).

    If a name has never reset, the age equals the number of elapsed bars, which
    the propagator weight maps to a small number - the conservative choice.
    """
    arr = cond.to_numpy(dtype=bool)
    T, N = arr.shape
    ivec = np.arange(T, dtype=float)[:, None]
    marker = np.where(arr, np.broadcast_to(ivec, arr.shape), -1.0)
    last = np.maximum.accumulate(marker, axis=0)
    age = ivec - last
    return pd.DataFrame(age, index=cond.index, columns=cond.columns)

def _propagator_remaining(age: pd.DataFrame, h: int, t0: float, beta: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of a standing transient displacement that decays within h bars
    under G(t) = (1 + t / t0) ** (-beta), evaluated at the current age."""
    a = age.clip(lower=0.0)
    g_now = (1.0 + a / t0) ** (-beta)
    g_fwd = (1.0 + (a + float(h)) / t0) ** (-beta)
    g_now = g_now.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    frac = 1.0 - g_fwd / g_now
    return frac.clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class ExcursionAgeFrontloadedPropagatorPeerRelaxation(BaseFactor):
    """Peer displacement weighted by the propagator's 6-bar remaining decay."""
    factor_id = 'excursion_age_frontloaded_propagator_peer_relaxa'
    name = 'Excursion-age front-loaded propagator relaxation'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Log price demeaned against sector x valuation-tercile peers, detrended by its own 30-bar peer-relative anchor and vol-standardised, then negated and weighted by the power-law propagator's remaining-decay fraction over the next 6 bars at the current excursion age and by a shrunk self-calibrated 6-bar reversion coefficient."
    window_length = 600
    inputs = ['close', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 3
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _ANCHOR_HL = 30.0
    _VAL_HL = 600.0
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _AGE_BAND = 0.5
    _AGE_CAP = 240.0
    _T0 = 4.0
    _BETA = 0.7
    _BETA_WIN = 480
    _KAPPA_LO = -0.4
    _KAPPA_HI = 1.2
    _SHRINK = 0.6
    _KAPPA_PRIOR = 0.2

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        uniq_lab = list(pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()))
        code_map = {lab: float(i) for i, lab in enumerate(uniq_lab)}
        sec_arr = np.array([code_map[labels[c]] for c in cols], dtype=float)
        sec_frame = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(sec_arr[None, :], len(idx), axis=0), index=idx, columns=cols)
        val = _blend_multiples(close, data, ['bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare'])
        if val.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            ter = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vs = val.ewm(halflife=self._VAL_HL, min_periods=1, adjust=False).mean()
            ter = _within_group_tercile(vs, sec_arr, self._K)
        codes_fine = sec_frame * 10.0 + ter.fillna(9.0)
        med_f, cnt_f = _group_median_count(p, codes_fine)
        med_c, cnt_c = _group_median_count(p, sec_frame)
        fine_ok = cnt_f.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS)
        med = med_f.where(fine_ok, med_c)
        cnt = cnt_f.where(fine_ok, cnt_c)
        q = (p - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        anchor = q.ewm(halflife=self._ANCHOR_HL, min_periods=15, adjust=False).mean()
        dis = q - anchor
        sd = dis.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (dis / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z))
        at_anchor = (z.abs() < self._AGE_BAND) | z.isna()
        age = _age_since_reset(at_anchor.fillna(True)).clip(0.0, self._AGE_CAP)
        g_front = _propagator_remaining(age, self.prediction_horizon, self._T0, self._BETA)
        z_fill = z.where(np.isfinite(z))
        phi = rolling_beta(z_fill, z_fill.shift(self.prediction_horizon), self._BETA_WIN)
        kappa_raw = (1.0 - phi).clip(self._KAPPA_LO, self._KAPPA_HI)
        kappa_raw = kappa_raw.where(np.isfinite(kappa_raw))
        rowmean = kappa_raw.mean(axis=1)
        rm = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(rowmean.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        rm = rm.where(np.isfinite(rm), self._KAPPA_PRIOR)
        kappa = self._SHRINK * kappa_raw.fillna(rm) + (1.0 - self._SHRINK) * rm
        signal = -(kappa * z * g_front)
        valid = z.notna() & g_front.notna() & kappa.notna()
        signal = signal.where(valid)
        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Excursion-age front-loaded propagator relaxation of peer displacement
programs.trading_idea: Bouchaud-style transient impact relaxes along a power-law propagator G(t)=(1+t/t0)^-beta, so the *fraction* of a displacement that unwinds inside a fixed 6-bar window depends almost entirely on the AGE of the excursion, not on its level: a gap that opened 3 bars ago sheds ~45% of its transient component in the next minute, while a gap that has been open 30+ bars sheds only ~10% (its remaining decay is spread over many minutes, which is exactly why the parent's level-based peer displacement had its IC peak at 24 bars rather than at 6). The child therefore scales the negated peer-relative displacement by the propagator's *remaining-decay-within-6-bars* fraction, evaluated at each name's own measured excursion age (bars since the peer-relative residual last sat at its anchor), and by an empirical-Bayes-shrunk, self-calibrated per-name 6-bar reversion coefficient kappa = 1 - beta_OLS(z_t on z_{t-6}), which lets genuinely trending names keep their sign instead of being forcibly faded. The edge persists because harvesting the front-loaded slice requires fast turnover for a small per-event dollar profit while warehousing inventory in a name whose remaining relaxation is only probabilistically identifiable, and because the arbitrageurs who do trade this relative-value gap are compensated on the slow (multi-minute) leg, not the first minute. Falsified if (a) replacing the age weight g(age) by a constant leaves the 6-bar IC unchanged, (b) old-excursion names (top age tercile) revert at 6 bars as strongly as young ones, or (c) the IC term structure still peaks at 24 bars rather than flattening/peaking near 6.
programs.description: Log price demeaned against sector x valuation-tercile peers and detrended by its own 30-bar peer-relative anchor, vol-standardised, then negated and weighted by (i) the power-law propagator's remaining-decay fraction over the next 6 bars evaluated at the current excursion age and (ii) a shrunk, self-calibrated per-name 6-bar reversion coefficient.

programs.code:
"""Horizon-6 closure-calibrated kernel response deficit.

Mechanism
---------
Step 1 (kept from the parent, which passed every gate): let m_t be the robust
common market return (cross-sectional median) and z_t its trailing z-score.  A
name's response to common shocks is a distributed lag

    y_t = sum_{j=0..J} theta_j z_{t-j} + e_t ,     y = r / sigma_r ,

estimated by trailing local projections on the LARGE-shock subsample
x_t = z_t * 1{|z_t| > c}, where news transmission rather than bid-ask bounce
dominates.  Applying the kernel to the observed market path gives the implied
per-bar response yhat_t, the per-bar shortfall gap_t = yhat_t - y_t, and an
event-anchored owed stock D_t = sum of gap since the last genuine common shock.

Step 2 (the child's new mechanism): the parent ranked D_t itself, so its
cross-section was dominated by names whose backlog drains over minutes -- its IC
peaked far beyond the fixed 6-bar forecast offset.  Here we convert the owed
stock into the part expected to be *delivered within the next 6 bars* by
self-calibrating, causally, the horizon-6 delivery coefficient

    beta_i = Cov_n( delivered_t , D_{t-h} ) / ( Var_n(D_{t-h}) + ridge ) ,
    delivered_t = - sum_{k=0..h-1} gap_{t-k} ,      h = 6 ,

which uses only information available at t (D_{t-h} was known at t-h, the
delivery is realised by t).  beta_i is blended with the cross-sectional prior
using its own regression R^2 (precision weighting), so noisy names collapse to
the pooled delivery speed instead of injecting noise.  The traded object is the
expected 6-bar delivery beta_i * D_t, damped where own-name relative volume is
high (a volume-backed residual is idiosyncratic news that persists, not a
mechanical repricing gap that closes).

Falsifiable: if the self-calibrated delivery coefficient carries information,
the child's IC at the fixed 6-bar offset must exceed the parent's and the IC
profile must shift toward the short end; otherwise it will not.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading towards its cross-sectional mean (empirical Bayes)."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _bars_since(flag: pd.Series, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Bars elapsed since the last True in flag (causal forward fill only)."""
    s = pd.Series(np.arange(len(flag.index), dtype=float), index=flag.index)
    last = s.where(flag.to_numpy()).ffill()
    out = (s - last).clip(0.0, cap)
    return out.fillna(cap)


def _rmean(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, nmin: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.rolling(int(n), min_periods=int(nmin)).mean()


@register_factor
class H6ClosureCalibratedKernelResponseDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Owed kernel response, scaled by a self-calibrated 6-bar delivery coefficient."""

    factor_id = 'h6_closure_calibrated_kernel_response_deficit'
    name = 'Horizon-6 closure-calibrated kernel response deficit'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Event-anchored shortfall of the realised vol-normalised path versus a trailing '
        'large-shock local-projection response kernel, multiplied by a causally '
        'self-calibrated, precision-blended horizon-6 delivery coefficient (trailing '
        'regression of realised 6-bar delivery on the 6-bar-lagged owed stock), damped '
        'where own-name relative volume is high.'
    )
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _J = 6                 # lags of the response kernel (bars)
    _n = 180               # trailing kernel estimation window
    _nmin = 80
    _nb = 200              # trailing window for the delivery-coefficient regression
    _nbmin = 70
    _vol_win = 180
    _vol_min = 60
    _thresh = 1.5          # |z| threshold defining a common shock
    _Lmax = 24             # cap on the event-anchored accumulation window
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.3
    _breg = 0.20           # ridge on the delivery regression (cross-sectional scale)
    _r0 = 0.02             # precision-blend prior strength on R^2
    _h = 6                 # delivery horizon == prediction horizon

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        T, N = len(idx), len(cols)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        need = int(self._nmin) + int(self._nbmin) + int(self._J) + int(self._h) + 5
        if T < need or N < 3:
            return zero

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        sig = (ret.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)

        # --- common factor: robust cross-sectional median return -------------------
        mkt = ret.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))
        shock = z.abs() > float(self._thresh)
        xs = z.where(shock, 0.0)
        base = (z * z).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()

        # --- event-conditional local projections: theta_j ---------------------------
        yhat = None
        for j in range(int(self._J) + 1):
            xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
            den = (xl * xl).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
            num = (y0.mul(xl, axis=0)
                   .rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
            denom = (den + float(self._ridge) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._shrink)).fillna(0.0)
            contrib = th.mul(z.shift(j).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            yhat = contrib if yhat is None else yhat.add(contrib)

        gap = (yhat - y).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        g0 = gap.fillna(0.0).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        cum = g0.cumsum()

        # --- anchor the accumulation at the last common shock ----------------------
        prev = cum.shift(1)
        mask = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], N, axis=1),
                            index=idx, columns=cols)
        anchor = prev.where(mask).ffill()
        alt = cum.shift(int(self._Lmax))
        age = _bars_since(shock, float(self._Lmax))
        use_evt = (age < float(self._Lmax)).to_numpy()
        anchor_eff = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(use_evt[:, None], anchor.to_numpy(), alt.to_numpy()),
            index=idx, columns=cols)
        owed = (cum - anchor_eff).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-20.0, 20.0)
        nbars = (age + 1.0).clip(1.0, float(self._Lmax))
        owed_n = owed.div(np.sqrt(nbars), axis=0).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # --- self-calibrated horizon-6 delivery coefficient ------------------------
        h = int(self._h)
        nb, nbmin = int(self._nb), int(self._nbmin)
        delivered = (-g0.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()).clip(-20.0, 20.0)
        X = owed.shift(h)
        Y = delivered
        both = X.notna() & Y.notna()
        Xf = X.where(both)
        Yf = Y.where(both)
        mx = _rmean(Xf, nb, nbmin)
        my = _rmean(Yf, nb, nbmin)
        mxy = _rmean(Xf * Yf, nb, nbmin)
        mxx = _rmean(Xf * Xf, nb, nbmin)
        myy = _rmean(Yf * Yf, nb, nbmin)
        cxy = mxy - mx * my
        vxx = (mxx - mx * mx).clip(lower=0.0)
        vyy = (myy - my * my).clip(lower=0.0)

        scale = vxx.median(axis=1)
        denb = vxx.add(float(self._breg) * scale, axis=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = (cxy / denb).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.5, 2.0)
        r2 = (cxy * cxy) / (vxx * vyy + _EPS)
        r2 = r2.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        beta_bar = beta.mean(axis=1)
        w = r2 / (r2 + float(self._r0))
        beta_eff = beta.fillna(0.0).mul(w).add((1.0 - w).mul(beta_bar, axis=0), axis=0)
        beta_eff = beta_eff.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.6, 1.6)

        expected_delivery = (beta_eff * owed_n).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # --- damping: volume-backed residuals are news, not repricing gaps ---------
        vol_tr = data.get('volume')
        if vol_tr is None:
            damp = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = (vol_tr.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
                 .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0))
            rv = ts_mean(v, h) / ts_mean(v, int(self._n)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            damp = 1.5 - rank(rv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).fillna(0.5)

        alive = ret.notna().rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        raw = (expected_delivery * damp).where(alive)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return (score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
                .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0))
programs.name: Horizon-6 closure-calibrated kernel response deficit
programs.trading_idea: The parent measured the right object (how much of its own habitual impulse-response a name still owes after a common shock) but ranked the raw owed stock, so its cross-section was dominated by names whose backlog drains over minutes — hence IC peaking at 24 bars, not at the fixed 6-bar offset. The child converts the owed stock into the amount expected to be *delivered inside the next 6 bars* by self-calibrating, per name and causally, the empirical horizon-6 delivery coefficient: a trailing regression of realised 6-bar delivery (minus the summed shortfall over the last 6 bars) on the deficit stock that existed 6 bars earlier, precision-blended with the cross-sectional prior via its own R-squared. Names whose backlog historically drains fast get amplified, slow-draining or non-converging names get shrunk or sign-flipped, so the signal is horizon-matched by construction rather than by luck. The edge persists because the delivery speed is a liquidity-provision property (spread, depth replenishment, participation) that is name-specific, non-stationary and must be re-estimated event-conditionally, and closing the gap means supplying liquidity into sub-minute transient impact where capacity is capped.
programs.description: Estimates each name's response kernel to large common market shocks by trailing shock-selected local projections, accumulates the vol-normalised shortfall of the realised path versus the kernel-implied path since the last common shock, then multiplies that owed stock by a causally self-calibrated horizon-6 delivery coefficient (precision-blended trailing regression of realised 6-bar delivery on the 6-bar-lagged deficit) and ranks the result cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Rank-CUSUM retracement liveness wedge: live slicing versus spent impact.

Mechanism
---------
The parent factor (Wilcoxon drift x Mood compression) showed that a rank-space
location shift carries a small positive six-bar IC, but its dispersion gate
added almost nothing marginal.  The reason is structural: once every increment
is replaced by its percentile inside the name's own trailing distribution, a
single violent tick can contribute at most 0.5 to the cumulative sum, so the
rank-CUSUM path is *already* jump-capped -- it grows only when many increments
are one-sided, i.e. exactly the footprint of a sliced metaorder
(Lillo-Farmer order-splitting autocorrelation).  A separate Mood scale gate is
therefore largely redundant with the location leg and mostly injects noise.

What the parent could NOT see is whether the pressure is still arriving.  Two
names with the same 24-bar rank drift are in completely different states:

*   the rank-CUSUM is sitting at its own within-window running extreme -- the
    parent order is unfinished, child orders keep hitting the same side, and
    the repricing continues over the next few bars;
*   the rank-CUSUM peaked earlier in the window and has since drifted back --
    flow has stopped, depth is refilling, and the transient part of the
    displacement is relaxing under the propagator, so the residual level is a
    reversal candidate rather than a continuation candidate.

So the new conditioning variable is a Page/CUSUM style *retracement fraction*:
(distance of the terminal CUSUM value below its directional extreme) divided by
that extreme.  Zero = live grind, near one = spent grind.  Signal = cross-
sectionally centred rank-drift x liveness gate, shrunk toward neutral for names
whose mid barely moved (where the rank transform degenerates into ties).

Falsifiable: if the six-bar cross-sectional IC of this product is zero or
negative -- i.e. if retraced rank-drifts continue and un-retraced ones revert --
the live-slicing / transient-relaxation reading is wrong.  Uses no volume, so it
stays orthogonal to the flow-imbalance family; every statistic is a trailing
rolling window, so the value at bar t uses only bars <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_increments(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar-to-bar log price increments, sanitised."""
    lvl = close.astype(float).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inc = np.log(lvl).diff()
    return inc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _uniformize(inc: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Probability-integral transform of each increment against its own trailing
    n-bar empirical distribution.  Causal: ts_rank looks back n bars only."""
    u = ts_rank(inc, n).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return u.clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _rank_cusum_state(u: pd.DataFrame, w: int) -> tuple:
    """Trailing w-bar rank-CUSUM path statistics.

    With c = u - 1/2 and C its running cumulative sum, the partial sums of the
    last w increments are S_j = C_{t-w+j} - C_{t-w}, j = 0..w (S_0 = 0).  We
    return the terminal value T = S_w and the directional extreme
    E = max_j S_j (if T >= 0) or -min_j S_j (if T < 0), both non-negative in the
    drift direction.  Only rolling max / min / shift are used, so the value at t
    depends on bars <= t exclusively.
    """
    valid = u.notna()
    c = (u - 0.5).where(valid, 0.0)
    cum = c.cumsum()
    base = cum.shift(w)

    term = cum - base
    hi = (cum.rolling(w, min_periods=w).max() - base).clip(lower=0.0)
    lo = (cum.rolling(w, min_periods=w).min() - base).clip(upper=0.0)

    ext = hi.where(term >= 0.0, -lo)          # extreme measured along the drift
    coverage = valid.astype(float).rolling(w, min_periods=w).mean()

    term = term.where(coverage >= 0.9)
    ext = ext.where(coverage >= 0.9)
    return term, ext


@register_factor
class RankCusumRetracementLivenessGrindWedge(BaseFactor):
    """Jump-capped rank drift conditioned on CUSUM-path liveness."""

    factor_id = "rank_cusum_retracement_liveness_grind_wedge"
    name = "Rank-CUSUM retracement liveness wedge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of (centred rank of the 24-bar rank-CUSUM drift of "
        "increments uniformized against their trailing 120-bar own-name "
        "distribution) times (a liveness gate: +1 when the CUSUM terminal value "
        "sits at its within-window directional extreme, -1 when it has retraced "
        "far from it), shrunk by the fraction of moving bars."
    )
    window_length = 160
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _ref = 120     # ~20 minutes: own-name reference increment distribution
    _win = 24      # ~4 minutes: rank-CUSUM path window

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)

        inc = _log_increments(close)
        u = _uniformize(inc, self._ref)

        term, ext = _rank_cusum_state(u, self._win)

        # Null scale of the terminal CUSUM: std = sqrt(w/12).  Used as a floor so
        # that near-zero drifts give a neutral (uninformative) retracement.
        eps = 0.25 * float(np.sqrt(self._win / 12.0))
        retrace = ((ext - term.abs()) / (ext + eps)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        retrace = retrace.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # Staleness trust: rank transforms degenerate when the mid barely moves.
        moving = (inc.abs() > 0.0).astype(float).where(inc.notna())
        trust = moving.rolling(self._win, min_periods=self._win).mean().clip(0.0, 1.0)

        loc_c = 2.0 * rank(term) - 1.0                 # centred jump-capped drift
        gate = 1.0 - 2.0 * rank(retrace)               # +1 live, -1 spent

        raw = loc_c * gate * trust.fillna(0.0)
        raw = raw.where(term.notna() & retrace.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Rank-CUSUM retracement liveness wedge
programs.trading_idea: Uniformizing each bar increment against the name's own trailing 120-bar increment distribution caps the contribution of any single violent tick at 0.5, so the cumulative sum of centred ranks (a rank-CUSUM / Page change-point path) measures *how many* increments were unusually one-sided rather than how large the biggest one was — it is by construction a grind detector and needs no separate dispersion gate. The genuinely new conditioning variable is the CUSUM path's *retracement from its own within-window extreme*: a metaorder still being sliced leaves the rank-CUSUM sitting at its running extreme (pressure is live and keeps repricing), whereas a displacement whose transient impact is already relaxing leaves the CUSUM well below its extreme even though the net level is still positive. Interacting cross-sectionally centred rank-drift with the retracement state therefore separates live grinds (continuation) from spent grinds (relaxation), which the parent's Mood dispersion gate could not do — it only measured increment scale, not whether pressure was still arriving. The edge persists because identifying live slicing requires the *shape and recency* of the rank path, not the size of the move; the slicing agent cannot front-run its own child orders, and one-minute net-of-spread capacity is far too small for a large arbitrageur.
programs.description: Uniformizes log increments against their own trailing 120-bar distribution, forms the 24-bar cumulative sum of centred ranks (jump-capped rank-CUSUM drift), and multiplies the cross-sectionally centred drift by a liveness gate equal to +1 when the CUSUM terminal value sits at its within-window extreme and -1 when it has retraced far from it, shrunk by the fraction of moving bars.

programs.code:
"""Increment-shape switched peer displacement: fade overshoots, ride grinds.

Mechanism
---------
A displacement from a valuation-comparable peer basket can be produced two ways
with opposite six-bar futures:

1.  A sliced metaorder (Lillo-Farmer): execution algorithms build the gap out of
    many *compressed* increments -- small relative to the name's own recent
    peer-residual increment distribution -- and keep arriving, so the gap keeps
    widening (continuation).
