2.  A liquidity-withdrawal overshoot: the same gap is built from a few increments
    drawn from the tails of that distribution; under the transient-impact
    propagator the displacement relaxes as depth refills, and that relaxation is
    front-loaded, i.e. it lands inside a sixty-second window (reversion).

The *level* of the peer displacement cannot separate the two states; the *shape*
of the increments that built it can.  So the child estimates both objects in
peer-relative space and lets the shape state switch the sign of the trade:

*   Comparables: static sector label crossed with the within-sector tercile of a
    slow blended log multiple (log P/B, log P/S); thin cells fall back to sector.
*   Peer-residual level q = log(close) - group median log(close); displacement
    z = q - EWMA_60(q), standardised by a 240-bar rolling sd and clipped.
*   Peer-residual increments dq = q.diff(), uniformized by their percentile in the
    trailing 120-bar own-name distribution (u in [0,1]).  mean(u,6) - 1/2 is a
    Wilcoxon rank-sum location shift (rank-based, hence automatically
    volatility-normalised); var(u,18) - 1/12 is a centred Mood-type dispersion
    statistic (negative = compressed grind, positive = tail-heavy overshoot).
*   Regime weight w = cross-sectional rank of the Mood statistic.  With weight w
    the signal fades the displacement, but only where the recent location shift is
    *concordant* with it (the gap is fresh, so relaxation is still owed); with
    weight 1-w it rides the peer-relative drift, damped by the remaining room
    before the peer anchor.

Every statistic is a trailing rolling window or a positive lag: the value at bar t
uses only bars <= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, sign, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None, industry: pd.DataFrame | None) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _log_multiple(close: pd.DataFrame, per_share: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    denom = per_share.reindex_like(close)
    denom = denom.where(np.isfinite(denom) & (denom > 0.0))
    px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
    ratio = px / denom
    ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
    return np.log(ratio)

def _blend_multiples(close: pd.DataFrame, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], fields: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
    num = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    for field in fields:
        raw = data.get(field)
        if raw is None:
            continue
        ps = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        if ps.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            continue
        lm = _log_multiple(close, ps)
        good = lm.notna()
        if good.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            continue
        num = num.add(lm.fillna(0.0), fill_value=0.0)
        den = den.add(good.astype(float), fill_value=0.0)
    den = den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return num / den

def _within_group_tercile(vs: pd.DataFrame, sec_arr: np.ndarray, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-coarse-group bucket (0..k-1) of a slow valuation coordinate."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vs.index, columns=vs.columns)
    for code in np.unique(sec_arr):
        sel = vs.columns[sec_arr == code]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        sub = vs[sel]
        r = sub.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        b = np.ceil(r * float(k)) - 1.0
        out[sel] = b.clip(0.0, float(k - 1))
    return out

def _group_median_count(vals: pd.DataFrame, codes: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Per-bar within-group median and live member count, broadcast to members."""
    V = vals.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    C = codes.reindex_like(vals).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    T, N = V.shape
    med = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros((T, N))
    finite_codes = C[np.isfinite(C)]
    uniq = np.unique(finite_codes) if finite_codes.size else np.array([])
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for c in uniq:
            mask = C == c
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            sub = np.where(mask, V, np.nan)
            gm = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1)
            gc = np.isfinite(sub).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            med[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gm[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
            cnt[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gc[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    return (med_df, cnt_df)

def _uniformize(inc: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Probability-integral transform of each increment against its own trailing
    n-bar empirical distribution (percentile in [0, 1]).  Causal."""
    u = ts_rank(inc, n)
    u = u.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return u.clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class IncrementShapeSwitchedPeerDisplacementFadeRide(BaseFactor):
    """Peer displacement whose trade sign is switched by increment-shape state."""
    factor_id = 'increment_shape_switched_peer_displacement_fade_'
    name = 'Increment-shape switched peer displacement (fade vs ride)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Peer-residual log price (sector x valuation-tercile comparables) gives a vol-standardised displacement from its own 60-bar anchor plus peer-residual increments; those increments are uniformized against their trailing 120-bar own-name distribution to form a 6-bar Wilcoxon location shift and an 18-bar Mood dispersion state, whose cross-sectional rank convexly blends fading a freshly built displacement (tail-heavy overshoot) with riding a compressed peer-relative grind (live metaorder), damped by room to the anchor.'
    window_length = 360
    inputs = ['close', 'bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 3
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _ANCHOR_HL = 60.0
    _VAL_HL = 600.0
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _REF = 120
    _FAST = 6
    _STATE = 18

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        uniq_lab = list(pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()))
        code_map = {lab: float(i) for i, lab in enumerate(uniq_lab)}
        sec_arr = np.array([code_map[labels[c]] for c in cols], dtype=float)
        sec_frame = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(sec_arr[None, :], len(idx), axis=0), index=idx, columns=cols)
        val = _blend_multiples(close, data, ['bookValuePerShare', 'revenuePerShare'])
        if val.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            ter = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vs = val.ewm(halflife=self._VAL_HL, min_periods=1, adjust=False).mean()
            ter = _within_group_tercile(vs, sec_arr, self._K)
        codes_fine = sec_frame * 10.0 + ter.fillna(9.0)
        med_f, cnt_f = _group_median_count(p, codes_fine)
        med_c, cnt_c = _group_median_count(p, sec_frame)
        fine_ok = cnt_f.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS)
        med = med_f.where(fine_ok, med_c)
        cnt = cnt_f.where(fine_ok, cnt_c)
        q = (p - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        anchor = q.ewm(halflife=self._ANCHOR_HL, min_periods=20, adjust=False).mean()
        dis = q - anchor
        sd = dis.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (dis / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z))
        dq = q.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        u = _uniformize(dq, self._REF)
        loc = ts_mean(u, self._FAST) - 0.5
        disp = (u.rolling(self._STATE, min_periods=self._STATE).var() - 1.0 / 12.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lc = (2.0 * rank(loc) - 1.0).where(loc.notna())
        zc = (2.0 * rank(z) - 1.0).where(z.notna())
        w = rank(disp).where(disp.notna())
        fresh = (sign(zc) * lc).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        fade = -zc * fresh
        room = (1.0 - sign(lc) * zc).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0) * 0.5
        ride = lc * room
        raw = w * fade + (1.0 - w) * ride
        raw = raw.where(zc.notna() & lc.notna() & w.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        out = rank(raw) - 0.5
        out = out.where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Increment-shape switched peer displacement (fade vs ride)
programs.trading_idea: Parent A knows *where* a name stands relative to its valuation-comparable peers but not *why* it got there, so it has to wait passively for relaxation — which is why its edge only matures at 24 bars. Parent B knows *how* a displacement was built (compressed increments = a live sliced metaorder; tail-heavy increments = a liquidity-withdrawal overshoot) but measures that drift on raw returns, where market-wide moves swamp the relative-value content. The child applies Parent B's nonparametric Wilcoxon location shift and Mood scale-compression statistic to the *peer-residual* log increments of Parent A's sector x valuation-tercile comparable basket, then uses the compression state as a regime switch on the displacement: dispersed (overshoot) names get the freshly-built peer displacement faded, compressed (grind) names get the peer-relative drift ridden, damped by how much room is left before the peer anchor. The interaction is the edge neither has alone: the shape statistic converts A's slow, state-ambiguous relative-value gap into an immediately actionable, horizon-matched signal, while the peer residualisation gives B's rank-drift a genuine convergence anchor instead of a naked directional bet.
programs.description: Log price demeaned against sector x valuation-tercile peers gives a peer-residual level (deviation from its own 60-bar anchor, vol-standardised) and peer-residual increments; the increments are uniformized against their own trailing 120-bar distribution to form a 6-bar Wilcoxon location shift and an 18-bar Mood dispersion state, and the cross-sectional dispersion rank convexly blends a fade of the freshly-built displacement with a ride of the compressed peer-relative grind.

programs.code:
"""Conversion-switched marked-Hawkes excursion vs swept displacement.

Mechanism
---------
Two channels are measured on ONE exponential kernel (halflife 3 bars):

  (i)  a *marked excursion intensity* -- each bar's range beyond its open/close
       endpoints, split into upper and lower parts, weighted by a square-root
       impact mark sqrt(volume/ADV) and exponentially accumulated.  Its shrunk
       imbalance is the slicing / self-excitation channel: aggression that
       probed a side and is still arriving.

  (ii) a *net displacement intensity* -- the market-demeaned (idiosyncratic)
       log return accumulated with the same kernel, in units of the name's own
       trailing residual volatility.  That is path which was actually converted
       into a permanent-looking move, i.e. transient impact of a swept level.

The conversion ratio

    c = |displacement intensity| / (|displacement intensity| + marked excursion
                                    path intensity + prior)

is computable only from both channels jointly.  Low c => the book absorbed the
probes and no net move was realised, so go WITH the probed side.  High c => the
path was fully swept into displacement, so go AGAINST it.  The switch uses the
cross-sectional rank of c so the polarity mix is well dispersed every bar and
insensitive to the absolute calibration of the two units.

The excursion channel is cross-sectionally residualised against trailing range
position, so a plain 'close sits low in its range' statistic cannot masquerade
as slicing persistence.  Everything is scaled by a saturating gate in absorbed
volume relative to ADV, since neither mechanism exists without traded size.

All statistics are trailing (ewm / rolling / positive lags) or purely
contemporaneous cross-sectional, hence causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, ts_max, ts_min
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_TINY = 1e-12

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _xs_resid1(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise (cross-sectional) OLS residual of y on [1, x].

    Contemporaneous per row -- uses no future information.  Closed form from row
    moments, fully vectorised.
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    cnt = mask.sum(axis=1)
    Y = y.where(mask)
    X = x.where(mask)
    Yc = Y.sub(Y.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    Xc = X.sub(X.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    sxx = (Xc * Xc).sum(axis=1)
    sxy = (Xc * Yc).sum(axis=1)
    ok = (sxx.abs() > 1e-10) & (cnt >= 8)
    beta = (sxy / sxx.where(ok)).fillna(0.0)
    resid = Yc - Xc.mul(beta, axis=0)
    return resid.where(mask)

@register_factor
class ConversionSwitchedMarkedHawkesExcursion(BaseFactor):
    """Switch marked-excursion continuation against swept-displacement snapback."""
    factor_id = 'hawkes_conversion_switched_marked_excursion_purg'
    name = 'Conversion-switched marked-Hawkes excursion vs swept displacement'
    category = 'microstructure'

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)

        up_abs = (hi - hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_abs = (lo_end - lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        up_frac = (up_abs / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        dn_frac = (dn_abs / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        base = adv(volume, self._adv_win).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        base = base.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        lam_up = (mark * up_frac).fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=self._halflife, min_periods=5).mean()
        lam_dn = (mark * dn_frac).fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=self._halflife, min_periods=5).mean()
        asym = (lam_up - lam_dn) / (lam_up + lam_dn + self._shrink)
        asym = asym.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)
        resid = ret.sub(mkt, axis=0)
        sigma = resid.rolling(self._sig_win, min_periods=self._sig_min).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        d_int = resid.fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=self._halflife, min_periods=5).mean()

        path = path.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)

        hi_w = ts_max(hi, self._rp_win)

        a_rel = (v_int / base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        gate = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._gate_scale)
        raw = gate * ((1.0 - w) * chan_e - w * chan_d)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw.where(close.notna())) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

"""Disjoint-window conversion efficiency switches the fresh impulse.

Mechanism
---------
The *state* is book permeability, estimated as a path-conversion efficiency

    c = |net residual displacement| / (|net residual displacement|
                                       + probed wick path on size-bearing bars)

measured over a 30-bar window that ENDS 3 bars before the present, so it is
mechanically decoupled from the impulse it will be asked to sign, then z-scored
against the name's own 240-bar history (the absolute level of c depends on tick
size and bar sparsity, not on liquidity) and centred cross-sectionally.

The *trigger* is fast: a decay-weighted, beta-residual displacement over the
last 3 bars expressed in the name's own robust grid quantum (a low quantile of
non-zero absolute returns), with a dead zone of half a quantum so that pure
discreteness / bounce noise does not fire.

High permeability (high c) => thin depth, a fresh impulse is mostly transient
impact and snaps back once flow pauses => trade AGAINST the impulse.  Low
permeability (low c) => a deep, absorptive book only moves when a persistent
metaorder is consuming real size => trade WITH the impulse.  Everything is
scaled by a saturating gate in volume absorbed over the trigger window relative
to average bar volume, because neither branch exists without traded size.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows or positive lags, hence causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_TINY = 1e-12

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)

@register_factor
class DisjointConversionEfficiencyGainSwitchedImpulse(BaseFactor):
    """Lagged path-conversion efficiency signs a fresh grid-scaled impulse."""
    factor_id = 'disjoint_conversion_efficiency_gain_switched_imp'
    name = 'Disjoint-window conversion efficiency switches the fresh impulse'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of (centred, lagged path-conversion-efficiency state) x (dead-zoned 3-bar beta-residual impulse in grid-quantum units), scaled by a saturating absorbed-volume gate: continuation for absorptive books, reversal for permeable ones.'
    window_length = 320
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _state_win = 30
    _state_lag = 3
    _z_window = 240
    _vol_window = 60
    _trig_win = 3
    _dead = 0.5
    _trig_scale = 2.0
    _q_window = 240
    _q_min = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _adv_window = 240
    _absorb_scale = 1.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        absr = ret.abs()
        nz = absr.where(absr > _TINY)
        q = nz.rolling(self._q_window, min_periods=self._q_min).quantile(0.2)
        q = q.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        mkt_bd = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt_bd, self._beta_window)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (ret - beta * mkt_bd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lo_all = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        hi_all = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        l_hi = np.log(hi_all)
        l_lo = np.log(lo_all)
        l_hi_end = np.log(_pair_max(open_, close).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        l_lo_end = np.log(_pair_min(open_, close).replace(0.0, np.nan))
        up_w = (l_hi - l_hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_w = (l_lo_end - l_lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        wick = (up_w + dn_w).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        med = volume.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=20).median()
        size_bar = ((volume > med) & med.notna() & volume.notna()).astype(float)
        r_sum = ts_sum(resid.fillna(0.0), self._state_win).shift(self._state_lag)
        w_sum = ts_sum((wick * size_bar).fillna(0.0), self._state_win).shift(self._state_lag)
        r_abs = r_sum.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        w_sum = w_sum.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
        prior = (2.0 * q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        c = (r_abs / (r_abs + w_sum + prior)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        c = c.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        zc = ts_zscore(c, self._z_window).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        w_state = 1.0 - 2.0 * rank(zc)
        w_state = w_state.where(zc.notna(), 0.0)
        r0 = resid.fillna(0.0)
        imp = (3.0 * r0 + 2.0 * r0.shift(1) + 1.0 * r0.shift(2)) / 6.0
        d = (imp / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-40.0, 40.0)
        dz = np.sign(d) * (d.abs() - self._dead).clip(lower=0.0)
        trig = np.tanh(dz / self._trig_scale)
        advb = adv(volume.fillna(0.0), self._adv_window)
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_rel = ts_sum(volume.fillna(0.0), self._trig_win) / (float(self._trig_win) * advb)
        a_rel = a_rel.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 100.0)
        gate = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._absorb_scale)
        raw = gate.fillna(0.0) * w_state.fillna(0.0) * trig.fillna(0.0)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

Here c is demoted to a pure STATE variable — a per-name estimate of book permeability (how many quanta of price the book gives up per unit of probed wick path), measured on a window that ends 3 bars before the present and z-scored against the name's own 240-bar history, hence mechanically decoupled from the current move — and it is used only to sign a genuinely FAST trigger: the dead-zoned, grid-quantum-scaled, beta-residual impulse of the last 3 bars. In a permeable (high-c) regime depth is thin, so a fresh impulse is mostly transient impact and snaps back as the queue refills; in an absorptive (low-c) regime price only moves when a persistent metaorder is eating real depth, so the fresh impulse continues. Because the switch is cross-sectionally centred, the factor's unconditional projection onto plain short-term reversal is ~zero by construction, so naive reversal harvesters cannot span it, and the profitable leg is exactly where supplying liquidity is expensive — a compensated risk, not a free lunch.

"""Conversion-weighted path channels with concentration-signed permanence.

Mechanism
---------
A 60-second (6-bar) path decomposes into (i) excursion that was probed but NOT
converted into net displacement (wicks beyond bar endpoints, printed on bars
that actually traded size) and (ii) beta-residual net displacement that WAS
realised.  The conversion ratio

    c = |net residual displacement| / (|net residual displacement| + probed path)

both in units of the name's own robust grid quantum, says which component the
window is made of: low c -> the book absorbed the probes and the endpoint mid is
a stale sample of where aggression reached, so go WITH the excursion side; high
c -> the path was fully converted into a net move and the *permanence* of that
move has to be judged.

Permanence is judged by the temporal SHAPE of participation, not its level.
When the window's volume mass is concentrated in one or two bars (high
Herfindahl of volume shares relative to the name's own trailing distribution),
the displacement is a genuine depth-consuming sweep and the repricing persists.
When the same displacement was delivered by evenly spread volume, it is unbacked
quote drift / inventory walking and it reverts.  Hence the displacement channel
carries a signed permanence coefficient

    kappa = (2 * ts_rank(concentration) - 1) - fade_prior

which is negative (fade) by default and turns positive only for genuinely
bursty participation.  Everything is scaled by a saturating gate in window
volume relative to average bar volume, since neither mechanism exists without
traded size.

All statistics are trailing rolling windows / positive lags, hence causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, rolling_beta, ts_rank, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_TINY = 1e-12


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)


def _participation_concentration(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Normalised Herfindahl concentration of the trailing n-bar volume shares.

    With p_i = v_i / sum(v):  HHI = sum(p_i^2) = sum(v_i^2) / (sum v_i)^2, which
    lies in [1/n, 1].  Rescaled to [0, 1] by (n*HHI - 1)/(n - 1): 0 means
    perfectly even participation across the window, 1 means the whole window's
    volume printed in a single bar.  Built from two trailing rolling sums, so
    the value at bar t uses only bars <= t.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    s1 = ts_sum(v, n)
    s2 = ts_sum(v * v, n)
    den = (s1 * s1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    hhi = (s2 / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    out = (float(n) * hhi - 1.0) / (float(n) - 1.0)
    return out.clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class ConcentrationSignedPermanenceConversionSwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Conversion ratio weights the channels; volume concentration signs them."""

    factor_id = 'conc_signed_permanence_conversion_switch'
    name = 'Concentration-signed permanence inside the conversion switch'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Blends probe-gated range-normalised wick asymmetry with beta-residual net '
        'displacement in grid-quantum units using weights (1-c) and c, where c is the '
        'fraction of the 6-bar probed path converted into net residual displacement, and '
        'the displacement leg carries a signed permanence coefficient built from the '
        'trailing rank of the Herfindahl concentration of 18-bar volume shares (fade when '
        'participation was even, extrapolate when it burst), all scaled by a saturating '
        'absorbed-volume gate and ranked cross-sectionally.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _win = 6
    _conc_window = 18
    _conc_rank_window = 120
    _q_window = 240
    _q_min = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _vol_window = 60
    _adv_window = 240
    _absorb_scale = 1.5
    _shrink = 0.25
    _c_prior = 0.5
    _d_scale = 3.0
    _fade_prior = 0.35

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = (
            data['volume']
            .astype(float)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .abs()
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        )

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        # --- robust per-name grid quantum (slow, deliberately not a fast vol) ---
        absr = ret.abs()
        nz = absr.where(absr > _TINY)
        q = nz.rolling(self._q_window, min_periods=self._q_min).quantile(0.2)
        q = q.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # --- beta-residual returns (strip common factor moves) ---
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        mkt_bd = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt_bd, self._beta_window)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (ret - beta * mkt_bd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # --- excursion (unconverted) geometry ---
        hi_end = _pair_max(open_, close)
        lo_end = _pair_min(open_, close)
        hi = _pair_max(high, hi_end)
        lo = _pair_min(low, lo_end)
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        up_w = (hi - hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_w = (lo_end - lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        asym = ((up_w - dn_w) / rng).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        wick = ((up_w + dn_w) / px).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)

        med = volume.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=20).median()
        gate = ((volume > med) & med.notna() & volume.notna()).astype(float)
        g = gate.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        a = asym.where(asym.notna(), 0.0)
        e_num = decay_linear(g * a, self._win)
        e_den = decay_linear(g, self._win)
        chan_e = (e_num / (e_den + self._shrink)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        chan_e = chan_e.clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # --- converted displacement and the conversion ratio ---
        d_sum = ts_sum(resid.fillna(0.0), self._win) / q
        d_sum = d_sum.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-25.0, 25.0)
        x_sum = ts_sum((wick * g).fillna(0.0), self._win) / q
        x_sum = x_sum.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        c = (d_sum.abs() / (d_sum.abs() + x_sum + self._c_prior)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        chan_d = np.tanh(d_sum / self._d_scale)

        # --- signed permanence from participation shape (the B ingredient) ---
        conc = _participation_concentration(volume, self._conc_window)
        k_raw = 2.0 * ts_rank(conc, self._conc_rank_window) - 1.0
        k_raw = k_raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
        kappa = k_raw - self._fade_prior

        # --- absorbed-volume saturating gate ---
        advb = volume.rolling(self._adv_window, min_periods=60).mean()
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_rel = ts_sum(volume.fillna(0.0), self._win) / (float(self._win) * advb)
        a_rel = a_rel.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 100.0)
        gate_abs = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._absorb_scale)

        raw = gate_abs * ((1.0 - c) * chan_e + c * kappa * chan_d)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Concentration-signed permanence inside the conversion switch
programs.trading_idea: Parent A shows that a short path splits into probed-but-unconverted excursion (which precedes continuation toward the probed side) and net residual displacement (which snaps back), with the conversion ratio c as the mixing state. Parent B's *contradicted* sign is the missing piece: evenly-spread participation does not mark an unfinished metaorder at 10-second resolution — it marks unbacked quote drift, and its displacement is the part that reverts, whereas displacement delivered by volume concentrated in one or two bars is a genuine depth-consuming sweep whose repricing is permanent and continues. The child therefore keeps A's conversion switch for *how much weight* the displacement channel gets, but lets B's participation-concentration state decide the *sign* of that channel (a Herfindahl-based concentration innovation shifted by a fade prior), so the same converted displacement is faded when it arrived evenly and extrapolated when it arrived in a burst. Neither parent can express this: A hard-codes one polarity on displacement and averages the two regimes together, while B applies its evenness gate to every path, including round-trips whose excursion was never converted, diluting the interaction that actually carries the edge; all windows are shortened to the 6-bar forecast scale so the edge sits at the pinned horizon rather than at 24 bars.
programs.description: Ranks gate_abs * [ (1-c)*volume-gated wick asymmetry + c*kappa*tanh(residual net displacement in grid-quantum units) ], where c is the fraction of the 6-bar probed path converted into beta-residual displacement and kappa is a trailing-rank participation-concentration innovation (Herfindahl of 18-bar volume shares) shifted by a transient-impact fade prior.

programs.code:
"""Core-vs-tail decomposition of a nonparametric rank drift.

Mechanism
---------
A short-run price displacement is an additive sum of bar increments, and those
increments have two distinguishable generators:

1.  *Core* increments -- drawn from the median region of the name's own recent
    increment distribution.  Execution algorithms slicing a parent order aim
    precisely at this: each child order is sized so it barely moves price, so a
    metaorder in progress builds displacement out of median-sized, serially
    concordant increments, and it keeps arriving until the parent is filled
    (Lillo-Farmer order-splitting persistence).

2.  *Tail* increments -- drawn from the tails of the own-name distribution.
    These are momentary depth withdrawals / sweeps; under the transient-impact
    propagator the displacement they create largely relaxes as depth refills,
    i.e. it reverts on the one-minute scale.

The parent factor multiplied a single Wilcoxon location shift by a coarse
cross-sectional dispersion gate, so the two generators were only crudely mixed.
Here they are *decomposed*: the same probability-integral-transformed increments
are partitioned by whether the increment sits inside the central 70% of the
name's trailing 120-bar distribution (core) or in its tails, and the two partial
drifts are signed oppositely -- core continues, tail reverts.

A second, genuinely new conditioning variable gates the core leg: the trailing
24-bar Spearman (rank) lag-1 autocorrelation of the uniformized increments.  A
real slicing schedule leaves serially concordant prints; an alternating sequence
of median-sized moves is bounce noise and deserves little weight.  The gate is
mapped to [0, 1] so it attenuates rather than flips the core leg.

Everything is rank-based (hence automatically volatility-normalised per name,
no z-scores, no betas) and uses no volume, keeping the factor structurally
removed from the flow-imbalance family.  All statistics are trailing rolling
windows: the value at bar t uses only bars <= t.

Falsifiable: if the IC of (core leg minus tail leg) at six bars is zero or
negative -- i.e. tail-driven displacement continues while core-driven drift
reverts -- the slicing / transient-impact reading is wrong.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_autocorr, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_increments(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar-to-bar log price increments, sanitised."""
    lvl = close.astype(float).abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    inc = np.log(lvl).diff()
    return inc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _uniform_scores(inc: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Probability-integral transform of each increment against its own trailing
    n-bar empirical distribution, centred: s in [-0.5, 0.5].  Causal."""
    u = ts_rank(inc, n).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    return u - 0.5

def _split_drift(s: pd.DataFrame, k: int, halfwidth: float):
    """Split the trailing k-bar mean rank-drift into a core part (increments in
    the central region of the own-name distribution) and a tail part.

    Both legs are trailing means over the SAME k bars, so they add back up to
    the undecomposed Wilcoxon location shift.  Bars with missing scores are
    treated as zero contribution and the window is required to be fully
    populated, so no future information can enter.
    """
    valid = s.notna()
    core = s.where(valid & (s.abs() <= halfwidth), 0.0)
    tail = s.where(valid & (s.abs() > halfwidth), 0.0)
    cnt = valid.astype(float).rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()
    ok = cnt >= float(k)
    core_d = ts_mean(core, k).where(ok)
    tail_d = ts_mean(tail, k).where(ok)
    return (core_d, tail_d)

def _persistence_weight(s: pd.DataFrame, m: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing Spearman-type lag-1 autocorrelation of the uniformized
    increments, mapped to a non-negative attenuation weight in [0, 1].
    +1 autocorr (concordant slicing prints) -> weight 1; -1 (alternating
    bounce) -> weight 0."""
    rho = rolling_autocorr(s, m, 1).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    rho = rho.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    return 0.5 * (1.0 + rho)

@register_factor
class CoreTailIncrementDriftDecompositionRunsGate(BaseFactor):
    """Core (slicing) drift minus tail (overshoot) drift, persistence-gated."""
    factor_id = 'core_tail_increment_drift_decomposition_runs_gat'
    name = 'Core-vs-tail increment drift decomposition with persistence gate'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of [rank of the persistence-gated core-region 6-bar rank drift] minus [rank of the tail-region 6-bar rank drift], where increments are uniformized against their own trailing 120-bar distribution and persistence is the trailing 24-bar Spearman lag-1 autocorrelation: long compressed, serially concordant up-grinds, short tail-driven up-displacements.'
    window_length = 160
    inputs = ['close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _ref = 120
    _fast = 6
    _persist = 24
    _halfwidth = 0.35

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        inc = _log_increments(close)
        s = _uniform_scores(inc, self._ref)
        core_d, tail_d = _split_drift(s, self._fast, self._halfwidth)
        w = _persistence_weight(s, self._persist)
        core_eff = (core_d * w).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        tail_eff = tail_d.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        core_c = 2.0 * rank(core_eff) - 1.0
        tail_c = 2.0 * rank(tail_eff) - 1.0
        raw = core_c - tail_c
        raw = raw.where(core_eff.notna() & tail_eff.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Core-vs-tail increment drift decomposition with Spearman persistence gate
programs.trading_idea: A 60-second displacement is an additive sum of increments, and the increments come from two different generators: median-region ('core') increments, which is how an execution algorithm walks price while slicing a metaorder, and own-name tail increments, which is how a momentary depth withdrawal overshoots and then relaxes under the transient-impact propagator. The parent multiplied one location statistic by a coarse cross-sectional dispersion gate; the child instead *decomposes* the same nonparametric rank-drift into its core and tail parts and signs them oppositely — core-generated drift should continue over the next six bars, tail-generated drift should revert — and gates only the core leg by the trailing Spearman (rank) lag-1 autocorrelation of increments, because a genuine slicing schedule produces serially concordant child-order prints while an alternating core path is just noise. This is falsifiable in a sharp way: the two legs must carry opposite-signed ICs, and the core leg's IC must be larger when rank autocorrelation is positive; if tail-driven displacement instead continues (permanent news repricing), the combined IC flips negative. The edge should persist because it requires classifying each 10-second increment against the name's own conditional increment distribution and tracking its serial concordance, the agent whose child orders create the core drift cannot profit by front-running itself, and net-of-spread capacity inside a one-minute window is too small for size-constrained arbitrageurs.
programs.description: Uniformizes each bar's log increment against its own trailing 120-bar empirical distribution, splits the last 6 uniform scores into median-region ('core') and tail contributions, weights the core leg by the trailing 24-bar Spearman lag-1 autocorrelation of the scores, and goes long cross-sectionally high core drift minus high tail drift.

programs.code:
"""Volume-backed fundamental spread-flow relay.

Mechanism
---------
Systematic style flow (ETF creations/redemptions, risk-model rebalances, quant
meta-orders) is executed over minutes and hits every name sharing a fundamental
characteristic at once.  Consequently a characteristic-sorted long-short spread
return carries positive short-horizon autocorrelation (unfinished basket flow),
while individual names' idiosyncratic displacements mean-revert.  Because
name-level microstructure noise (bounce, one-off liquidity gaps) is
idiosyncratic, it diversifies away inside the spread: the spread return is a
much cleaner read on live flow than any single name's price path.

The factor:
  1. builds L1-normalised, cross-sectionally demeaned rank weights on five
     point-in-time fundamental characteristics (size, value, quality,
     investment, leverage), sequentially orthogonalised so each style carries
     its own information;
  2. realises each style's per-bar spread return and turns it into a flow
     z-score (EWMA mean over trailing volatility);
  3. gates each style's flow by a bounded *footprint* multiplier: the
     weight-weighted relative volume of that style's own constituents versus
     their trailing norm -- real basket execution leaves a volume trace, noise
     does not;
  4. projects the gated flow back onto each name through its spread weight and
     ranks cross-sectionally.  The idiosyncratic residual is deliberately
     DISCARDED, so the signal contains no own-name displacement term.

Everything is trailing: characteristics are already point-in-time step
functions, spread returns use only bar t, and all smoothing is causal
(ewm / trailing rolling).

Falsifiable: if 10-second characteristic-spread returns are not positively
autocorrelated at the 6-bar horizon, or if volume-unbacked style moves continue
as strongly as volume-backed ones, the flow-propagation mechanism is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_MIN_NAMES = 6
_STYLES = ("marketCap", "earningsYield", "roe", "assetGrowth", "debtToEquity")


def _numeric(df, like: pd.DataFrame):
    """Align a (possibly sparse / object-typed) field onto the price panel."""
    if df is None:
        return None
    out = df.reindex(index=like.index, columns=like.columns)
    out = out.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _row_l1_scale(w: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale each row so that sum(|w|) == 1 (rows of zeros stay NaN)."""
    d = w.abs().sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return w.div(d, axis=0)


def _spread_weights(char: pd.DataFrame, valid: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Demeaned cross-sectional rank weights: a dollar-neutral long-short spread.

    Names with a missing characteristic or a dead price get exactly zero weight,
    so the surviving weights still sum to zero (the market factor cancels).
    """
    c = char.where(valid)
    rk = c.rank(axis=1, pct=True)
    enough = rk.notna().sum(axis=1) >= _MIN_NAMES
    rk = rk.where(enough, np.nan)
    w = rk.sub(rk.mean(axis=1), axis=0).fillna(0.0)
    return _row_l1_scale(w).fillna(0.0)


def _orthogonalise(weights):
    """Row-wise sequential Gram-Schmidt on the weight vectors (per bar)."""
    basis = []
    for w in weights:
        v = w
        for u in basis:
            num = (v * u).sum(axis=1)
            den = (u * u).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            v = v - u.mul((num / den).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
        basis.append(_row_l1_scale(v).fillna(0.0))
    return basis


def _flow_z(f: pd.Series, hl: float, vol_win: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal flow score: decayed mean spread return over its trailing scale."""
    m = f.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=12).mean()
    s = f.rolling(vol_win, min_periods=60).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = m / s
    return z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _footprint_gate(absw: pd.DataFrame, relvol: pd.DataFrame, win: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Bounded multiplier: are this style's own constituents unusually active?"""
    num = (absw * relvol).sum(axis=1)
    den = absw.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    t = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    base = t.rolling(win, min_periods=60).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    g = (t / base).clip(0.25, 4.0) ** 0.5
    return g.fillna(1.0)


@register_factor
class FundamentalSpreadFlowBackedStyleRelay(BaseFactor):
    """Continuation of volume-backed fundamental style flow, residual discarded."""

    factor_id = "fundamental_spread_flow_backed_style_relay"
    name = "Volume-backed fundamental spread-flow relay"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of each name's characteristic loading times the "
        "recent volume-backed flow z-score of the orthogonalised fundamental "
        "spreads (size, value, quality, investment, leverage): long the names "
        "whose style baskets are currently being bought with a volume footprint."
    )
    window_length = 360
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "marketCap",
        "earningsYield",
        "roe",
        "assetGrowth",
        "debtToEquity",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _halflife = 6.0     # matched to the forecast horizon: unfinished basket flow
    _vol_win = 360      # ~1 hour of 10s bars: scale of the spread return
    _act_win = 360      # trailing norm for the volume footprint

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)

        volume = _numeric(data.get("volume"), close)
        if volume is None:
            volume = close * 0.0
        volume = volume.abs().fillna(0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change()
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.01, 0.01)
        valid = ret.notna() & close.notna()

        advol = adv(volume, self._act_win).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relvol = (volume / advol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        relvol = relvol.clip(0.0, 10.0).fillna(1.0)

        raw_weights = []
        for key in _STYLES:
            ch = _numeric(data.get(key), close)
            if ch is None:
                continue
            if int(ch.notna().sum().sum()) == 0:
                continue
            raw_weights.append(_spread_weights(ch, valid))

        if not raw_weights:
            return pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        weights = _orthogonalise(raw_weights)

        sig = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        load = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        ret0 = ret.fillna(0.0)

        for w in weights:
            f = (w * ret0).sum(axis=1)               # style spread return, bar t
            z = _flow_z(f, self._halflife, self._vol_win)
            g = _footprint_gate(w.abs(), relvol, self._act_win)
            sig = sig + w.mul((z * g).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            load = load + w.abs()

        sig = sig.where((load > 0.0) & valid)
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        out = rank(sig)
        return out.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Volume-backed fundamental spread-flow relay
programs.trading_idea: Systematic style flow (ETF creation/redemption baskets, risk-model rebalances, quant metaorders) is worked over minutes and touches every name sharing a fundamental characteristic simultaneously, so the return of a characteristic-sorted long-short spread is positively autocorrelated at the 10-second scale even while individual names' idiosyncratic displacements mean-revert; individual-name bounce noise diversifies away inside the spread, so the spread return is a far cleaner read on ongoing flow than any single name's price path. The child therefore estimates, bar by bar, purely-fundamental orthogonalised spread returns (size, value, quality, investment, leverage), converts each into a flow z-score that is up-weighted only when the spread's own constituents are simultaneously unusually active in volume (real basket execution leaves a volume footprint; noise-driven spread moves do not), and projects that flow back onto each name through its characteristic loading — deliberately discarding the idiosyncratic residual, which is exactly the over-mined carrier that made the parent 71% redundant with the book. It is falsifiable in two independent ways: if 10-second characteristic-spread returns are not positively autocorrelated over the next 6 bars the flow-propagation reading is dead, and if volume-unbacked spread moves continue as strongly as volume-backed ones the footprint gate is spurious. The edge survives arbitrage because monetising it requires holding the crowded style tilt across dozens of names for ~one minute, where the round-trip spread cost across the whole basket caps capacity, and because the flow itself is mandated rebalancing that keeps being generated rather than being competed away.
programs.description: Per-bar cross-sectional long-short spread returns on five orthogonalised point-in-time fundamental characteristics (marketCap, earningsYield, roe, assetGrowth, debtToEquity) are smoothed into flow z-scores, scaled by a bounded style-level relative-volume gate, and projected back onto each name via its spread weight; the cross-sectional rank of that projection is the signal, containing no own-name displacement term.

programs.code:
"""Endpoint-noise-anchored horizon-matched lag-kernel beta backlog.

Mechanism
---------
Expected forward 6-bar return of the *observed close* decomposes into

    E[(C_{t+6} - C_t)/C_t]  ~=  owed efficient-price drift  +  decay of the
                                current close-vs-efficient-price wedge.

1. Owed drift (Parent B's kernel, de-biased).  With
       r_t = sum_{l=0..L} b_l m_{t-l} + e_t,
   the part of E[sum_{j=1..H} r_{t+j}] driven by ALREADY OBSERVED market
   returns is  sum_{l=1..L} b_l * sum_{k=0}^{min(H,l)-1} m_{t-k}.  With L=H=6
   this is a kernel matched by construction to the fixed 6-bar offset.  Both
   the own return and the market return are built from the bar's range-centre
   (H+L)/2 rather than the close: the centre averages two order statistics of
   the intrabar mid path, so it carries much less microstructure noise, which
   removes the errors-in-variables attenuation that shrinks close-based lagged
   betas toward zero.

2. Wedge decay (Parent A's mechanism, in return units).  u = (centre - C)/C is
   the signed sub-bar dislocation of the closing print from the low-noise
   anchor.  Only the transient fraction of it dies inside the horizon, so it
   enters multiplied by the two-scale noise share phi = (1 - VR_6)*6/5 and by
   1/(1 + V/medV), which keeps quiet bars (noise) and discounts heavy bars
   (permanent impact).

The backlog term is amplified by a frozen-centre staleness gate: names whose
efficient-price anchor does not update are exactly where catch-up accumulates.
All estimation is trailing-only and deterministic.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, cols) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.DataFrame(
        np.repeat(s.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1),
        index=s.index,
        columns=cols,
    )


def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal cap-weighted market return (weights = previous bar's market cap)."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w.to_numpy()))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret).sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    den = w.sum(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)


def _rolling_lag_beta(
    y: pd.DataFrame, x_df: pd.DataFrame, lag: int, n: int, min_obs: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS loading of own return on the market return lagged ``lag`` bars."""
    x = x_df.shift(lag)
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    my = yy.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mx = xx.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxy = (yy * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxx = (xx * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    cov = mxy - my * mx
    var = (mxx - mx * mx).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cov / var).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _shrink_cs(b: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a loading toward its cross-sectional mean."""
    row = b.mean(axis=1)
    return b.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _two_scale_noise_share(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of 1-bar return variance that is transient noise.

    Efficient price + i.i.d. noise gives Var(r1) = s2 + 2u2 and
    Var(rk)/k = s2 + 2u2/k, hence phi = 2u2/Var(r1) = (1 - VR)*k/(k-1).
    All terms are trailing rolling moments, so the value at t uses only <= t.
    """
    mp = max(k * 4, n // 2)
    v1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).var()
    rk = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()
    vk = rk.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).var()
    denom = (float(k) * v1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    phi = (1.0 - vk / denom) * (float(k) / float(k - 1))
    return phi.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class EndpointNoiseAnchoredLagKernelBacklog(BaseFactor):
    """Efficient-price beta backlog plus the dying part of the endpoint wedge."""

    factor_id = "endpoint_noise_anchored_lag_kernel_backlog_h6"
    name = "Endpoint-noise-anchored lag-kernel beta backlog (h=6)"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Horizon-matched lag-1..6 market catch-up estimated on noise-robust "
        "range-centre returns and amplified by a frozen-centre staleness gate, "
        "plus the transient-share-weighted, quiet-bar-discounted dislocation of "
        "the close from its bar's range centre; vol-normalised and ranked."
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _n_lags = 6
    _beta_window = 240
    _beta_min = 80
    _shrink = 0.5
    _vol_window = 240
    _vol_min = 60
    _noise_window = 180
    _med_window = 60

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()

        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        centre = 0.5 * (hi + lo)

        p = centre.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        c = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rc = p.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        rcl = c.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace(
                [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
            )

        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(rc, mcap)
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, cols)

        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        pred = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        valid = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for lag in range(1, self._n_lags + 1):
            b = _rolling_lag_beta(
                rc, mkt_df, lag, self._beta_window, self._beta_min
            ).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
            b_s = _shrink_cs(b, self._shrink)
            span = min(h, lag)
            s_l = mkt.rolling(span, min_periods=span).sum()
            pred = pred.add(b_s.mul(s_l, axis=0).fillna(0.0))
            valid = valid.add(b_s.notna().astype(float))
        pred = pred.where(valid >= 3.0)

        # staleness of the low-noise anchor: fraction of bars with a frozen centre
        frozen = ((rc.abs() < 1e-12) & rc.notna()).astype(float)
        frozen_frac = frozen.rolling(120, min_periods=40).mean()
        gate = 0.5 + rank(frozen_frac).fillna(0.5)

        # dying part of the close-vs-anchor wedge, in return units
        u = ((centre - close) / c).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        med = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).rolling(
            self._med_window, min_periods=max(10, self._med_window // 3)
        ).median()
        rel = (volume / med.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        rel = rel.clip(0.0, 20.0).fillna(1.0)
        quiet_w = 1.0 / (1.0 + rel)
        phi = _two_scale_noise_share(rcl, h, self._noise_window)
        row_med = phi.median(axis=1)
        phi = phi.T.fillna(row_med).T.fillna(0.5)
        wedge = phi * quiet_w * u

        forecast = pred.fillna(0.0) * gate + wedge.fillna(0.0)

        alive = (rcl.notna().rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0) & close.notna()
        usable = pred.notna() | wedge.notna()
        forecast = forecast.where(alive & usable)

        sigma = rcl.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        scale = (sigma * float(np.sqrt(float(h)))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        fz = (forecast / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        return rank(fz).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

programs.trading_idea: Parent B forecasts the 6-bar return still *owed* to a slow repricer by folding its distributed-lag market loadings against the already-observed market path, but it measures both the loadings and the starting point with the closing print, which Parent A shows is the noisiest single sample of the efficient price: (H+L)/2 averages two order statistics of the intrabar mid path and so carries far less microstructure noise. The child therefore rebuilds Parent B's kernel on the range-centre price — killing the errors-in-variables attenuation that biases lagged betas toward zero and biases the market regressor — and then adds, in the *same return units*, the piece of the current close-to-centre dislocation that provably dies inside the horizon: phi * (centre - close)/close, where phi = (1 - VR_6)*6/5 is the two-scale share of one-bar variance that is transient, discounted by 1/(1 + V/medV) so only quiet-bar dislocations (noise, not permanent impact) count. The interaction is the edge: the forecast target is close_{t+6} - close_t, so the correct prediction is efficient-price drift owed by the lag kernel PLUS mechanical decay of the noise wedge between the observed close and the efficient anchor — a name can be owed catch-up while its last print already overshot, and neither parent can tell those states apart, while the noise-robust anchor also makes the catch-up loadings themselves more accurate; the whole backlog is amplified where the centre price is frozen (genuine staleness).

"""Cross-sectional volume-move concordance regime flip on fresh flow pressure.

Mechanism
---------
Two microstructure states generate mid-price displacement at second scales:

1. *Paid* displacement -- informed / metaorder flow walks the book, so repricing
   occurs exactly where the executed volume is.  Order-flow imbalance is
   strongly autocorrelated (Lillo-Farmer), so this displacement CONTINUES.
2. *Unpaid* displacement -- thin-book quote drift, dealer inventory shuffling,
   or absorption (large volume, no move) in other names.  Under Bouchaud's
   propagator this component is transient and RELAXES.

A single name cannot separate the two over a one-minute window: the per-name
volume/|return| coupling estimated on six bars is noise.  The cross-section
can.  Each bar we compute the Spearman concordance, across names, between
self-normalised volume and self-normalised absolute repricing.  That single
scalar is a dimensionless, high-power read of which regime is operative:
tight coupling = repricing is being paid for; broken coupling = displacement
is appearing where flow is not.

The carrier is the parent's one genuinely robust object -- the sqrt(volume)
weighted mean bar-return sign over the last 6 bars (square-root impact law,
bounded in [-1, 1], immune to single giant prints, no per-name normalisation).
The parent's report showed this carrier reverts *unconditionally*.  The claim
here is that the unconditional reversion is a regime average: the conditional
IC is a + b * g, with a < 0 (parent) and b > 0 (this mechanism), so the pure
interaction signal carrier x g earns b * Var(g) > 0 and is, by construction,
nearly uncorrelated with any static reversal or momentum factor (E[g] ~ 0).

Falsifiable: split bars by the sign of the concordance-regime gate; the
conditional ICs of fresh sqrt-law pressure must have OPPOSITE signs.  If they
do not -- if the gate carries no interaction -- the child collapses to the
parent's negative IC and the paid-vs-unpaid reading is refuted.

All statistics are trailing: cross-sectional ranks use only bar t, the gate
uses an exponentially weighted mean and a trailing z-score of past bars.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_change(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar-to-bar log price change."""
    lvl = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    chg = np.log(lvl).diff()
    return chg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _sqrt_law_pressure(sgn: pd.DataFrame, wgt: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """sqrt(volume)-weighted mean of bar-return signs over a trailing n-bar window.

    Bounded in [-1, 1]; +1 = every traded bar repriced up.  The sqrt weighting
    implements the square-root impact law: size matters, but sub-linearly.
    """
    num = ts_sum(sgn * wgt, n)
    den = ts_sum(wgt, n).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _row_spearman(x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional Spearman correlation between two panels.

    Implemented as the row-wise Pearson correlation of the cross-sectional
    percentile ranks, on the names where both are observed.  Uses only
    information from bar t (plus the trailing normalisers built upstream).
    """
    ux = rank(x)
    uy = rank(y)
    mask = ux.notna() & uy.notna()
    ux = ux.where(mask)
    uy = uy.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    mx = ux.mean(axis=1)
    my = uy.mean(axis=1)
    cov = (ux * uy).mean(axis=1) - mx * my
    sx = ux.std(axis=1, ddof=0)
    sy = uy.std(axis=1, ddof=0)
    denom = (sx * sy).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = cov / denom
    out = out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return out.where(n >= min_names)


@register_factor
class XsFlowMoveConcordanceRegimePressureFlip(BaseFactor):
    """Fresh sqrt-law flow pressure, signed by the panel's flow-move coupling regime."""

    factor_id = "xs_flow_move_concordance_regime_pressure_flip"
    name = "Cross-sectional volume-move concordance regime flip on fresh flow pressure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectionally centred rank of 6-bar sqrt(volume)-weighted directional "
        "pressure, multiplied by tanh of the trailing z-score of the per-bar "
        "cross-sectional Spearman concordance between self-normalised volume and "
        "self-normalised absolute repricing: continuation when the panel's "
        "flow-move coupling is abnormally tight, reversal when it breaks down."
    )
    window_length = 480
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _fast = 6        # carrier window, matched to the forecast horizon
    _norm = 120      # ~20 min per-name normaliser for volume and |repricing|
    _hl = 6          # ewm halflife (bars) for the regime statistic
    _reg = 360       # ~1 hour trailing window for the regime z-score
    _min_reg = 120
    _min_names = 10

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        chg = _log_change(close)
        sgn = np.sign(chg).fillna(0.0)
        wgt = np.sqrt(volume)

        # --- carrier: fresh square-root-law weighted directional pressure -----
        pressure = _sqrt_law_pressure(sgn, wgt, self._fast)
        carrier = 2.0 * rank(pressure) - 1.0

        # --- regime: cross-sectional flow / repricing concordance -------------
        absmove = chg.abs()
        vnorm = volume / ts_mean(volume, self._norm).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        anorm = absmove / ts_mean(absmove, self._norm).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vnorm = vnorm.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        anorm = anorm.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        conc = _row_spearman(vnorm, anorm, self._min_names)
        conc_s = conc.ewm(halflife=self._hl, min_periods=self._hl).mean()
        mu = conc_s.rolling(self._reg, min_periods=self._min_reg).mean()
        sd = conc_s.rolling(self._reg, min_periods=self._min_reg).std()
        z = (conc_s - mu) / sd.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        gate = np.tanh(z)

        signal = carrier.mul(gate, axis=0)
        signal = signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Cross-sectional volume–move concordance regime flip on fresh flow pressure
programs.trading_idea: At the 10-second scale a mid-price displacement is either *paid for* by order flow (informed metaorder slicing: repricing happens where the trades are) or *unpaid* (thin-book quote drift, dealer inventory shuffling, absorption elsewhere). A single name cannot tell these apart over one minute — the estimate is pure noise — but the whole cross-section can: each bar, the Spearman concordance between names' self-normalised volume and their self-normalised absolute repricing is a high-power, dimensionless read on which regime the market is in. When concordance is abnormally high, one-sided flow is unfinished informed flow and fresh sqrt-volume-weighted pressure continues over the next ~minute; when concordance collapses, displacement is being generated without flow backing it, so it is transient inventory/quote noise and relaxes. The parent showed that fresh pressure unconditionally *reverts* (IC < 0); this child asserts the reversion is a regime average and that the sign of the conditional IC is governed by the panel-wide flow–move coupling, i.e. IC_conditional ≈ a + b·g with a<0 and b>0, so the pure interaction earns b·Var(g) > 0. The edge survives arbitrage because exploiting it requires recomputing a panel-wide dependence statistic in real time and *flipping the sign* of a short-horizon flow signal within a minute — most desks run either a momentum or a reversal book, not a state-switching one, and the net-of-spread capacity at this scale is tiny.
