programs.trading_idea: Treat each name's 10-second tape as a 4-state Markov chain on the lattice (sign of the bar return) x (activity above/below its own trailing median volume). If the chain were time-reversible, Kolmogorov's criterion holds and the net circulation around the 2x2 cycle is zero; a non-zero circulation (an entropy-producing cycle flux, computable as an antisymmetric lag-1 cross-covariance of the two binary channels, i.e. a discrete Levy area on the sign lattice) identifies WHICH participant is marginal: counter-clockwise flux means directional legs die at activity peaks (market-maker inventory pressure terminates aggressive flow, so fade when busy / drift when quiet), clockwise flux means direction flips during the quiet pauses of a working program and extends when the scheduler accelerates (so continue when busy). Because the marginal-participant regime persists for many minutes while the cycle itself has a period of only a few bars, the trailing flux tells you the sign of the NEXT quarter-turn given the current quadrant, giving the forecast -flux x direction-state x activity-state. It survives arbitrage because the statistic is second-order and time-asymmetric — it is identically zero for any process in which volume and direction are merely contemporaneously coupled, so it is invisible to linear volume/volatility/momentum screens — and because its economic content (who is the marginal trader right now) is regenerated by every new program rather than destroyed by trading it.
programs.description: Signal = -(normalized 120-bar cycle flux of the (return-sign, activity-sign) 4-state chain, cross-sectionally median-purged) x (4-bar mean return-sign) x (4-bar mean activity-sign), cross-sectionally ranked; all inputs are bounded in [-1,1].

programs.code:
"""Kernel-deficit / transient-impact snapback, routed by idiosyncratic variance share.

Mechanism
---------
Two distinct repricing gaps live in a 10-second bar:

1. SYSTEMATIC DELIVERY GAP.  Let m_t be the cross-sectional median return and
   z_t its trailing z-score.  Each name responds to common shocks through a
   distributed lag  y_t = sum_j theta_j z_{t-j} + e_t  (y = r / sigma_r), whose
   coefficients are only identified where *news* transmission dominates the
   bid-ask bounce, i.e. on large-|z| bars.  Trailing shock-selected local
   projections give theta_j causally; folding the kernel onto the observed market
   path yields yhat_t.  The signed shortfall accumulated since the most recent
   genuine common shock (capped) is the beta catch-up still OWED.

2. IDIOSYNCRATIC LIQUIDITY COST.  Aggressive size walks finite visible depth, so
   the mid ends far from the extreme the bar printed.  The sector-common part of
   that displacement is basket information and persists; the name-specific part
   is the temporary cost of immediacy and decays as passive depth replenishes
   over roughly the next minute.  A participation-weighted, sector-demeaned
   close-location value, negated, is therefore a fast snapback signal.

The synthesis: the SAME trailing variance decomposition decides which gap is the
meaningful object for a given name.  High trailing market R-squared => its path
is mostly common, so the kernel deficit is informative; low R-squared => its path
is mostly local, so the range-position liquidity cost is informative.  We blend
the two centred cross-sectional ranks with weights (rank of R^2, 1 - that), then
amplify the blend where the two channels agree in sign and damp it where they
disagree: agreement means a mechanical repricing lag still paying transient
impact (closes fast), disagreement means the residual is idiosyncratic news
(permanent, must not be chased).  The fast channel supplies the timing, the
kernel deficit supplies direction and size, which is why the interaction should
bite at the fixed 6-bar offset rather than drifting out to 24 bars.

Causal throughout: trailing rolling windows, positive lags only; sector labels
are static metadata taken from the earliest available observation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import correlation, decay_linear, rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading toward its cross-sectional mean (empirical Bayes)."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _bars_since(flag: pd.Series, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Bars elapsed since the last True in ``flag`` (forward fill only, causal)."""
    s = pd.Series(np.arange(len(flag.index), dtype=float), index=flag.index)
    last = s.where(flag.to_numpy()).ffill()
    out = (s - last).clip(0.0, cap)
    return out.fillna(cap)


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int = 3):
    """One static label per ticker from a quarterly text field (first valid obs)."""
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = '__POOL__'
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else '__POOL__'
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), '__POOL__')
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank mapped to [-1, 1], NaNs preserved."""
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return (r - 0.5) * 2.0


@register_factor
class KernelDeficitRoutedTransientImpactSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Owed beta catch-up and idio range-position snapback, routed by variance share."""

    factor_id = 'kernel_deficit_routed_transient_impact_snapback'
    name = 'Kernel-deficit / transient-impact snapback routed by variance share'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Blends the event-anchored shock-selected local-projection kernel deficit '
        '(owed systematic catch-up) with the negated sector-purged, participation-'
        'weighted within-bar close-location value (transient-impact snapback), '
        'weighting the two channels by the cross-sectional rank of trailing market '
        'R-squared and amplifying the blend where the channels agree in sign.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # kernel / deficit channel
    _J = 4
    _n = 180
    _nmin = 90
    _vol_win = 180
    _vol_min = 60
    _thresh = 1.5
    _Lmax = 12
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.3
    # microstructure channel
    _part_win = 60
    _agg_win = 3
    _part_cap = 4.0
    _den_shrink = 0.5
    _beta_win = 120
    # interaction
    _kappa = 0.6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        T, N = len(idx), len(cols)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._nmin) + int(self._J) + 5 or N < 3:
            return zero

        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sig = (ret.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)

        # ---------- channel 1: event-anchored kernel delivery deficit -------------
        mkt = ret.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))
        shock = z.abs() > float(self._thresh)
        xs = z.where(shock, 0.0)
        base = (z * z).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()

        yhat = None
        for j in range(int(self._J) + 1):
            xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
            den = (xl * xl).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
            num = (y0.mul(xl, axis=0)
                   .rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
            denom = (den + float(self._ridge) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._shrink)).fillna(0.0)
            contrib = th.mul(z.shift(j).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            yhat = contrib if yhat is None else yhat.add(contrib)

        gap = (yhat - y).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cum = gap.fillna(0.0).cumsum()
        prev = cum.shift(1)
        mask = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], N, axis=1),
                            index=idx, columns=cols)
        anchor = prev.where(mask).ffill()
        alt = cum.shift(int(self._Lmax))
        age = _bars_since(shock, float(self._Lmax))
        use_evt = (age < float(self._Lmax)).to_numpy()
        anchor_eff = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(use_evt[:, None], anchor.to_numpy(), alt.to_numpy()),
            index=idx, columns=cols)
        nbars = (age + 1.0).clip(1.0, float(self._Lmax))
        deficit = (cum - anchor_eff).div(np.sqrt(nbars), axis=0)
        deficit = deficit.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(int(self._J), min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        deficit = deficit.where(alive)

        # ---------- channel 2: idio participation-weighted range snapback ---------
        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = ((close - lo) - (hi - close)) / rng
        clv = clv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        vbase = ts_mean(volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
                        int(self._part_win)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        part = (volume / vbase).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, float(self._part_cap))
        ok = clv.notna() & part.notna()
        c = clv.where(ok, 0.0)
        w = part.where(ok, 0.0)
        disp = (decay_linear(w * c, int(self._agg_win))
                / (decay_linear(w, int(self._agg_win)) + float(self._den_shrink)))
        disp = disp.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get('sector'), cols)
        fallback = _broadcast(disp.mean(axis=1), disp)
        if lab is not None:
            gmean = disp.T.groupby(lab).transform('mean').T
            gmean = gmean.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
        else:
            gmean = fallback
        snap = -(disp - gmean)                     # closed LOW on volume => bounce
        snap = snap.where(ok.rolling(int(self._agg_win), min_periods=1).sum() > 0)

        # ---------- router: trailing market R-squared -----------------------------
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, ret)
        rho = correlation(ret, mkt_df, int(self._beta_win))
        r2 = rho.pow(2.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        s = rank(r2)
        s = s.where(s.notna(), 0.5)

        a = _centred_rank(deficit)                 # systematic owed catch-up
        b = _centred_rank(snap)                    # idio transient-impact snapback
        a_ok, b_ok = a.notna(), b.notna()
        s_eff = s.where(b_ok, 1.0).where(a_ok, 0.0)
        af, bf = a.fillna(0.0), b.fillna(0.0)

        core = s_eff * af + (1.0 - s_eff) * bf
        conc = np.sign(af.to_numpy()) * np.sign(bf.to_numpy())
        conc = pd.DataFrame(conc, index=idx, columns=cols)
        raw = core * (1.0 + float(self._kappa) * conc)

        valid = a_ok | b_ok
        raw = raw.where(valid)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return (score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
                .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0))
programs.name: Kernel-deficit / transient-impact snapback routed by variance share
programs.trading_idea: Parent A measures how much of a name's kernel-implied response to the last common market shock is still *owed* (a systematic delivery gap that closes slowly), while Parent B measures how far a name closed inside its own heavy-volume bar range after sector-common flow is purged (an idiosyncratic, fast-decaying cost of immediacy). The child routes the two signals by the same trailing variance decomposition that makes each one valid: for names whose returns are largely market-explained (high trailing R-squared) the owed-beta deficit is the meaningful object, while for high-idiosyncratic-share names the participation-weighted range displacement is the meaningful object — and it then amplifies the blend where the two channels agree in sign and damps it where they disagree. The interaction carries edge neither parent has: sign concordance separates a *mechanical* repricing lag (a name that under-delivered the common impulse AND is sitting low in a heavy-volume range, i.e. still paying transient impact) from *news* (an under-delivering name that is nonetheless closing high on its own volume, where the gap is permanent and must not be chased). Because the fast liquidity-cost channel supplies the timing while the kernel deficit supplies direction and size, the combined signal fires exactly on the ~1-minute transient-impact decay window rather than drifting out to the parents' 24-bar peak.
programs.description: Blends (i) the event-anchored, shock-selected local-projection kernel deficit of each name's vol-normalised return path versus its implied response to the common market shock, and (ii) the negative of its sector-purged, participation-weighted within-bar close-location value, weighting the two by the cross-sectional rank of trailing market R-squared and multiplicatively amplifying (damping) the blend where the two channels agree (disagree) in sign.

programs.code:
"""Noise-share-scaled centre-price beta backlog.

Mechanism
---------
Two mispricing legs are measured on the SAME 6-bar clock as the forecast and
both are scaled by the fraction of price variance that actually dies inside
that clock:

1. Efficient-price backlog.  The bar's range centre c = (max(H,O,C) +
   min(L,O,C)) / 2 averages two order statistics of the intrabar mid path and
   therefore carries far less microstructure noise than the single closing
   sample.  Using centre-to-centre returns as the efficient price, each name's
   loading on the common shock is estimated by a trailing SHOCK-SELECTED
   regression of its 6-bar cumulative vol-normalised return Y on the 6-bar
   cumulative market shock S (only |S| above its trailing scale contributes,
   the sample where news transmission rather than bid-ask bounce dominates),
   with a ridge and empirical-Bayes cross-sectional shrinkage.  The backlog
   D = (beta * S - Y) / sqrt(6) is the horizon-matched undelivered response.

2. Endpoint noise leg.  u = (C - c) / c / sigma is the closing print's
   dislocation from the bar's own range centre in return-vol units.  It is
   weighted by 1 / (1 + V / medianV) so QUIET bars - where the dislocation is
   transient quote noise, not permanent impact - dominate, and aggregated with
   linear decay over 3 bars.

Since close-based cumulative return = centre-based cumulative return + change
in endpoint dislocation, the total close-based gap is (D - u); the fraction of
it that closes within k = 6 bars is the two-scale noise share
phi = (1 - VR_6) * 6/5, which is used as the multiplicative coefficient.  High
phi names are the ones whose gaps close inside the fixed horizon; low phi names
owe their catch-up much later and are damped.

Signal = rank(phi * (D - u_eff)); positive means under-delivered / dislocated
below centre -> expect positive 6-bar return.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _noise_share(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int, nmin: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fraction of one-bar return variance that is transient at horizon k.

    Efficient price plus i.i.d. additive noise gives Var(r1) = s2 + 2u2 and
    Var(rk)/k = s2 + 2u2/k, so with VR = Var(rk)/(k Var(r1)),
    phi = 2u2 / Var(r1) = (1 - VR) * k/(k-1).  All terms are trailing rolling
    statistics, hence causal.
    """
    v1 = ret.rolling(int(n), min_periods=int(nmin)).var()
    rk = ret.rolling(int(k), min_periods=int(k)).sum()
    vk = rk.rolling(int(n), min_periods=int(nmin)).var()
    denom = (float(k) * v1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    vr = vk / denom
    phi = (1.0 - vr) * (float(k) / float(k - 1))
    return phi.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading toward its cross-sectional mean."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


@register_factor
class NoiseShareScaledCentrePriceBetaBacklog(BaseFactor):
    """Horizon-matched centre-price response deficit scaled by the 6-bar noise share."""

    factor_id = 'noise_share_scaled_centre_price_beta_backlog'
    name = 'Noise-share-scaled centre-price beta backlog'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Ranks the two-scale (k=6) noise share times the sum of (i) the horizon-matched '
        'undelivered response of the low-noise range-centre price path to the 6-bar '
        'cumulative common shock, using a shock-selected shrunk trailing loading, and '
        '(ii) minus the quiet-bar-weighted closing dislocation from the bar range centre.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 6           # horizon-matched accumulation (bars) = prediction_horizon
    _n = 240         # trailing loading-estimation window
    _nmin = 90
    _vol_win = 240
    _vol_min = 60
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.3
    _phi_n = 180
    _phi_min = 90
    _med_win = 60
    _agg = 3

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if len(idx) < int(self._nmin) + 3 * int(self._K) or len(cols) < 3:
            return zero

        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()

        # ---- low-noise efficient-price proxy: the bar's high-low centre ------
        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        centre = 0.5 * (hi + lo)
        cpx = centre.replace(0.0, np.nan).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        r_c = cpx.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        r_cl = (close.replace(0.0, np.nan).pct_change()
                .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2))

        sig = (r_cl.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (r_c / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # ---- common shock from the low-noise cross-sectional median ----------
        mkt = r_c.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))

        K = int(self._K)
        S = z.rolling(K, min_periods=K).sum().fillna(0.0)
        Y = y.fillna(0.0).rolling(K, min_periods=K).sum()
        alive = y.notna().rolling(K, min_periods=1).sum() > 0

        # ---- shock-selected trailing loading of Y on S -----------------------
        sS = (S.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
              .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        w = (S.abs() > sS).astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        num = (Y.fillna(0.0).mul(w * S, axis=0)
               .rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
        den = ((w * S * S).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
        base = ((S * S).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
        denom = (den + float(self._ridge) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        beta = _shrink_cs(beta.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._shrink)).fillna(0.0)

        deficit = (beta.mul(S, axis=0) - Y) / float(np.sqrt(float(K)))
        deficit = deficit.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # ---- endpoint dislocation leg, weighted toward quiet bars ------------
        u = ((close - centre) / cpx / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        u = u.clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        med = (volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
               .rolling(int(self._med_win), min_periods=max(10, int(self._med_win) // 3))
               .median().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        rel = (volume / med).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 20.0).fillna(1.0)
        wq = 1.0 / (1.0 + rel)
        u_eff = decay_linear((wq * u).fillna(0.0), int(self._agg))
        u_eff = u_eff.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- horizon-matched transient share as the shared coefficient ------
        phi = _noise_share(r_cl, K, int(self._phi_n), int(self._phi_min))
        row_med = phi.median(axis=1)
        phi = phi.T.fillna(row_med).T.fillna(0.5)

        raw = (phi * (deficit - u_eff)).where(alive)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Noise-share-scaled centre-price beta backlog
programs.trading_idea: Parent B's owed-beta deficit is real but slow: it is measured on close prices, so bid-ask bounce contaminates the 'already delivered' term, and it pools names whose gaps close in 6 bars with names whose gaps close in 30, which is why its IC peaks at 24 bars. Parent A supplies exactly the two missing pieces: (i) the range centre (H+L)/2 is a much lower-noise sample of the efficient price than the single close, so the horizon-matched response deficit D = beta_i * S_t - Y_t (6-bar cumulative common shock times a shock-selected trailing loading, minus the realized 6-bar centre-price path) becomes an uncontaminated measure of undelivered repricing; and (ii) the two-scale noise share phi = (1-VR_6)*6/5 is precisely the fraction of one-bar close variance that dies inside the fixed 6-bar horizon, so it is the correct per-name coefficient on how much of any gap actually closes by t+6 — used as a multiplicative state variable it selects the fast-closing names instead of averaging them with slow ones. The residual close-minus-centre endpoint dislocation, down-weighted on heavy-volume bars (permanent impact) and up-weighted on quiet bars (pure quote noise), is then the second, faster leg of the same total close-based gap and enters with the same sign, so the interaction gives a horizon-matched decomposition — owed efficient-price response plus decaying endpoint noise, both scaled by the measured 6-bar transient share — that neither parent has alone.
programs.description: Ranks phi * (horizon-matched centre-price beta backlog minus quiet-bar-weighted endpoint dislocation), where the backlog is the shock-selected trailing loading applied to the 6-bar cumulative market shock minus the realized 6-bar vol-normalised centre-price return, and phi is the two-scale (k=6) microstructure noise share.

programs.code:
"""Donchian-window expiry: the resistance/support shift that is already known.

Mechanism
---------
Breakout and stop-order traders condition on trailing extremes: the N-bar high
H_N(t) = max(p_{t-N+1..t}) and the N-bar low L_N(t).  Over the next h bars the
window rolls forward and the oldest h bars leave it.  The part of the level's
future move that is caused by *entering* prints is unforecastable under a
martingale; the part caused by *expiring* prints is fully known today:

    H_N(t+h) >= max(p_{t-N+1+h..t}) = H_{N-h}(t)      (survivor max)

so if the running N-bar high was printed inside the expiring block, the
resistance level drops with certainty from H_N(t) to H_{N-h}(t) with no news.
A lower trigger level mechanically raises the probability that any given path
sets off stop-buy / breakout orders, and the induced flow pushes price up.
Mirror image for an expiring N-bar low: support rises, stop-sell triggers get
easier, flow pushes price down.

The known level shift is mapped into economically meaningful units with the
reflection principle for a driftless random walk,

    P(touch level L within h bars) ~ 2 * Phi( -(L - p_t) / (sigma * sqrt(h)) ),

clipped at one, so a level shift only matters when the barrier is close enough
to be reached inside exactly the next h bars.  The signal is the up-side
probability gain minus the down-side probability gain, summed over the
lookbacks the crowd plausibly watches, scaled by a saturating volume/ADV gate
(mechanical trigger flow needs active participants).

All statistics are trailing rolling extrema of past-and-present bars, so the
value at t uses only information available at t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import math
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _hit_prob(dist: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Reflection-principle probability of touching a barrier `dist` horizon-sigmas
    away within the horizon (dist <= 0 means the barrier is already breached)."""
    d = dist.clip(lower=0.0)
    vals = 2.0 * special.ndtr(-d.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    vals = np.clip(vals, 0.0, 1.0)
    return pd.DataFrame(vals, index=dist.index, columns=dist.columns)

@register_factor
class DonchianExpiryLevelShiftBreakoutTriggerDrift(BaseFactor):
    """Known-in-advance Donchian level shift from expiring extremes."""
    factor_id = 'donchian_expiry_level_shift_breakout_trigger_dri'
    name = 'Donchian expiry level-shift breakout-trigger drift'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Certain shift of trailing 30/60/120-bar Donchian highs and lows caused by the oldest 6 bars expiring, converted into reflection-principle barrier-hit probability gains over the next 6 bars, netted up minus down, gated by a saturating volume/ADV activity term and ranked cross-sectionally.'
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ['close', 'high', 'low', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _windows = (30, 60, 120)
    _vol_win = 240
    _vol_min = 60
    _adv_win = 240
    _adv_min = 60
    _d_clip = 8.0
    _act_scale = 1.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)

        def _get(field: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
            df = data.get(field)
            if df is None:
                return close.copy()
            return df.astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        high = _get('high')
        low = _get('low')
        volume = _get('volume').abs()
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        p = np.log(px).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hi = np.log(high.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lo = np.log(low.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hi = pd.concat([hi, p], axis=0).groupby(level=0).max().reindex(index=idx)[cols] if False else hi.where(hi >= p, p)
        lo = lo.where(lo <= p, p)
        ret = p.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sigma = ret.rolling(self._vol_win, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        sh = (sigma * math.sqrt(float(h))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        valid = pd.DataFrame(False, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for N in self._windows:
            m = int(N) - h
            if m < h:
                continue
            hi_full = hi.rolling(int(N), min_periods=int(N)).max()
            hi_surv = hi.rolling(m, min_periods=m).max()
            lo_full = lo.rolling(int(N), min_periods=int(N)).min()
            lo_surv = lo.rolling(m, min_periods=m).min()
            d_up_full = ((hi_full - p) / sh).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            d_up_surv = ((hi_surv - p) / sh).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            d_dn_full = ((p - lo_full) / sh).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            d_dn_surv = ((p - lo_surv) / sh).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            d_up_full = d_up_full.clip(-self._d_clip, self._d_clip)
            d_up_surv = d_up_surv.clip(-self._d_clip, self._d_clip)
            d_dn_full = d_dn_full.clip(-self._d_clip, self._d_clip)
            d_dn_surv = d_dn_surv.clip(-self._d_clip, self._d_clip)
            up_gain = _hit_prob(d_up_surv) - _hit_prob(d_up_full)
            dn_gain = _hit_prob(d_dn_surv) - _hit_prob(d_dn_full)
            contrib = (up_gain - dn_gain).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            valid = valid | contrib.notna()
            total = total + contrib.fillna(0.0)
        advb = volume.rolling(self._adv_win, min_periods=self._adv_min).mean()
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        a_rel = volume.rolling(h, min_periods=2).mean() / advb
        a_rel = a_rel.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 50.0)
        gate = 1.0 - np.exp(-a_rel / self._act_scale)
        raw = (total * gate).where(valid)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Donchian expiry level-shift breakout-trigger drift
programs.trading_idea: The parent showed that the *mechanically known* part of a trailing-window estimator's future move forecasts returns, but a moving-average anchor drifts diffusely, which is why its IC kept building out to 24 bars. Breakout/stop traders instead condition on trailing extremes (N-bar Donchian high/low), and an extreme is a *discrete* object: if the running N-bar high was printed inside the block of bars that expires over the next h bars, then the resistance level falls to the second-highest survivor with certainty and no new information, so the conditional probability that a driftless path triggers stop-buy/breakout orders jumps at a known instant; symmetrically an expiring N-bar low lifts the support level and makes stop-sell triggers easier. Converting the known level shift into a barrier-hit-probability change with the reflection principle (2Φ(−d/σ√h)) makes the signal fire only when price is close enough to actually reach the level within exactly the next 6 bars, so the edge should be concentrated at the target horizon rather than smeared across 24 bars. It resists arbitrage because each event is tiny and window-specific, the profit requires guessing which lookbacks the crowd watches, and the counter-trade means standing in front of mechanically arriving trigger flow.
programs.description: For lookbacks N in {30,60,120} bars it computes the certain shift of the trailing Donchian high/low caused by the oldest h=6 bars expiring (max over N bars minus max over the surviving N−h bars, and the mirror for the low), converts each shift into the change in the reflection-principle probability that price touches that level within the next 6 bars, sums the up-minus-down probability gains across lookbacks, scales by a saturating volume/ADV activity gate and ranks cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Side-split realized inverse depth: the mid follows the path of least resistance.

Mechanism
---------
We cannot see the book, but we can see what it *cost* in executed volume to move
the mid each way.  Over a trailing window, the sum of positive log returns divided
by the sqrt-volume consumed on those bars is a realized estimate of inverse ask
depth (displacement per unit of consumed liquidity); the same statistic on down
bars estimates inverse bid depth.  If the ask side is thin relative to the bid,
then even *balanced* order flow drifts the mid upward - buy orders travel far, sell
orders travel little - and because queue-replenishment / hidden-liquidity rates are
strongly autocorrelated at the second-to-minute scale, that asymmetry persists over
the next few bars.

The statistic is built from magnitudes only (per-side efficiencies), and is then
cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the trailing 6-bar and 60-bar net returns,
so the surviving signal is the *wedge* between price-based and volume-based
directionality rather than the short-horizon reversal channel that standard
signed-flow factors already span.

Falsifiable: forward 6-bar returns should load POSITIVELY on log(up-side
efficiency / down-side efficiency) after the return purge.  If the loading is zero,
or if it disappears entirely once the return ranks are purged, then the per-side
impact-efficiency ratio carries no latent-depth information and the reading is
wrong.

All statistics are trailing rolling sums or same-bar cross-sectional operations:
the value at bar t uses only information available at t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delta, rank, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank, centred row by row (mean zero per bar)."""
    r = rank(df)
    return r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

def _xs_purge(y: pd.DataFrame, z: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise cross-sectional OLS residual of y on z (both row-centred).

    Uses only same-bar cross-sectional information, so it is causal.
    """
    yz = (y * z).sum(axis=1)
    zz = (z * z).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = (yz / zz).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    return y.sub(z.mul(beta, axis=0))

@register_factor
class RealizedInverseDepthSideWedgeMomentumPurged(BaseFactor):
    """Realized inverse ask depth minus inverse bid depth, purged of net returns."""
    factor_id = 'realized_inverse_depth_side_wedge_momentum_purge'
    name = 'Side-split realized inverse depth wedge (momentum-purged)'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Log ratio of up-side to down-side realized impact efficiency (sum of signed-side log displacement per unit sqrt(volume) consumed on that side over 60 bars), cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the 6-bar and 60-bar net-return ranks: long names whose upward moves are cheap in volume terms relative to their downward moves.'
    window_length = 72
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _win = 60
    _fast = 6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        vol = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        vol = vol.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        lp = np.log(close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        v = np.sqrt(vol.clip(lower=0.0))
        up = ret.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dn = (-ret).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        v_up = v.where(ret > 0, 0.0)
        v_dn = v.where(ret < 0, 0.0)
        disp_up = ts_sum(up, self._win)
        disp_dn = ts_sum(dn, self._win)
        vol_up = ts_sum(v_up, self._win)
        vol_dn = ts_sum(v_dn, self._win)
        tot_disp = disp_up + disp_dn
        tot_vol = vol_up + vol_dn
        k_d = 0.05 * tot_disp
        k_v = 0.05 * tot_vol
        eff_up = (disp_up + k_d) / (vol_up + k_v).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eff_dn = (disp_dn + k_d) / (vol_dn + k_v).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ratio = (eff_up / eff_dn).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        raw = np.log(ratio.where(ratio > 0.0))
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        active = (tot_vol > 0.0) & (tot_disp > 0.0)
        raw = raw.where(active)
        y = _centred_rank(raw)
        z_fast = _centred_rank(delta(lp, self._fast))
        z_slow = _centred_rank(delta(lp, self._win))
        res = _xs_purge(y, z_fast)
        z_slow_orth = _xs_purge(z_slow, z_fast)
        res = _xs_purge(res, z_slow_orth)
        signal = rank(res.where(raw.notna()))
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Side-split realized inverse depth wedge (momentum-purged)
programs.trading_idea: With no depth feed, the volume it actually took to move the mid up versus down is a consistent estimator of latent book imbalance: displacement-per-unit-sqrt-volume on up bars measures inverse ask depth, the same statistic on down bars measures inverse bid depth. When the ask is thin relative to the bid, mechanically balanced order flow drifts the mid upward (buys travel far, sells travel little), and queue-replenishment rates are strongly autocorrelated over minutes, so the asymmetry survives well past one bar. Crucially the statistic is built from magnitudes only and is then cross-sectionally orthogonalised against the 6-bar and 60-bar net returns, so it is not a repackaged reversal/momentum signal — it is the wedge between price-based and volume-based directionality. The edge persists because harvesting it requires taking or posting on the thin side, where net-of-spread capacity at the one-minute scale is tiny, and any size traded on that side refills the very depth hole that produced the signal.
programs.description: For each name over a trailing 60-bar window, computes displacement per unit sqrt(volume) separately for up bars and down bars (realized inverse ask depth vs inverse bid depth), takes the log of their ratio, and cross-sectionally purges the resulting rank of the 6-bar and 60-bar net-return ranks; long names whose upward moves are cheap in volume terms relative to their downward moves.

programs.code:
"""Shock-deficit residual split by volume-clock permanence.

Mechanism
---------
Let m_t be the common (cross-sectional median) return and z_t its trailing
z-score.  Each name's vol-normalised return y_t = r_t / sigma_t responds to the
common shock as a distributed lag

    y_t = sum_{j=0..J} theta_j z_{t-j} + e_t ,

with theta_j estimated by *event-conditional* trailing local projections, i.e.
using the shock-selected regressor x_t = z_t * 1{|z_t| > c} so that news
transmission, not bid-ask bounce, identifies the kernel.  Applying the kernel to
the observed market path gives yhat_t, and gap_t = yhat_t - y_t is the per-bar
shortfall.

Parent A accumulated that shortfall since the last common shock and treated a
positive deficit as unconditionally owed.  But a shortfall can arise two ways:
(i) trades pushed the price away from the implied path -- transient inventory
impact that decays as depth refills, so the deficit really is owed and closes;
or (ii) the price drifted away while the tape was quiet -- pure quote revision,
close to permanent and often still unfolding, so the deficit widens instead of
closing.  Parent B's two-clock test separates exactly these cases, so here it is
applied not to raw price but to the *residual* path

    R_t = cumsum(y - yhat) ,
    W   = corr(R, cumulative normalized volume) - corr(R, linear time ramp),

over fast trailing windows.  W > 0: the residual was paid for with trades
(transient -> deficit closes); W < 0: it accrued in the quiet bars (permanent ->
deficit persists / widens, sign flips).

To work at the fixed 6-bar offset the accumulation is exponentially discounted
(half-life ~4 bars) inside the event-anchored window, so only the freshly opened,
fast-decaying part of the gap enters the score.

All statistics are trailing: rolling windows, positive lags, forward fills only,
so the value at bar t sees only bars <= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import correlation, rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_EPS = 1e-12

def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading towards its cross-sectional mean (empirical Bayes)."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)

def _bars_since(flag: pd.Series, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Bars elapsed since the last True in flag (causal forward fill only)."""
    s = pd.Series(np.arange(len(flag.index), dtype=float), index=flag.index)
    last = s.where(flag.to_numpy()).ffill()
    return (s - last).clip(0.0, cap).fillna(cap)

def _disc_cumsum(df: pd.DataFrame, phi: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A_t = sum_{s<=t} phi^{t-s} x_s, computed with a causal recursive EW mean."""
    alpha = 1.0 - phi
    return df.ewm(alpha=alpha, adjust=False).mean() / max(alpha, _EPS)

def _volume_clock(volume: pd.DataFrame, norm_window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cumulative volume in units of the name's own recent typical bar."""
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    scale = ts_mean(v, norm_window).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    vn = (v / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    return vn.cumsum()

def _ramp(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ramp = np.arange(len(frame.index), dtype=float)
    return pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(ramp[:, None], frame.shape[1], axis=1), index=frame.index, columns=frame.columns)

@register_factor
class ShockDeficitResidualVolumeClockPermanenceSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Owed catch-up when the residual was trade-paid; continuation when it was quiet."""
    factor_id = 'shock_deficit_residual_volume_clock_permanence_s'
    name = 'Shock-deficit residual split by volume-clock permanence'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Discounted event-anchored deficit of the realized vol-normalised path versus a trailing event-conditional impulse-response kernel on common market shocks, multiplied by a signed gate from the residual path's volume-clock minus calendar-clock trend alignment (trade-paid residuals close the deficit, quiet residuals continue)."
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _J = 6
    _n = 240
    _nmin = 90
    _vol_win = 240
    _vol_min = 60
    _thresh = 1.5
    _Lmax = 15
    _phi = 0.85
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.3
    _norm_window = 240
    _w_fast = 20
    _w_slow = 40

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        T, N = (len(idx), len(cols))
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._nmin) + int(self._J) + 5 or N < 3:
            return zero
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sig = ret.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min)).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        y = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)
        mkt = ret.median(axis=1)
        mvol = mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min)).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0)
        shock = z.abs() > float(self._thresh)
        xs = z.where(shock, 0.0)
        base = (z * z).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
        yhat = None
        for j in range(int(self._J) + 1):
            xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
            den = (xl * xl).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
            num = y0.mul(xl, axis=0).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
            denom = (den + float(self._ridge) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._shrink)).fillna(0.0)
            contrib = th.mul(z.shift(j).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            yhat = contrib if yhat is None else yhat.add(contrib)
        gap = (yhat - y).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        phi = float(self._phi)
        A = _disc_cumsum(gap.fillna(0.0), phi)
        age = _bars_since(shock, float(self._Lmax))
        disc = pd.Series(np.power(phi, age.to_numpy() + 1.0), index=idx)
        mask = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], N, axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        anchor = A.shift(1).where(mask).ffill().fillna(0.0)
        d_anch = A - anchor.mul(disc, axis=0)
        use = age.to_numpy() < float(self._Lmax)
        deficit = pd.DataFrame(np.where(use[:, None], d_anch.to_numpy(), A.to_numpy()), index=idx, columns=cols)
        var_a = (1.0 - np.power(phi, 2.0 * (age.to_numpy() + 1.0))) / (1.0 - phi * phi)
        var_f = 1.0 / (1.0 - phi * phi)
        eff = pd.Series(np.sqrt(np.where(use, var_a, var_f)), index=idx)
        dn = deficit.div(eff, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        resid_path = (y - yhat).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).cumsum()
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vclock = _volume_clock(volume, int(self._norm_window))
        tclock = _ramp(close)
        w_fast = correlation(resid_path, vclock, int(self._w_fast)) - correlation(resid_path, tclock, int(self._w_fast))
        w_slow = correlation(resid_path, vclock, int(self._w_slow)) - correlation(resid_path, tclock, int(self._w_slow))
        wedge = (0.5 * (w_fast + w_slow)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gate = 2.0 * (rank(wedge) - 0.5)
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(int(self._J), min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        raw = (dn * gate).where(alive & wedge.notna() & dn.notna())
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Shock-deficit residual split by volume-clock permanence
programs.trading_idea: Parent A measures how much of a name's own kernel-implied response to the last common market shock it has still not delivered, but assumes every such gap is owed and will close; Parent B knows that a displacement is transient inventory impact when it was paid for with trades and near-permanent quote revision when it accrued while the tape was quiet — but it applies that test to raw price, which is dominated by the common beta response. The child applies B's two-clock test to A's object: it builds the *residual* path (realized minus kernel-implied vol-normalised return since the last large common shock) and asks whether that residual accumulated in the heavy-volume bars (corr with the cumulative volume clock) or in the quiet bars (corr with the calendar ramp). A trade-aligned residual is transient impact, so the discounted deficit is genuinely owed and closes over the next few bars (long positive deficit); a quiet residual is a permanent, still-unfolding repricing, so the same deficit will widen rather than close and the sign flips. Neither parent can make this distinction: A signs all deficits the same way, B has no benchmark path against which to define a residual, and the interaction is what converts a 24-bar catch-up effect into a 6-bar one by discounting the accumulation with a ~4-bar half-life so only the still-open, fast-decaying part survives.
programs.description: Estimates each name's event-conditional distributed-lag response kernel to common (cross-sectional median) shocks by trailing local projections on the large-|z| subsample, accumulates the exponentially discounted deficit of the realized vol-normalised path versus the kernel-implied path since the last common shock, and multiplies it by a signed gate equal to the cross-sectional rank of the residual path's volume-clock minus calendar-clock trend alignment (positive = trade-paid/transient, negative = quiet/permanent).

programs.code:
"""In-window release fraction: trade-clock weighted probe / displacement switch.

Mechanism
---------
Two components of a recent price path carry opposite predictive polarity:

  * probed excursion that was NOT converted into net displacement (wicks beyond
    the bar endpoints, printed on bars that actually traded size) -- the endpoint
    mid is a stale sample of where aggression reached, so the mid catches up;
  * beta-residual net displacement that WAS converted (a level was swept) --
    transient price impact, which relaxes back.

The state variable that selects between them is the conversion ratio

    c = |displacement stock| / (|displacement stock| + probe stock)

both measured in units of the name's own robust grid quantum.  What is new here
is the CLOCK.  Outstanding pressure relaxes in *trade time*, not calendar time:
the per-bar retention is a = exp(-speed / kappa) with speed = recent volume /
ADV, so the outstanding stock of pressure is S_t = sum_tau a^tau x_{t-tau} and
the part of it that will actually be released during the next H = 6 bars is
(1 - a^H) * S_t.  Ranking names by that in-window release quantity, rather than
by the raw stock, matches the mechanism to the fixed 6-bar forecast offset and
replaces any hand-set absorption gate with a derived one (fast clocks release
nearly all of their outstanding pressure inside the window, slow clocks almost
none).

All statistics are trailing rolling windows and positive lags, hence causal.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_TINY = 1e-12

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=idx, columns=cols)

def _decay_stock(x: pd.DataFrame, a: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Outstanding stock S_t = sum_{tau=0}^{k-1} a_t^tau * x_{t-tau}.

    ``a`` is a per-name, time-varying retention in (0, 1).  Only positive lags
    are used, so the value at t depends on information up to t only.
    """
    xf = x.fillna(0.0)
    out = xf.copy()
    w = a.copy()
    for tau in range(1, k):
        out = out + w * xf.shift(tau)
        w = w * a
    return out

@register_factor
class InWindowReleaseFractionProbeDisplacementSwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Trade-clock release-fraction weighted probe / displacement polarity switch."""
    factor_id = 'inwindow_release_fraction_probe_displacement_swi'
    name = 'In-window release fraction: trade-clock weighted probe/displacement switch'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Accumulates signed probe-excursion and beta-residual displacement stocks with a per-name trade-clock exponential retention, blends them with conversion-ratio weights (1-c) and -c, and scales by the fraction of the stock expected to relax inside the 6-bar forecast window before cross-sectional ranking.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _H = 6
    _K = 24
    _q_window = 240
    _q_min = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _vol_window = 60
    _adv_window = 240
    _speed_window = 6
    _kappa = 3.0
    _c_prior = 0.5
    _scale = 4.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        absr = ret.abs()
        nz = absr.where(absr > _TINY)
        q = nz.rolling(self._q_window, min_periods=self._q_min).quantile(0.2)
        q = q.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mkt = ret.mean(axis=1, skipna=True).fillna(0.0)
        mkt_bd = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, mkt_bd, self._beta_window)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (ret - beta * mkt_bd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        advb = adv(volume.fillna(0.0), self._adv_window)
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        speed = ts_mean(volume.fillna(0.0), self._speed_window) / advb
        speed = speed.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.05, 20.0)
        a = np.exp(-speed / self._kappa)
        a = a.clip(0.05, 0.98).fillna(0.75)
        f = 1.0 - a ** float(self._H)
        hi_end = _pair_max(open_, close)
        lo_end = _pair_min(open_, close)
        hi = _pair_max(high, hi_end)
        lo = _pair_min(low, lo_end)
        up_w = (hi - hi_end).clip(lower=0.0)
        dn_w = (lo_end - lo).clip(lower=0.0)
        med = volume.rolling(self._vol_window, min_periods=20).median()
        gate = ((volume > med) & med.notna() & volume.notna()).astype(float)
        probe = ((up_w - dn_w) / px / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        x_p = (probe * gate).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        x_t = (resid / q).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        s_p = _decay_stock(x_p, a, self._K)
        s_t = _decay_stock(x_t, a, self._K)
        c = (s_t.abs() / (s_t.abs() + s_p.abs() + self._c_prior)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        chan_p = np.tanh(s_p / self._scale)
        chan_t = np.tanh(s_t / self._scale)
        raw = f * ((1.0 - c) * chan_p - c * chan_t)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        raw = raw.where(q.notna() & advb.notna())
        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
