programs.code:
"""Peer-cohesion and effective-hedge-leg gated comparability-hedged snapback.

Mechanism
---------
A name's short-run move splits into a peer-basket-spanned part and a residual.
Only the residual is a candidate for fast liquidity-provision repair, and the
repair happens only if the residual is *cheaply hedgeable*.  Hedgeability is
measured here as an explicit statistical property of the peer group rather than
assumed:

  (a) SPECTRAL COHESION.  For a group of n names whose returns are standardised
      by their own trailing volatility (so each has unit variance), the variance
      of the equally-weighted group mean is (1 + (n-1) * rho_bar) / n under an
      equicorrelation approximation.  Inverting a trailing estimate of that
      variance gives rho_bar, i.e. how close the group's covariance spectrum is
      to a single dominant eigenvalue.  High rho_bar => the basket spans the
      name => the residual is a near-riskless hedge => repair is fast.

  (b) EFFECTIVE NUMBER OF LIVE HEDGE LEGS.  Peers are weighted by a
      size-comparability kernel exp(-|log mcap_i - log mcap_j| / h) inside the
      industry (or sector) group.  Restricting those weights to peers that
      actually traded in the last H bars and taking the participation ratio
      (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) gives the effective count of tradable, comparable
      hedge legs.  One live peer is not a hedge; several are.

The impulse is horizon-symmetric: the trailing H=6-bar cumulative residual of
the name's standardised return against its comparability-weighted peer basket
(trailing hedge beta).  Its loading is estimated by a pooled robust sign-slope
b = sum(sign(x) y) / sum(|x|) -- consistent for y = b x under symmetric noise
and tail-robust at 10-second sampling -- fitted separately in each cell of a
2x2 grid of (cohesion) x (effective live legs) and shrunk to the all-cell fit.

Causality: every cross-sectional statistic is taken inside a single timestamp;
every time-series statistic is a trailing rolling window or a positive lag; the
fit pairs the realised target over (t-6 -> t) with regressors observed at t-6.
Static per-ticker inputs (group label, comparability weight) use each name's
EARLIEST available observation, so no future value enters the weights.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static peer-group key per ticker: industry when available, else sector."""
    labels = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[0]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _static_log_size(columns: pd.Index, mcap) -> np.ndarray:
    """Earliest available log market cap per ticker (NaN when unavailable)."""
    out = np.full(len(columns), np.nan)
    if mcap is None:
        return out
    for i, col in enumerate(columns):
        if col not in mcap.columns:
            continue
        ser = pd.to_numeric(mcap[col], errors="coerce")
        ser = ser[np.isfinite(ser) & (ser > 0.0)]
        if len(ser) == 0:
            continue
        out[i] = float(np.log(ser.iloc[0]))
    return out


def _group_matrices(labels: pd.Series, log_size: np.ndarray, columns: pd.Index,
                    band: float):
    """Comparability weight matrix (zero diagonal), its square, and group masks."""
    n = len(columns)
    W = np.zeros((n, n))
    Gd = np.zeros((n, n))
    pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(columns)}
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        idxs = [pos[c] for c in list(members) if c in pos]
        if not idxs:
            continue
        block = np.ix_(idxs, idxs)
        Gd[block] = 1.0
        if len(idxs) < 2:
            continue
        m = log_size[idxs]
        d = np.abs(m[:, None] - m[None, :])
        d = np.where(np.isfinite(d), d, 1.0)
        w = np.exp(-d / float(band))
        np.fill_diagonal(w, 0.0)
        W[block] = w
    Gx = Gd.copy()
    np.fill_diagonal(Gx, 0.0)
    return W, W * W, Gd, Gx


def _vol_scale(df: pd.DataFrame, win: int, minp: int, cap: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sd = df.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = df / sd
    return out.where(np.isfinite(out)).clip(-cap, cap)


def _sign_slope(x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, win: int,
                minp: int, min_obs: float, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Trailing pooled robust slope b = sum(sign(x) * y) / sum(|x|)."""
    valid = mask & x.notna() & y.notna()
    xs = x.where(valid)
    ys = y.where(valid)
    num_row = (np.sign(xs) * ys).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).fillna(0.0)
    den_row = xs.abs().sum(axis=1, min_count=1).fillna(0.0)
    num = num_row.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    den = den_row.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    nobs = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(float).rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum()
    b = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    b = b.where(np.isfinite(b) & (nobs >= float(min_obs)))
    return b.clip(-cap, cap)


@register_factor
class PeerCohesionEffectiveHedgeLegGatedSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Snapback of a comparability-hedged residual, gated by measured hedgeability."""

    factor_id = "peer_cohesion_effective_hedge_leg_gated_snapback"
    name = "Peer-cohesion & effective-hedge-leg gated comparability-hedged snapback"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Forecast of the cross-sectionally demeaned 6-bar forward return from the "
        "6-bar comparability-kernel-hedged residual displacement, loaded by a "
        "trailing pooled robust sign-slope fitted inside 2x2 cells of peer-group "
        "spectral cohesion x effective number of live comparable hedge legs."
    )
    window_length = 1200
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6
    _SD_WIN = 360
    _SD_MIN = 120
    _COH_WIN = 360
    _COH_MIN = 180
    _FIT_WIN = 600
    _FIT_MIN = 200
    _MIN_OBS = 400.0
    _SHRINK = 0.6
    _CAP_B = 3.0
    _BAND = 1.0
    _MIN_PEERS = 3.0
    _MIN_GRP = 4.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        H = self._H
        zeros = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"))
        log_size = _static_log_size(cols, data.get("marketCap"))
        W, W2, Gd, Gx = _group_matrices(labels, log_size, cols, self._BAND)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp.diff()
        sd = r.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (r / sd).where(np.isfinite(r / sd)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        if z.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zeros

        Zf = z.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        P = z.notna().to_numpy().astype(float)

        # ---- comparability-weighted leave-one-out peer basket ----------------
        num_b = Zf @ W.T
        den_b = P @ W.T
        peer_cnt = pd.DataFrame(P @ Gx.T, index=idx, columns=cols)
        basket = np.where(den_b > 1e-10, num_b / np.where(den_b > 1e-10, den_b, 1.0), np.nan)
        basket = pd.DataFrame(basket, index=idx, columns=cols)
        basket = basket.where(peer_cnt >= self._MIN_PEERS)

        beta = rolling_beta(z, basket, self._SD_WIN).clip(0.0, 2.5)
        resid = z - beta * basket
        x = ts_sum(resid, H)
        x = x.where(np.isfinite(x)).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        if x.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zeros

        # ---- target: cross-sectionally demeaned realised H-bar return -------
        rr = lp - lp.shift(H)
        y = _vol_scale(rr.sub(rr.median(axis=1), axis=0), self._SD_WIN, self._SD_MIN, 5.0)

        # ---- state (a): spectral cohesion of the peer group ------------------
        num_g = Zf @ Gd.T
        den_g = P @ Gd.T
        n_live = pd.DataFrame(den_g, index=idx, columns=cols)
        zbar = np.where(den_g > 0.0, num_g / np.where(den_g > 0.0, den_g, 1.0), np.nan)
        zbar = pd.DataFrame(zbar, index=idx, columns=cols).where(n_live >= self._MIN_GRP)
        v_bar = zbar.rolling(self._COH_WIN, min_periods=self._COH_MIN).var()
        n_bar = n_live.rolling(self._COH_WIN, min_periods=self._COH_MIN).mean()
        rho = (n_bar * v_bar - 1.0) / (n_bar - 1.0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rho = rho.where(np.isfinite(rho)).clip(-0.5, 1.0)

        # ---- state (b): effective number of LIVE comparable hedge legs -------
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            act = pd.DataFrame(P, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0), 0.0)
            act = (ts_sum(v, H) > 0.0).astype(float)
        A = act.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        s1 = A @ W.T
        s2 = A @ W2.T
        eff = np.where(s2 > 1e-12, (s1 * s1) / np.where(s2 > 1e-12, s2, 1.0), np.nan)
        eff = pd.DataFrame(eff, index=idx, columns=cols)
        eff = eff.where(np.isfinite(eff) & (peer_cnt >= self._MIN_PEERS))

        g_coh = (rank(rho) - 0.5).where(rho.notna())
        g_leg = (rank(np.log1p(eff)) - 0.5).where(eff.notna())

        xl = x.shift(H)
        coh_l = g_coh.shift(H)
        leg_l = g_leg.shift(H)

        base = xl.notna() & y.notna()
        state_fit = coh_l.notna() & leg_l.notna()
        state_now = g_coh.notna() & g_leg.notna()

        b_all = _sign_slope(xl, y, base, self._FIT_WIN, self._FIT_MIN,
                            self._MIN_OBS, self._CAP_B)

        cells = (
            ((coh_l > 0.0) & (leg_l > 0.0), (g_coh > 0.0) & (g_leg > 0.0)),
            ((coh_l > 0.0) & (leg_l <= 0.0), (g_coh > 0.0) & (g_leg <= 0.0)),
            ((coh_l <= 0.0) & (leg_l > 0.0), (g_coh <= 0.0) & (g_leg > 0.0)),
            ((coh_l <= 0.0) & (leg_l <= 0.0), (g_coh <= 0.0) & (g_leg <= 0.0)),
        )

        pred = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        good = pd.DataFrame(False, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for fit_mask, cur_mask in cells:
            b_c = _sign_slope(xl, y, fit_mask & state_fit & base, self._FIT_WIN,
                              self._FIT_MIN, self._MIN_OBS, self._CAP_B)
            b_c = b_c.where(b_c.notna(), b_all)
            b_u = self._SHRINK * b_c + (1.0 - self._SHRINK) * b_all
            b_u = b_u.where(np.isfinite(b_u))
            sel = (cur_mask & state_now & x.notna()).astype(float)
            contrib = sel * x.fillna(0.0).mul(b_u.fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            pred = pred + contrib.fillna(0.0)
            avail = sel.mul(b_u.notna().astype(float), axis=0)
            good = good | (avail > 0.0)

        signal = pred.where(good & x.notna())
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))
        out = np.sign(signal) * np.sqrt(signal.abs())
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Peer-cohesion & effective-hedge-leg gated comparability-hedged snapback
programs.trading_idea: A dislocation in a name relative to its peer basket only snaps back fast if a market maker can actually neutralise it, and hedgeability is a *measurable spectral property* of the peer group: when the group's trailing covariance is close to one-factor (high average pairwise correlation, estimated from the variance of the cross-sectional mean of vol-standardised returns), the basket spans the name's risk and the hedge residual is almost riskless, so it is repaired within seconds; when the group's spectrum is spread across many directions the 'residual' is genuine idiosyncratic information and is never repaired. Second, the hedge must be executable across several comparable names at once, so the state variable is the *effective number of live hedge legs* — the participation ratio (sum(w)^2/sum(w^2)) of size-comparability weights restricted to peers that actually traded in the last minute — rather than raw aggregate peer activity, because a hedge concentrated in one peer imports that peer's own idiosyncratic risk. Falsifiable prediction: the reversal loading on a horizon-matched 6-bar comparability-hedged residual displacement is strongly negative in high-cohesion / many-live-legs cells and ~0 in low-cohesion or few-legs cells, and (unlike the parent) the conditioned signal's information should peak at ~6 bars because high-cohesion repairs have a sub-minute half-life while the slow, 24-bar component lives entirely in the low-cohesion cells. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a hedging-capital and simultaneous-liquidity constraint: in the states where the constraint binds the trade is unattractive, and in the states where it does not bind the profit is precisely the compensation for supplying that capacity.
programs.description: Forecast of the cross-sectionally demeaned 6-bar forward return from the 6-bar comparability-kernel-hedged residual displacement, loaded by a trailing pooled robust sign-slope fitted separately inside 2x2 cells of peer-group spectral cohesion (average pairwise correlation from the variance of the group's mean standardised return) crossed with the effective number of live comparable hedge legs.

programs.code:
"""Autocovariance-identified transient gain with quiet/traded participation split.

Mechanism
---------
Observed (market-hedged) log mid is modelled as an efficient price plus an AR(1)
pricing error:

    p_t = m_t + e_t,   m_t random walk,   e_t = rho * e_{t-1} + eta_t.

Under that model the return autocovariances are

    gamma_0 = sigma_m^2 + 2 sigma_e^2 (1 - rho)
    gamma_j = -sigma_e^2 (1 - rho)^2 rho^{j-1},   j >= 1,

so rho is identified by gamma_2 / gamma_1 and the *transient variance share* by
-gamma_1 / gamma_0.  Both are estimable from trailing autocovariances alone --
no forward returns, no horizon-matched OLS, no cross-sectional beta shrinkage
(which is what made the parent's gains noise-dominated and slow to adapt).

Which bars carry pricing-error innovations rather than efficient-price
innovations is settled microstructurally: displacement that arrives with prints
is a metaorder footprint (permanent, and by order splitting / Hawkes clustering
it continues), displacement with essentially no prints is quote flicker or
dealer inventory skew that re-centres.  So the bar return is split by the
participation share g = v / (v + trailing mean v) into a traded leg (z * g) and
a quiet leg (z * (1 - g)).

The 6-bar forecast is then exactly horizon-matched:

    forecast = -share * (1 - rho^6) * sum_i rho^i * quiet_{t-i}
               + phi * sum_{i<6} traded_{t-i}

where phi is the trailing lag-1 autocorrelation of the traded leg (floored at
zero: order-splitting continuation only).  Every statistic is trailing and uses
positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _trailing_autocov(x: pd.DataFrame, lag: int, n: int, minp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing pairwise-complete autocovariance of x at a positive lag.

    Causal: only backward rolling sums of contemporaneously observed pairs.
    """
    xl = x.shift(lag)
    m = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(xl)
    a = x.where(m)
    b = xl.where(m)
    cnt = m.astype(float).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
    c = cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    sab = (a * b).rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
    sa = a.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
    sb = b.rolling(n, min_periods=minp).sum()
    cov = sab / c - (sa / c) * (sb / c)
    return cov.where(cnt >= float(minp))


def _geom_accum(x: pd.DataFrame, rho: pd.DataFrame, length: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """sum_{i=0}^{length-1} rho_t^i * x_{t-i} with a per-name, time-varying rho.

    rho is used as of time t (itself estimated from data <= t), so the whole
    accumulation is causal.
    """
    x0 = x.fillna(0.0)
    out = x0.copy()
    w = rho.copy()
    for i in range(1, length):
        out = out + w * x0.shift(i).fillna(0.0)
        w = w * rho
    return out


@register_factor
class AutocovIdentifiedTransientGainSplitH6(BaseFactor):
    """Horizon-matched permanent/transient forecast with self-identified gains."""

    factor_id = 'autocov_identified_transient_gain_split_h6'
    name = 'Autocovariance-identified transient gain, quiet/traded split'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Splits market-hedged, vol-normalised bar returns into a traded leg '
        '(participation share) and a quiet leg, accumulates the quiet leg with '
        'per-name geometric weights rho^i identified from trailing lag-2/lag-1 '
        'return autocovariances, and forms the 6-bar forecast '
        '-(transient share)(1-rho^6)*quiet accumulation + (traded-leg lag-1 '
        'autocorrelation)*(6-bar traded displacement); the rank of that forecast '
        'is the signal.'
    )
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _VOL_WIN = 240
    _VOL_MIN = 60
    _BASE_WIN = 120
    _BASE_MIN = 30
    _ID_WIN = 600
    _ID_MIN = 300
    _ACC_LEN = 12
    _RHO_MAX = 0.95
    _TRUST_MAX = 0.5
    _PHI_MAX = 0.5
    _H = 6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        vol_raw = data.get('volume')
        if vol_raw is None:
            return zero
        volume = vol_raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # market-hedged idiosyncratic return (robust cross-sectional centring)
        u = r.sub(r.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        sd = u.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (u / sd).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # participation share: how much of this bar's move was actually printed
        v = volume.where(np.isfinite(volume) & (volume >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
        base = v.rolling(self._BASE_WIN, min_periods=self._BASE_MIN).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g = (v / (v + base)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        quiet = z * (1.0 - g)
        traded = z * g

        # --- identification of the transient (pricing-error) structure -------
        g1 = _trailing_autocov(z, 1, self._ID_WIN, self._ID_MIN)
        g2 = _trailing_autocov(z, 2, self._ID_WIN, self._ID_MIN)
        g0 = z.rolling(self._ID_WIN, min_periods=self._ID_MIN).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)

        ident = (g1 < 0.0) & (g2 < 0.0)
        rho = (g2 / g1).where(ident)
        rho = rho.where(np.isfinite(rho)).clip(0.0, self._RHO_MAX).fillna(0.0)

        # transient variance share = -gamma_1 / gamma_0 (zero => no reversion)
        trust = (-g1 / g0)
        trust = trust.where(np.isfinite(trust)).clip(0.0, self._TRUST_MAX).fillna(0.0)

        err = _geom_accum(quiet, rho, self._ACC_LEN)
        rev = -trust * (1.0 - rho.pow(float(self._H))) * err

        # --- traded-leg continuation gain (order splitting) ------------------
        ac1 = _trailing_autocov(traded, 1, self._ID_WIN, self._ID_MIN)
        var_a = traded.rolling(self._ID_WIN, min_periods=self._ID_MIN).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        phi = (ac1 / var_a)
        phi = phi.where(np.isfinite(phi)).clip(0.0, self._PHI_MAX).fillna(0.0)
        foot = traded.rolling(self._H, min_periods=3).sum()
        cont = phi * foot.fillna(0.0)

        signal = rev + cont

        valid = (
            sd.notna()
            & base.notna()
            & z.notna()
            & g0.notna()
            & g1.notna()
        )
        signal = signal.where(valid)
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal))

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Autocovariance-identified transient gain, quiet/traded split
programs.trading_idea: Model each name's hedged log mid as efficient price plus an AR(1) pricing error: displacement that arrives with prints is an efficient-price innovation (permanent, and by order-splitting/Hawkes clustering it keeps arriving), while displacement with essentially no prints is dealer quote-skew / flicker that decays at rate rho. The parent estimated the two channel gains by trailing horizon-matched OLS on realised forward returns, which at 10-second resolution is noise-dominated and slow; here both gains are *identified without any forward return* from trailing return autocovariances — under the model gamma_j = -sigma_e^2(1-rho)^2 rho^(j-1), so rho = gamma_2/gamma_1, the transient variance share is -gamma_1/gamma_0, and the traded leg's own lag-1 autocorrelation is the continuation coefficient — giving an exactly horizon-matched forecast -(transient share)(1-rho^6)*(decay-accumulated quiet displacement) + phi*(6-bar traded footprint) that uses every bar of data. The edge persists because harvesting the quiet leg means supplying liquidity against a dealer re-centring its quote (inventory risk) and the traded leg means aligning with possibly-informed persistent metaorder flow (adverse selection); neither is free, and the cross-sectional ordering depends on per-name dispersion in the *identified* noise persistence, which requires jointly estimating participation and the autocovariance structure rather than reading a single reversal window.
programs.description: Splits market-hedged, vol-normalised 10s returns into a traded leg (participation share v/(v+trailing mean v)) and a quiet leg, accumulates the quiet leg with per-name geometric weights rho^i where rho and the transient variance share are identified from trailing lag-1/lag-2 return autocovariances, and forms the horizon-matched forecast -(share)(1-rho^6)*quiet accumulation + (traded-leg lag-1 autocorrelation)*(6-bar traded displacement); the signal is the cross-sectional rank of that forecast.

programs.code:
"""Participation-shape switched Dimson beta gap.

Mechanism
---------
Two ingredients, interacted.

1) A horizon-matched systematic dislocation.  With a staleness-robust Dimson
   beta (sum of trailing univariate loadings on the cap-weighted market at lags
   0, 1, 2) the name *should* have moved beta * M_t(6) over the last 6 bars but
   actually moved r_t(6).  The gap

       D_t = beta_t * M_t(6) - r_t(6)

   is the un-absorbed systematic move net of what the name has already done,
   standardised by trailing idiosyncratic volatility over the same horizon.
   (The parent this comes from folded a distributed-lag kernel against trailing
   market returns but never subtracted the own-return leg, so it collapsed into
   a beta-timed bet on 1-minute market reversal.)

2) The shape of participation.  Normalised Shannon entropy of the last 30
   bars' volume shares, minus its own 120-bar mean, then cross-sectionally
   rank-centred to [-1, 1].  High = volume spread evenly across bars
   (scheduler-like, uninformed provision); low = volume mass concentrated in
   one or two bars (sweep / news print).

The signal is D_t * state_t, scaled by a trade-clock deliverable share
1 - exp(-lambda * 6) where lambda is the trailing fraction of bars that
actually traded (a gap can only be closed on bars where trading happens).
Economically: in an evenly-participating name a gap versus the beta-implied
path is transient inventory pressure and mean-reverts inside the minute (collect
it); in a burst-participating name the displacement is informed and keeps
extending (fade it).  Because the state is centred both in time (own 120-bar
mean) and in the cross-section (rank - 0.5), the unconditional beta-timing and
momentum loadings are purged and only the interaction survives.

All statistics are trailing: the value at bar t uses only bars <= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal cap-weighted market return (weights = previous-bar market cap)."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w.to_numpy()))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret).sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    den = w.sum(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)


def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, cols) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=s.index, columns=cols)


def _rolling_beta(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS slope of y on x, written out from trailing rolling moments."""
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    my = yy.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mx = xx.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxy = (yy * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxx = (xx * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    cov = mxy - my * mx
    var = (mxx - mx * mx).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cov / var).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _normalized_volume_entropy(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shannon entropy of trailing n-bar volume shares divided by log(n).

    With p_i = v_i / S:  H = log(S) - (1/S) * sum(v_i log v_i), computed from two
    trailing rolling sums with the usual 0*log0 = 0 convention.  Result in
    [0, 1]: 1 = perfectly even participation, low = a few bursty bars dominate.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    tot = ts_sum(v, n)
    vlogv = (v * np.log(v.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)
    s_vlogv = ts_sum(vlogv, n)
    tot_safe = tot.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ent = np.log(tot_safe) - s_vlogv / tot_safe
    ent = ent.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / float(np.log(n))
    return ent.clip(0.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class ParticipationShapeSwitchedDimsonBetaGapH6(BaseFactor):
    """Beta gap collected under even participation, faded under bursty participation."""

    factor_id = 'participation_shape_switched_dimson_beta_gap_h6'
    name = 'Participation-shape switched Dimson beta gap (6-bar)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Cross-sectional rank of (Dimson-beta-implied 6-bar market return minus realised '
        '6-bar own return, idiosyncratic-vol scaled) times the cross-sectionally ranked '
        'innovation in the normalised Shannon entropy of 30-bar volume shares, scaled by '
        'the trade-clock deliverable share 1-exp(-arrival rate * 6).'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _beta_window = 240
    _beta_min = 60
    _idio_window = 120
    _idio_min = 60
    _rate_window = 240
    _rate_min = 60
    _ent_span = 30
    _ent_norm = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx = close.index
        cols = close.columns
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            volume = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            volume = volume.astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

        mcap = data.get('marketCap')
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- cap-weighted market and staleness-robust Dimson beta -------------
        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(ret, mcap)
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, cols)

        b0 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df, self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        b1 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df.shift(1), self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        b2 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df.shift(2), self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        beta = b0.clip(-2.0, 4.0)
        beta = beta.add(b1.clip(-2.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)).add(b2.clip(-2.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0))
        beta = beta.clip(0.0, 3.0)
        # empirical-Bayes style shrink of the loading towards one
        beta = 0.5 * beta + 0.5
        beta = beta.where(b0.notna())

        # ---- horizon-matched systematic dislocation ---------------------------
        m_h = mkt.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        r_h = ret.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        gap = beta.mul(m_h, axis=0) - r_h

        resid = ret - beta * mkt_df
        idio = resid.rolling(self._idio_window, min_periods=self._idio_min).std()
        scale = (idio * float(np.sqrt(float(h)))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap_z = (gap / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- participation-shape state (even vs bursty) -----------------------
        ent = _normalized_volume_entropy(volume, self._ent_span)
        ent_innov = ent - ts_mean(ent, self._ent_norm)
        state = 2.0 * (rank(ent_innov) - 0.5)
        state = state.where(ent_innov.notna())

        # ---- trade-clock deliverable share ------------------------------------
        traded = (volume.abs() > 0.0).astype(float)
        lam = traded.rolling(self._rate_window, min_periods=self._rate_min).mean().clip(0.0, 1.0)
        deliver = 1.0 - np.exp(-lam * float(h))
        deliver = deliver.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)

        raw = gap_z * state * (0.25 + 0.75 * deliver)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        alive = ret.notna().rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        raw = raw.where(alive)

        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Participation-shape switched Dimson beta gap (6-bar)
programs.trading_idea: Parent A measured how much market-driven move a name still 'owes' but never subtracted the name's own realised move, so it degenerated into a beta-timed bet on 1-minute market reversal; parent B measured the *shape* of participation (even scheduler-like volume vs. one-bar bursts) but applied it to raw own-path momentum, which the book already spans. The child builds a proper horizon-matched dislocation D = (Dimson beta x trailing 6-bar market return) - (own trailing 6-bar return), i.e. the unabsorbed systematic move net of what the name actually did, and lets B's participation-shape state decide whether that gap is a liquidity error to collect or information to respect: when the last 30 bars' volume is spread evenly across bars (uninformed / scheduled provision, entropy innovation high) an idiosyncratic gap versus the beta-implied path is transient inventory pressure and closes inside the next minute, so trade D long; when volume mass is concentrated in one or two bars (sweep / news print, entropy innovation low) the displacement is informed and keeps extending, so the same gap must be faded. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because it converts a benchmark-relative dislocation of known sign ambiguity into a state-dependent trade, purging the unconditional beta-timing loading (A) and the unconditional momentum loading (B) that killed both parents.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of [ (Dimson-beta-implied 6-bar market return minus realised 6-bar own return, scaled by idiosyncratic vol) x (cross-sectionally ranked innovation in the normalised Shannon entropy of 30-bar volume shares) x trade-clock deliverable share 1-exp(-arrival rate*6) ]: collect the beta gap in evenly-participating names, fade it in burst-participating names.

programs.code:
"""Clock-matched routing between owed kernel backlog and transient-impact snapback.

Mechanism
---------
Two repricing gaps coexist in a 10-second mid-price bar:

1. SYSTEMATIC DELIVERY GAP (owed backlog).  With m_t the cross-sectional median
   return and z_t its trailing z-score, each name responds to common shocks
   through a distributed lag y_t = sum_j theta_j z_{t-j} + e_t (y = r / sigma_r),
   identified on large-|z| bars where news transmission dominates the bounce.
   Folding the trailing shock-selected kernel onto the observed market path gives
   yhat_t; the signed shortfall accumulated since the most recent genuine common
   shock is the beta catch-up still OWED.

2. IDIOSYNCRATIC LIQUIDITY COST.  Aggressive size walks finite visible depth, so
   the mid ends far from the extreme the bar printed.  The sector-common part of
   that displacement is basket information (permanent); the name-specific part is
   the temporary cost of immediacy and decays as passive depth replenishes.  A
   participation-weighted, sector-demeaned close-location value, negated, is a
   fast snapback signal.

SYNTHESIS - the update clock decides *which* gap is tradable at a FIXED horizon.
Let lambda be the trailing fraction of bars whose mid actually moved (the name's
re-quote rate) and clock = lambda * H.  Information in the backlog channel is
HUMP-shaped in clock, not monotone: for clock >> 1 the mid re-quotes every bar,
the backlog is already closed and the measured deficit is microstructure noise;
for clock << 1 the backlog is genuine but is delivered after the evaluation
offset.  So the deficit channel gets a clock-matching kernel peaked at
clock = 1, further multiplied by the rank of trailing market R-squared (a backlog
only exists if the path is market-driven).  The snapback channel gets the
monotone fast-clock weight clock/(1+clock) times the idiosyncratic variance
share, because a transient impact can only revert on bars where the quote moves.
Finally the sign-concordance amplifier (agreement = mechanical repricing lag
still paying transient impact; disagreement = idiosyncratic news that must not be
chased) is scaled by the Poisson deliverable share 1 - exp(-clock), so the
concordance premium is claimed only where delivery can physically happen inside
the window.

Everything is trailing-window / positive-lag causal; sector labels are static
metadata taken from the earliest available observation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import correlation, decay_linear, rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading toward its cross-sectional mean (empirical Bayes)."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _bars_since(flag: pd.Series, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Bars elapsed since the last True in ``flag`` (forward fill only, causal)."""
    s = pd.Series(np.arange(len(flag.index), dtype=float), index=flag.index)
    last = s.where(flag.to_numpy()).ffill()
    out = (s - last).clip(0.0, cap)
    return out.fillna(cap)


def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int = 3):
    """One static label per ticker from a quarterly text field (first valid obs)."""
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = '__POOL__'
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else '__POOL__'
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), '__POOL__')
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab


def _centred_rank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional rank mapped to [-1, 1], NaNs preserved."""
    r = rank(df.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
    return (r - 0.5) * 2.0


def _clock_terms(lam: pd.DataFrame, h: float, s: float):
    """Clock-matching kernel, fast-clock weight and Poisson deliverable share.

    clock = lambda * H is the expected number of re-quotes inside the forecast
    window.  ``w_match`` peaks at clock == 1 (re-quote interval matched to the
    horizon), ``w_fast`` rises monotonically with clock, ``deliver`` is the
    Poisson probability of at least one re-quote inside the window.
    """
    clock = (lam * float(h)).clip(1e-3, 50.0)
    u = np.log(clock)
    w_match = np.exp(-0.5 * (u / float(s)) ** 2)
    w_fast = clock / (1.0 + clock)
    deliver = 1.0 - np.exp(-clock)
    return w_match, w_fast, deliver


@register_factor
class ClockMatchedKernelBacklogVsImpactSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Owed kernel backlog vs idio impact snapback, routed by the re-quote clock."""

    factor_id = 'clock_matched_kernel_backlog_vs_impact_snapback'
    name = 'Clock-matched kernel backlog vs transient-impact snapback'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Routes the event-anchored shock-selected local-projection kernel deficit '
        '(owed systematic catch-up) against the negated sector-purged, participation-'
        'weighted within-bar close-location value (transient-impact snapback) using a '
        'horizon-clock-matching kernel in the trailing mid re-quote rate times market '
        'R-squared for the first channel and a fast-clock weight times idiosyncratic '
        'variance share for the second, amplifying sign concordance in proportion to '
        'the Poisson share of backlog deliverable within 6 bars.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # kernel / deficit channel
    _J = 4
    _n = 180
    _nmin = 90
    _vol_win = 180
    _vol_min = 60
    _thresh = 1.5
    _Lmax = 12
    _ridge = 0.15
    _shrink = 0.3
    # microstructure channel
    _part_win = 60
    _agg_win = 3
    _part_cap = 4.0
    _den_shrink = 0.5
    # routers
    _beta_win = 120
    _rate_win = 240
    _rate_min = 60
    _match_s = 1.0
    _kappa = 0.6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        T, N = len(idx), len(cols)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._nmin) + int(self._J) + 5 or N < 3:
            return zero

        h = float(self.prediction_horizon)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data['volume'].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = (px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        sig = (ret.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        y = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)

        # ---------- channel 1: event-anchored kernel delivery deficit -------------
        mkt = ret.median(axis=1)
        mvol = (mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_win), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
                .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        z = ((mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
             .clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0))
        shock = z.abs() > float(self._thresh)
        xs = z.where(shock, 0.0)
        base = (z * z).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()

        yhat = None
        for j in range(int(self._J) + 1):
            xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
            den = (xl * xl).rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean()
            num = (y0.mul(xl, axis=0)
                   .rolling(int(self._n), min_periods=int(self._nmin)).mean())
            denom = (den + float(self._ridge) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._shrink)).fillna(0.0)
            contrib = th.mul(z.shift(j).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            yhat = contrib if yhat is None else yhat.add(contrib)

        gap = (yhat - y).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cum = gap.fillna(0.0).cumsum()
        prev = cum.shift(1)
        mask = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], N, axis=1),
                            index=idx, columns=cols)
        anchor = prev.where(mask).ffill()
        alt = cum.shift(int(self._Lmax))
        age = _bars_since(shock, float(self._Lmax))
        use_evt = (age < float(self._Lmax)).to_numpy()
        anchor_eff = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(use_evt[:, None], anchor.to_numpy(), alt.to_numpy()),
            index=idx, columns=cols)
        nbars = (age + 1.0).clip(1.0, float(self._Lmax))
        deficit = (cum - anchor_eff).div(np.sqrt(nbars), axis=0)
        deficit = deficit.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(int(self._J), min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        deficit = deficit.where(alive)

        # ---------- channel 2: idio participation-weighted range snapback ---------
        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = ((close - lo) - (hi - close)) / rng
        clv = clv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        vbase = ts_mean(volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan),
                        int(self._part_win)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        part = (volume / vbase).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, float(self._part_cap))
        ok = clv.notna() & part.notna()
        c = clv.where(ok, 0.0)
        w = part.where(ok, 0.0)
        disp = (decay_linear(w * c, int(self._agg_win))
                / (decay_linear(w, int(self._agg_win)) + float(self._den_shrink)))
        disp = disp.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get('sector'), cols)
        fallback = _broadcast(disp.mean(axis=1), disp)
        if lab is not None:
            gmean = disp.T.groupby(lab).transform('mean').T
            gmean = gmean.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
        else:
            gmean = fallback
        snap = -(disp - gmean)                     # closed LOW on volume => bounce
        snap = snap.where(ok.rolling(int(self._agg_win), min_periods=1).sum() > 0)

        # ---------- router 1: own re-quote clock (Poisson delivery capacity) ------
        moved = ((ret.abs() > 1e-12) & ret.notna()).astype(float)
        moved = moved.where(ret.notna())
        lam = moved.rolling(int(self._rate_win), min_periods=int(self._rate_min)).mean()
        lam = lam.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        lam = lam.where(lam.notna(), _broadcast(lam.median(axis=1), lam)).fillna(0.5)
        w_match, w_fast, deliver = _clock_terms(lam, h, float(self._match_s))

        # ---------- router 2: trailing market variance share ----------------------
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, ret)
        rho = correlation(ret, mkt_df, int(self._beta_win))
        r2 = rho.pow(2.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        s_sys = rank(r2)
        s_sys = s_sys.where(s_sys.notna(), 0.5)

        a = _centred_rank(deficit)                 # systematic owed catch-up
        b = _centred_rank(snap)                    # idio transient-impact snapback
        a_ok, b_ok = a.notna(), b.notna()
        af, bf = a.fillna(0.0), b.fillna(0.0)

        wd = (w_match * (0.25 + s_sys)).where(a_ok, 0.0)
        ws = (w_fast * (0.25 + (1.0 - s_sys))).where(b_ok, 0.0)
        core = (wd * af + ws * bf) / (wd + ws + 0.10)

        conc = np.sign(af.to_numpy()) * np.sign(bf.to_numpy())
        conc = pd.DataFrame(conc, index=idx, columns=cols)
        amp = 1.0 + float(self._kappa) * conc * deliver
        raw = core * amp * (0.30 + 0.70 * deliver)

        valid = a_ok | b_ok
        raw = raw.where(valid)
        score = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return (score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
                .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0))

programs.trading_idea: Parent A showed that an owed systematic-catch-up kernel deficit and an idiosyncratic participation-weighted range-position snapback are complementary, routed by how much of a name's variance is market-explained; Parent B showed that whether owed mass can be *paid* inside a fixed 6-bar window depends on the name's own re-quote intensity lambda, but it amplified the deficit monotonically in lambda and its sign flipped. The reason is that information content in lambda is hump-shaped, not monotone: for lambda*H >> 1 (mid re-quotes every bar) the backlog is already arbitraged away and the measured 'deficit' is bid-ask/latency noise, while for lambda*H << 1 the backlog is real but is delivered after the evaluation offset (exactly why A's IC drifts out to 24 bars) — so a monotone lambda gain loads the deficit channel precisely where the fast reversal channel actually dominates, inverting the sign. The child therefore routes with a two-dimensional state: a clock-matching kernel exp(-0.5(log(lambda*H))^2) times market-R-squared rank feeds the kernel-deficit channel (backlog whose re-quote interval matches the horizon and whose path is common), while a fast-clock weight lambda*H/(1+lambda*H) times idiosyncratic variance share feeds the transient-impact snapback channel (liquidity cost can only revert if the quote moves), and the sign-concordance amplifier is itself scaled by the Poisson deliverable share 1-exp(-lambda*H) so the 'mechanical repricing lag' premium is only claimed where the mid can physically move inside the window.
programs.description: Blends an event-anchored, shock-selected local-projection kernel delivery deficit with a negated sector-purged participation-weighted within-bar close-location value, weighting the two channels by (i) a horizon-clock-matching kernel / fast-clock weight built from the name's trailing mid re-quote rate and (ii) trailing market R-squared, then amplifying the blend where the channels agree in sign in proportion to the Poisson share of backlog deliverable within 6 bars.

"""Hodge-gradient latency ladder with horizon-matched owed delivery.

Mechanism
---------
For peers i, j define the antisymmetric lead-lag score
    s_ij(k) = cov(z_i,t , z_j,t-k) - cov(z_j,t , z_i,t-k)
on vol-standardised returns z.  S(k) is an antisymmetric flow on the complete
peer graph and, by the Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition, splits into a gradient
part s_ij ~ phi_i - phi_j (a transitive latency ladder) plus a curl part
(cyclic, non-transitive noise).  The least-squares Hodge potential is the row
mean of S, and because covariance is bilinear that row mean collapses to a
two-term object involving only the peer AGGREGATE:
    phi_i(k) ~ cov(z_i,t, m_t-k) - cov(m_t, z_i,t-k),
where m is the leave-one-out peer aggregate.  No O(N^2) matrix is needed.
Antisymmetrising removes the symmetric part of the cross-covariance (common
autocorrelation, contemporaneous beta contamination), leaving pure latency.

The per-lag gradient responses a_k = beta_k - gamma_k are then folded into a
horizon-matched distributed-lag projection: the coefficient on m_{t-j} in the
cumulative next-6-bar forecast is sum_{k=j+1..6} a_k, i.e. exactly the response
mass that has not yet been delivered inside the forecast window.  The result is
a predicted 6-bar vol-standardised return (expected sign +1).  It is shrunk by a
stability gate comparing long- and short-window potentials, a cheap proxy for
the gradient-vs-curl energy share: a true potential is stationary across
sub-windows, curl noise flips sign.

Everything is causal: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker (sector preferred, else industry)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[0]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _roll_mean(x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return x.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()


def _roll_cov(x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing covariance, written out so NaN handling stays explicit."""
    return _roll_mean(x * y, n, mp) - _roll_mean(x, n, mp) * _roll_mean(y, n, mp)


def _expit_df(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = special.expit(df.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)


def _xs_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sg = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sg, axis=0)


def _loo_aggregate(zfill: pd.DataFrame, live: pd.DataFrame, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sub = zfill.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    liv = live.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    tot = (sub * liv).sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    cnt = liv.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    denom = cnt - liv
    out = np.where(denom >= float(min_peers), (tot - sub * liv) / np.maximum(denom, 1.0), np.nan)
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=zfill.index, columns=zfill.columns)


@register_factor
class HodgeLatencyLadderOwedDelivery(BaseFactor):
    """Latency potential from the Hodge gradient of the peer lead-lag flow."""

    factor_id = 'hodge_latency_ladder_owed_delivery_h6'
    name = 'Hodge-gradient latency ladder owed delivery'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Antisymmetric (Hodge-gradient) lag-1..6 response of a name to its '
        'leave-one-out sector return aggregate, folded into a horizon-matched '
        'distributed-lag projection of the aggregate last six bars (undelivered '
        'response), shrunk by long-vs-short-window potential agreement, ranked.'
    )
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ['close', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _K = 6
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _W_LONG = 600
    _MP_LONG = 300
    _W_SHORT = 150
    _MP_SHORT = 90
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _GATE_SLOPE = 1.5

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        if px.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero

        r = np.log(px).diff()
        sd = r.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (r / sd).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z))
        live = z.notna()
        zfill = z.fillna(0.0)
        livef = live.astype(float)

        # ---- leave-one-out peer aggregate (sector groups, market fallback) ----
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        m = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for lab in pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()):
            sel = [c for c in cols if labels[c] == lab]
            if len(sel) < self._MIN_PEERS + 1:
                continue
            m.loc[:, sel] = _loo_aggregate(zfill[sel], livef[sel], self._MIN_PEERS).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        if m.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            m = _loo_aggregate(zfill, livef, self._MIN_PEERS)
        mkt = _loo_aggregate(zfill, livef, self._MIN_PEERS)
        m = m.where(m.notna(), mkt)

        msd = m.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mz = (m / msd).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        mz = mz.where(np.isfinite(mz)).fillna(0.0)

        WL, MPL = self._W_LONG, self._MP_LONG
        varm = _roll_cov(mz, mz, WL, MPL).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        varz = _roll_cov(zfill, zfill, WL, MPL).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        # ---- per-lag antisymmetric (Hodge gradient) response ----
        a = {}
        for k in range(1, self._K + 1):
            beta = _roll_cov(zfill, mz.shift(k), WL, MPL) / varm
            gamma = _roll_cov(mz, zfill.shift(k), WL, MPL) / varz
            a[k] = (beta - gamma).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # ---- horizon-matched cumulative kernel: C_j = sum_{k=j+1..K} a_k ----
        acc = a[self._K] * 0.0
        csum = {}
        for k in range(self._K, 0, -1):
            acc = acc + a[k]
            csum[k - 1] = acc

        pred = None
        for j in range(0, self._K):
            term = csum[j] * mz.shift(j)
            pred = term if pred is None else pred + term

        # ---- gradient-stability gate (gradient vs curl proxy) ----
        M6 = mz.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum().shift(1)
        Z6 = zfill.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum().shift(1)
        phi_L = _roll_cov(zfill, M6, WL, MPL) - _roll_cov(mz, Z6, WL, MPL)
        phi_S = _roll_cov(zfill, M6, self._W_SHORT, self._MP_SHORT) - _roll_cov(
            mz, Z6, self._W_SHORT, self._MP_SHORT
        )
        agree = (_xs_z(phi_L) * _xs_z(phi_S)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        gate = _expit_df(self._GATE_SLOPE * agree.fillna(0.0))

        signal = gate * pred
        signal = signal.where(np.isfinite(signal) & live & mz.ne(0.0))

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Hodge-gradient latency ladder with horizon-matched owed delivery
programs.trading_idea: Pairwise lag-1 lead-lag scores between peers form an antisymmetric flow on the peer graph; by the Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition that flow splits into a *gradient* part generated by a scalar latency potential (a genuine leader/laggard ladder) and a *curl* part (cyclic, non-transitive noise that carries no ordering). The least-squares Hodge potential of that network collapses algebraically to a two-term object per name — the asymmetry between cov(own return today, peer-aggregate return k bars ago) and cov(peer-aggregate today, own return k bars ago) — so the ladder is computable exactly without any O(N^2) matrix, and antisymmetrising automatically annihilates the symmetric part of the cross-covariance (common autocorrelation and contemporaneous beta contamination), which is what makes ordinary lead-lag regressions unreliable. I then convert the per-lag gradient responses into a *horizon-matched* distributed-lag projection: summing the response kernel over the lags whose mass still falls inside the next 6 bars gives the fraction of the peer basket's last 60 seconds of movement that a laggard has not yet delivered, and that undelivered amount is the predicted 6-bar return; the estimate is shrunk by a gradient-stability gate (agreement between a long- and a short-window potential), which is a cheap proxy for gradient-vs-curl energy share. It is falsifiable: if the antisymmetrised kernel (beta_k - gamma_k) is replaced by the raw forward kernel beta_k the 6-bar IC should fall materially, and if the ladder were pure curl the stability gate would add nothing. The edge survives arbitrage because a latency ladder is only identifiable over long trailing windows while its members rotate, and harvesting it requires simultaneously executing a laggard against a peer basket for a few basis points of expected delivery, i.e. real inventory and hedge-slippage risk per event.

"""Delivery-deficit-purged band relaxation with dual horizon-matched slopes.

Mechanism
---------
A peer-relative displacement at the one-minute scale mixes two components with
opposite futures:

  (i)  OWED BETA -- a recent common (market) shock that the name has not yet
       transmitted, measured as the accumulated shortfall of its realized
       vol-normalised path versus the path implied by its own trailing
       impulse-response kernel (local projections on large common shocks only,
       anchored at the last genuine shock).  This component is *delivered*:
       positive deficit precedes positive returns, and delivery requires trading
       activity to resume.

  (ii) TRANSIENT IMPACT -- the part of the band-limited peer-relative
       displacement (fast-minus-slow EWMA of the log price versus its
       sector x size-tercile peer median, half-lives bracketing the 6-bar
       horizon) that is *orthogonal* to the owed beta.  This component relaxes,
       and it relaxes only once the pushing flow has stopped.

Parent A applied one self-measured relaxation slope to the whole band, so the
slope was contaminated by the owed beta hiding inside it; parent B accumulated
the deficit with a constant sign, ignoring each name's measured closure speed.
Here the two states are Gram-Schmidt separated on trailing windows, a third
channel carries their interaction (band x tanh(deficit), purged of both), and
each channel receives its OWN horizon-matched slope: the trailing OLS
coefficient of the realized 6-bar peer-relative return on that channel lagged
exactly 6 bars, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the peer-group median.  The
weighted sum is therefore a predicted 6-bar return (expected sign +1).

All statistics are causal: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_EPS = 1e-12

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _within_group_tercile(vs: pd.DataFrame, sec_arr: np.ndarray, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-coarse-group bucket (0..k-1) of a slow conditioning coordinate."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vs.index, columns=vs.columns)
    for code in np.unique(sec_arr):
        sel = vs.columns[sec_arr == code]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        r = vs[sel].rank(axis=1, pct=True)
        b = np.ceil(r * float(k)) - 1.0
        out[sel] = b.clip(0.0, float(k - 1))
    return out

def _group_median_count(vals: pd.DataFrame, codes: pd.DataFrame):
    """Per-bar within-group median and live count, broadcast back to members."""
    V = vals.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    C = codes.reindex_like(vals).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    med = np.full(V.shape, np.nan)
    cnt = np.zeros(V.shape)
    finite_codes = C[np.isfinite(C)]
    uniq = np.unique(finite_codes) if finite_codes.size else np.array([])
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        for c in uniq:
            mask = C == c
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            sub = np.where(mask, V, np.nan)
            gm = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1)
            gc = np.isfinite(sub).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
            med[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gm[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
            cnt[mask] = np.broadcast_to(gc[:, None], mask.shape)[mask]
    med_df = pd.DataFrame(med, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    cnt_df = pd.DataFrame(cnt, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    return (med_df, cnt_df)

def _expit_df(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = special.expit(df.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=df.index, columns=df.columns)

def _shrink_cs(df: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading toward its cross-sectional mean."""
    row = df.mean(axis=1)
    return df.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)

def _bars_since(flag: pd.Series, cap: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Bars elapsed since the last True in flag (forward fill only -> causal)."""
    s = pd.Series(np.arange(len(flag.index), dtype=float), index=flag.index)
    last = s.where(flag.to_numpy()).ffill()
    return (s - last).clip(0.0, cap).fillna(cap)

def _roll_slope(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing univariate OLS slope of y on x (both panels, column-wise)."""
    cv = x.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).cov(y)
    vr = x.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cv / vr).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _orth(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Residual of y after projecting out x on a trailing window (causal)."""
    b = _roll_slope(y, x, n, mp).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
    return y - b * x.fillna(0.0)

@register_factor
class DeliveryDeficitPurgedBandRelaxationDualSlope(BaseFactor):
    """Owed-beta delivery and purged band relaxation, each with its own 6-bar slope."""
    factor_id = 'delivery_deficit_purged_band_relaxation_dual_slo'
    name = 'Delivery-deficit-purged band relaxation dual slope'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Horizon-band peer-relative displacement and event-anchored kernel-implied response deficit are orthogonalised into three causal channels (deficit, purged band, purged interaction); each gets its own trailing 6-bar-offset regression slope shrunk to the sector x size peer median, with opposite volume gates on the delivery and relaxation channels; the summed predicted 6-bar return is ranked cross-sectionally.'
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 3
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _SIZE_HL = 600.0
    _HL_FAST = 3.0
    _MIN_FAST = 6
    _HL_SLOW = 30.0
    _MIN_SLOW = 30
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _H = 6
    _J = 6
    _LP_WIN = 240
    _LP_MIN = 90
    _THRESH = 1.5
    _LMAX = 30
    _RIDGE = 0.15
    _CS_SHRINK = 0.3
    _REG_WIN = 300
    _REG_MIN = 150
    _ORTH_WIN = 300
    _ORTH_MIN = 120
    _SHRINK = 0.5
    _FLOW_FAST = 3
    _FLOW_SLOW = 24
    _FLOW_SLOPE = 0.75

    def calc(self, data: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        T, N = (len(idx), len(cols))
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if T < int(self._REG_MIN) + int(self._H) + 10 or N < 3:
            return zero
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        uniq_lab = list(pd.unique(labels.reindex(cols).to_numpy()))
        code_map = {lab: float(i) for i, lab in enumerate(uniq_lab)}
        sec_arr = np.array([code_map[labels[c]] for c in cols], dtype=float)
        sec_frame = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(sec_arr[None, :], T, axis=0), index=idx, columns=cols)
        ter = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mc = data.get('marketCap')
        if mc is not None:
            m = mc.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            m = m.where(np.isfinite(m) & (m > 0.0))
            if m.notna().to_numpy().sum() > 0:
                lm = np.log(m).ffill()
                sm = lm.ewm(halflife=self._SIZE_HL, min_periods=1, adjust=False).mean()
                ter = _within_group_tercile(sm, sec_arr, self._K)
        codes_fine = sec_frame * 10.0 + ter.fillna(9.0)
        med_f, cnt_f = _group_median_count(p, codes_fine)
        med_c, cnt_c = _group_median_count(p, sec_frame)
        fine_ok = cnt_f.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS)
        med = med_f.where(fine_ok, med_c)
        cnt = cnt_f.where(fine_ok, cnt_c)
        codes_used = codes_fine.where(fine_ok, sec_frame)
        q = (p - med).where(cnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
        fast = q.ewm(halflife=self._HL_FAST, min_periods=self._MIN_FAST, adjust=False).mean()
        slow = q.ewm(halflife=self._HL_SLOW, min_periods=self._MIN_SLOW, adjust=False).mean()
        band = fast - slow
        sdb = band.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        zb = (band / sdb).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        sig = ret.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        y = (ret / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        y0 = y.fillna(0.0)
        mkt = ret.median(axis=1)
        mvol = mkt.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (mkt / mvol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0)
        shock = z.abs() > float(self._THRESH)
        xs = z.where(shock, 0.0)
        base = (z * z).rolling(self._LP_WIN, min_periods=self._LP_MIN).mean()
        yhat = None
        for j in range(int(self._J) + 1):
            xl = xs.shift(j).fillna(0.0)
            den = (xl * xl).rolling(self._LP_WIN, min_periods=self._LP_MIN).mean()
            num = y0.mul(xl, axis=0).rolling(self._LP_WIN, min_periods=self._LP_MIN).mean()
            denom = (den + float(self._RIDGE) * base).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            th = num.div(denom, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            th = _shrink_cs(th.clip(-3.0, 3.0), float(self._CS_SHRINK)).fillna(0.0)
            contrib = th.mul(z.shift(j).fillna(0.0), axis=0)
            yhat = contrib if yhat is None else yhat.add(contrib)
        gap = (yhat - y).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        cum = gap.fillna(0.0).cumsum()
        prev = cum.shift(1)
        mask = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(shock.to_numpy()[:, None], N, axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        anchor = prev.where(mask).ffill()
        alt = cum.shift(int(self._LMAX))
        age = _bars_since(shock, float(self._LMAX))
        use_evt = (age < float(self._LMAX)).to_numpy()
        anchor_eff = pd.DataFrame(np.where(use_evt[:, None], anchor.to_numpy(), alt.to_numpy()), index=idx, columns=cols)
        deficit = cum - anchor_eff
        nbars = (age + 1.0).clip(1.0, float(self._LMAX))
        dz = deficit.div(np.sqrt(nbars), axis=0)
        dz = dz.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        u1 = dz
        u2 = _orth(zb, u1, self._ORTH_WIN, self._ORTH_MIN)
        inter = (zb * np.tanh(dz.fillna(0.0))).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        u3 = _orth(_orth(inter, u1, self._ORTH_WIN, self._ORTH_MIN), u2, self._ORTH_WIN, self._ORTH_MIN)
        dq = q - q.shift(self._H)
        sdq = dq.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        yq = (dq / sdq).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        chans = [u1, u2, u3]
        betas = []
        for u in chans:
            xlag = u.shift(self._H)
            b = _roll_slope(yq, xlag, self._REG_WIN, self._REG_MIN).clip(-1.5, 1.5)
            b = b.where(np.isfinite(b))
            bmed, bcnt = _group_median_count(b, codes_used)
            bfill = bmed.where(bcnt.fillna(0.0) >= float(self._MIN_PEERS))
            bfill = bfill.where(np.isfinite(bfill), b)
            bs = self._SHRINK * b + (1.0 - self._SHRINK) * bfill
            betas.append(bs)
        vol = data.get('volume')
        if vol is None:
            gate_rev = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
            gate_del = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
            vf = v.rolling(self._FLOW_FAST, min_periods=self._FLOW_FAST).mean()
            vs = v.rolling(self._FLOW_SLOW, min_periods=self._FLOW_SLOW).mean()
            fr = np.log((vf + 1.0) / (vs + 1.0))
            fsd = fr.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
            fz = (fr / fsd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
            gate_rev = _expit_df(-self._FLOW_SLOPE * fz)
            gate_del = _expit_df(self._FLOW_SLOPE * fz)
        f1 = betas[0] * u1 * gate_del
        f2 = betas[1] * u2 * gate_rev
        f3 = betas[2] * u3 * gate_rev
        parts = [f1, f2, f3]
        fc = None
        for pt in parts:
            pt = pt.where(np.isfinite(pt))
            fc = pt.fillna(0.0) if fc is None else fc.add(pt.fillna(0.0))
        valid = (np.isfinite(u1) | np.isfinite(u2)) & np.isfinite(betas[0].fillna(0.0))
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(self._H, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        raw = fc.where(valid & alive)
        out = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Delivery-deficit-purged band relaxation with dual horizon-matched slopes
programs.trading_idea: A peer-relative price displacement has two economically opposite futures: the part that is *owed beta* — a common shock the name has not yet transmitted through its own estimated impulse-response kernel — should be *delivered* (continuation), while the part orthogonal to that owed response is transient liquidity-demand impact that should *relax*. Parent A applied one self-measured relaxation slope to the whole band displacement, so its slope was contaminated by the un-delivered beta hiding inside the band (a name that owes catch-up looks 'displaced' but will not revert); Parent B accumulated the delivery deficit but imposed a single constant sign on it, ignoring how fast each name actually closes gaps at the 6-bar offset. The child Gram–Schmidt-separates the two state variables, then estimates a *separate* trailing horizon-matched slope for each channel (realized 6-bar peer-relative return regressed on the channel lagged exactly 6 bars, empirical-Bayes shrunk to the sector×size peer group), and gates the relaxation channels by flow cessation while gating the delivery channel by flow resumption — because transient impact only decays once pushing stops, whereas owed beta only gets transmitted when trading restarts. The interaction channel (band × tanh(deficit), purged of both parents) captures the sign-conditional reversion speed that neither parent can express: the same displacement mean-reverts when no beta is owed in its direction and trends when it is.
programs.description: Builds a horizon-band peer-relative displacement (fast-minus-slow EWMA of log price versus sector×size-tercile peer median, vol-standardised) and an event-anchored kernel-implied response deficit (trailing large-shock local-projection impulse response to the common market return), orthogonalises them into three causal channels (deficit, purged band, purged sign-interaction), gives each its own trailing 6-bar-offset regression slope shrunk to peer-group medians, applies opposite volume gates to the relaxation and delivery channels, and cross-sectionally ranks the summed predicted 6-bar return.
