programs.trading_idea: The parent proved that probe excursion (unconverted wick, size-backed) and beta-residual net displacement both carry information, but it imposed the polarity switch with a hand-built conversion ratio, so its predictive mass leaked out to 24 bars — a hand-set state variable is only right on average, and averaging a continuation regime against a reversion regime leaves a slow, low-frequency residual. Here the polarity is made endogenous and horizon-locked: for each name we estimate, from its own trailing record at exactly the 6-bar lead, the correlation between each channel measured at t-6 and the realised 6-bar residual displacement ending at t, and use those (soft-thresholded, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the cross-sectional pooled value) as the channel loadings. Because the loading is fitted at the same offset at which we trade, the signal is a direct 6-bar forecast rather than a slow proxy, and its sign flips per name as its liquidity-provision regime alternates between inventory absorption (probes precede catch-up) and information (displacement is permanent). The edge survives arbitrage because there is no fixed sign to arbitrage — a trader fading a static polarity is whipsawed whenever the regime rotates, and recovering the regime requires per-name, horizon-matched estimation on 10-second data.
programs.description: Two size-gated path channels in units of each name's robust grid quantum — signed unconverted wick excursion and beta-residual net displacement over the last 6 bars — combined with per-name loadings equal to their own trailing lag-6 correlation with realised 6-bar residual displacement (soft-thresholded and shrunk toward the cross-sectional pooled correlation), scaled by a saturating absorbed-volume gate and ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Self-calibrated beta-gap response kernel, conditioned on participation shape.

Mechanism
---------
Parent A folded a distributed-lag kernel of own returns on the MARKET return to
form an 'owed catch-up'; parent B built a horizon-matched dislocation

    D_t = beta_t * M_t(H) - r_t(H)            (Dimson beta, H = 6 bars)

and switched its sign on a participation-shape state.  Both DECLARED that D is a
catch-up claim and both realised the opposite sign: at 10-second granularity the
mechanical stale-quote component of D is delivered inside 1-3 bars (A's |IC|
peaked at 3 bars), so what is left over the *fixed* 6-bar evaluation offset is
the persistence of the one-sided metaorder flow that created the divergence.

This child does not declare the polarity.  It re-points A's distributed-lag
machinery onto B's dislocation variable and estimates the horizon-matched
cumulative response

    kappa_t = sum_{l=1..H} beta_l ,  beta_l = trailing OLS slope of
              (r_t / idio-vol) on D_{t-l},

which is exactly the loading that maps today's D into the sum of returns over
the next H bars.  The kernel is estimated SEPARATELY on bars whose
participation-shape state (normalised Shannon entropy innovation of 30-bar
volume shares) was even/scheduled versus bursty/sweep at the time the gap was
measured, so the interaction of B's state with A's kernel decides sign and size
per name and per regime.  The prediction kappa * D is capped by A's Poisson
trade-clock deliverable share 1-exp(-lambda*H) (a gap can only move on bars the
name actually prints) and weighted by a falsifiable trust statistic: the
cross-sectional rank of |kappa_even - kappa_burst|, which switches the factor
off where participation shape adds nothing.

All statistics are trailing: the value at bar t uses only bars <= t.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_EPS = 1e-12

def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal cap-weighted market return (weights = previous-bar market cap)."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w.to_numpy()))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret).sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    den = w.sum(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)

def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, cols) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(s.to_numpy()[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=s.index, columns=cols)

def _rolling_beta_masked(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame, n: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS slope of y on x using only bars where mask is True.

    Written out from trailing rolling moments; rolling min_periods counts only
    non-NaN entries, so masked-out bars simply do not contribute.  Causal.
    """
    m = y.notna() & x.notna() & mask.fillna(False)
    yy = y.where(m)
    xx = x.where(m)
    my = yy.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mx = xx.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxy = (yy * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxx = (xx * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    cov = mxy - my * mx
    var = (mxx - mx * mx).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cov / var).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _rolling_beta(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ones = pd.DataFrame(True, index=y.index, columns=y.columns)
    return _rolling_beta_masked(y, x, ones, n, min_obs)

def _shrink_cs(b: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Empirical-Bayes style shrink of a loading towards its cross-sectional mean."""
    row = b.mean(axis=1)
    return b.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)

def _normalized_volume_entropy(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shannon entropy of trailing n-bar volume shares divided by log(n).

    H = log(S) - (1/S) * sum(v_i log v_i) with the 0*log0 = 0 convention, from
    two trailing rolling sums.  1 = perfectly even participation, low = a few
    bursty bars dominate.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    tot = ts_sum(v, n)
    vlogv = (v * np.log(v.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)
    s_vlogv = ts_sum(vlogv, n)
    tot_safe = tot.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ent = np.log(tot_safe) - s_vlogv / tot_safe
    ent = ent.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan) / float(np.log(n))
    return ent.clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class SelfCalibratedGapResponseKernelParticipationStateH6(BaseFactor):
    """Dislocation times its own state-conditional 6-bar response kernel."""
    factor_id = 'selfcalibrated_gap_response_kernel_participation'
    name = 'Self-calibrated beta-gap response kernel, participation-state conditional (6-bar)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of (current Dimson-beta 6-bar dislocation) times its own horizon-matched cumulative response kernel (sum of trailing OLS loadings of vol-normalised own returns on the dislocation at lags 1..6, estimated separately in even- and bursty-participation states), scaled by the trade-clock deliverable share 1-exp(-arrival rate * 6) and a kernel-disagreement trust weight.'
    window_length = 480
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _beta_window = 240
    _beta_min = 60
    _idio_window = 120
    _idio_min = 60
    _kern_window = 300
    _kern_min_pool = 80
    _kern_min_state = 40
    _rate_window = 240
    _rate_min = 60
    _ent_span = 30
    _ent_norm = 120
    _shrink = 0.6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx = close.index
        cols = close.columns
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            volume = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            volume = volume.astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = data.get('marketCap')
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(ret, mcap)
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, cols)
        b0 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df, self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        b1 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df.shift(1), self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        b2 = _rolling_beta(ret, mkt_df.shift(2), self._beta_window, self._beta_min)
        beta = b0.clip(-2.0, 4.0)
        beta = beta.add(b1.clip(-2.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)).add(b2.clip(-2.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0))
        beta = beta.clip(0.0, 3.0)
        beta = 0.5 * beta + 0.5
        beta = beta.where(b0.notna())
        resid = ret - beta * mkt_df
        idio = resid.rolling(self._idio_window, min_periods=self._idio_min).std()
        idio_safe = idio.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        m_h = mkt.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        r_h = ret.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        gap = beta.mul(m_h, axis=0) - r_h
        scale_h = idio_safe * float(np.sqrt(float(h)))
        gap_z = (gap / scale_h).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        y_z = (ret / idio_safe).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        ent = _normalized_volume_entropy(volume, self._ent_span)
        ent_innov = ent - ts_mean(ent, self._ent_norm)
        ent_r = rank(ent_innov).where(ent_innov.notna())
        even = ent_r > 0.5
        burst = ent_r <= 0.5
        k_pool = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        k_even = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        k_burst = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        c_pool = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        c_even = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        c_burst = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for lag in range(1, h + 1):
            x_l = gap_z.shift(lag)
            bp = _rolling_beta(y_z, x_l, self._kern_window, self._kern_min_pool)
            bp = bp.clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            k_pool = k_pool.add(bp.fillna(0.0))
            c_pool = c_pool.add(bp.notna().astype(float))
            be = _rolling_beta_masked(y_z, x_l, even.shift(lag), self._kern_window, self._kern_min_state).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            k_even = k_even.add(be.fillna(0.0))
            c_even = c_even.add(be.notna().astype(float))
            bb = _rolling_beta_masked(y_z, x_l, burst.shift(lag), self._kern_window, self._kern_min_state).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
            k_burst = k_burst.add(bb.fillna(0.0))
            c_burst = c_burst.add(bb.notna().astype(float))
        k_pool = k_pool.where(c_pool >= 4.0)
        k_even = k_even.where(c_even >= 4.0)
        k_burst = k_burst.where(c_burst >= 4.0)
        k_pool = _shrink_cs(k_pool, self._shrink)
        k_even = _shrink_cs(k_even, self._shrink)
        k_burst = _shrink_cs(k_burst, self._shrink)
        k_sel = k_pool.copy()
        k_sel = k_sel.where(~(even & k_even.notna()), k_even)
        k_sel = k_sel.where(~(burst & k_burst.notna()), k_burst)
        k_sel = k_sel.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        disagree = (k_even - k_burst).abs()
        trust = rank(disagree).where(disagree.notna()).fillna(0.5)
        trust_w = 0.35 + 0.65 * trust
        traded = ((volume.abs() > 0.0) | (ret.abs() > 1e-12)).astype(float)
        traded = traded.where(ret.notna())
        lam = traded.rolling(self._rate_window, min_periods=self._rate_min).mean()
        lam = lam.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        deliver = 1.0 - np.exp(-lam * float(h))
        deliver = deliver.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)
        raw = k_sel * gap_z * (0.25 + 0.75 * deliver) * trust_w
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        raw = raw.where(alive)
        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Self-calibrated beta-gap response kernel, participation-state conditional (6-bar)
programs.trading_idea: Both parents declared that an un-absorbed systematic dislocation D = (Dimson beta x 6-bar market return) - (own 6-bar return) is a catch-up claim to be collected, and both realised the OPPOSITE sign, because at 10-second granularity genuine stale-quote catch-up is delivered within 1-3 bars (parent A's |IC| peaked at 3 bars) so nothing mechanical is left to harvest at the fixed 6-bar offset; what remains at t+1..t+6 is the persistence of the one-sided metaorder flow that produced the divergence in the first place, i.e. relative-return continuation, not reversal. The child therefore stops declaring the sign and instead estimates it: parent A's distributed-lag machinery is re-pointed from the market return onto parent B's dislocation variable, folding trailing loadings of vol-normalised own returns on D at lags 1..6 into a single horizon-matched response coefficient kappa (exactly the offset the run scores), and parent B's participation-shape state (volume-share entropy innovation: even/scheduled vs. bursty/sweep) is used to estimate that kernel SEPARATELY in the two states, so the same gap is collected where the data say gaps close and extended where the data say they extend. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because the per-name, per-state impulse response is the object that decides polarity, delivered mass is capped by A's Poisson re-quote/trade-clock share 1-exp(-lambda*6) (a gap only moves on bars the name actually prints), and the state-kernel disagreement |kappa_even - kappa_burst| is a falsifiable trust statistic that switches the factor off when participation shape carries no incremental information about closure.
programs.description: Computes the Dimson-beta-implied minus realised 6-bar dislocation (idiosyncratic-vol scaled), estimates its horizon-matched cumulative response coefficient by summing trailing OLS loadings of vol-normalised own returns on the lagged dislocation over lags 1..6 separately for even-participation and bursty-participation bars (volume-entropy innovation state), and ranks the product of the current state's shrunk kernel with the current dislocation, scaled by the trade-clock deliverable share and a kernel-disagreement trust weight.

programs.code:
"""Concordant under-reaction gap, gated by lag-share and non-response hazard.

Mechanism
---------
If a name's total response to a market move arrives with a distributed lag, then
after an observed market path it carries a *measurable* deficit

    gap_t = B_total * sum_{k<H} m_{t-k}  -  sum_{k<H} r_{t-k},

where B_total is estimated once, robustly, by regressing the name's H-bar
cumulative return on the market's H-bar cumulative return (aggregation absorbs
the whole lag kernel, unlike six separately fitted one-bar lag betas).  Two
sharpened conditioners decide whether that deficit is really *owed*:

  1. Sign concordance.  Only a deficit whose sign matches the sign of the market
     move is under-reaction; the opposite sign means the name over-responded or
     had idiosyncratic news, which is permanent and should not be extrapolated.
  2. Path efficiency.  |sum m| / sum |m| over the same window separates a
     genuine level shift (owed catch-up) from a retraced round trip (nothing is
     owed, and naive folds mistake the wiggle for a debt).

Amplification uses a *conditional* staleness statistic - the empirical hazard
P(|r| ~ 0 | large market shock) - plus the estimated late-response share, thin
recent traded volume and small size, all trailing-only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal cap-weighted market return (weights = previous bar's market cap)."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w.to_numpy()))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret).sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    den = w.sum(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)


def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, cols) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.to_numpy(), dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=cols)


def _rolling_slope(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, min_obs: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing OLS slope of y on x, written out as trailing rolling moments.

    Value at t uses only bars <= t (no centering, no negative shifts).
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    my = yy.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mx = xx.rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxy = (yy * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    mxx = (xx * xx).rolling(n, min_periods=min_obs).mean()
    cov = mxy - my * mx
    var = (mxx - mx * mx).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (cov / var).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _shrink_cs(b: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a per-name loading towards its cross-sectional mean."""
    row = b.mean(axis=1)
    return b.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)


def _nrank(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return rank(df).fillna(0.5)


@register_factor
class ConcordUnderreactionLagShareNonrespHazard(BaseFactor):
    """Beta-adjusted under-reaction gap admitted only when it is genuinely owed."""

    factor_id = 'concord_underreaction_lagshare_nonresp_hazard'
    name = 'Concordant under-reaction gap (lag-share / non-response hazard gated)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Trailing total-response beta from an aggregated 6-bar cumulative regression gives the '
        'beta-adjusted 6-bar under-reaction gap; the gap is kept at full weight only when its sign '
        'is concordant with the market move, amplified by late-response share, conditional '
        'non-response hazard, thin relative volume and small size, and scaled by a market '
        'path-efficiency / impulse-strength switch.'
    )
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _est_window = 240
    _est_min = 80
    _vol_min = 60
    _shrink = 0.4

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        n_est = int(self._est_window)

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        mcap = data.get('marketCap')
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- market path -------------------------------------------------
        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(ret, mcap)
        mkt_df = _broadcast(mkt, idx, cols)
        S = mkt.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        S_df = _broadcast(S, idx, cols)

        alive = ret.notna().rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        R = ret.fillna(0.0).rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum().where(alive)

        # ---- total response beta (aggregated) and contemporaneous beta ----
        b_tot = _rolling_slope(R, S_df, n_est, self._est_min).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        b_now = _rolling_slope(ret, mkt_df, n_est, self._est_min).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        b_tot_s = _shrink_cs(b_tot, self._shrink)
        b_now_s = _shrink_cs(b_now, self._shrink)

        denom = b_tot_s.abs().clip(lower=0.15)
        lag_share = ((b_tot_s - b_now_s) / denom).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        lag_share = lag_share.where(b_tot_s > 0.15)

        # ---- beta-adjusted under-reaction gap ----------------------------
        gap = b_tot_s.mul(S, axis=0) - R
        vol_b = ret.rolling(n_est, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        scale = (vol_b * float(np.sqrt(float(h)))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gap_z = (gap / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        gap_z = gap_z.where(alive & b_tot_s.notna())

        # sign concordance: only a deficit in the direction of the market move
        # is under-reaction; the opposite sign is over-reaction / idio news.
        s_sign = np.sign(S_df)
        g_sign = np.sign(gap_z)
        concord = (s_sign * g_sign) > 0
        mult = pd.DataFrame(np.where(concord.to_numpy(), 1.0, 0.25), index=idx, columns=cols)

        # ---- conditional non-response hazard: P(|r| ~ 0 | market shock) ---
        sig_m = mkt.rolling(n_est, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        shock_s = (mkt.abs() > sig_m).fillna(False).astype(float)
        shock_df = _broadcast(shock_s, idx, cols)
        own_sd = ret.rolling(n_est, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        nonresp = ((ret.abs() < 0.25 * own_sd) & ret.notna()).astype(float)
        num_h = (shock_df * nonresp).rolling(n_est, min_periods=self._vol_min).mean()
        den_h = shock_df.rolling(n_est, min_periods=self._vol_min).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        hazard = (num_h / den_h).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # ---- thin recent trading and small size --------------------------
        vol_tr = data.get('volume')
        if vol_tr is None:
            rvol = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vol_tr = vol_tr.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol_tr = vol_tr.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0)
            base_v = ts_mean(vol_tr, n_est).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            rvol = (ts_mean(vol_tr, h) / base_v).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        slow = (
            0.35 * _nrank(hazard)
            + 0.25 * _nrank(-rvol)
            + 0.25 * _nrank(lag_share)
            + 0.15 * _nrank(-mcap)
        )
        gate_slow = 0.5 + 1.0 * slow

        raw = gap_z * mult * gate_slow

        # ---- market state: only a persistent (efficient) shock is owed ----
        abs_sum = mkt.abs().rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eff = (S.abs() / abs_sum).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.3)
        impulse = (S.abs() / (sig_m * float(np.sqrt(float(h))) + _EPS))
        impulse = impulse.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 8.0)
        switch = pd.Series(special.expit(1.5 * (impulse.to_numpy() - 0.8)), index=idx)
        gate_mkt = switch * (0.25 + 0.75 * eff)

        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        sig = sig.mul(gate_mkt, axis=0)
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Concordant under-reaction gap gated by lag-share and non-response hazard
programs.trading_idea: The parent proved that stale names owe catch-up to observed market moves, but it folded six separately-estimated one-bar lag betas against raw trailing market sums — so it (a) counted owed mass from market wiggles that were immediately retraced and (b) could not tell a genuinely lagging name from one whose beta-adjusted deviation came from permanent idiosyncratic news, which is why its predictive mass leaked outside the 6-bar window and flipped sign by 12 bars. The child replaces that with a single robust aggregation estimator: the total (long-run) response beta from a trailing regression of the name's 6-bar cumulative return on the market's 6-bar cumulative return, and a lag-share statistic (total beta minus contemporaneous beta, normalised) that measures what fraction of the total response arrives late; the owed amount is then the beta-adjusted 6-bar gap, admitted only when its sign is concordant with the sign of the market move (genuine under-reaction) rather than discordant (over-reaction / idiosyncratic news, which is permanent), and only when the market path over those 6 bars was efficient (|sum m| / sum|m| high), i.e. a real level shift rather than a round trip. The edge persists because collecting one to two basis points of catch-up in names that do not update their mid on many shock bars requires paying a wide spread in thin, low-attention names, so second-scale arbitrage capital is systematically absent exactly where the conditional non-response hazard P(mid frozen | large market shock) is highest. It is falsified if the concordant and discordant halves of the gap forecast forward returns identically, if the path-efficiency gate does not discriminate, or if the lag-share/non-response-hazard conditioners add nothing over the raw beta-adjusted gap.
programs.description: Trailing beta-adjusted 6-bar under-reaction gap (total-response beta times market 6-bar return minus own 6-bar return), volatility-normalised, kept full weight only when its sign is concordant with the market move, amplified by the name's late-response share, conditional non-response hazard, thin relative volume and small size, and scaled by a market path-efficiency / impulse-strength switch.

programs.code:
"""Model-validated transitory repayment, matched to the fixed 6-bar offset.

Mechanism
---------
Write the log mid as p_t = m_t + u_t with m a random walk (permanent) and u an
AR(1) transitory pricing error with coefficient phi.  Then the return
autocovariances are exactly

    gamma_k = -sigma_u^2 * phi^(k-1) * (1 - phi)^2 ,   k >= 1,

so (i) phi is identified by gamma_2 / gamma_1, (ii) sigma_u^2 by
-gamma_1 / (1 - phi)^2, (iii) the *testable* restriction gamma_3 / gamma_2 =
gamma_2 / gamma_1 gives a specification check, and (iv) the fraction of the
current error repaid within exactly h bars is (1 - phi^h):

    E[ sum_{i=1..h} r_{t+i} | u_t ] = -u_t * (1 - phi^h).

The parent factor's IC rose monotonically out to 24 bars because it summed a
mechanical anchor drift that accrues over the whole anchor window.  Here the
horizon is handled inside the mechanism: (1 - phi^h) with h = 6 down-weights
names whose dislocation only pays back later, keeping the subset whose
repayment half-life matches the fixed forecast offset.

The dislocation itself is measured with a phi-tuned geometric filter
d_t = sum_j phi^j r_{t-j} (the lookback is chosen per name by the estimated
persistence, not by a hand-set constant), and converted to a return forecast by
the Wiener coefficient beta = Cov(u, d) / Var(d) = [sigma_u^2 / (1 + phi)] /
Var(d), which shrinks toward zero whenever the recent path is dominated by
permanent moves.  Everything is a trailing rolling statistic or a positive lag,
hence causal.

Falsifiable: if the (1 - phi^6) horizon weight does not move the IC peak toward
6 bars, or if the geometric-decay specification gate adds nothing, the
RW + AR(1) reading of short-horizon dislocations is wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import covariance, delay, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _lag_cov(r: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing n-bar autocovariance of returns at positive lag k (causal)."""
    out = covariance(r, delay(r, int(k)), int(n))
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _phi_filter(r: pd.DataFrame, phi: pd.DataFrame, j_max: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Geometric trailing-return filter d_t = sum_{j<j_max} phi_t^j * r_{t-j}.

    phi is a per-name, per-time DataFrame known at t; only positive lags of r
    are used, so the value at t sees only bars <= t.
    """
    out = None
    for j in range(int(j_max)):
        w = phi.pow(float(j))
        term = (w * r.shift(j)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        out = term if out is None else out + term
    if out is None:
        return r * 0.0
    return out


@register_factor
class GeometricAutocovValidatedTransitoryRepayment(BaseFactor):
    """Wiener-projected 6-bar repayment of an autocovariance-identified pricing error."""

    factor_id = "geometric_autocov_validated_transitory_repayment"
    name = "Spec-test-validated transitory repayment (6-bar matched)"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "Identifies the AR(1) transitory-pricing-error persistence phi from the "
        "ratio of trailing return autocovariances, measures the dislocation with a "
        "phi-tuned geometric trailing-return filter, converts it to a return "
        "forecast via the Wiener coefficient and the horizon-matched repaid "
        "fraction (1 - phi^6), gates it by the geometric-decay specification test "
        "gamma_3/gamma_2 == gamma_2/gamma_1, de-means cross-sectionally and ranks."
    )
    window_length = 400
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _cov_win = 240        # bars used to estimate the autocovariance function
    _var_win = 120        # bars used for Var(d) in the Wiener shrinkage
    _var_min = 60
    _j_max = 16           # truncation of the geometric dislocation filter
    _phi_lo = 0.02
    _phi_hi = 0.93
    _tol = 0.35           # tolerance of the geometric-decay specification test
    _trust_default = 0.35
    _fc_clip = 0.05

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        p = np.log(px).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        r = p.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.1, 0.1)

        n = int(self._cov_win)
        g1 = _lag_cov(r, 1, n)
        g2 = _lag_cov(r, 2, n)
        g3 = _lag_cov(r, 3, n)

        # Transitory component requires negative low-order autocovariances.
        valid = (g1 < 0.0) & (g2 < 0.0)

        ratio = (g2 / g1.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)
        ratio = ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        phi = ratio.clip(self._phi_lo, self._phi_hi)
        phi_f = phi.fillna(self._phi_lo)

        # phi-tuned geometric dislocation (self-selected lookback per name).
        d = _phi_filter(r, phi_f, self._j_max)

        # Model-implied transitory variance and Wiener projection coefficient.
        one_m = (1.0 - phi).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        sig_u2 = (-g1).clip(lower=0.0) / (one_m * one_m)
        cov_ud = sig_u2 / (1.0 + phi)
        var_d = (
            d.rolling(int(self._var_win), min_periods=int(self._var_min))
            .var()
            .replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        beta = (cov_ud / var_d).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # Specification test: successive autocovariance ratios must agree.
        rb = (g3 / g2.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(valid)
        rb = rb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 2.0)
        trust = np.exp(-(rb - phi).abs() / float(self._tol))
        trust = trust.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        trust = trust.fillna(float(self._trust_default))

        # Horizon-matched repaid fraction at the fixed forecast offset.
        h = float(self.prediction_horizon)
        repaid = 1.0 - phi.pow(h)

        fc = -repaid * beta * d
        fc = fc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
        fc = fc.clip(-self._fc_clip, self._fc_clip)

        # A common transitory error is a factor move, not a name-level bounce.
        fc = fc.sub(fc.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        raw = (fc * trust).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        sig = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return (
            sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Spec-test-validated transitory repayment (6-bar matched)
programs.trading_idea: Model log-price as random walk plus an AR(1) transitory pricing error; that model forces the return autocovariances to decay geometrically (gamma_{k+1}/gamma_k = phi), so phi, the error variance, and — crucially — the *fraction of the error that is repaid inside exactly h bars*, (1 - phi^h), are all identifiable causally from a name's own trailing autocovariance function. The parent's edge grew monotonically with horizon because it summed a mechanical drift that accrues over the whole anchor window; here the (1 - phi^6) factor explicitly down-weights names whose dislocation pays back slower than the fixed 6-bar offset and keeps only errors whose half-life matches it, so the IC should concentrate at the target horizon instead of leaking to 24 bars. Two further disciplines make it falsifiable rather than a re-tuned reversal: the dislocation is measured with a phi-tuned geometric filter (window self-selected per name, not a hand-set constant) and shrunk by the Wiener coefficient Cov(u,d)/Var(d), which automatically kills names whose recent path is dominated by permanent (random-walk) moves; and the whole forecast is gated by a specification test — gamma_3/gamma_2 must equal gamma_2/gamma_1 — so we only trade when the geometric-decay assumption that licenses the repayment estimate actually holds. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a 60-second, spread-paying, name-specific liquidity rebate on a small model-consistent subset, i.e. capacity-limited rather than information-based.
programs.description: Per name, estimates the AR(1) persistence of the transitory pricing error from the ratio of trailing return autocovariances, builds a phi-tuned geometric trailing-return dislocation, projects it onto the expected 6-bar repayment (Wiener-shrunk and scaled by 1 - phi^6), gates it by a geometric-decay specification test, removes the cross-sectional mean, and ranks.

programs.code:
"""Participation-burstiness switched idiosyncratic close-location snapback.

Mechanism
---------
1) Displacement leg (from parent A, whose sign was confirmed).  On a 10-second
   bar aggressive size walks the visible book and the mid ends far from the
   extreme it printed.  The close-location value inside the bar range, weighted
   continuously by traded participation, aggregated over exactly the forecast
   horizon (6 bars), sector-demeaned to strip the common/informational part and
   up-weighted for names with a high idiosyncratic variance share, measures the
   *name-specific* part of that displacement -- i.e. the temporary cost of
   immediacy that decays as passive depth replenishes.

2) State leg (from parent B, with its economics corrected).  Normalised Shannon
   entropy of the last 30 bars' volume shares, minus its own 120-bar mean, then
   cross-sectionally rank-centred and NEGATED to give *burstiness*.  High
   burstiness = volume mass concentrated in one or two bars = a one-shot
   impatient sweep, whose price impact is predominantly transient, so the
   snapback is real.  Low burstiness (evenly spread volume) is the signature of
   an ongoing sliced metaorder still working the book; its footprint persists,
   so the same geometry must NOT be faded and in the extreme tail extends.
   This is why parent B's 'even participation = uninformed noise' reading
   realized with the opposite sign: even participation in a 10-second clock is
   order splitting, not uninformed provision.

The product keeps a positive average loading on the reversal (mean state weight
0.5) while letting the state modulate and, at the evenly-participating extreme,
flip it -- so the factor is neither parent's unconditional loading.

Causal throughout: trailing rolling windows and positive lags only.  Sector
labels are treated as static metadata taken from each name's first observation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import correlation, rank, returns, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)

def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)

def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int=3):
    """One static label per ticker from a quarterly text field (first valid obs).

    Groups smaller than ``min_size`` are pooled so tiny groups are not demeaned
    to exactly zero.  Returns None when no usable partition exists.
    """
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = '__POOL__'
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else '__POOL__'
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), '__POOL__')
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab

def _norm_volume_entropy(volume: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shannon entropy of trailing n-bar volume shares, divided by log(n).

    With p_i = v_i / S:  H = log(S) - (1/S) * sum(v_i log v_i), built from two
    trailing rolling sums with the 0*log0 = 0 convention.  1 = perfectly even
    participation; low = a couple of bursty bars dominate.
    """
    v = volume.abs().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    tot = ts_sum(v, n)
    vlogv = (v * np.log(v.replace(0.0, np.nan))).fillna(0.0)
    s_vlogv = ts_sum(vlogv, n)
    tot_safe = tot.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ent = (np.log(tot_safe) - s_vlogv / tot_safe) / float(np.log(float(n)))
    return ent.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)

@register_factor
class BurstinessSwitchedIdioClvTransientSnapbackH6(BaseFactor):
    """Fade idio intrabar displacement when volume is bursty; respect it when sliced."""
    factor_id = 'burstiness_switched_idio_clv_transient_snapback_'
    name = 'Participation-burstiness switched idio close-location snapback (6-bar)'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Cross-sectional rank of the negative participation-weighted, sector-purged, idiosyncratic-variance-scaled 6-bar close-location displacement times (0.5 + burstiness), burstiness being the rank-centred negative innovation in the normalised Shannon entropy of 30-bar volume shares.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _vol_window = 60
    _beta_window = 120
    _ent_span = 30
    _ent_norm = 120
    _part_cap = 4.0
    _shrink = 2.0
    _share_floor = 0.35
    _state_base = 0.5

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close'].astype(float)
        idx = close.index
        cols = close.columns
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        open_ = data['open'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        high = data['high'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        low = data['low'].astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol_raw = data.get('volume')
        if vol_raw is None:
            volume = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            volume = vol_raw.astype(float).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).abs()
        hi = _pair_max(high, _pair_max(open_, close))
        lo = _pair_min(low, _pair_min(open_, close))
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        clv = (close - lo - (hi - close)) / rng
        clv = clv.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        vclean = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        base = ts_mean(vclean, self._vol_window)
        part = (vclean / base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, self._part_cap)
        valid = clv.notna() & part.notna()
        c = clv.where(valid, 0.0)
        w = part.where(valid, 0.0)
        num = ts_sum(w * c, h)
        den = ts_sum(w, h)
        disp = (num / (den + self._shrink)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        disp = disp.where(valid.rolling(h, min_periods=1).sum() > 0)
        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get('sector'), cols)
        fallback = _broadcast(disp.mean(axis=1), disp)
        if lab is not None:
            gmean = disp.T.groupby(lab).transform('mean').T
            gmean = gmean.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
        else:
            gmean = fallback
        idio = disp - gmean
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        mkt = _broadcast(ret.mean(axis=1), ret)
        rho = correlation(ret, mkt, self._beta_window)
        share = (1.0 - rho.pow(2.0)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        share = share.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.5)
        idio_w = self._share_floor + share
        ent = _norm_volume_entropy(volume, self._ent_span)
        ent_innov = ent - ts_mean(ent, self._ent_norm)
        burst = -2.0 * (rank(ent_innov) - 0.5)
        burst = burst.where(ent_innov.notna(), 0.0)
        state = self._state_base + burst
        raw = -(idio * idio_w * state)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = rank(raw)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)

programs.trading_idea: Parent A established that a sector-purged, participation-weighted close-location value reverts over the next minute because heavy traded size walks finite visible depth and the resulting displacement is mostly the temporary cost of immediacy. Parent B's state variable is the right conditioner but its economics were inverted: in 10-second bars evenly-spread volume is the signature of an *ongoing sliced metaorder* (order-splitting persistence, the most robust HFT regularity) whose footprint keeps pushing, whereas volume mass concentrated in one or two bars is a one-shot impatient sweep whose impact is overwhelmingly transient — which is exactly why B's 'even participation = uninformed, collect the gap' loading realized with the opposite sign. The child therefore keeps A's confirmed idiosyncratic displacement signal but scales the reversal by cross-sectionally centred *burstiness* (negative 30-bar volume-entropy innovation): full-strength snapback when the last 30 bars' volume is concentrated, attenuated and, in the most evenly-participating tail, flipped to continuation because the same liquidity demander will return to the book. The interaction carries edge neither parent has because it separates transient-impact displacement from live-metaorder displacement — A pools both and dilutes its reversal, B applies the state to a benchmark-gap leg the book already spans and with the wrong economic polarity.

"""Omori activity-clock giveback deficit.

Mechanism
---------
A large idiosyncratic 10-second move is mostly the temporary cost of immediacy:
visible depth was consumed and the displacement must be repaid.  Seismology says
the relaxation of a shock (its aftershock cascade) follows an Omori-Utsu law; the
market analogue is that repayment is metered by *activity time*, not bar time --
depth only refills when quoting and trading actually happen.  So for a shock of
signed size s (in residual-vol units) that occurred k bars ago, the fraction of
the eventual giveback already delivered is modelled as

    G = Acc / (Acc + kappa * abar)

where Acc is the integrated post-shock activity (|standardized residual return|
blended with volume participation) and abar the name's typical per-bar activity,
so kappa is a half-repayment clock expressed in *bars of normal activity*.

For every past shock we book two things:

  1. FRESH INCREMENT.  Projecting H = 6 bars of activity forward, the giveback
     expected to arrive over exactly the declared forecast horizon is
     -phi * s * (G(Acc + H*abar) - G(Acc)).

  2. DEFICIT / SURPLUS.  What the name *should* have repaid by now is
     -phi * s * G; what it actually did is the realized signed displacement A
     since the shock bar.  The gap (-phi*s*G - A) is owed (if the giveback has
     not happened) or over-repaid (if the retracement overshot), and is only
     collectible while relaxation is still in progress, hence weighted by 1 - G.

Shocks superpose linearly (ETAS superposition), so the signal is the sum over
lags k = 1..30.  Names with no recent shock score neutral.  Everything is
trailing: rolling betas, rolling vols, positive shifts and trailing cumulative
sums only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


@register_factor
class OmoriActivityClockGivebackDeficit(BaseFactor):
    """Predicted 6-bar return from unpaid (or over-paid) shock giveback in activity time."""

    factor_id = "omori_activity_clock_giveback_deficit"
    name = "Omori activity-clock giveback deficit"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Superposes, over shocks in the last 30 bars, the Omori-style transient "
        "giveback still owed in activity time: the horizon-matched next-6-bar "
        "repayment increment plus a collectibility-weighted correction for the "
        "deficit or surplus of repayment realized so far."
    )
    window_length = 260
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # estimation windows
    _beta_n = 180
    _vol_n = 180
    _vol_min = 90
    _act_n = 60
    # shock selection / relaxation model
    _theta = 2.0
    _lags = 30
    _kappa = 8.0
    _phi = 0.5
    _psi = 1.0
    _h = 6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        if len(idx) < int(self._vol_min) + int(self._lags) + 10 or len(cols) < 3:
            return zero

        px = close.abs().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lr = np.log(px).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        # ---- beta-purged idiosyncratic return, standardized ---------------------
        mkt = lr.median(axis=1)
        mdf = _broadcast(mkt, close)
        beta = rolling_beta(lr, mdf, int(self._beta_n))
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        e = lr - beta * mdf
        e = e.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sig = (e.rolling(int(self._vol_n), min_periods=int(self._vol_min))
               .std().replace(0.0, np.nan))
        u = (e / sig).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # ---- activity clock: |standardized move| blended with participation ------
        vol = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        vbase = adv(vol, int(self._vol_n)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vpart = (vol / vbase).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 5.0)
        act = (0.5 * u.abs() + 0.5 * vpart).clip(0.0, 6.0)

        valid = u.notna() & act.notna()
        u0 = u.where(valid, 0.0)
        a0 = act.where(valid, 0.0)

        abar = ts_mean(a0, int(self._act_n))
        abar = abar.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=1e-3)

        # ---- mainshock series ---------------------------------------------------
        q = u0.where(u0.abs() >= float(self._theta), 0.0)

        cs_u = u0.cumsum()
        cs_a = a0.cumsum()

        kappa = float(self._kappa)
        phi = float(self._phi)
        psi = float(self._psi)
        hh = float(self._h)
        c = kappa * abar
        fwd = hh * abar

        total = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for k in range(1, int(self._lags) + 1):
            s = q.shift(k)
            acc = cs_a - cs_a.shift(k)          # activity since the shock bar
            disp = cs_u - cs_u.shift(k)         # realized signed post-shock move
            g = (acc / (acc + c)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
            gn = ((acc + fwd) / (acc + fwd + c)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            gn = gn.clip(0.0, 1.0)

            fresh = (-phi) * s * (gn - g)
            deficit = ((-phi) * s * g - disp) * (1.0 - g)
            deficit = deficit.where(s.abs() > 0.0, 0.0)

            step = (fresh + psi * deficit).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            total = total + step.fillna(0.0)

        # ---- convert vol-unit prediction into return units ----------------------
        med = sig.median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        vscale = sig.div(med, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        vscale = vscale.clip(0.2, 5.0).fillna(1.0)
        pred = (total * vscale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        ready = sig.notna() & abar.notna() & u.notna()
        pred = pred.where(ready)

        score = (rank(pred) - 0.5).where(pred.notna())
        return score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Omori activity-clock giveback deficit
programs.trading_idea: Treat each large idiosyncratic 10-second move as a 'mainshock' whose transient (liquidity-taking) component must be repaid, and — as in the Omori–Utsu law for aftershocks — assume the repayment is metered not by wall-clock bars but by the *aftershock activity* that follows: repayment progresses with integrated post-shock trade/volatility flow via a hyperbolic saturation G = Acc/(Acc + kappa*Acc_typical), because depth only refills when someone actually quotes and trades. For every past shock the factor books what the name *should* have given back by now (phi*shock*G), compares it with what it actually gave back (the realized signed post-shock displacement), and forecasts (i) the fresh giveback increment expected over exactly the next 6 bars of projected activity plus (ii) an error-correction on the accumulated deficit or surplus, superposing all shocks in the last 30 bars ETAS-style. The edge survives arbitrage because ordinary reversal/impact-decay signals measure elapsed *bars*, so they systematically mistime repayment for names that went quiet after the shock (giveback still owed) versus names that churned heavily (already repaid, and any further retracement is an over-repayment that itself snaps back); the mispricing is small per event but events are frequent. Falsifiable: if repayment is governed by bar time rather than activity time the activity-clock deficit should carry no incremental information, and if over-retracement does not snap back the error-correction term should degrade the signal.
programs.description: For each shock bar (|beta-purged, vol-standardized return| >= 2) in the last 30 bars, computes the Omori-style expected transient giveback delivered so far in activity time (integrated |return|+participation since the shock, hyperbolic saturation) versus the realized signed post-shock displacement, and sums the horizon-matched next-6-bar giveback increment plus a collectibility-weighted deficit correction across all shocks; the resulting predicted return (rescaled by residual vol) is cross-sectionally ranked.
