I therefore measure the consumption intensity of the level the price is standing on: traded volume per unit of recency-weighted local time within one window-sigma of the current mid, scaled by the name's own average volume. A level revisited *cheaply* (much time, little volume) still holds unfilled passive inventory and supplies a restoring force, so the last minute's move gives back; a level revisited *expensively* (lots of volume per unit of time spent there) has had its queue repeatedly hit and depleted, so the same move extends — which is exactly why the parent's pure recurrence gate loaded backwards in liquid names, where price returns precisely to the levels that are clearing volume. The edge should persist because queue-state at a specific price is a structural, per-name, nonparametric path/volume statistic worth only a few ticks per episode, too small and too estimation-heavy to attract arbitrage capital, and because it is a pure interaction (per-name time-centred gate x recent move) it is invisible to momentum/reversal screens.
programs.description: Recency-weighted local time of the mid within one window-sigma of its current level is combined with the traded volume accumulated in those same bars to form a scale-free 'volume consumed per unit of time spent at this level' statistic; its trailing z-score gates the sign of the normalized 6-bar move (depleted level -> continuation, quietly-pinned level -> reversal), cross-sectionally ranked and demeaned.

programs.code:
"""Horizon-integrated leader-Kuramoto phase advance of Epps-corrected precision dislocations.

Mechanism
---------
Step 1 (relative-value coordinate).  Vol-standardised 10-second log returns x are
aggregated over K bars and whitened by the precision of the lag-1 corrected
covariance Sigma* = Sigma0 + Sigma1 + Sigma1^T (Epps / Hayashi-Yoshida style
de-biasing), symmetrised, diagonally shrunk and eigenvalue-floored.  The whitened
move is cross-sectionally purged of the plain aggregated move and z-scored, giving
p: a genuine precision dislocation rather than a staleness artefact.

Step 2 (oscillator kinematics).  With v = p - p[-1], the pair (p / rms(p),
-v / rms(v)) places each name on the unit circle, theta = atan2(-vhat, phat), so
p = rho cos(theta).  The per-bar phase increment dtheta is wrapped to (-pi, pi]
and summarised by trailing CIRCULAR statistics: omega_i = arg(mean e^{i dtheta})
is the measured angular frequency (radians / bar) and coh_i = |mean e^{i dtheta}|
is the phase-locking value, i.e. how steadily the oscillator actually rotates.

Step 3 (leader field and forward integration).  The antisymmetric row-sums of the
same lag-1 correlation matrix rank names from leader to laggard; only leaders
(weights u = max(0, -lambda)) enter the mean field (R_L, psi_L, omega_L).  The
Kuramoto map theta <- theta + omega_i + kappa_i R_L sin(psi_L - theta) is then
Euler-integrated for exactly the declared 6 bars while psi_L advances at
omega_L, and the signal is the FINITE predicted change of the dislocation

    rho * ( cos(theta_{t+6}) - cos(theta_t) ) ,

weighted by the cross-sectional rank of the phase-locking value.  This is the
horizon-matched version of the parent's instantaneous derivative (which it nests
as the Delta theta -> 0 limit) and it is finally orthogonalised cross-sectionally
against p, so only timing information survives.

Causality: the covariance / role estimator applied to bars [a, a+step) uses only
rows [a-W, a); everything else is a trailing rolling statistic or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional operation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _corrected_precision_and_role(x_win: np.ndarray, eig_floor: float, shrink: float, min_frac: float):
    """Return (precision of lag-1-corrected covariance, lagginess vector).

    x_win : (m, n) array of vol-standardised returns strictly in the past.
    Both outputs come from the same trailing window; (None, None) on degeneracy.
    """
    if x_win.ndim != 2:
        return (None, None)
    m, n = x_win.shape
    if m < 60 or n < 4:
        return (None, None)
    finite = np.isfinite(x_win)
    cnt = finite.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
    xw = np.where(finite, x_win, 0.0)
    xw = np.nan_to_num(xw, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    xc = xw - xw.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    c0 = xc.T @ xc / float(max(m - 1, 1))
    c1 = xc[1:, :].T @ xc[:-1, :] / float(max(m - 2, 1))
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(c0)) and np.all(np.isfinite(c1))):
        return (None, None)
    diag0 = np.diag(c0)
    avg = float(np.mean(diag0))
    if not np.isfinite(avg) or avg <= 1e-12:
        return (None, None)
    sig = c0 + c1 + c1.T
    sig = 0.5 * (sig + sig.T)
    sig = (1.0 - shrink) * sig + shrink * avg * np.eye(n)
    try:
        w, v = np.linalg.eigh(sig)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        return (None, None)
    if not (np.all(np.isfinite(w)) and np.all(np.isfinite(v))):
        return (None, None)
    w = np.maximum(w, eig_floor * avg)
    prec = v / w @ v.T
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(prec)):
        return (None, None)
    sd = np.sqrt(np.maximum(diag0, 1e-12))
    r1 = c1 / np.outer(sd, sd)
    r1 = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(r1, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0), -1.0, 1.0)
    lag = (r1.sum(axis=1) - r1.sum(axis=0)) / float(max(n - 1, 1))
    lag = np.clip(lag, -1.0, 1.0)
    lag = np.where(cnt >= min_frac * float(m), lag, np.nan)
    return (prec, lag)

def _rms(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing root-mean-square over the last n bars (causal)."""
    return np.sqrt((df * df).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean())

def _wrap(a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Wrap angles into (-pi, pi]."""
    return (a + np.pi) % (2.0 * np.pi) - np.pi

@register_factor
class LeaderKuramotoHorizonIntegratedPhaseAdvance(BaseFactor):
    """Six-bar forward integration of leader-anchored Kuramoto phase dynamics."""
    factor_id = 'leader_kuramoto_horizon_integrated_phase_advance'
    name = 'Horizon-integrated leader-Kuramoto phase advance'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Phase of the lag-1-corrected precision-whitened dislocation is integrated forward exactly 6 bars using a circular-statistics estimate of each name's angular frequency and Kuramoto entrainment toward the measured-leader mean field; the score is the predicted finite change rho*(cos(theta_{t+6})-cos(theta_t)), weighted by the phase-locking value and purged cross-sectionally of the dislocation level."
    window_length = 500
    inputs = ['close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 6
    _H = 6
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _EST_WIN = 360
    _REFIT = 60
    _SHRINK = 0.3
    _EIG_FLOOR = 0.2
    _MIN_FRAC = 0.5
    _RMS_WIN = 120
    _RMS_MP = 30
    _PH_WIN = 120
    _K0 = 0.06
    _K1 = 0.12
    _MIN_LEAD = 4
    _COH_FLOOR = 0.2

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        vol = ret.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=int(self._VOL_WIN // 2)).std()
        vol = vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (ret / vol).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        agg = x.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum()
        valid_agg = agg.notna() & vol.notna()
        xf = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        aggf = agg.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        n_rows, n_cols = xf.shape
        yv = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        lagm = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        w_est = int(self._EST_WIN)
        step = int(self._REFIT)
        a = max(w_est, self._VOL_WIN + self._K)
        while a < n_rows:
            prec, lag = _corrected_precision_and_role(xf[a - w_est:a, :], self._EIG_FLOOR, self._SHRINK, self._MIN_FRAC)
            end = min(a + step, n_rows)
            if prec is not None:
                yv[a:end, :] = aggf[a:end, :] @ prec
                lagm[a:end, :] = np.repeat(np.asarray(lag, dtype=float)[None, :], end - a, axis=0)
            a += step
        ydf = pd.DataFrame(yv, index=idx, columns=cols)
        ydf = ydf.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid_agg)
        xdf = agg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid_agg)
        ym = ydf.sub(ydf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        xm = xdf.sub(xdf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        denom = (xm * xm).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta_xs = (xm * ym).sum(axis=1) / denom
        res = ym.sub(xm.mul(beta_xs.fillna(0.0), axis=0))
        res = res.where(ydf.notna() & xdf.notna())
        rstd = res.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        p = res.sub(res.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(rstd, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        vel = p - p.shift(1)
        rp = _rms(p, self._RMS_WIN, self._RMS_MP).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rv = _rms(vel, self._RMS_WIN, self._RMS_MP).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ph = (p / rp).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        vh = (vel / rv).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        phv = ph.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        vhv = vh.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        rho = np.sqrt(phv * phv + vhv * vhv)
        theta = np.arctan2(-vhv, phv)
        theta_df = pd.DataFrame(theta, index=idx, columns=cols)
        dth_arr = _wrap(theta_df.to_numpy(dtype=float) - theta_df.shift(1).to_numpy(dtype=float))
        dth = pd.DataFrame(dth_arr, index=idx, columns=cols)
        pw = int(self._PH_WIN)
        mp = int(max(pw // 3, 20))
        cbar = np.cos(dth).rolling(pw, min_periods=mp).mean()
        sbar = np.sin(dth).rolling(pw, min_periods=mp).mean()
        cb = cbar.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        sb = sbar.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        omega = pd.DataFrame(np.arctan2(sb, cb), index=idx, columns=cols).clip(-1.3, 1.3)
        coh = pd.DataFrame(np.sqrt(cb * cb + sb * sb), index=idx, columns=cols)
        lagdf = pd.DataFrame(lagm, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lam = (2.0 * rank(lagdf) - 1.0).where(lagdf.notna())
        cos_t = pd.DataFrame(np.cos(theta), index=idx, columns=cols)
        sin_t = pd.DataFrame(np.sin(theta), index=idx, columns=cols)
        ok = cos_t.notna() & sin_t.notna() & lam.notna() & omega.notna() & coh.notna()
        u = (-lam).clip(lower=0.0).where(ok).fillna(0.0)
        usum = u.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        n_lead = (u > 0.05).sum(axis=1)
        c_field = (u * cos_t.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        s_field = (u * sin_t.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        r_field = np.sqrt(c_field * c_field + s_field * s_field)
        psi0 = np.arctan2(s_field.to_numpy(dtype=float), c_field.to_numpy(dtype=float))
        om_field = (u * omega.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        kappa = (float(self._K0) + float(self._K1) * lam).clip(-0.1, 0.25)
        om = omega.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        ka = kappa.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        rl = np.nan_to_num(r_field.to_numpy(dtype=float), nan=0.0)[:, None]
        psi = np.nan_to_num(psi0, nan=0.0)[:, None].copy()
        oml = np.nan_to_num(om_field.to_numpy(dtype=float), nan=0.0)[:, None]
        th_fwd = theta.copy()
        for _ in range(int(self._H)):
            th_fwd = th_fwd + om + ka * rl * np.sin(psi - th_fwd)
            psi = psi + oml
        amp = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(rho, nan=np.nan), 0.0, 3.0)
        dp = amp * (np.cos(th_fwd) - np.cos(theta))
        dpdf = pd.DataFrame(dp, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        wgt = (rank(coh) - float(self._COH_FLOOR)) / (1.0 - float(self._COH_FLOOR))
        wgt = wgt.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).where(coh.notna())
        score = (dpdf * wgt).where(ok)
        field_mask = (n_lead >= self._MIN_LEAD).astype(float).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        score = score.mul(field_mask, axis=0)
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sm = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        pm = p.where(score.notna())
        pm = pm.sub(pm.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        sm0 = sm.fillna(0.0)
        pm0 = pm.fillna(0.0)
        den2 = (pm0 * pm0).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        b2 = (pm0 * sm0).sum(axis=1) / den2
        resid = sm.sub(pm.mul(b2.fillna(0.0), axis=0))
        resid = resid.where(score.notna())
        sc = resid.sub(resid.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        mad = sc.abs().median(axis=1)
        scale = mad.rolling(200, min_periods=5).mean()
        scale = scale.fillna(mad)
        scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
        out = sc.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Horizon-integrated leader-Kuramoto phase advance of precision dislocations
programs.trading_idea: The parent showed that the phase (timing) of a lag-1-corrected, precision-whitened relative-value dislocation carries information, but it scored the *instantaneous* Kuramoto derivative dtheta/dt, which is a one-bar object — hence its IC peaked at 1 bar and had decayed by 6. Here the same oscillator is integrated forward exactly 6 bars: each name's angular frequency omega_i and its phase-locking value are estimated by circular statistics on trailing per-bar phase increments, the leader-weighted mean field is advanced at its own frequency, and the signal is the finite-difference predicted change rho*(cos(theta_{t+6}) - cos(theta_t)) rather than its derivative. This matters because at the fixed 6-bar offset the cross-section is dominated by *who crosses a turning point within six bars* (Delta_theta ranges from ~1 to ~4 radians across names), which is a strictly different ranking from -sin(theta); names whose phase does not rotate coherently get down-weighted by the phase-locking gate instead of contributing noise. The predicted change is finally orthogonalised cross-sectionally against the dislocation level itself, so the factor carries only the timing information and cannot collapse into the already-mined dislocation-reversal family; the edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating an Epps-corrected precision, a lead/lag role matrix and per-name phase kinematics from a 6-minute trailing window, which is re-estimated faster than a discretionary or slow-fitting arbitrageur can follow.
programs.description: Estimates each name's oscillator phase in the lag-1-corrected precision-whitened dislocation metric, measures its angular frequency and phase-locking value from trailing circular statistics of phase increments, integrates Kuramoto entrainment toward the measured-leader mean field forward 6 bars, and scores the predicted 6-bar change in the whitened dislocation after cross-sectionally purging the dislocation level.

programs.code:
"""Dealer hedge-footprint reversal: fade displacement priced without own trade flow.

Mechanism.  A dealer that absorbs one-sided demand in a sector offsets the risk in
the sector's most liquid proxy names.  The proxy is then repriced by quote
adjustment and hedge execution rather than by its own informed trade flow, so its
observable fingerprint is a multi-minute displacement while its OWN volume clock
runs slow relative to the volume clock of its sector peers.  That displacement is
inventory, not information, and it is walked back as the hedge is unwound inside
the next minute.  A displacement that instead arrived on the name's own heavy
volume is trade-supported and largely permanent, so it should be followed rather
than faded.  The factor therefore multiplies a per-name volatility-normalised
displacement by a *signed* tilt in the peer-minus-own flow deficit, and amplifies
it by the name's within-sector dollar-liquidity rank (only the liquid proxy is
used as a hedge vehicle).  Every statistic is a trailing rolling moment, a
positive lag, or a same-row cross-sectional operation, so the value at bar t uses
only information available at t; the sector label is a static attribute read from
its first observed value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, stddev, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(df, cols) -> pd.Series:
    """First observed (hence causal) static group label per column."""
    lab = {}
    if isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame):
        for c in cols:
            if c in df.columns:
                s = df[c].dropna()
                lab[c] = str(s.iloc[0]) if len(s) > 0 else "UNK"
            else:
                lab[c] = "UNK"
    else:
        for c in cols:
            lab[c] = "UNK"
    return pd.Series(lab, index=pd.Index(cols))


def _group_median(df: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, min_members: int = 3) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise median inside each static group, broadcast back to the columns.

    Groups with too few members fall back to the whole-market row median.
    Purely same-row (cross-sectional) arithmetic, so no look-ahead in time.
    """
    ncol = max(1, df.shape[1])
    mkt = df.median(axis=1)
    mkt_np = mkt.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1)
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(mkt_np, ncol, axis=1), index=df.index, columns=df.columns)
    for g in pd.unique(labels.to_numpy()):
        cols = labels.index[labels.to_numpy() == g]
        cols = [c for c in cols if c in df.columns]
        if len(cols) >= min_members:
            med = df[cols].median(axis=1)
            med = med.where(np.isfinite(med), mkt)
            out.loc[:, cols] = np.repeat(med.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1), len(cols), axis=1)
    return out


@register_factor
class DealerHedgeFootprintFlowDeficitSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Reversal of displacement carried by peer flow rather than own flow."""

    factor_id = "dealer_hedge_footprint_flow_deficit_split"
    name = "Dealer hedge-footprint reversal (peer-flow minus own-flow split)"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Decay-weighted 18-bar market-demeaned displacement, normalised by the "
        "name's own trailing volatility, multiplied by a signed tilt from the "
        "cross-sectional rank of log(sector-median normalised volume / own "
        "normalised volume) and amplified by within-sector dollar-liquidity "
        "rank, then ranked cross-sectionally."
    )
    window_length = 500
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _W = 18       # displacement / flow-deficit window (~3 minutes)
    _ADV = 390    # trailing activity normaliser
    _SIG = 240    # trailing volatility window
    _FLIP = 0.40  # rank below which own-flow-heavy names flip to continuation

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        ncol = max(1, len(cols))

        px = close.astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)

        # ---- returns: winsorised at 4 trailing sigmas, market demeaned -------
        r = np.log(px).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sd = r.rolling(int(self._SIG), min_periods=60).std()
        lim = sd.to_numpy(dtype=float) * 4.0
        lim = np.where(np.isfinite(lim) & (lim > 0.0), lim, 1.0e6)
        r = pd.DataFrame(np.clip(r.to_numpy(dtype=float), -lim, lim), index=idx, columns=cols)
        ri = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        # ---- displacement over the window, own-volatility normalised ---------
        W = int(self._W)
        disp = decay_linear(ri.fillna(0.0), W)
        sig = stddev(ri, int(self._SIG)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (disp / sig).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # ---- volume clocks: own vs sector peers ------------------------------
        vol = data["volume"].astype(float).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        vol = vol.where(vol >= 0.0)
        advv = vol.rolling(int(self._ADV), min_periods=60).mean()
        u = vol / advv.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u))
        umed = u.median(axis=1).to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1)
        fillmat = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(umed, ncol, axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u), fillmat)
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u), 1.0).clip(0.0, 10.0)
        ubar = ts_mean(u, W)

        labels = _static_labels(data.get("sector"), cols)
        peer = _group_median(ubar, labels)
        fd = np.log((peer + 0.25) / (ubar + 0.25))          # flow deficit
        fd = fd.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- hedge-vehicle status: within-sector dollar liquidity ------------
        dv = (px * vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        advd = dv.rolling(int(self._ADV), min_periods=60).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        la = np.log(advd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        la_rel = la - _group_median(la, labels)
        hedge = 0.5 + rank(la_rel)                          # in [0.5, 1.5]

        # ---- signed split: fade untraded displacement, follow traded ---------
        tilt = rank(fd) - float(self._FLIP)
        raw = -1.0 * z * tilt * hedge

        ok = (
            np.isfinite(z.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(fd.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(la_rel.to_numpy(dtype=float))
            & np.isfinite(ubar.to_numpy(dtype=float))
        )
        sig_df = pd.DataFrame(
            np.where(ok, raw.to_numpy(dtype=float), np.nan), index=idx, columns=cols
        )

        out = rank(sig_df) - 0.5
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Dealer hedge-footprint reversal (peer-flow minus own-flow split)
programs.trading_idea: When a dealer absorbs one-sided demand in a sector, it lays the risk off in the sector's most liquid proxy names, so those proxies get repriced by quote adjustment and hedge execution rather than by their own informed trade flow. The observable fingerprint is a multi-minute displacement in a liquid name whose OWN volume clock is running slow while its sector peers' volume clock is running fast; that displacement is dealer inventory, not information, and it is walked back as the hedge is unwound. Conversely, a displacement that arrived on the name's own heavy volume is trade-supported and largely permanent, so the same displacement should be followed, not faded — the reversal coefficient is therefore predicted to be monotone increasing in the peer-minus-own flow deficit and to change sign for the heaviest own-flow names. The edge persists because harvesting it means warehousing the inventory the dealer is shedding, and because the ranking needs three simultaneously-observed per-name states (own volume clock, peer volume clock, and liquidity-proxy status inside the sector) that a pooled calendar-time reversal factor cannot see.
programs.description: Decay-weighted 18-bar market-demeaned displacement, volatility-normalised per name, multiplied by a signed tilt from the cross-sectional rank of the log ratio of sector-median to own normalised volume (flow deficit) and amplified by the name's within-sector dollar-liquidity rank; ranked cross-sectionally so high values are predicted hedge-unwind reversals.

programs.code:
"""Directional resilience asymmetry: which side of the book is thinner?

Mechanism: for every traded bar the square-root impact law gives a per-bar
price-impact coefficient k = |r| / sqrt(V).  Estimating the trailing median of
k separately over up-bars and down-bars yields a unit-free proxy for depth
asymmetry: high k on up-bars means little volume is required to lift the price
(thin ask), low k on down-bars means large volume is absorbed on the way down
(thick bid).  Depth asymmetry persists over minutes and predicts short-horizon
drift toward the thin side (order-book-imbalance effect).  The signal is
residualised per name against its own scaled cumulative return so that it is
not a momentum relabelling, sector-demeaned, and modulated by current relative
flow intensity (a thin book only produces drift if orders are arriving).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _roll_mean(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing mean that skips NaNs (pandas rolling is causal by design)."""
    return df.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()

def _trailing_residual(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current residual of a trailing OLS y ~ a + b x over the last n bars.

    All moments are trailing rolling means, so the value at t uses only <= t.
    """
    my = _roll_mean(y, n, mp)
    mx = _roll_mean(x, n, mp)
    mxy = _roll_mean(y * x, n, mp)
    mxx = _roll_mean(x * x, n, mp)
    cov = mxy - my * mx
    var = (mxx - mx * mx).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = (cov / var).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    return y - my - beta * (x - mx)

def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row robust standardisation (median / MAD) with a std fallback."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    return dev.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

def _sector_demean(df: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise demean within sector groups, using each row's own labels."""
    if labels is None:
        return df
    step = max(1, len(labels.index) // 200)
    sample = labels.iloc[::step]
    try:
        uniq = pd.unique(sample.values.ravel())
    except Exception:
        return df
    out = df.copy()
    for s in uniq:
        if not isinstance(s, str) or s == '':
            continue
        m = labels == s
        grp = df.where(m)
        cnt = grp.notna().sum(axis=1)
        gm = grp.mean(axis=1).where(cnt >= 3, 0.0)
        out = out.where(~m, df.sub(gm, axis=0))
    return out

@register_factor
class DirectionalResilienceAsymmetrySqrtImpactThinness(BaseFactor):
    """Long names whose up-side is thin (cheap to lift) versus their down-side."""
    factor_id = 'directional_resilience_asymmetry_sqrt_impact_thi'
    name = 'Directional Resilience Asymmetry (up/down sqrt-impact thinness)'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Normalised difference between trailing medians of the square-root impact coefficient |log-return|/sqrt(volume) on up-bars versus down-bars, residualised per name against its own scaled window return, sector-demeaned, robust-z-scored cross-sectionally and scaled by relative volume intensity.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _IMP_WIN = 60
    _MIN_SIDE = 8
    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _FAST_VOL = 6
    _SLOW_VOL = 60

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        ret = _log_returns(close)
        traded = vol > 0.0
        sq = np.sqrt(vol.where(traded))
        k = (ret.abs() / sq).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        up = traded & (ret > 0.0)
        dn = traded & (ret < 0.0)
        n = self._IMP_WIN
        mp = self._MIN_SIDE
        med_up = k.where(up).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).median()
        med_dn = k.where(dn).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).median()
        cnt_up = ts_sum(up.astype(float), n)
        cnt_dn = ts_sum(dn.astype(float), n)
        denom = (med_up + med_dn).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        asym = (med_up - med_dn) / denom
        valid = (cnt_up >= float(mp)) & (cnt_dn >= float(mp))
        asym = asym.where(valid)
        sig = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=max(int(n * 0.5), 10)).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        mom = (ts_sum(ret.fillna(0.0), n) / (sig * np.sqrt(float(n)))).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        resid = _trailing_residual(asym, mom, self._BETA_WIN, 60)
        resid = resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        labels = data.get('sector')
        if labels is not None:
            labels = labels.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).ffill()
            labels = labels.where(labels.notna(), 'UNKNOWN').astype(str)
        resid = _sector_demean(resid, labels)
        z = _cs_robust_z(resid)
        slow = ts_mean(vol, self._SLOW_VOL).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        relvol = (ts_mean(vol, self._FAST_VOL) / slow).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gain = 0.5 + rank(relvol).fillna(0.5)
        score = (z * gain).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
programs.name: Directional Resilience Asymmetry (up/down sqrt-impact thinness)
programs.trading_idea: From OHLCV alone one can estimate which side of the book is thinner: for each traded bar compute the square-root-law impact coefficient |r|/sqrt(V) and take the trailing median separately over up-bars and down-bars. A high up-side coefficient means little volume is needed to lift the price (thin ask), a low down-side coefficient means large volume is absorbed on the way down (thick bid); depth asymmetry of this kind is persistent over minutes and is the classic order-book-imbalance predictor, so price should drift toward the thin side over the next ~1 minute. The edge survives arbitrage precisely because harvesting it requires crossing the spread in the direction the book is thin, i.e. paying the very impact the signal measures, and because the estimate is a per-name ratio (unit-free) rather than a tradeable price level. Falsified if the asymmetry precedes reversal (negative IC) or if per-name residualisation against the window's own cumulative return destroys the IC, which would show it is just relabelled momentum.
programs.description: Trailing 60-bar medians of the per-bar square-root impact coefficient |log-return|/sqrt(volume) computed separately on up-bars and down-bars; their normalised difference (up-side thinness minus down-side thinness) is residualised per name against the window's own scaled cumulative return, sector-demeaned, cross-sectionally robust-z-scored, and scaled by current relative volume intensity.

programs.code:
"""Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback.

Mechanism: basket / program executions (index rebalances, ETF create-redeem
arbitrage, cash-flow programs) spread dollars across names in proportion to
capitalisation weight, not in proportion to fundamental beta.  The displacement
they cause in name i therefore scales with weight_i / depth_i, i.e. with
kappa_i = marketCap_i / trailing dollar volume = the inverse of dollar turnover.

The parent factor *assumed* the mechanical push equalled kappa times the
cap-weighted market return, so all of its cross-sectional dispersion came from a
nearly static characteristic timed by one common market scalar.  Here the push is
MEASURED.  Each bar:

  1. build cross-sectionally standardised exposures z_kappa and z_beta;
  2. project z_kappa onto z_beta cross-sectionally and keep the residual e_t --
     the impact-elasticity exposure that is orthogonal to the information
     (beta) channel, a principled replacement for a rank difference;
  3. read the realised *mechanical factor return*
         g_t = sum_i e_it r_it / sum_i e_it^2,
     the per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on e -- the actual
     displacement per unit of impact elasticity;
  4. gate g_t by a basket-program detector G_t (cross-sectional correlation
     between each name's dollar-volume-share deviation from its trailing norm
     and the direction of the cap-weight vector, scaled by aggregate relative
     activity), then accumulate G_t g_t with an exponential memory and lag it
     one bar so only past information is used;
  5. signal = -(e_it) x standardised accumulation: fade the mechanical push.

Everything is trailing or contemporaneous; no forward shifts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, returns, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar Series across all tickers."""
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.reindex(index), dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)


def _xs_corr(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional Pearson correlation between two aligned frames."""
    mask = a.notna() & b.notna()
    aa = a.where(mask)
    bb = b.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    ac = aa.sub(aa.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    bc = bb.sub(bb.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (ac * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = np.sqrt((ac * ac).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) * (bc * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1))
    out = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return out.where(n >= min_names)


def _xs_standardise(df: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional z-score (robust to a few missing names)."""
    n = df.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sd = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    z = z.where(_row_broadcast(n, df.index, df.columns) >= float(min_names))
    return z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _xs_orthogonalise(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional residual of y on x (both already demeaned-ish).

    slope_t = sum_i y_it x_it / sum_i x_it^2 over names where both exist.
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    xx = x.where(mask)
    yc = yy.sub(yy.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    xc = xx.sub(xx.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (yc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (xc * xc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    slope = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
    resid = yc.sub(xc.mul(slope, axis=0))
    resid = resid.sub(resid.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return resid.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _xs_factor_return(exposure: pd.DataFrame, ret: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 8) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional OLS slope of returns on an exposure."""
    mask = exposure.notna() & ret.notna()
    e = exposure.where(mask)
    r = ret.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    e = e.sub(e.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    r = r.sub(r.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (e * r).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = (e * e).sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    g = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return g.where(n >= min_names)


@register_factor
class ProgramGatedElasticityFactorReturnSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Fade the measured mechanical (weight-per-depth) cross-sectional push."""

    factor_id = "program_gated_elasticity_factor_return_snapback"
    name = "Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity exposure times minus an "
        "exponentially accumulated, program-gated cross-sectional factor return "
        "measured on that same exposure."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "marketCap"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        L = 120           # trailing estimation window (20 minutes on 10s bars)
        mp = max(20, L // 2)
        hl = 4.0          # exponential memory of the accumulated push (bars)
        min_names = 8

        # ---------------- returns ----------------
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)

        # ---------------- capitalisation weights ----------------
        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
        med_cap = mcap.median(axis=1)
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).ffill()
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        cap = mcap.where(mcap.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_cap, idx, cols))

        cap_tot = cap.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        w = cap.div(cap_tot, axis=0)

        # cap-weighted market return over names quoting this bar (beta reference)
        w_av = w.where(ret.notna())
        denom = w_av.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        m = (w_av * ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / denom
        m = m.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---------------- basket-program detector ----------------
        vol = data["volume"].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dv = (close.abs() * vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        tot_dv = dv.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        share = dv.div(tot_dv, axis=0)
        share_bar = ts_mean(share, L)

        dev_share = share - share_bar          # allocation anomaly this bar
        dev_w = w - share_bar                  # direction of the cap-weight vector
        tilt = _xs_corr(dev_share, dev_w, min_names)

        act = tot_dv / tot_dv.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        act = act.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.25, 6.0)

        G = 0.10 + tilt.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0) * np.sqrt(act)
        G = G.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.10)

        # ---------------- exposures: elasticity and beta ----------------
        advdv = adv(dv, L).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        turnover = (advdv / cap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        turnover = turnover.where(turnover > 0.0)
        kappa = -np.log(turnover)              # weight-per-depth fragility

        m_df = _row_broadcast(m.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret.fillna(0.0), m_df, L)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 5.0)

        z_kappa = _xs_standardise(kappa, min_names)
        z_beta = _xs_standardise(beta, min_names)

        # beta-orthogonal mechanical exposure
        e = _xs_orthogonalise(z_kappa, z_beta)

        # ---------------- measured mechanical factor return ----------------
        g = _xs_factor_return(e, ret, min_names)
        sig_g = g.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        g_std = (g / sig_g).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        push = (G * g_std).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        P = push.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=20).mean().shift(1)
        P = P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(0.0)
        P_df = _row_broadcast(P, idx, cols)

        # ---------------- signal ----------------
        valid = e.notna() & ret.notna()
        raw = (-e) * P_df
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)

        out = raw.sub(raw.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Program-gated elasticity factor-return snapback
programs.trading_idea: Basket/program executions allocate dollars by capitalisation weight rather than by fundamental beta, so their price displacement loads on a name's weight-per-unit-depth elasticity kappa = marketCap / dollar-volume, a characteristic that is orthogonal to beta only after explicit projection. Rather than *assuming* the mechanical push equals kappa times the cap-weighted market return (the parent's single common scalar, which makes every cross-sectional bet a static pattern timed by a beta-like market signal), I *measure* it: each bar I run a cross-sectional regression of returns on the beta-orthogonalised elasticity exposure and read off the realised 'mechanical factor return' g_t — the actual displacement per unit of impact elasticity, cleanly separated from the information (beta) channel. Accumulating g_t with an exponential memory only over bars whose cross-sectional volume-allocation vector tilts toward the cap-weight vector (the basket footprint) isolates uncompensated liquidity demand, which must relax; the signal is minus the name's orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulation. It survives arbitrage because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving the depth-heterogeneous mechanical component un-hedged, and capturing it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window.
programs.description: Per bar, cross-sectionally regress returns on the beta-orthogonalised index-flow impact elasticity (-log dollar turnover) to extract a mechanical factor return; accumulate it with an exponential kernel gated by a basket-program detector (alignment of dollar-volume-share deviations with the cap-weight vector), and short names in proportion to their orthogonal elasticity exposure times that accumulated push.

programs.code:
"""Confirmed basket-push projection fade.

Mechanism: program / basket executions (index rebalances, ETF create-redeem
arbitrage) allocate dollars across constituents in proportion to capitalisation
weight, so the displacement they cause in name i scales with weight_i / depth_i,
i.e. with an inverse-dollar-turnover elasticity kappa_i.  Information, by contrast,
moves name i by its beta.  Instead of *assuming* the mechanical push equals
(kappa_i - beta_i) x market move, this factor MEASURES it: in every bar a
cross-sectional regression of beta-purified, volatility-standardised returns z_i on
the (demeaned) elasticity kappa_i yields the realized impact loading lambda_t and
the purity R^2_t of that one-factor description of the residual cross-section.  The
model-predicted push is p_i = lambda_t * kappa_i.  Only the portion of the realized
residual that the elasticity model predicted AND the price actually realized is
liquidity-driven and must relax, so the reversible component is taken as the
sign-agreeing overlap  sign(p_i) * min(|p_i|, |z_i|).  These confirmed pushes are
accumulated with an exponential kernel whose halflife matches the forecast horizon
(lagged two bars so the fast Epps / staleness catch-up is already complete), gated
by (a) a basket-footprint detector -- does the cross-sectional deviation of each
name's dollar-volume share from its own trailing norm point along the index-weight
vector? -- and (b) a self-normalising purity gate R^2 / (R^2 + trailing median R^2).
The signal fades the accumulated confirmed push.  Everything is trailing or
contemporaneous only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, delay, rank, returns, rolling_beta, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _row_broadcast(s: pd.Series, index, columns) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a per-bar Series across all tickers."""
    arr = np.repeat(np.asarray(s.reindex(index), dtype=float)[:, None], len(columns), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=index, columns=columns)

def _xs_corr(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int=5) -> pd.Series:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional Pearson correlation between two aligned frames."""
    mask = a.notna() & b.notna()
    aa = a.where(mask)
    bb = b.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    ac = aa.sub(aa.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    bc = bb.sub(bb.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    num = (ac * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
    den = np.sqrt((ac * ac).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) * (bc * bc).sum(axis=1, min_count=1))
    out = num / den.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return out.where(n >= min_names)

def _exp_lagged_sum(df: pd.DataFrame, k: int, lag: int, halflife: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sum_{j=lag}^{lag+k-1} 0.5**((j-lag)/halflife) * df.shift(j).  Causal."""
    out = None
    for j in range(lag, lag + k):
        wj = float(0.5 ** ((j - lag) / halflife))
        term = df.shift(j) * wj
        out = term if out is None else out.add(term, fill_value=0.0)
    return out

@register_factor
class ConfirmedBasketPushProjectionFade(BaseFactor):
    """Fade only the elasticity-predicted AND price-confirmed part of basket pushes."""
    factor_id = 'confirmed_basket_push_projection_elasticity_load'
    name = 'Confirmed basket-push projection fade'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Per-bar cross-sectional regression of beta-purified, vol-standardised returns on an inverse-dollar-turnover impact elasticity gives a realized impact loading and its purity; the factor is minus the exponentially decayed sum of each name's sign-agreeing overlap between predicted push and realized residual, gated by a basket-footprint detector."
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        L = 120
        mp = 60
        K = 14
        lag = 2
        hl = 6.0
        min_names = 8
        ret = returns(data).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        mcap = data.get('marketCap')
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mcap = mcap.where(mcap > 0.0)
        med_cap = mcap.median(axis=1)
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).ffill()
        med_cap = med_cap.where(med_cap > 0.0).fillna(1.0)
        cap = mcap.where(mcap.notna(), _row_broadcast(med_cap, idx, cols))
        cap_tot = cap.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        w = cap.div(cap_tot, axis=0)
        w_av = w.where(ret.notna())
        denom = w_av.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        m = (w_av * ret).sum(axis=1, min_count=1) / denom
        m = m.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        m_df = _row_broadcast(m.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(ret.fillna(0.0), m_df, L)
        beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 5.0)
        beta = delay(beta, 1)
        resid = ret - beta * m_df
        sigma = ret.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (resid / sigma).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        vol = data['volume'].reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        dv = (close.abs() * vol).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        advdv = adv(dv, L).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        turnover = (advdv / cap).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        turnover = turnover.where(turnover > 0.0)
        kappa = -np.log(turnover)
        kc = rank(kappa) - 0.5
        kc = kc.where(kappa.notna())
        tot_dv = dv.sum(axis=1, min_count=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        share = dv.div(tot_dv, axis=0)
        share_bar = ts_mean(share, L)
        dev_share = share - share_bar
        dev_w = w - share_bar
        tilt = _xs_corr(dev_share, dev_w)
        act = tot_dv / tot_dv.rolling(L, min_periods=mp).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        act = act.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.25, 6.0).fillna(1.0)
        g = 0.1 + tilt.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0) * np.sqrt(act)
        g = g.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 4.0).fillna(0.1)
        valid = z.notna() & kc.notna() & beta.notna()
        zz = z.where(valid)
        kk = kc.where(valid)
        zz = zz.sub(zz.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(valid)
        kk = kk.sub(kk.mean(axis=1), axis=0).where(valid)
        n_ok = valid.sum(axis=1)
        Skk = (kk * kk).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        Skz = (kk * zz).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        Szz = (zz * zz).sum(axis=1, min_count=1)
        lam = Skz / Skk.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lam = lam.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(n_ok >= min_names)
        r2 = lam * lam * Skk / Szz.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        r2 = r2.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        r2_med = r2.rolling(2 * L, min_periods=mp).median()
        r2_med = r2_med.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(lower=0.005).fillna(0.05)
        conf = (r2 / (r2 + r2_med)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        lam_df = _row_broadcast(lam.fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        p = (lam_df * kk).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        agree = np.sign(p) * np.sign(zz) > 0.0
        overlap = np.sign(p) * np.minimum(p.abs(), zz.abs())
        confirmed = overlap.where(agree, 0.0).where(valid, 0.0)
        gate = _row_broadcast((g * conf).fillna(0.0), idx, cols)
        contrib = (gate * confirmed).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        P = _exp_lagged_sum(contrib, K, lag, hl)
        P = P.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-40.0, 40.0)
        live = kc.notna() & sigma.notna() & ret.notna()
        raw = (-P).where(live)
        out = raw.sub(raw.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Confirmed basket-push projection fade
programs.trading_idea: Basket/program executions push each constituent by (its cap weight)/(its depth), i.e. in proportion to an inverse-dollar-turnover elasticity kappa, whereas information moves names by beta. Rather than *assuming* that push equals (kappa - beta) x market move (the parent's degenerate structure: one scalar times an almost-static cross-sectional vector), I *measure* it: in every bar I run a cross-sectional regression of beta-purified, vol-standardised returns on kappa, which yields the realized per-bar impact loading lambda_t and its explanatory purity R^2_t; the mechanical push predicted for name i is p_i = lambda_t * kappa_i. Only the part of a name's realized residual that the elasticity model predicted AND the price actually realized is reversible, so I fade the sign-agreeing overlap sign(p)*min(|p|,|z|) accumulated over an exponentially-decayed window (halflife = horizon) of bars whose volume-allocation shape carries a basket footprint. The edge persists because market-neutral books hedge index exposure with beta, leaving weight/depth heterogeneity of mechanical impact unhedged, and harvesting it requires simultaneous many-name execution inside a one-minute window; it is falsifiable because the confirmed-overlap truncation must beat using either the fitted push alone or the raw residual alone, the R^2 purity gate and program-shape gate must add IC, and sign inversion must lose.

programs.code:
"""Recurrence-state conditional Rice block-memory forecast.

Mechanism
---------
Step 1 (Parent B coordinate).  Market-purge 10-second log returns with the
cross-sectional median, standardise by a trailing 120-bar volatility and form the
6-bar (60-second) block displacement disp = sum(r_res) / (sigma * sqrt(6)).  For a
stationary Gaussian-copula increment process the probability that two adjacent
block displacements have opposite signs is arccos(rho)/pi (Rice), so
rho = cos(pi * p_flip) inverts the trailing sign-flip frequency into a scale-free,
jump-robust estimate of the lag-6 block autocorrelation a 6-bar forecast needs.

Step 2 (Parent A state variable, measured in the relative-value coordinate).  The
cumulative market-purged return S is the name's relative-value level.  Its
local-time / recurrence density

    occ(t) = (1/N) * #{ k in 1..N : |S(t-k) - S(t)| <= BAND * sd_N(S) }

says whether the current relative level is habitually revisited (accepted value,
high occupancy) or fresh, never-visited territory (a live excursion, low
occupancy).  A trailing z-score of occ, passed through tanh, gives soft state
weights u_pin and u_fresh that sum to one.

Step 3 (the synthesis).  The pooled Rice coefficient mixes two opposite regimes:
inventory / bid-ask bounce around an accepted level (rho < 0, displacement snaps
back) and sliced metaorder flow on a fresh excursion (rho > 0, displacement
continues).  So rho is estimated TWICE, weighting each historical block pair by
the state that prevailed when the *second* block began (u shifted by one block),
each shrunk toward zero by the number of independent weighted pairs.  The forecast
uses the coefficient of the state the name is in right now:

    signal = ( u_fresh * rho_fresh + u_pin * rho_pin ) * disp .

Causality: every statistic is a trailing rolling window, a positive lag, or a
contemporaneous cross-sectional operation; no coefficient is fitted on future rows.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import math
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, stddev, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices (causal)."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _recurrence_density(s: pd.DataFrame, eps: pd.DataFrame, n: int, min_frac: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Local-time density: share of the last n bars spent within eps of the current level.

    Only positive lags of ``s`` are compared with the current row, so the value at
    t uses information up to and including t.  Bars where either endpoint (or the
    bandwidth) is missing are dropped from numerator and denominator alike.
    """
    hits = None
    tot = None
    for k in range(1, int(n) + 1):
        prev = s.shift(k)
        valid = s.notna() & prev.notna() & eps.notna()
        hit = ((s - prev).abs() <= eps) & valid
        hf = hit.astype(float)
        vf = valid.astype(float)
        hits = hf if hits is None else hits + hf
        tot = vf if tot is None else tot + vf
    denom = tot.where(tot >= float(min_frac) * float(n))
    return hits / denom

def _weighted_rice_rho(cur: pd.DataFrame, prev: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, n: int, block: int, min_w: float, prior_blocks: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """State-weighted Rice inversion of the trailing block sign-flip frequency.

    ``w`` in [0, 1] is the state membership of each historical block pair (already
    lagged so it describes the state BEFORE the second block).  p_flip is the
    weighted flip frequency over the trailing n bars; rho = cos(pi * p_flip) is
    shrunk toward zero using the weighted number of independent block pairs.
    All moments are trailing rolling sums.
    """
    prod = (cur * prev).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = prod.notna() & (prod.abs() > 0.0) & w.notna()
    wv = w.where(valid, 0.0).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
    fl = wv.where((prod < 0.0) & valid, 0.0)
    mp = max(int(n // 4), 20)
    w_tot = wv.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum()
    w_flip = fl.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum()
    p = (w_flip / w_tot.where(w_tot > 0.0)).clip(0.02, 0.98)
    rho = np.cos(math.pi * p)
    n_eff = w_tot / float(block)
    rho = rho * (n_eff / (n_eff + float(prior_blocks)))
    return rho.where(w_tot >= float(min_w))

@register_factor
class RecurrenceStateConditionalRiceBlockMemoryForecast(BaseFactor):
    """Block AR(1) forecast whose coefficient is re-estimated inside each local-time state."""
    factor_id = 'recurrence_state_conditional_rice_block_memory_f'
    name = 'Recurrence-state conditional Rice block-memory forecast'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Standardised market-purged 6-bar displacement times a recurrence-state-conditional lag-6 block autocorrelation: Rice's rho = cos(pi * p_flip) estimated separately from block pairs begun in habitual (high local-time) versus fresh (low local-time) relative-value territory, blended by the name's current occupancy state."
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ['close']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _BLOCK = 6
    _SIGMA_WIN = 120
    _RHO_WIN = 480
    _MIN_W = 30.0
    _PRIOR_BLOCKS = 8.0
    _N_REC = 60
    _BAND = 0.75
    _REC_MINF = 0.6
    _ZWIN = 240

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        ret = _log_returns(close)
        med = ret.median(axis=1)
        rres = ret.sub(med, axis=0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        rfill = rres.fillna(0.0)
        k = int(self._BLOCK)
        sigma = stddev(rfill, self._SIGMA_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        scale = (sigma * math.sqrt(float(k))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        disp = (ts_sum(rfill, k) / scale).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        disp = disp.where(sigma.notna())
        prev = delay(disp, k)
        level = rfill.cumsum()
        n_rec = int(self._N_REC)
        sd_s = level.rolling(n_rec, min_periods=int(n_rec * 3 // 4)).std()
        sd_s = sd_s.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eps = float(self._BAND) * sd_s
        occ = _recurrence_density(level, eps, n_rec, float(self._REC_MINF))
        occ = occ.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        z_occ = ts_zscore(occ, int(self._ZWIN)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        th = np.tanh(z_occ)
        u_pin = (0.5 * (1.0 + th)).where(z_occ.notna())
        u_fresh = (0.5 * (1.0 - th)).where(z_occ.notna())
        w_pin = u_pin.shift(k)
        w_fresh = u_fresh.shift(k)
        rho_pin = _weighted_rice_rho(disp, prev, w_pin, int(self._RHO_WIN), k, float(self._MIN_W), float(self._PRIOR_BLOCKS))
        rho_fresh = _weighted_rice_rho(disp, prev, w_fresh, int(self._RHO_WIN), k, float(self._MIN_W), float(self._PRIOR_BLOCKS))
        num = (u_fresh * rho_fresh).fillna(0.0) + (u_pin * rho_pin).fillna(0.0)
        den = u_fresh.where(rho_fresh.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0) + u_pin.where(rho_pin.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        rho_now = num / den.where(den > 0.05)
        rho_now = rho_now.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        forecast = (rho_now * disp).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        forecast = forecast.where(disp.notna() & rho_now.notna())
        out = forecast.sub(forecast.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Recurrence-state conditional Rice block-memory forecast
programs.trading_idea: Parent B estimated a per-name lag-6 block autocorrelation by inverting Rice's sign-concordance law (rho = cos(pi*p_flip)) and applied it to the current 60-second displacement, but it pooled block pairs across two physically opposite states, so the pooled coefficient is a state-frequency-weighted average of a positive (metaorder continuation) and a negative (inventory bounce) coefficient — which is exactly why its unconditional forecast realized the wrong sign. Parent A supplies the missing state variable: the local-time / recurrence density of the market-purged relative-value level, which distinguishes a level the path habitually revisits (an accepted value, where the flow is bounce and displacement snaps back) from fresh, never-visited territory (a live excursion, where sliced flow keeps pushing). The child therefore estimates Rice's concordance coefficient *separately* in the pinned and fresh recurrence states — weighting each historical block pair by the state that prevailed when that block began — and forecasts with the coefficient belonging to the name's state right now. The interaction is the edge: A's occupancy state has no per-name coefficient and no direction, B's coefficient is contaminated by state mixing; conditioning one on the other de-mixes the two regimes and lets the same displacement reverse in pinned names and continue in fresh ones, self-calibrated per name.
programs.description: Standardised market-purged 6-bar displacement multiplied by a recurrence-state-conditional lag-6 block autocorrelation: Rice's rho = cos(pi*p_flip) is estimated twice from trailing adjacent 6-bar block pairs, weighted by whether the spread level was in habitual (high local-time) or fresh (low local-time) territory when the block began, then blended by the name's current occupancy state and applied to the current displacement.

programs.code:
"""Magnitude-regime-split Rice block sign-concordance forecast.

Mechanism: for a stationary elliptical increment process the probability that
two adjacent increments have opposite signs is arccos(rho)/pi (Rice), so
rho = cos(pi * p_flip) inverts the trailing sign-flip frequency into the lag-k
block autocorrelation a k-bar forecast needs.  The parent applied this estimator
unconditionally.  That is biased for forecasting purposes because a 10-second
mid-price tape mixes two generating mechanisms with opposite memory: a large
population of small, quote-noise / inventory-driven 60-second displacements that
alternate sign, and a much smaller population of large displacements generated by
sliced metaorders whose impact keeps accumulating.  An equally weighted sign-flip
count is dominated by the noise regime, so the estimated rho is negative almost
everywhere and the forecast degenerates into blanket reversal.

This child conditions the concordance estimate on the magnitude regime of the
*previous* block (|standardised displacement| above / below one sigma), producing
two coefficients rho_big and rho_small, and applies the one matching the name's
current regime.  Everything is a trailing rolling statistic, so the value at t
uses only information <= t.  Price data only; one estimation window, one
shrinkage prior, one (scale-free) regime threshold.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import delay, stddev, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices (causal)."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _rice_rho_conditional(
    cur: pd.DataFrame,
    prev: pd.DataFrame,
    mask: pd.DataFrame,
    n: int,
    block: int,
    min_pairs: float,
    prior_blocks: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rice-inverted lag-`block` autocorrelation using only pairs where `mask`.

    p_flip is counted over the last n bars on informative, in-regime pairs
    (both block displacements present, product non-zero, mask true); Rice is
    inverted, rho = cos(pi * p_flip), and shrunk toward zero with the number of
    *independent* block pairs (count / block) in the window.
    """
    prod = (cur * prev).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    valid = prod.notna() & (prod.abs() > 0.0) & mask.fillna(False)
    v = valid.astype(float)
    flip = (valid & (prod < 0.0)).astype(float)

    mp = max(int(n // 4), 30)
    cnt = v.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum()
    n_flip = flip.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum()

    p = (n_flip / cnt.where(cnt > 0.0)).clip(0.02, 0.98)
    rho = np.cos(math.pi * p)

    n_eff = cnt / float(block)
    rho = rho * (n_eff / (n_eff + float(prior_blocks)))
    return rho.where(cnt >= float(min_pairs))


@register_factor
class RiceMagnitudeRegimeSplitBlockConcordanceH6(BaseFactor):
    """Regime-matched block AR(1) forecast with Rice-inverted coefficients."""

    factor_id = "rice_magnitude_regime_split_block_concordance_h6"
    name = "Magnitude-split Rice block concordance forecast"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Standardised trailing 6-bar displacement times a Rice-inverted lag-6 "
        "block autocorrelation estimated separately on large- and small-magnitude "
        "prior blocks, the coefficient chosen by the name's current magnitude "
        "regime; cross-sectionally demeaned."
    )
    window_length = 740
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _BLOCK = 6            # displacement / forecast block = the fixed horizon
    _SIGMA_WIN = 120      # trailing per-name volatility scale (~20 min)
    _RHO_WIN = 600        # concordance estimation window (~100 min)
    _TAU = 1.0            # regime threshold in units of block sigma (scale-free)
    _MIN_BIG = 48.0       # minimum in-regime pairs, large-displacement branch
    _MIN_SMALL = 60.0     # minimum in-regime pairs, small-displacement branch
    _PRIOR_BLOCKS = 8.0   # shrinkage prior in independent block pairs

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        ret = _log_returns(close)
        # strip the common (market) component: it is not the object of interest
        rres = ret.sub(ret.median(axis=1), axis=0)

        k = int(self._BLOCK)
        sigma = stddev(rres.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        scale = (sigma * math.sqrt(float(k))).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        disp = (ts_sum(rres.fillna(0.0), k) / scale).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        disp = disp.where(sigma.notna())

        prev = delay(disp, k)  # previous, non-overlapping block

        big_prev = prev.abs() > self._TAU
        small_prev = prev.abs() <= self._TAU

        rho_big = _rice_rho_conditional(
            disp, prev, big_prev, self._RHO_WIN, k, self._MIN_BIG, self._PRIOR_BLOCKS
        )
        rho_small = _rice_rho_conditional(
            disp, prev, small_prev, self._RHO_WIN, k, self._MIN_SMALL, self._PRIOR_BLOCKS
        )

        cur_big = disp.abs() > self._TAU
        coef = rho_big.where(cur_big, rho_small)

        forecast = (coef * disp).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        out = forecast.sub(forecast.median(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Magnitude-split Rice block concordance forecast
programs.trading_idea: The parent's Rice inversion, rho = cos(pi*p_flip), is unbiased only if all block pairs are drawn from ONE mechanism; in reality a 10-second mid-price tape mixes two: (a) many small, quote-noise / inventory-driven 60-second displacements that alternate sign, and (b) far fewer large displacements produced by sliced metaorders whose impact keeps accumulating. Because the sign-flip counter weights every pair equally, the noise regime — which supplies the large majority of pairs — dominates p_flip, so the parent estimated a negative rho almost everywhere and turned into an indiscriminate reversal signal; that is exactly why its realised IC came out with the opposite sign to the declaration. The child estimates Rice's concordance separately conditional on the magnitude regime of the *previous* block (|standardised displacement| above vs. below one sigma) and applies the coefficient belonging to the regime the name is currently in, so the same formula reverses small displacements and extends large, flow-driven ones with per-name coefficients. Falsifiable core: rho estimated on large-|prev| pairs should be systematically more positive than rho on small-|prev| pairs, and the regime-matched forecast should carry positive IC at 6 bars; the edge persists because reversion desks apply one common, magnitude-blind reversion coefficient, and separating the two regimes requires continuous per-name re-estimation whose per-name payoff is tiny.
