        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = lp.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.05, 0.05)
        vol = ret.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=int(self._VOL_WIN // 2)).std()
        vol = vol.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (ret / vol).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        agg = x.rolling(self._K, min_periods=self._K).sum()
        valid = agg.notna() & vol.notna()
        xf = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        aggf = agg.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        n_rows, n_cols = xf.shape
        yv = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        rv = np.full((n_rows, n_cols), np.nan, dtype=float)
        w_est = int(self._EST_WIN)
        step = int(self._REFIT)
        a = max(w_est, self._VOL_WIN + self._K)
        while a < n_rows:
            prec, role = _epps_precision_role(xf[a - w_est:a, :], self._SHRINK, self._EIG_FLOOR, self._MIN_FRAC)
            end = min(a + step, n_rows)
            if prec is not None:
                yv[a:end, :] = aggf[a:end, :] @ prec
                rv[a:end, :] = np.repeat(np.asarray(role, dtype=float)[None, :], end - a, axis=0)
            a += step
        ydf = pd.DataFrame(yv, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
        xdf = agg.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(valid)
        ym = ydf.sub(ydf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        xm = xdf.sub(xdf.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        den = (xm * xm).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        beta = ((xm * ym).sum(axis=1) / den).fillna(0.0)
        res = ym.sub(xm.mul(beta, axis=0)).where(ydf.notna() & xdf.notna())
        rsd = res.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        p = res.sub(res.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(rsd, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        qi, qq = _gabor_quadrature(p, self._PERIOD, self._FIR_LEN, self._SIGMA, self._COVER)
        theta = pd.DataFrame(np.arctan2(qq.to_numpy(dtype=float), qi.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols)
        amp_raw = np.sqrt(qi * qi + qq * qq)
        amp_ref = amp_raw.median(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        amp = amp_raw.div(amp_ref, axis=0).clip(0.0, 3.0)
        dth = _wrap(theta - theta.shift(1))
        omega = dth.rolling(self._OM_WIN, min_periods=int(self._OM_WIN // 3)).mean()
        roledf = pd.DataFrame(rv, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        lam = (2.0 * rank(roledf) - 1.0).where(roledf.notna())
        ok = theta.notna() & omega.notna() & amp.notna() & lam.notna()
        u = (-lam).clip(lower=0.0).where(ok).fillna(0.0)
        usum = u.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        n_lead = (u > 0.05).sum(axis=1)
        cth = pd.DataFrame(np.cos(theta.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols)
        sth = pd.DataFrame(np.sin(theta.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols)
        c_f = (u * cth.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        s_f = (u * sth.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        om_f = (u * omega.where(ok).fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1) / usum
        r_f = np.sqrt(c_f * c_f + s_f * s_f)
        psi = pd.Series(np.arctan2(s_f.to_numpy(dtype=float), c_f.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx)
        om0 = 2.0 * np.pi / float(self._PERIOD)
        kappa = (float(self._KA) + float(self._KB) * lam) * om0
        g = kappa.mul(r_f, axis=0)
        g = g.where(g.abs() > 1e-05)
        detune = omega.sub(om_f, axis=0)
        ratio = (detune / g).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        locked = ratio.abs() <= float(self._LOCK)
        rc = ratio.clip(-float(self._LOCK), float(self._LOCK))
        asin = pd.DataFrame(np.arcsin(rc.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols)
        phi_star = asin.where(g > 0.0, np.pi - asin)
        lam_rate = g.abs() * np.sqrt((1.0 - rc * rc).clip(lower=0.0))
        relax = 1.0 - pd.DataFrame(np.exp(-(lam_rate * float(self._H)).clip(0.0, 30.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols)
        phi = _wrap(theta.sub(psi, axis=0))
        dphi = _wrap(phi_star - phi) * relax
        dtheta = dphi.add(om_f * float(self._H), axis=0)
        theta_fwd = theta + dtheta
        disp = amp * (pd.DataFrame(np.cos(theta_fwd.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=idx, columns=cols) - cth)
        disp = disp.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        n_rec = int(self._NREC)
        sd_p = p.rolling(n_rec, min_periods=int(n_rec * 3 // 4)).std()
        sd_p = sd_p.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        band = float(self._BAND) * sd_p
        pv = p.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        u1 = pv + disp.fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
        l0a, l1a = _dual_log_occupancy(pv, u1, band.to_numpy(dtype=float), n_rec, float(self._OCC_MINF))
        l0 = pd.DataFrame(l0a, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        l1 = pd.DataFrame(l1a, index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        grad = (l1 - l0).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        w_grad = (0.5 + 0.5 * np.tanh(float(self._GSLOPE) * grad)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        w_grad = w_grad.where(grad.notna(), 0.5)
        z_occ = ts_zscore(l0, int(self._ZWIN)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        w_fresh = (0.5 - 0.5 * np.tanh(z_occ)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        w_fresh = w_fresh.where(z_occ.notna(), 0.0)
        med = p.rolling(n_rec, min_periods=int(n_rec * 3 // 4)).median()
        field_ok = n_lead >= self._MIN_LEAD
        lock_mask = (locked & ok).fillna(False)
        lock_mask = lock_mask.where(field_ok, False).fillna(False).astype(bool)
        state_ok = p.notna() & sd_p.notna() & l0.notna()
        lock_mask = lock_mask & state_ok
        lock_leg = (disp * w_grad).where(lock_mask)
        rev_mask = state_ok & ~lock_mask
        rev_leg = (float(self._CREV) * w_fresh * (med - p).clip(-4.0, 4.0)).where(rev_mask)
        sig = lock_leg.fillna(0.0) + rev_leg.fillna(0.0)
        sig = sig.where(lock_mask | rev_mask)
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sc = sig.sub(sig.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        mad = sc.abs().median(axis=1)
        scale = mad.rolling(200, min_periods=5).mean().fillna(mad)
        scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
        out = sc.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Adler locking displacement routed by spread occupation potential
programs.trading_idea: Parent A produces a genuine finite-horizon *direction*: the Adler entrainment solution says where a phase-locked name's Epps-corrected precision-whitened dislocation should stand six bars from now, including the fold-over when entrainment carries it past its turning point. What it cannot know is whether the destination is reachable: a predicted displacement only completes inside six bars if it moves the spread *down* its own empirical potential, and Parent B's local time supplies exactly that potential — with U_i(u) = -log rho_i(u) from the trailing kernel occupation density of the whitened spread, moves toward habitually revisited levels are cheap and complete, moves into virgin territory stall or truncate. The child therefore evaluates the occupation density at BOTH the current level and the Adler-predicted target level and weights the displacement by the density gradient between them, while names that fail the locking criterion (no direction available) are instead pulled from fresh, unoccupied levels back to their habitual median. The interaction is the edge: A has direction with no notion of barrier, B's freshness gate is directionless (which is precisely why its declared fade sign was contradicted — freshness says a level is unaccepted, not which way it resolves), and only the signed density difference between origin and destination converts occupancy into a completion probability for a specific forecast.
programs.description: Computes the closed-form 6-bar Adler phase-locking displacement of the Epps-corrected precision-whitened dislocation (causal Gabor phase/amplitude, leader-only mean field, locking-margin relaxation) and multiplies it by a weight built from the trailing Gaussian-kernel occupation-density difference between the predicted target level and the current level; unlocked names get a freshness-weighted pull from unoccupied levels back to their habitual median spread.

programs.code:
"""Opacity-conditioned unbacked displacement: fade quiet moves in transparent
names, follow them in hard-to-value names.

Mechanism
---------
Over the fixed 6-bar forecast window, a name's peer-demeaned log return is split
into (a) the part its own aggressive flow paid for -- trailing Kyle lambda times
the 6-bar sum of normalized signed sqrt-volume -- and (b) an UNBACKED residual
(quote shading / fleeting quotes / hedging pressure with no print behind it).

The permanence of (b) is conditioned on the *information environment* of the
name, measured from point-in-time quarterly fundamentals (a static cross-
sectional characteristic, which is all quarterly data can honestly supply at a
10-second sampling frequency):

  * Transparent, cash-generating, low-intangible, low-leverage names have a
    tight consensus fair value; an unbacked move is inventory noise and reverts.
  * Opaque names (loss-makers, R&D- and intangible-heavy, highly levered, low
    FCF yield) have wide valuation disagreement; there price discovery happens
    in quotes rather than trades, so an unbacked move is slow-diffusing
    information and continues.

The transparency score is demeaned within sector so the signal is not a sector
bet, and size / liquidity proxies are deliberately excluded so the conditioner
is not a re-labelled illiquidity factor.

Causality: cross-sectional operations act within a single timestamp; all
time-series operations are trailing rolling windows or positive lags.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, src) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker text group key (last observed non-null label)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    if src is None:
        return labels
    for col in columns:
        if col not in src.columns:
            continue
        ser = src[col].dropna()
        if len(ser) == 0:
            continue
        val = ser.iloc[-1]
        if isinstance(val, str):
            txt = val.strip()
            if txt:
                labels[col] = txt
        elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
            labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _codes(labels: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> np.ndarray:
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(columns).values)
    return np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)

def _group_center(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_members: int, use_median: bool) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-group centering; groups smaller than min_members use the row."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        allsub = np.where(finite, arr, np.nan)
        mu_all = np.nanmedian(allsub, axis=1) if use_median else np.nanmean(allsub, axis=1)
        for k in np.unique(codes):
            m = codes == k
            if int(m.sum()) < int(min_members):
                out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu_all[:, None]
                continue
            sub = np.where(finite[:, m], arr[:, m], np.nan)
            mu = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1) if use_median else np.nanmean(sub, axis=1)
            out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu[:, None]
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)

@register_factor
class OpacityConditionedUnbackedDisplacementSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Fade unbacked displacement in transparent names, follow it in opaque ones."""
    factor_id = 'opacity_conditioned_unbacked_displacement_split_'
    name = 'Opacity-conditioned unbacked displacement split'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Sector-demeaned 6-bar log return minus own Kyle-lambda impact of signed sqrt-volume (unbacked displacement), damped by attribution confidence and multiplied by minus a sector-neutral fundamental transparency score.'
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ['close', 'open', 'volume', 'sector', 'earningsYield', 'freeCashFlowYield', 'incomeQuality', 'intangiblesToAssets', 'rdToRevenue', 'debtToAssets']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _K = 6
    _MIN_SEC = 4
    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _NORM_WIN = 180
    _SD_WIN = 360
    _SD_MIN = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        K = self._K
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret1 = (lp - lp.shift(1)).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d))
        rK = (lp - lp.shift(K)).where(lambda d: np.isfinite(d))
        codes_sec = _codes(_static_labels(cols, data.get('sector')), cols)
        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            f = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vol = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
            op = data.get('open')
            if op is not None:
                op = op.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
                op = op.where(np.isfinite(op) & (op > 0.0))
                dmid = lp - np.log(op)
            else:
                dmid = ret1
            sgn = np.sign(dmid.fillna(0.0))
            sgn = sgn.where(sgn != 0.0, np.sign(ret1.fillna(0.0)))
            rv = np.sqrt(vol)
            scale_v = ts_mean(rv, self._NORM_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            f = (sgn * rv / scale_v).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
            f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)
        lam = rolling_beta(ret1, f, self._BETA_WIN)
        lam = lam.where(np.isfinite(lam)).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        imp = (lam * ts_sum(f, K)).where(lambda x: np.isfinite(x)).fillna(0.0)
        d_ret = _group_center(rK, codes_sec, self._MIN_SEC, False)
        d_imp = _group_center(imp, codes_sec, self._MIN_SEC, False)
        sd = rK.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        u = ((d_ret - d_imp) / sd).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        conf = 1.0 / (1.0 + (d_imp.abs() / sd).clip(0.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0))
        acc = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        specs = [('earningsYield', 1.0), ('freeCashFlowYield', 1.0), ('intangiblesToAssets', -1.0), ('rdToRevenue', -1.0), ('debtToAssets', -1.0)]
        for field, direction in specs:
            raw = data.get(field)
            if raw is None:
                continue
            x = raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            x = x.where(np.isfinite(x))
            if x.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            r = rank(direction * x)
            acc = acc + r.fillna(0.0)
            cnt = cnt + r.notna().astype(float)
        iq = data.get('incomeQuality')
        if iq is not None:
            q = iq.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            q = q.where(np.isfinite(q))
            if q.notna().to_numpy().sum() > 0:
                r = rank(-(q - 1.0).abs().clip(0.0, 5.0))
                acc = acc + r.fillna(0.0)
                cnt = cnt + r.notna().astype(float)
        transp = acc / cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        transp = transp.where(np.isfinite(transp))
        if transp.notna().to_numpy().sum() > 0:
            tn = _group_center(transp, codes_sec, self._MIN_SEC, True)
            xs_sd = tn.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            a = tn.div(xs_sd, axis=0).clip(-1.5, 1.5) / 1.5
            a = a.where(np.isfinite(a)).fillna(0.0)
        else:
            a = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        weight = (0.3 + a).clip(-1.3, 1.3)
        raw_sig = -u * conf * weight
        valid = u.notna() & sd.notna()
        raw_sig = raw_sig.where(valid & np.isfinite(raw_sig))
        out = rank(raw_sig) - 0.5
        out = out.where(raw_sig.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Opacity-conditioned unbacked displacement split
programs.trading_idea: At 10-second resolution the parent's 'valuation multiple' is degenerate — per-share fundamentals are quarterly step functions, so its 6-bar multiple change collapses into a peer-demeaned return and the fundamental machinery bought only complexity (hence tiny residual IC and negative marginal ΔIC). The child keeps the one component with real content — the flow-UNBACKED part of a peer-demeaned 6-bar move, i.e. displacement in excess of the name's own Kyle-lambda impact of its signed sqrt-volume — and replaces the degenerate anchor with the one thing quarterly fundamentals *can* legitimately supply intraday: a static cross-sectional measure of how hard the name is to value (low earnings/FCF yield, loss-making, R&D- and intangible-heavy, levered), sector-neutralised so it is not a sector or size bet. Mechanism: for transparent, cash-generating names many participants agree on fair value, so a quote move with no trade behind it is dealer inventory/quote-shading noise and snaps back within seconds; for opaque names price discovery genuinely happens in quotes rather than prints (information is expensive to verify), so the same unbacked move is slow-diffusing information and continues. The factor is therefore a *sign-flipping interaction*, near-orthogonal to the book's many unconditional 'quiet displacement reverts' factors, and the edge persists because HFT liquidity providers condition on order flow and depth, not on quarterly accounting opacity — the two data domains sit on different clocks and are rarely joined.
programs.description: Computes the sector-demeaned 6-bar log return minus the name's own Kyle-lambda-implied impact of its normalized signed sqrt-volume (the 'unbacked' displacement), scales it by attribution confidence, and multiplies by minus a sector-neutral fundamental transparency score so anchored names' unbacked moves are faded and opaque names' unbacked moves are followed.

programs.code:
"""Flow-backing-split pooled lag-profile kernel, horizon-matched to 6 bars.

Mechanism
---------
A standing peer-relative displacement is a *level*; its autocorrelation decays
slowly, so a level-based reversion signal only pays out over many minutes.  The
horizon-matched object for a fixed 6-bar offset is the linear projection of the
next 6-bar idiosyncratic return onto a profile of DISJOINT past return blocks

    b1 = u(t-1..t),  b2 = u(t-5..t-2),  b3 = u(t-17..t-6),  b4 = u(t-53..t-18)

(u = sector-demeaned, vol-standardised bar return).  The projection weights are
estimated causally: at every bar we already observe pairs (predictor at t-6,
outcome realised over t-5..t), and those pairs are pooled across the panel over
a long trailing window.  Blocks whose relaxation is slower than the forecast
window receive near-zero weight automatically, instead of diluting the fast
component (which is what pushes level-based signals' IC out to 24 bars).

The conditioning interaction: the lag profile is state-dependent in traded
flow.  Light-volume displacements are liquidity-provider inventory and unwind
front-loaded (large negative weight on the freshest block); volume-backed
displacements carry a permanent (Kyle) component and keep their sign.  Two
kernels are therefore estimated - one per flow state - each shrunk toward the
unconditional kernel (empirical Bayes).

All statistics are trailing: rolling windows and positive lags only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static coarse peer label per ticker: sector when present, else industry."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (industry, sector):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
    return labels


def _group_resid(vals: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract the per-bar within-group median (market median if group thin)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=vals.index, columns=vals.columns)
    mkt = vals.median(axis=1)
    arr = labels.reindex(vals.columns).to_numpy()
    for lab in pd.unique(arr):
        sel = vals.columns[arr == lab]
        if len(sel) == 0:
            continue
        sub = vals[sel]
        if len(sel) >= 3:
            med = sub.median(axis=1)
            cnt = sub.notna().sum(axis=1)
            med = med.where(cnt >= 3, mkt)
        else:
            med = mkt
        out[sel] = sub.sub(med, axis=0)
    return out


def _pooled(df: pd.DataFrame, win: int, minp: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Trailing window sum per name, then pooled across names (causal)."""
    return df.rolling(win, min_periods=minp).sum().sum(axis=1)


def _broadcast(s: pd.Series, idx: pd.Index, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    a = s.reindex(idx).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    return pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(a[:, None], len(cols), axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)


@register_factor
class FlowBackingSplitPooledLagKernel(BaseFactor):
    """Flow-state-conditional, pooled, causally calibrated 6-bar lag kernel."""

    factor_id = 'flow_backing_split_pooled_lag_kernel_h6'
    name = 'Flow-backing-split pooled lag-profile kernel (6 bars)'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = (
        'Fitted 6-bar-ahead idiosyncratic return from four disjoint trailing '
        'return blocks, with weights estimated causally from pooled '
        '(predictor at t-6, realised 6-bar outcome) pairs separately for '
        'high- and low-recent-volume states and shrunk to the unconditional '
        'kernel, rescaled by residual volatility.'
    )
    window_length = 1500
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector', 'industry']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _BLOCK_EDGES = (2, 6, 18, 54)
    _CAL_WIN = 1200
    _CAL_MIN = 400
    _SHRINK = 0.35
    _MIN_OBS = 1500.0
    _W_CLIP = 2.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        p = np.log(px)
        if p.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero

        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        r = p.diff()
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'), data.get('industry'))
        ri = _group_resid(r, labels)
        sd = ri.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        u = (ri / sd).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u))
        uf = u.fillna(0.0)

        cs = {}
        for n in self._BLOCK_EDGES:
            cs[n] = uf.rolling(int(n), min_periods=int(n)).sum()
        e = self._BLOCK_EDGES
        blocks = [cs[e[0]], cs[e[1]] - cs[e[0]], cs[e[2]] - cs[e[1]], cs[e[3]] - cs[e[2]]]
        y = cs[e[1]]  # realised h-bar residual return (h == 6 == e[1])

        # --- flow-backing state: recent 6-bar volume vs the name's own norm ---
        vol = data.get('volume')
        if vol is None:
            f = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
            v6 = v.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
            vbase = v.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).mean() * float(h)
            f = np.log((v6 + 1.0) / (vbase + 1.0))
            f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)
        hi = f > 0.0

        gate = sd.notna() & sd.shift(h).notna() & cs[e[3]].shift(h).notna() & y.notna()
        st6 = hi.shift(h).fillna(False)
        hi6 = st6 & gate
        lo6 = (~st6) & gate

        nobs = _pooled(gate.astype(float), self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN)

        w_hi_list = []
        w_lo_list = []
        for bk in blocks:
            xk = bk.shift(h)
            prod = (y * xk)
            sq = xk * xk
            a_hi = _pooled(prod.where(hi6, 0.0).fillna(0.0), self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN)
            b_hi = _pooled(sq.where(hi6, 0.0).fillna(0.0), self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN)
            a_lo = _pooled(prod.where(lo6, 0.0).fillna(0.0), self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN)
            b_lo = _pooled(sq.where(lo6, 0.0).fillna(0.0), self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN)
            a_all = a_hi + a_lo
            b_all = b_hi + b_lo
            k = float(self._SHRINK)
            w_hi = (a_hi + k * a_all) / (b_hi + k * b_all + 1e-9)
            w_lo = (a_lo + k * a_all) / (b_lo + k * b_all + 1e-9)
            w_hi = w_hi.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-self._W_CLIP, self._W_CLIP)
            w_lo = w_lo.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(-self._W_CLIP, self._W_CLIP)
            w_hi_list.append(w_hi)
            w_lo_list.append(w_lo)

        pred = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for bk, w_hi, w_lo in zip(blocks, w_hi_list, w_lo_list):
            wdf = _broadcast(w_hi, idx, cols).where(hi, _broadcast(w_lo, idx, cols))
            pred = pred + wdf * bk.fillna(0.0)

        pred = pred * sd  # forecast of the raw 6-bar log return
        enough = _broadcast(nobs, idx, cols) >= self._MIN_OBS
        valid = sd.notna() & cs[e[3]].notna() & pred.notna() & np.isfinite(pred) & enough
        signal = pred.where(valid)

        out = rank(signal) - 0.5
        out = out.where(signal.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Flow-backing-split pooled lag-profile kernel (6 bars)
programs.trading_idea: The parent forecast a *level* (a standing peer-relative displacement) and therefore inherited the level's slow autocorrelation, so its information only cashed out over many minutes (IC rising monotonically to 24 bars). The correct horizon-matched object is not a level but the projection of the *next 6-bar* idiosyncratic return onto a profile of disjoint past return blocks (lags 1-2, 3-6, 7-18, 19-54), whose weights are estimated causally from realised (predictor at t-6, outcome over t-5..t) pairs pooled across the panel; blocks whose relaxation is slower than the window automatically receive near-zero weight instead of diluting the fast component. The crucial interaction is that this lag profile is state-dependent in trade flow: displacements built on light volume are almost pure liquidity-provider inventory and unwind front-loaded (large negative weight on the freshest block), whereas volume-backed displacements carry a permanent Kyle component and keep or extend their sign, so estimating one blended kernel — as the parent effectively did — cancels the fast, tradable part. The edge survives arbitrage because it pays a small vol-scaled premium per event for supplying immediacy precisely in the light-flow state where inventory must be warehoused with no confirming order flow, and because identifying the state-conditional kernel requires pooled estimation over heavily overlapping observations rather than a single visible price pattern.
programs.description: Sector-median-demeaned, vol-standardised 10-second returns are aggregated into four disjoint trailing blocks; a causally- and cross-sectionally-pooled regression of the realised 6-bar residual return on the same blocks lagged 6 bars, estimated separately for high- and low-recent-volume states (empirical-Bayes shrunk to the unconditional kernel), gives the weights, and the signal is the resulting fitted 6-bar return forecast rescaled by the name's residual volatility.

programs.code:
"""Silence-spell hazard: survival-weighted quote-ramp extrapolation.

Mechanism: a mid move printed in a (near-)zero-volume bar is a maker walking an
untested reservation quote.  That walk persists only while no trade arrives to
challenge it, and when a trade finally arrives only the permanent component of
the walked displacement survives.  Therefore the expected return over exactly
the next H = 6 bars is

    E[r_{t->t+6}]  ~  mu_quiet(t) * sum_{k=1..6} S_t(k)
                      - theta1 * D_t * (1 - S_t(6))
                      - theta2 * D_break * exp(-age_traded / hl),

where S_t(k) is the trailing-estimated probability that the current silence
spell survives k more bars (hazard estimated separately for young and old
spells, i.e. duration dependence / aging), mu_quiet is the drift rate per quiet
bar, D_t is the untested displacement accumulated inside the current spell, and
D_break is the displacement of a spell that has just been broken by a trade
(its transient part relaxing).  This is a horizon-matched extrapolation rather
than a band-pass filter: the hazard tells you *how much of the next 60 seconds*
the quote is still free to walk.

Falsifiable: if silent mid moves are just stale-quote noise, then weighting the
drift by the survival of silence adds nothing and the 6-bar IC collapses to zero
(and the interaction of drift with expected remaining quiet bars carries no
sign).  If the aging hazard is the real conditioner, IC at the fixed 6-bar
offset should exceed the parent's level-and-bandpass expression.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, stddev
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# causal helpers (trailing windows / positive lags only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _run_length(flag: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Number of consecutive True values ending at t (0 where flag is False).

    Closed-form and fully causal: cumulative count minus the count at the last
    False bar (forward-filled, i.e. only past information).
    """
    f = flag.astype(float)
    cs = f.cumsum()
    base = cs.where(~flag).ffill().fillna(0.0)
    return (cs - base).clip(lower=0.0)


def _spell_cumsum(x: pd.DataFrame, flag: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cumulative sum of x over the current uninterrupted run of `flag`.

    Zero on bars where flag is False (the spell is closed).  Causal.
    """
    xf = (x * flag.astype(float)).fillna(0.0)
    cs = xf.cumsum()
    base = cs.where(~flag).ffill().fillna(0.0)
    return cs - base


def _ewm_rate(num: pd.DataFrame, den: pd.DataFrame, hl: float, mp: int,
              den_floor: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing exponentially-weighted conditional rate num/den (a hazard)."""
    n = num.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=mp).mean()
    d = den.ewm(halflife=hl, min_periods=mp).mean()
    d = d.where(d >= den_floor)
    return (n / d).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _cs_normal_score(df: pd.DataFrame, min_names: int = 5) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional van der Waerden score: inverse-normal of the row rank."""
    valid = df.notna()
    cnt = valid.sum(axis=1)
    pct = df.rank(axis=1, pct=True).clip(0.005, 0.995)
    z = pd.DataFrame(
        stats.norm.ppf(pct.to_numpy(dtype=float)),
        index=df.index,
        columns=df.columns,
    )
    mask = valid.to_numpy() & (cnt.to_numpy() >= min_names)[:, None]
    return z.where(mask)


@register_factor
class SilenceSpellHazardSurvivalRampExtrapolation(BaseFactor):
    """Extrapolate an untested quote ramp only as far as silence is expected to last."""

    factor_id = "silence_spell_hazard_survival_ramp_extrapolation"
    name = "Silence-spell hazard: survival-weighted quote-ramp extrapolation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Age-bucketed trade-arrival hazard inside silence spells converts a quiet-bar "
        "drift rate into an explicit 6-bar forecast (drift x expected remaining quiet "
        "bars), net of the transient share of the untested within-spell displacement "
        "weighted by the probability it is tested inside the horizon, plus a decayed "
        "snapback for spells that have just been broken by a trade."
    )
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # --- parameters ------------------------------------------------------
    _H = 6              # forecast offset in bars (must match prediction_horizon)
    _VOL_WIN = 180      # trailing window defining each name's own volume norm
    _SIGMA_WIN = 120    # trailing window for per-name return scaling
    _C = 0.20           # 'quiet' = volume <= C * trailing average volume
    _A_SPLIT = 2        # spell-age bucket boundary (young vs. old silence)
    _HL_H = 300.0       # hazard estimator half-life (a slow state)
    _HL_MU = 5.0        # drift-rate estimator half-life (quiet bars only)
    _HL_REV = 2.0       # relaxation half-life of a just-tested displacement
    _THETA1 = 0.5       # transient share reversed when the spell is tested
    _THETA2 = 0.5       # transient share reversed after the spell broke
    _MIN_P = 100        # warm-up bars before hazard output is trusted
    _MIN_W = 0.15       # min effective quiet weight for a trusted drift rate

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        vol = volume.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = _log_returns(close)
        sigma = stddev(ret.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        r = (ret / sigma).clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- quiet / traded state ----------------------------------------
        base = adv(vol, self._VOL_WIN)
        quiet = (vol <= (self._C * base)) & base.notna()
        quiet = quiet.fillna(False)
        traded = ~quiet

        age_q = _run_length(quiet)         # consecutive quiet bars ending at t
        age_a = _run_length(traded)        # consecutive traded bars ending at t
        qf = quiet.astype(float)

        # ---- untested displacement accumulated inside the current spell ---
        disp = _spell_cumsum(r, quiet).clip(-20.0, 20.0)

        # ---- age-dependent trade-arrival hazard (trailing, per name) ------
        q_prev = quiet.shift(1).fillna(False)
        age_prev = age_q.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
        young = q_prev & (age_prev <= float(self._A_SPLIT))
        old = q_prev & (age_prev > float(self._A_SPLIT))
        arrive = traded.astype(float)

        h_y = _ewm_rate((traded & young).astype(float), young.astype(float),
                        self._HL_H, self._MIN_P, 0.02)
        h_o = _ewm_rate((traded & old).astype(float), old.astype(float),
                        self._HL_H, self._MIN_P, 0.01)
        h_u = arrive.ewm(halflife=self._HL_H, min_periods=self._MIN_P).mean()

        h_y = h_y.fillna(h_u).fillna(0.5).clip(0.02, 0.98)
        h_o = h_o.fillna(h_u).fillna(0.5).clip(0.02, 0.98)

        # ---- survival of the silence spell over the next H bars -----------
        surv = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        n_quiet = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for k in range(1, self._H + 1):
            age_k = age_q + float(k - 1)
            h_k = h_o.where(age_k > float(self._A_SPLIT), h_y)
            surv = surv * (1.0 - h_k)
            n_quiet = n_quiet + surv
        surv_h = surv.clip(0.0, 1.0)
        n_quiet = n_quiet.clip(0.0, float(self._H))

        # ---- drift rate per quiet bar ------------------------------------
        w_q = qf.ewm(halflife=self._HL_MU, min_periods=self._MIN_P).mean()
        m_q = (qf * r).ewm(halflife=self._HL_MU, min_periods=self._MIN_P).mean()
        mu = (m_q / w_q.where(w_q >= self._MIN_W)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mu = mu.clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # ---- leg 1: extrapolate the ramp only as far as silence survives --
        leg1 = (mu * n_quiet * qf).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- leg 2: transient share reversed when the spell gets tested ---
        leg2 = (-self._THETA1 * disp * (1.0 - surv_h) * qf).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- leg 3: relaxation of a spell that has just been broken ------
        d_break = disp.shift(1).where(age_a == 1.0).ffill()
        decay = np.exp(-(age_a - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0) / self._HL_REV)
        leg3 = (-self._THETA2 * d_break * decay).where(age_a >= 1.0, 0.0)
        leg3 = leg3.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        forecast = leg1 + leg2 + leg3

        ok = sigma.notna() & base.notna() & w_q.notna() & h_u.notna()
        score = _cs_normal_score(forecast.where(ok))
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Silence-spell hazard: survival-weighted quote-ramp extrapolation
programs.trading_idea: A mid-price that walks in bars with (near-)zero prints is a maker repricing an untested reservation quote; the walk continues only for as long as no trade arrives to challenge it, and once a trade does arrive only the permanent share of the walk survives. So the correct 6-bar forecast is not a filtered level or rate of the silent drift, but the drift rate multiplied by the *expected number of still-silent bars inside the next six*, computed from a trailing, age-dependent trade-arrival hazard (silence spells age: hazard differs for fresh vs. long-lived quiet), minus the transient share of the already-accumulated untested displacement times the probability that it gets tested within the horizon. This makes the signal explicitly horizon-matched at the fixed 6-bar offset — names in a young, low-hazard silence spell get the full six bars of extrapolation, names whose spell is about to break or has just broken get the snapback instead. The edge persists because harvesting it requires quoting in thin, rarely-traded names where the round-trip spread cost is of the same order as the 60-second drift, so fast arbitrageurs cannot lift it away.
programs.description: Splits bars into quiet (volume below a fraction of trailing average volume) and traded, estimates a per-name age-bucketed trade-arrival hazard from quiet bars, converts it into the survival probability and expected count of quiet bars over the next 6 bars, and returns the cross-sectional normal score of [quiet-bar drift rate x expected remaining quiet bars] minus [transient share of the untested within-spell displacement x probability the spell is tested] minus [decayed snapback of the displacement of a spell that just broke].

programs.code:
"""Pooled local-projection response of flow and displacement, split by turnover regime.

Mechanism
---------
Parent evidence kept: (i) mid displacement decomposes into flow-explained
(idiosyncratic vs basket-common) and flow-unexplained (quote-shading) parts that
carry OPPOSITE-signed information; (ii) whether that information resolves inside
the forecast window depends on the name's business clock (volume rate), not on
calendar age.

Parent defect (from the report): the polarity of each leg was *assumed*
(+idio, -basket, -1/2 quiet) and the delivery gate was *assumed* multiplicative.
The realised IC profile flips sign between 6 and 24 bars and IS/VAL disagree -
the signature of an un-calibrated response profile, not of a missing horizon.

Fix, at the pinned 6-bar offset:

    channels   P1 = recent own signed sqrt-volume flow
               P2 = recent ex-self sector peer flow      (commonality channel)
               P3 = fresh (1-3 bar) peer-purged, vol-standardised displacement
               P4 = older (4-12 bar) peer-purged, vol-standardised displacement

    target     y_t = cross-sectional z of (log P_t - log P_{t-6})

    estimator  pooled trailing normal equations over names x time:
                   b(t) = ( sum_i sum_{u<=t} X_i(u) X_i(u)' + ridge )^{-1}
                          ( sum_i sum_{u<=t} X_i(u) y_i(u) ),  X = P shifted 6

The multivariate partials do the orthogonalisation the parent hand-coded: the
coefficient on P1 is the own-flow effect controlling for peer flow (idio), the
coefficient on P2 the basket-common effect, and the coefficients on P3/P4 the
effect of displacement NOT explained by flow (quote shading) at two relaxation
lags.  Pooling across names buys the estimation precision that per-name rolling
betas lacked.  The parent's delivery gate becomes an ESTIMATED interaction: two
separate coefficient vectors, one for fast-turnover names (forecast volume rate
above the cross-sectional median) and one for slow ones.

Falsifiable: (a) the fitted expectation should have positive 6-bar IC with a
profile that peaks at ~6 bars rather than growing to 24; (b) |coefficients| in
the fast-turnover state should exceed those in the slow state; (c) the estimated
sign on the fresh-displacement channel should be negative (quote shading fades)
while own-flow-controlling-for-peer-flow should be positive.

All statistics are causal: trailing rolling / ewm windows, positive lags only,
cross-sectional operations act inside a single timestamp, and every regression is
a trailing normal-equation solve computed in this file.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_codes(columns: pd.Index, sector: pd.DataFrame | None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Integer-coded static sector label per ticker (last observed text value)."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    if sector is not None:
        for col in columns:
            if col not in sector.columns:
                continue
            ser = sector[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(columns).values)
    return np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)


def _peer_ex_self_mean(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-sector mean EXCLUDING the own column (contemporaneous only)."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    vals = np.where(finite, arr, 0.0)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    row_sum = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    row_cnt = finite.sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float)
    for k in np.unique(codes):
        m = codes == k
        if int(m.sum()) < int(min_peers):
            s = row_sum - vals[:, m]
            c = row_cnt - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        else:
            s = vals[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None] - vals[:, m]
            c = finite[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float) - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
            res = np.where(c > 0.0, s / np.where(c > 0.0, c, 1.0), np.nan)
        out[:, m] = res
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)


def _cs_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional z-score inside each timestamp (no time-series information)."""
    mu = df.mean(axis=1)
    sd = df.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = df.sub(mu, axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    return z.where(np.isfinite(z)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)


def _pooled_coefs(
    preds_lagged: list[pd.DataFrame],
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    mask: pd.DataFrame,
    n: int,
    n_min: int,
    ridge: float,
    half_life: float,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing pooled (names x time) multivariate OLS coefficients.

    Solves b(t) = (S_xx(t) + ridge I)^-1 S_xy(t) where the sufficient statistics
    are rolling sums over the last n bars of cross-name sums of products.  All
    inputs are already lagged, so the value at t uses only information <= t.
    """
    k = len(preds_lagged)
    idx = y.index
    good_mask = mask.astype(float)
    valid = good_mask * y.notna().astype(float)
    for p in preds_lagged:
        valid = valid * p.notna().astype(float)
    xa = [p.fillna(0.0) * valid for p in preds_lagged]
    ya = y.fillna(0.0) * valid

    t_len = len(idx)
    mat = np.zeros((t_len, k, k))
    vec = np.zeros((t_len, k))
    for a in range(k):
        for b in range(a, k):
            s = (xa[a] * xa[b]).sum(axis=1).rolling(n, min_periods=n_min).sum()
            arr = s.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            mat[:, a, b] = arr
            mat[:, b, a] = arr
        sv = (xa[a] * ya).sum(axis=1).rolling(n, min_periods=n_min).sum()
        vec[:, a] = sv.to_numpy(dtype=float)

    tr = np.trace(mat, axis1=1, axis2=2)
    eye = np.eye(k)[None, :, :]
    lam = ridge * np.where(np.isfinite(tr) & (tr > 0.0), tr, 0.0) / float(k)
    mat_r = mat + lam[:, None, None] * eye

    coefs = np.full((t_len, k), np.nan)
    ok = (
        np.isfinite(mat_r).all(axis=(1, 2))
        & np.isfinite(vec).all(axis=1)
        & np.isfinite(tr)
        & (tr > 0.0)
    )
    if bool(ok.any()):
        pinv = np.linalg.pinv(mat_r[ok])
        coefs[ok] = np.einsum('tij,tj->ti', pinv, vec[ok])

    out = pd.DataFrame(coefs, index=idx)
    out = out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    out = out.ewm(halflife=half_life, min_periods=1).mean()
    return out.fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class PooledLpTurnoverRegimeFlowDisplacement(BaseFactor):
    """Fitted 6-bar return from a pooled, turnover-regime-split local projection."""

    factor_id = 'pooled_lp_turnover_regime_flow_displacement_h6'
    name = 'Pooled LP response of flow and displacement by turnover regime'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Cross-sectionally standardised channels (own signed sqrt-volume flow, ex-self sector '
        'peer flow, fresh and older peer-purged vol-standardised displacement) are mapped to '
        'expected 6-bar return by pooled trailing normal-equation regressions estimated '
        'separately for fast- and slow-turnover names; the score is each name\'s fitted value.'
    )
    window_length = 720
    inputs = ['close', 'open', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _NORM_WIN = 180
    _SD_WIN = 240
    _SD_MIN = 60
    _FLOW_DECAY = 6
    _FRESH = 3
    _OLD_WIN = 9
    _VOL_WIN = 120
    _VOL_MIN = 30
    _FAST_HL = 6.0
    _FAST_MIN = 20
    _MIN_PEERS = 4
    _CAL_WIN = 360
    _CAL_MIN = 120
    _COEF_HL = 60.0
    _RIDGE = 0.05
    _SMOOTH = 2

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        vol_raw = data.get('volume')
        if vol_raw is None:
            return zero
        vol = vol_raw.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        vol = vol.where(np.isfinite(vol) & (vol >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # ---- trade direction: intra-bar mid change, else bar-over-bar change ----
        op = data.get('open')
        if op is not None:
            op = op.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            op = op.where(np.isfinite(op) & (op > 0.0))
            dmid = lp - np.log(op)
        else:
            dmid = r
        s_dir = np.sign(dmid.fillna(0.0))
        s_dir = s_dir.where(s_dir != 0.0, np.sign(r.fillna(0.0)))

        rv = np.sqrt(vol)
        sc = ts_mean(rv, self._NORM_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        f = (s_dir * rv / sc).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)

        codes = _static_codes(cols, data.get('sector'))

        # ---- peer-purged displacement and sector-common flow --------------------
        r_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(r, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        f_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(f, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        f_peer = f_peer.where(np.isfinite(f_peer)).fillna(0.0)

        u = (r - r_peer).where(np.isfinite(r) & np.isfinite(r_peer))
        sd = u.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        x = (u / sd).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
        base_ok = x.notna() & sd.notna()

        # ---- four causal channels ----------------------------------------------
        x0 = x.fillna(0.0)
        p_flow = decay_linear(f, self._FLOW_DECAY)
        p_pflow = decay_linear(f_peer, self._FLOW_DECAY)
        p_fresh = ts_sum(x0, self._FRESH) / float(np.sqrt(float(self._FRESH)))
        p_old = ts_sum(x0.shift(self._FRESH), self._OLD_WIN) / float(np.sqrt(float(self._OLD_WIN)))

        preds = [
            _cs_z(p_flow.where(base_ok)),
            _cs_z(p_pflow.where(base_ok)),
            _cs_z(p_fresh.where(base_ok)),
            _cs_z(p_old.where(base_ok)),
        ]

        # ---- turnover regime: forecast volume rate vs cross-sectional median ----
        v_long = vol.rolling(self._VOL_WIN, min_periods=self._VOL_MIN).mean().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        v_fast = vol.ewm(halflife=self._FAST_HL, min_periods=self._FAST_MIN).mean()
        phi = (v_fast / v_long).clip(0.0, 6.0)
        phi = phi.where(np.isfinite(phi))
        med = phi.median(axis=1)
        dev = phi.sub(med, axis=0)
        m_fast = dev.gt(0.0) & phi.notna()
        m_slow = dev.le(0.0) & phi.notna()

        # ---- pooled local projection at the pinned offset ----------------------
        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        y = _cs_z((lp - lp.shift(h)).where(np.isfinite(lp - lp.shift(h))))
        preds_lag = [p.shift(h) for p in preds]
        mf_lag = m_fast.astype(float).shift(h).fillna(0.0) > 0.5
        ms_lag = m_slow.astype(float).shift(h).fillna(0.0) > 0.5

        cf_fast = _pooled_coefs(
            preds_lag, y, mf_lag, self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN, self._RIDGE, self._COEF_HL
        )
        cf_slow = _pooled_coefs(
            preds_lag, y, ms_lag, self._CAL_WIN, self._CAL_MIN, self._RIDGE, self._COEF_HL
        )

        valid = preds[0].notna()
        for p in preds[1:]:
            valid = valid & p.notna()

        yhat = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for mk, cf in ((m_fast, cf_fast), (m_slow, cf_slow)):
            contrib = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
            for c, p in enumerate(preds):
                contrib = contrib + p.fillna(0.0).mul(cf.iloc[:, c], axis=0)
            yhat = yhat + contrib.where(mk & valid, 0.0)

        out = yhat.where(valid)
        out = decay_linear(out.fillna(0.0), self._SMOOTH).where(valid)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        sdr = out.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        out = out.div(sdr, axis=0)
        out = out.where(valid, 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Pooled local-projection response of flow & displacement, split by turnover regime
programs.trading_idea: The parent proved that flow-attributed and quiet displacement carry opposite-signed information, but it *assumed* the polarity (+idio, −basket, −quiet) and *assumed* a multiplicative volume-clock delivery gate; the evaluation shows the assumed polarity is only weakly right at 6 bars and outright wrong by 12-24 bars, and the IS/VAL sign instability is exactly what an assumed, un-calibrated response profile produces. The child instead estimates the response empirically at the pinned offset: a cross-name **pooled multivariate local projection** of realised 6-bar returns on four causal channels (own signed sqrt-volume flow, sector peer flow, fresh 1-3-bar peer-purged displacement, older 4-12-bar displacement), solved from trailing normal equations, so the multivariate partials themselves separate idiosyncratic flow, basket-common flow and flow-unexplained (quote-shading) displacement — no hand-set sign, no per-name Kyle-lambda noise. Because impact only resolves inside the window when the name's business clock is running, the coefficient vector is estimated separately in two turnover states (fast vs slow relative to the cross-sectional median of forecast/long-run volume rate), which converts the parent's assumed θ shrinkage into a falsifiable, estimated interaction. The edge should persist because pooling plus exact horizon matching is a statistical-efficiency edge, not a public formula: it requires jointly maintaining a panel of causal channel innovations and a rolling 4x4 pooled regression on a 10-second grid, and the positions it takes are concentrated in fast-turnover states where capacity is bounded by impact cost.
programs.description: Builds four causal channels (own signed sqrt-volume flow, ex-self sector peer flow, fresh and older peer-purged vol-standardised displacement), cross-sectionally standardises them, fits pooled trailing 4-variable normal-equation regressions of realised 6-bar returns on the 6-bar-lagged channels separately for fast- and slow-turnover names, and scores each name by its fitted expected 6-bar return using its current turnover regime's coefficients.

programs.code:
"""Diurnal-clock-normalised paid/unpaid dislocation, purged of the trailing-window version.

Mechanism: intraday volume and variance carry a strong deterministic time-of-day
profile.  Trailing-window standardisation (what almost every intraday signal
uses) therefore confuses 'it is near the open/close' with 'something happened',
both in the size of a displacement and in whether that displacement was paid for
with aggressive volume.  We estimate the market-wide diurnal shape of |return|
and of volume from PRIOR days' same-time bars (pooled across names for
robustness), deseasonalise both channels, and measure the dislocation as
displacement per unit of *expected* noise, gated by *unexpected* volume:
unexpectedly heavy volume => temporary impact that decays (reversal);
unexpectedly quiet tape => quote repricing that persists (continuation).
Finally the score is cross-sectionally purged, bar by bar, of the conventional
trailing-window displacement and of the trailing-window volume-gated
displacement, so the surviving signal is exactly the diurnal correction.
Falsified if trailing-window standardisation already spans the effect, in which
case the purged score has no forecasting power.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import stddev, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_EPS = 1e-12

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns, robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(close > 0.0)
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _tod_key(index) -> pd.Series:
    """Seconds-since-midnight label for each bar (time-of-day bucket)."""
    try:
        idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(index)
        key = idx.hour * 3600 + idx.minute * 60 + idx.second
        return pd.Series(np.asarray(key, dtype=float), index=index)
    except Exception:
        return pd.Series(np.zeros(len(index)), index=index)

def _prior_day_profile(s: pd.Series, tod: pd.Series) -> tuple:
    """(profile, level) where profile[t] = mean of s over *previous* bars sharing
    the same time-of-day bucket and level[t] = mean of s over all previous bars.
    Both strictly exclude the current bar, hence causal."""
    sf = s.fillna(0.0)
    cnt = s.notna().astype(float)
    csum = sf.groupby(tod).cumsum() - sf
    ccnt = cnt.groupby(tod).cumsum() - cnt
    prof = csum / ccnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    lvl = (sf.cumsum() - sf) / (cnt.cumsum() - cnt).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (prof, lvl)

def _diurnal_shape(s: pd.Series, tod: pd.Series, fallback_win: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Multiplicative time-of-day shape (mean 1-ish).  Falls back to a trailing
    market-activity ratio when there is not yet a prior day at this bucket."""
    prof, lvl = _prior_day_profile(s, tod)
    lvl_safe = lvl.where(lvl > 0.0)
    shape = prof / lvl_safe
    mp = max(5, int(fallback_win // 4))
    recent = s.rolling(fallback_win, min_periods=mp).mean() / lvl_safe
    shape = shape.fillna(recent)
    return shape.clip(0.2, 5.0).fillna(1.0)

def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row robust standardisation (median / MAD with std fallback)."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    return dev.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

def _cs_residualize2(y: pd.DataFrame, x1: pd.DataFrame, x2: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise (cross-sectional) OLS residual of y on {x1, x2} with intercept.
    Uses only contemporaneous cross-sectional information -> no look-ahead."""
    mask = y.notna() & x1.notna() & x2.notna()
    yv = y.where(mask)
    a = x1.where(mask)
    b = x2.where(mask)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1)
    yv = yv.sub(yv.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    a = a.sub(a.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    b = b.sub(b.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    s11 = (a * a).sum(axis=1)
    s22 = (b * b).sum(axis=1)
    s12 = (a * b).sum(axis=1)
    t1 = (a * yv).sum(axis=1)
    t2 = (b * yv).sum(axis=1)
    det = s11 * s22 - s12 * s12
    ok = (det.abs() > 1e-10) & (n >= 6)
    det_safe = det.where(ok)
    beta1 = ((s22 * t1 - s12 * t2) / det_safe).where(ok).fillna(0.0)
    beta2 = ((s11 * t2 - s12 * t1) / det_safe).where(ok).fillna(0.0)
    res = yv.sub(a.mul(beta1, axis=0)).sub(b.mul(beta2, axis=0))
    return res.where(mask)

@register_factor
class DiurnalVarianceClockPurgedPaidUnpaidDislocation(BaseFactor):
    """Diurnal-clock-normalised dislocation split, purged of its trailing-window twin."""
    factor_id = 'diurnal_variance_clock_purged_paid_unpaid_disloc'
    name = 'Diurnal-clock-normalised paid/unpaid dislocation (purged)'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Deseasonalises returns and volume by a causally estimated market-wide time-of-day profile, forms a 6-bar displacement z-score gated by the deseasonalised volume surprise (heavy volume -> reversal, quiet tape -> continuation), then cross-sectionally residualises it against the conventional trailing-window displacement and its volume-gated version.'
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _DISP = 6
    _SIG_WIN = 240
    _FALLBACK = 60
    _GATE = 1.5

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume'].reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        vol = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        ret = _log_returns(close)
        tod = _tod_key(close.index)
        m_abs = ret.abs().median(axis=1)
        shape_r = _diurnal_shape(m_abs, tod, self._FALLBACK)
        m_vol = vol.median(axis=1)
        shape_v = _diurnal_shape(m_vol, tod, self._FALLBACK)
        sr = shape_r.where(shape_r > 0.0)
        sv = shape_v.where(shape_v > 0.0)
        r_des = ret.div(sr, axis=0)
        sig_des = stddev(r_des, self._SIG_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        disp_des = ts_sum(r_des.fillna(0.0), self._DISP)
        z_des = (disp_des / (sig_des * np.sqrt(float(self._DISP)))).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        z_des = z_des.where(sig_des.notna())
        base_v = ts_mean(vol, self._SIG_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rel_v_des = ts_mean(vol, self._DISP).div(base_v).div(sv, axis=0)
        u_des = _cs_robust_z(np.log1p(rel_v_des.clip(lower=0.0)))
        sig_tr = stddev(ret, self._SIG_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z_tr = (ts_sum(ret.fillna(0.0), self._DISP) / (sig_tr * np.sqrt(float(self._DISP)))).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        z_tr = z_tr.where(sig_tr.notna())
        rel_v_tr = ts_mean(vol, self._DISP).div(base_v)
        u_tr = _cs_robust_z(np.log1p(rel_v_tr.clip(lower=0.0)))
        zd = _cs_robust_z(z_des)
        zt = _cs_robust_z(z_tr)
        y = -zd * np.tanh(u_des / self._GATE)
        x1 = -zt
        x2 = -zt * np.tanh(u_tr / self._GATE)
        resid = _cs_residualize2(y, x1, x2)
        score = _cs_robust_z(resid).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        return score.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Diurnal-clock-normalised paid/unpaid dislocation (purged of the trailing-window version)
programs.trading_idea: Intraday volume and variance follow a strong deterministic time-of-day profile, so a bar's volume looks 'heavy' and its displacement looks 'large' mostly because of *where in the session* it sits; every trailing-window standardisation therefore mixes a mechanical clock effect into the paid-versus-unpaid dislocation split. This child estimates the market-wide diurnal shape of |return| and of volume causally from prior days' same-time bars (pooled cross-sectionally for robustness), deseasonalises both channels, and only then measures the dislocation and the volume surprise: what remains is a genuine conditional surprise — displacement per unit of *expected* noise, paid for with *unexpectedly* aggressive volume (temporary impact that decays, hence reversal) or printed on unexpectedly quiet tape (quote repricing that persists, hence continuation). To make the claim falsifiable and non-redundant, the score is cross-sectionally purged each bar of the conventional trailing-window dislocation and of the trailing-window volume-gated dislocation, so only the diurnal correction survives. The edge persists because the correction requires multi-day, cross-name estimation of a seasonal profile that convenience-driven intraday signals skip, and it is largest at low-liquidity times of day where spread costs deter high-capacity arbitrage.
programs.description: Deseasonalises bar returns and volume by a causally estimated market-wide time-of-day profile, forms a 6-bar displacement z-score and a volume-surprise gate on the deseasonalised channels (reversal when volume is unexpectedly heavy, continuation when unexpectedly quiet), then cross-sectionally residualises that score against the equivalent trailing-window-standardised signals.

programs.code:
"""Out-of-sample hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation.

Mechanism
---------
A short-run single-name move splits into a peer-common part (the leave-one-out
industry basket move, scaled by a trailing beta) and a peer-idiosyncratic
residual.  Liquidity providers can only warehouse -- and therefore repair --
the residual when the peer basket genuinely replicates the name; the honest
measure of that is the *out-of-sample* replication quality of the hedge,
i.e. one minus the ratio of lagged-beta residual mean square to own return
mean square, estimated on a window that ends before the impulse.

Two statistical choices follow directly from the mechanism:

  * The beta used to build the residual is computed from data ending H=6 bars
    before the impulse window, so the 6-bar residual is a genuine out-of-sample
    dislocation rather than an in-sample residual that is mechanically
    orthogonal to the basket and whose persistence is biased downwards.
  * The impulse is HORIZON-SYMMETRIC: the residual is cumulated over exactly
    H=6 bars, matching the fixed 6-bar forecast offset.

The loading is a pure interaction: the centred cross-sectional rank of hedge
precision multiplies the (negated) residual, so high-precision names are
forecast to mean-revert and high-basis-risk names to continue.  This makes the
factor close to orthogonal to plain reversal and falsifiable in both halves of
the cross-section.

Causality: all cross-sectional statistics are taken within one timestamp; all
time-series statistics are trailing rolling windows or positive lags.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, rolling_beta, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sector, industry) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker peer-group key: industry when present, else sector."""
    labels = pd.Series("ALL", index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in (sector, industry):
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                val = val.strip()
                if val:
                    labels[col] = val
            elif val is not None and not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val)):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels


def _loo_mean(a: pd.DataFrame, labels: pd.Series, min_peers: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Within-group mean of ``a`` EXCLUDING the name itself (leave-one-out)."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)
    for _, members in labels.groupby(labels).groups.items():
        cols = [c for c in list(members) if c in a.columns]
        if not cols:
            continue
        sub = a[cols]
        present = sub.notna().to_numpy().astype(float)
        vals = sub.fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
        tot = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        cnt = present.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
        excl_sum = tot - vals
        excl_cnt = cnt - present
        ok = excl_cnt >= float(min_peers)
        safe = np.where(excl_cnt > 0.0, excl_cnt, 1.0)
        res = np.where(ok, excl_sum / safe, np.nan)
        out[cols] = pd.DataFrame(res, index=a.index, columns=cols)
    return out


@register_factor
class OosHedgePrecisionSignFlipPeerResidual(BaseFactor):
    """Peer-residual dislocation whose loading flips with out-of-sample hedge precision."""

    factor_id = "oos_hedge_precision_signflip_peer_residual_h6"
    name = "OOS hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Minus the 6-bar cumulative leave-one-out industry-basket residual return "
        "(beta from data ending 6 bars earlier) times the centred cross-sectional "
        "rank of trailing out-of-sample hedge precision, so well-replicated names "
        "are forecast to revert and high-basis-risk names to continue."
    )
    window_length = 600
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "industry", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _H = 6
    _MIN_PEERS = 3
    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _Q_WIN = 180
    _Q_MIN = 60
    _SD_WIN = 360
    _SD_MIN = 120

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        H = self._H

        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get("sector"), data.get("industry"))

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        r = lp - lp.shift(1)
        r = r.where(np.isfinite(r))

        # Peer-common channel: leave-one-out industry basket return.
        rp = _loo_mean(r, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
        rp = rp.where(np.isfinite(rp))

        # Beta estimated on a window ending H bars before now => residual is OOS.
        beta = rolling_beta(r, rp, self._BETA_WIN)
        beta = beta.where(np.isfinite(beta)).clip(-4.0, 4.0).shift(H)

        u = r - beta * rp                    # out-of-sample one-bar residual
        u = u.where(np.isfinite(u))

        # Horizon-symmetric impulse: H-bar cumulative residual, vol standardised.
        e = u.rolling(H, min_periods=H).sum()
        sd = e.rolling(self._SD_WIN, min_periods=self._SD_MIN).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = e / sd
        z = z.where(np.isfinite(z)).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # Hedge precision = trailing out-of-sample predictive R^2 of the basket,
        # measured strictly before the impulse window (shifted by H bars).
        ms_u = (u * u).rolling(self._Q_WIN, min_periods=self._Q_MIN).mean().shift(H)
        ms_r = (r * r).rolling(self._Q_WIN, min_periods=self._Q_MIN).mean().shift(H)
        q = 1.0 - ms_u / ms_r.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        q = q.where(np.isfinite(q)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # Hedge legs must be tradable right now: peer basket traded in last H bars.
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            live = pd.DataFrame(True, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0), 0.0)
            v6 = ts_sum(v, H)
            peer_v = _loo_mean(v6, labels, self._MIN_PEERS)
            live = peer_v.fillna(0.0) > 0.0

        valid = z.notna() & q.notna() & live
        if valid.to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        gate = rank(q.where(valid)) - 0.5      # in [-0.5, 0.5], sign-flexible loading
        sig = (-z.where(valid)) * (2.0 * gate)
        sig = sig.where(np.isfinite(sig))

        out = rank(sig) - 0.5
        out = out.where(sig.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: OOS hedge-precision sign-flipping peer-residual dislocation
programs.trading_idea: A dealer will only absorb (and therefore repair) a single-name dislocation if the peer basket actually replicates that name, and the honest measure of replication is *out-of-sample* basis risk, not in-sample fit: residuals taken with a beta estimated on data ending before the impulse retain the true dislocation, whereas in-sample residuals are mechanically orthogonalised and their persistence is biased away. So the child conditions on trailing predictive R-squared of the leave-one-out industry basket for the name (1 - MSE of lagged-beta residuals / own return variance), measured strictly before the impulse window: where hedge precision is high the 6-bar idiosyncratic residual is cheap inventory and snaps back within the same 6-bar clock, where basis risk is large the same residual is unhedgeable information and continues. The factor is therefore a pure interaction (signed by the cross-sectional rank of hedge precision), which makes it nearly orthogonal to plain reversal and falsifiable in two directions at once: if the interaction is noise, both halves of the cross-section should show the same sign. The edge survives arbitrage because it is a basis-risk/capital constraint on the liquidity provider, not a mispricing: nobody can warehouse a residual whose hedge does not track it, and that condition is measured, not assumed.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of minus the 6-bar cumulative leave-one-out-industry-basket residual return (beta estimated from data ending 6 bars earlier, so the residual is out-of-sample), multiplied by the centred cross-sectional rank of trailing out-of-sample hedge precision (1 - residual MSE / return MSE, lagged 6 bars), so reversal is expressed for well-replicated names and continuation for high-basis-risk names; restricted to names whose peer basket actually traded in the last 6 bars.

programs.code:
"""Aggregate impact-elasticity regime routed over excess-paid vs unpaid hedged drift.

Mechanism
---------
A name's 10-second beta-hedged, sector-demeaned excursion is decomposed by HOW it was
paid for, bar by bar:

  (1) UNPAID leg - residual move weighted by mu_v/(v+mu_v), i.e. concentrated in bars
      whose own traded volume is far below the name's trailing norm.  Nobody bought this
      move; it is a dealer shading quotes on private adverse-selection / inventory
      beliefs, so it tends to CONTINUE.
  (2) EXCESS-PAID leg - residual move weighted by v/(v+mu_v), but with each bar's own
      square-root-law expected impact removed.  The expected part (c_i * sqrt(v/mu_v),
      with c_i a trailing per-name slope of |residual return| on sqrt relative volume)
      is the flow-justified, quasi-permanent component; only the EXCESS displacement is
      over-payment / transient impact and is mechanically repaid.

Whether that repayment happens is a market-WIDE state: the current price of risk
transfer.  Measured as an aggregate Kyle elasticity

    lambda_t = Cov_W(|m_s|, A_s) / Var_W(A_s),   m_s = mean_i r_{i,s},
               A_s = mean_i sqrt(v_{i,s}/mu_{i,s}),

a HIGH lambda means each unit of aggregate participation shoves prices (thin
risk-bearing capacity): single-name excess displacement is inventory imbalance repaid
within a few bars, so fade it hard.  A COLLAPSE in lambda means flow is being absorbed
cheaply, so volume-driven excursions are informed and the paid leg flips to
continuation.  The unpaid leg is treated in mirror image: unpriced quote shading is most
informative when the market absorbs flow (low lambda) and closest to stale-mid drag when
lambda is high.

Causality: market factor, betas, residual std, volume norms, per-name impact slopes, the
aggregate elasticity and its z-score are all trailing rolling statistics; cross-sectional
operations act inside a single timestamp only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rolling_beta, stddev, ts_mean, ts_sum
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _log_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bar log returns robust to zero / negative / missing prices."""
    c = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
    lc = np.log(c)
    return (lc - lc.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar cross-sectional median/MAD standardisation with std fallback."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    return dev.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, source) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker text label (sector); defaults to one pooled group."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    if source is None:
        return labels
    for col in columns:
        if col not in source.columns:
            continue
        ser = source[col].dropna()
        if len(ser) == 0:
            continue
        val = ser.iloc[-1]
        if isinstance(val, str) and val.strip():
            labels[col] = val.strip()
    return labels

def _group_demean(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_members: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-group mean removal; thin groups fall back to the full row."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sub = np.where(np.isfinite(arr), arr, np.nan)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        mu_all = np.nanmean(sub, axis=1)
        for k in np.unique(codes):
            m = codes == k
            if int(m.sum()) < int(min_members):
                out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu_all[:, None]
                continue
            mu = np.nanmean(sub[:, m], axis=1)
            out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu[:, None]
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)

def _market_factor(r1: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Equal-weighted cross-sectional mean return (the common factor)."""
    arr = r1.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    sub = np.where(np.isfinite(arr), arr, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        m_raw = np.nanmean(sub, axis=1)
    m = np.where(np.isfinite(m_raw), m_raw, 0.0)
    return pd.Series(m, index=r1.index)

def _elasticity_z(m: pd.Series, a: pd.Series, w_est: int, w_z: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Trailing z-score of the aggregate impact elasticity Cov(|m|,A)/Var(A)."""
    absm = m.abs()
    mp_e = max(20, w_est // 2)
    cov = absm.rolling(w_est, min_periods=mp_e).cov(a)
    var = a.rolling(w_est, min_periods=mp_e).var().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    lam = (cov / var).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    mp_z = max(60, w_z // 3)
    mu = lam.rolling(w_z, min_periods=mp_z).mean()
    sd = lam.rolling(w_z, min_periods=mp_z).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = ((lam - mu) / sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return z.clip(-3.0, 3.0)

@register_factor
class AggregateImpactElasticityExcessPaidQuietSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Excess-paid displacement faded in expensive-risk-transfer regimes, unpaid quote drift followed in cheap ones."""
    factor_id = 'aggregate_impact_elasticity_gated_excess_paid_qu'
    name = 'Aggregate impact-elasticity gated excess-paid vs unpaid drift split'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Splits the beta-hedged, sector-demeaned, vol-normalised 30-bar residual drift into an unpaid (low own-volume weighted) leg and a paid leg carrying only the displacement in excess of each name trailing sqrt-law expected impact, then combines their cross-sectional robust z-scores with weights set by the trailing z-score of an aggregate impact elasticity (rolling slope of |market return| on mean relative participation): the excess-paid leg is faded hard when risk transfer is expensive and flips to continuation when it is cheap.'
    window_length = 900
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'sector']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _SPLIT_WIN = 30
    _VOL_WIN = 150
    _IMP_WIN = 300
    _BETA_WIN = 180
    _SIGMA_WIN = 300
    _W_EST = 90
    _W_Z = 600
    _MIN_PEERS = 3

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        r1 = _log_returns(close)
        volume = data.get('volume')
        if volume is None:
            vol = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vol = volume.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        mu_v = ts_mean(vol, self._VOL_WIN)
        mu_v = mu_v.where(np.isfinite(mu_v) & (mu_v > 0.0))
        tot = (vol + mu_v).replace(0.0, np.nan)
