        p_paid = (vol / tot).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        p_paid = p_paid.where(np.isfinite(p_paid))
        q_quiet = 1.0 - p_paid
        relv = (vol / mu_v).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        x_flow = np.sqrt(relv.clip(lower=0.0)).clip(upper=5.0)
        m_ser = _market_factor(r1)
        a_ser = x_flow.mean(axis=1).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).ffill().fillna(0.0)
        z_lam = _elasticity_z(m_ser, a_ser, self._W_EST, self._W_Z)
        mkt = pd.DataFrame(np.repeat(m_ser.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1), index=idx, columns=cols)
        beta = rolling_beta(r1, mkt, self._BETA_WIN)
        beta = beta.where(np.isfinite(beta)).clip(-4.0, 4.0).fillna(1.0)
        resid = (r1 - beta * mkt).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sigma = stddev(resid.fillna(0.0), self._SIGMA_WIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rz = (resid / sigma).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        labels = _static_labels(cols, data.get('sector'))
        codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(cols).values)
        codes = np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)
        rz_d = _group_demean(rz, codes, self._MIN_PEERS)
        rz_d = rz_d.where(np.isfinite(rz_d)).fillna(0.0)
        xf = x_flow.where(np.isfinite(x_flow)).fillna(0.0)
        c_imp = rolling_beta(rz_d.abs(), xf, self._IMP_WIN)
        c_imp = c_imp.where(np.isfinite(c_imp)).clip(0.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
        expected = (c_imp * xf).clip(lower=0.0)
        excess = (np.sign(rz_d) * (rz_d.abs() - expected)).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        excess = excess.where(np.isfinite(excess)).fillna(0.0)
        n = self._SPLIT_WIN
        pw = p_paid.where(np.isfinite(p_paid)).fillna(0.0)
        qw = q_quiet.where(np.isfinite(q_quiet)).fillna(0.0)
        p_cnt = ts_sum(pw, n)
        q_cnt = ts_sum(qw, n)
        paid_leg = ts_sum(excess * pw, n) / np.sqrt(p_cnt.clip(lower=0.25))
        quiet_leg = ts_sum(rz_d * qw, n) / np.sqrt(q_cnt.clip(lower=0.25))
        valid = (p_cnt >= 1.0) & (q_cnt >= 3.0) & sigma.notna() & mu_v.notna()
        paid_leg = paid_leg.where(valid)
        quiet_leg = quiet_leg.where(valid)
        z_paid = _cs_robust_z(paid_leg)
        z_quiet = _cs_robust_z(quiet_leg)
        tan = np.tanh(z_lam.astype(float))
        w_paid = (0.5 + tan).clip(-0.5, 1.5)
        w_quiet = (1.0 - 0.5 * tan).clip(0.5, 1.5)
        w_paid = w_paid.where(np.isfinite(w_paid)).fillna(1.0)
        w_quiet = w_quiet.where(np.isfinite(w_quiet)).fillna(1.0)
        score = z_quiet.mul(w_quiet, axis=0) - z_paid.mul(w_paid, axis=0)
        score = score.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        score = score.sub(score.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        out = score.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Aggregate impact-elasticity gated excess-paid vs unpaid drift split
programs.trading_idea: The parent proved that routing a market-wide state onto the traded leg of a hedged excursion adds combination value, but its state variable (share of cross-sectional variance carried by the equal-weighted market factor) is only a proxy for the thing that actually decides whether temporary impact gets repaid: the price the market is currently charging for risk transfer. The child measures that price directly as an aggregate Kyle elasticity — the trailing regression slope of |market-factor return| on cross-sectional mean relative participation — so a HIGH slope means each unit of aggregate flow is moving prices a lot (thin risk-bearing capacity, single-name traded excursions are inventory imbalance that is repaid within seconds), while a collapse in the slope means flow is being absorbed and volume-driven moves are informational and continue. Second, the child fixes what the parent's traded leg actually contains: instead of summing all active-bar residual drift (which mixes permanent, flow-justified repricing with over-payment), it subtracts each bar's own square-root-law expected impact, estimated per name as a trailing slope of |residual return| on sqrt(volume/typical volume), so the faded object is the EXCESS displacement beyond what the flow paid for — the mechanically transient part. The edge survives arbitrage because it requires jointly estimating a per-name impact elasticity and an aggregate liquidity-price state at 10-second resolution, and because the traded leg's sign flips with the regime, so anyone trading the unconditional version earns roughly nothing and does not compete the conditional version away.
programs.description: Beta-hedged, sector-demeaned, vol-normalised 30-bar residual drift is split into an unpaid leg (weighted by mu_v/(v+mu_v), i.e. quiet quote repricing) and a paid leg carrying only displacement in EXCESS of each name's trailing sqrt-law expected impact; the two cross-sectionally robust-z legs are combined with weights driven by the trailing z-score of an aggregate impact elasticity (rolling slope of |market return| on mean relative participation), which fades the excess-paid leg hard when risk transfer is expensive and flips it to continuation when the market absorbs flow.

programs.code:
"""Peer-confirmed quiet repricing vs basket-attributed traded impact.

Mechanism
---------
Two orthogonal partitions of a name's recent (30-bar) drift are combined:

1.  QUIET vs ACTIVE bars (volume at or below the name's own trailing 25th
    percentile).  Quiet-bar drift is market-maker quote repricing that nobody
    has traded against yet; active-bar drift already contains paid, decaying
    impact.
2.  BASKET vs IDIOSYNCRATIC flow.  The name's normalised signed sqrt-volume is
    regressed (trailing OLS) on the contemporaneous within-sector, ex-self peer
    signed flow: f = beta * f_peer + e.  beta * f_peer is index/basket-style
    demand (uninformed about a single name -> transitory pressure); e is
    single-name liquidity demand (plausibly informed -> permanent).

The quiet-bar drift is FOLLOWED, but only in proportion to how much the ex-self
industry peer basket is quietly repricing in the same direction: shared untraded
repricing is information; a lone mid drifting with no volume and no peer move is
stale-quote flicker.  The active-bar drift is attributed with a trailing
Kyle-lambda into a basket-flow displacement (faded), an idiosyncratic-flow
displacement (followed) and an unexplained remainder (faded).  Fade legs are
scaled by leave-one-out peer activity (hedge legs must be tradable) and
amplified when the transitory push moved the name further from its
industry-demeaned log book-multiple anchor.

Causality: every cross-sectional operation acts inside a single timestamp; every
time-series operation is a trailing rolling window or a positive lag.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import warnings
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rolling_beta, stddev, ts_mean, ts_rank, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _static_labels(columns: pd.Index, sources: list) -> pd.Series:
    """Static per-ticker group key; later sources override earlier ones."""
    labels = pd.Series('ALL', index=columns, dtype=object)
    for src in sources:
        if src is None:
            continue
        for col in columns:
            if col not in src.columns:
                continue
            ser = src[col].dropna()
            if len(ser) == 0:
                continue
            val = ser.iloc[-1]
            if isinstance(val, str):
                txt = val.strip()
                if txt:
                    labels[col] = txt
            elif val is not None and (not (isinstance(val, float) and np.isnan(val))):
                labels[col] = str(val)
    return labels

def _codes(labels: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> np.ndarray:
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(labels.reindex(columns).values)
    return np.asarray(codes, dtype=np.int64)

def _group_center(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_members: int, use_median: bool) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-group centering; groups smaller than min_members fall back
    to the whole row."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter('ignore')
        allsub = np.where(finite, arr, np.nan)
        mu_all = np.nanmedian(allsub, axis=1) if use_median else np.nanmean(allsub, axis=1)
        for k in np.unique(codes):
            m = codes == k
            if int(m.sum()) < int(min_members):
                out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu_all[:, None]
                continue
            sub = np.where(finite[:, m], arr[:, m], np.nan)
            mu = np.nanmedian(sub, axis=1) if use_median else np.nanmean(sub, axis=1)
            out[:, m] = arr[:, m] - mu[:, None]
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)

def _peer_ex_self_mean(x: pd.DataFrame, codes: np.ndarray, min_members: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-bar within-group mean EXCLUDING the own column (leave-one-out)."""
    arr = x.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    finite = np.isfinite(arr)
    vals = np.where(finite, arr, 0.0)
    out = np.full(arr.shape, np.nan)
    row_sum = vals.sum(axis=1)[:, None]
    row_cnt = finite.sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float)
    for k in np.unique(codes):
        m = codes == k
        if int(m.sum()) < int(min_members):
            s = row_sum - vals[:, m]
            c = row_cnt - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        else:
            s = vals[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None] - vals[:, m]
            c = finite[:, m].sum(axis=1)[:, None].astype(float) - finite[:, m].astype(float)
        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):
            res = np.where(c > 0.0, s / np.where(c > 0.0, c, 1.0), np.nan)
        out[:, m] = res
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=x.index, columns=x.columns)

def _cs_robust_z(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row robust standardisation (median / MAD, std fallback), winsorised."""
    med = df.median(axis=1)
    dev = df.sub(med, axis=0)
    mad = dev.abs().median(axis=1) * 1.4826
    sd = df.std(axis=1)
    scale = mad.where(mad > 0.0, sd)
    scale = scale.where(scale > 0.0, np.nan)
    return dev.div(scale, axis=0).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

def _rolling_quantile(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, q: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing q-quantile over the last n bars (windows end at the current bar)."""
    mp = max(int(n * 0.5), 10)
    return df.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).quantile(q)

@register_factor
class PeerConfirmedQuietVsBasketAttributedTradedSplit(BaseFactor):
    """Follow peer-confirmed quiet repricing and idio-flow impact; fade basket push."""
    factor_id = 'peer_confirmed_quiet_vs_basket_attributed_traded'
    name = 'Peer-confirmed quiet repricing vs basket-attributed traded impact'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Splits 30 bars of volatility-normalised returns into quiet-bar and active-bar drift, scales the quiet leg by ex-self industry peer quiet-drift concordance, attributes the active leg into basket-flow and idiosyncratic-flow Kyle displacements plus an unexplained remainder, and scores +quiet +idio -(basket + remainder) with the fade gated by peer activity and by industry-demeaned book-multiple overextension.'
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ['close', 'open', 'volume', 'sector', 'industry', 'bookValuePerShare']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _SPLIT = 30
    _VOLWIN = 150
    _Q = 0.25
    _SIGWIN = 120
    _BETA = 180
    _NORM = 180
    _ANCH = 360
    _ACT = 300
    _MIN_PEERS = 3
    _MIN_SEC = 4

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        n = self._SPLIT
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lp = np.log(px)
        ret = (lp - lp.shift(1)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        sigma = stddev(ret.fillna(0.0), self._SIGWIN).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        r = (ret / sigma).clip(-8.0, 8.0).fillna(0.0)
        labels_ind = _static_labels(cols, [data.get('sector'), data.get('industry')])
        codes_ind = _codes(labels_ind, cols)
        labels_sec = _static_labels(cols, [data.get('sector')])
        codes_sec = _codes(labels_sec, cols)
        raw_vol = data.get('volume')
        if raw_vol is None:
            vol = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            vol = raw_vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            vol = vol.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        thr = _rolling_quantile(vol, self._VOLWIN, self._Q).fillna(0.0)
        quiet = vol <= thr
        active = ~quiet
        q_cnt = ts_sum(quiet.astype(float), n)
        a_cnt = ts_sum(active.astype(float), n)
        q_den = np.sqrt(q_cnt.clip(lower=1.0))
        a_den = np.sqrt(a_cnt.clip(lower=1.0))
        quiet_drift = ts_sum(r.where(quiet, 0.0), n) / q_den
        active_drift = ts_sum(r.where(active, 0.0), n) / a_den
        op = data.get('open')
        if op is not None:
            o = op.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            o = o.where(np.isfinite(o) & (o > 0.0))
            dmid = lp - np.log(o)
        else:
            dmid = ret
        sgn = np.sign(dmid.fillna(0.0))
        sgn = sgn.where(sgn != 0.0, np.sign(ret.fillna(0.0)))
        rv = np.sqrt(vol)
        f = (sgn * rv / ts_mean(rv, self._NORM).replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        f = f.where(np.isfinite(f)).fillna(0.0)
        f_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(f, codes_sec, self._MIN_SEC)
        f_peer = f_peer.where(np.isfinite(f_peer)).fillna(0.0)
        b = rolling_beta(f, f_peer, self._BETA)
        b = b.where(np.isfinite(b)).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
        f_com = b * f_peer
        f_idio = f - f_com
        lam = rolling_beta(r, f, self._BETA)
        lam = lam.where(np.isfinite(lam)).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)
        imp_com = lam * ts_sum(f_com.where(active, 0.0), n) / a_den
        imp_idio = lam * ts_sum(f_idio.where(active, 0.0), n) / a_den
        imp_com = imp_com.where(np.isfinite(imp_com))
        imp_idio = imp_idio.where(np.isfinite(imp_idio))
        resid = active_drift - imp_com.fillna(0.0) - imp_idio.fillna(0.0)
        valid = (q_cnt >= 3.0) & (a_cnt >= 3.0) & sigma.notna()
        z_q = _cs_robust_z(quiet_drift.where(valid))
        z_com = _cs_robust_z(imp_com.where(valid))
        z_idio = _cs_robust_z(imp_idio.where(valid))
        z_res = _cs_robust_z(resid.where(valid))
        zq_peer = _peer_ex_self_mean(z_q, codes_ind, self._MIN_PEERS)
        zq_peer = zq_peer.where(np.isfinite(zq_peer)).fillna(0.0)
        conc = np.tanh(2.0 * zq_peer) * np.sign(z_q.fillna(0.0))
        mq = (1.0 + 0.6 * conc).clip(0.4, 1.6)
        if raw_vol is None:
            gate = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            live = ts_sum(vol, self._ACT) > 0.0
            own_act = (ts_rank(ts_sum(vol, 6), self._ACT) - 0.5).where(live)
            own_act = own_act.where(np.isfinite(own_act))
            peer_act = _peer_ex_self_mean(own_act, codes_ind, self._MIN_PEERS)
            peer_act = peer_act.where(np.isfinite(peer_act)).fillna(0.0)
            gate = (1.0 + peer_act).clip(0.3, 1.7)
        anchor = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        bv = data.get('bookValuePerShare')
        if bv is not None:
            per = bv.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            per = per.where(np.isfinite(per) & (per > 0.0))
            ratio = px / per
            ratio = ratio.where(np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio > 0.0))
            if ratio.notna().to_numpy().sum() > 0:
                lm = np.log(ratio)
                spread = _group_center(lm, codes_ind, self._MIN_PEERS, True)
                az = ts_zscore(spread.where(np.isfinite(spread)), self._ANCH).clip(-4.0, 4.0)
                anchor = np.tanh(az.where(np.isfinite(az)).fillna(0.0))
        trans = z_com.fillna(0.0) + z_res.fillna(0.0)
        amp = (1.0 + 0.5 * np.sign(trans) * anchor).clip(0.5, 1.5)
        raw_score = 1.0 * mq * z_q.fillna(0.0) + 0.3 * z_idio.fillna(0.0) - 0.7 * gate * amp * trans
        raw_score = raw_score.where(valid & z_q.notna() & np.isfinite(raw_score))
        out = _cs_robust_z(raw_score)
        out = out.sub(out.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Peer-confirmed quiet repricing vs basket-attributed traded impact
programs.trading_idea: Parent B splits recent drift into quiet-bar (untraded quote repricing, persists) and traded-bar (paid impact, decays) components but treats every name in isolation; Parent A shows that at 10-second resolution the *source* of a push — sector-basket flow versus single-name idiosyncratic flow — determines its permanence, and that fades only pay when the peer hedge legs are live. The child crosses those two axes: the quiet-bar drift is followed only to the extent the ex-self industry peer basket is quietly repricing the same way (shared untraded information = genuine repricing; a lone name's mid drifting with no volume and no peer move is stale-quote flicker), while the traded-bar drift is decomposed via trailing OLS of the name's signed sqrt-volume on ex-self peer flow into a basket-flow-implied Kyle displacement (faded hardest, scaled by peer activity so the hedge is executable and amplified when the push stretched the name further from its industry-demeaned book-multiple anchor) and an idiosyncratic-flow-implied displacement (followed, because informed single-name demand continues). The interaction is the edge: Parent B fades all traded drift including informed idiosyncratic prints and follows all quiet drift including pure stale-mid noise, whereas Parent A has no untraded/traded partition at all — attributing each partition separately tells you which sixty-second displacements are wrong *and* repairable inside the six-bar horizon.
programs.description: Splits the last 30 bars of volatility-normalised log returns into quiet-bar and active-bar drift, scales the quiet leg by ex-self industry peer quiet-drift concordance, decomposes the active leg into basket-flow and idiosyncratic-flow Kyle displacements plus an unexplained residual, and scores +peer-confirmed quiet drift +idiosyncratic-flow impact −(basket impact + unexplained active drift) with the fade gated by peer activity and by industry-demeaned book-multiple overextension.

programs.code:
"""Valuation-ambiguity-gated permanence of intraday price impact.

Mechanism
---------
A bar-level push in the mid is a mixture of (i) permanent, information-driven
relocation and (ii) transient, inventory-driven impact that market makers repay.
The book already contains many estimators of *how much* of a push is repaid and
on which clock.  This factor conditions on *which names* repay: the permanent
share of impact should rise with fundamental valuation ambiguity, because
ambiguity is exactly where information asymmetry (and hence informed aggressive
flow) concentrates - high intangibles / R&D / SBC intensity, rich price-to-book,
no dividend or earnings anchor, poor cash-to-accrual earnings quality.  Where
value is hard-anchored by cash flows and tangible book, aggressive flow is
dominantly liquidity motivated and the push reverts.

Expressed as a forecast, E[r_{t->t+6}] ~= -(k_bar - c*o_t) * P_t where P_t is the
outstanding push stock and o_t is the ambiguity score; the *new* information
relative to unconditional reversal factors is the interaction c * (o_t - mean o)
* P_t, which is what this factor computes.  To keep the claim about ambiguity
rather than liquidity, the ambiguity score is cross-sectionally orthogonalised
against trailing-volatility and dollar-volume ranks before it multiplies the
push.

All time-series statistics are causal (trailing windows, positive lags only);
the fundamental fields are point-in-time quarterly step functions and are used
only through cross-sectional ranks with defensive NaN handling.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _row_center(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract the per-bar cross-sectional mean (NaN-skipping)."""
    return df.sub(df.mean(axis=1), axis=0)


def _proj_resid(y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Row-wise (cross-sectional) residual of y after projecting on x."""
    num = (y * x).sum(axis=1)
    den = (x * x).sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    return y - x.mul(beta, axis=0)


def _static_labels(lab_df, cols) -> pd.Series | None:
    """Collapse a static text field into one label per ticker (causal ffill)."""
    if lab_df is None:
        return None
    try:
        lab = lab_df.reindex(columns=cols).ffill()
        if len(lab.index) == 0:
            return None
        s = lab.iloc[-1]
    except Exception:
        return None
    vals = ["_NA_" if (v is None or (isinstance(v, float) and not np.isfinite(v))) else str(v)
            for v in list(s.values)]
    return pd.Series(vals, index=cols)


def _group_demean(df: pd.DataFrame, labels) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Remove the per-bar group (sector) mean; tiny groups are pooled."""
    if labels is None:
        return _row_center(df)
    lab = labels.reindex(df.columns)
    lab = lab.where(lab.notna(), "_NA_").astype(str)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    lab = lab.where(lab.map(counts) >= 4, "_POOL_")
    try:
        means = df.T.groupby(lab.values).transform("mean").T
    except Exception:
        return _row_center(df)
    return df - means


@register_factor
class ValuationAmbiguityGatedImpactPermanenceH6(BaseFactor):
    """Push stock x centred, liquidity-purged valuation-ambiguity score."""

    factor_id = "valuation_ambiguity_gated_impact_permanence_h6"
    name = "Valuation-ambiguity gated impact permanence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Volume-backed, sector-idiosyncratic, volatility-scaled 6-bar push stock "
        "interacted with a cross-sectionally centred valuation-ambiguity score "
        "(intangibles, R&D, SBC, price/book vs earnings/dividend yield and earnings "
        "quality) that is first orthogonalised against trailing volatility and "
        "dollar-volume ranks: pushes persist in ambiguous names, revert in anchored ones."
    )
    window_length = 260
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "sector",
        "intangiblesToAssets",
        "rdToRevenue",
        "sbcToRevenue",
        "pbRatio",
        "earningsYield",
        "dividendYield",
        "incomeQuality",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _SDWIN = 240      # trailing window for return-volatility scaling
    _MINP = 40
    _VWIN = 240       # trailing window for volume percentile / dollar volume
    _K = 5            # push lags retained beyond the current bar (~1 min total)
    _THETA = 0.8      # calendar decay of the outstanding push stock
    _M0 = 0.6         # partial weight on the current bar (mid flicker purge)
    _ZCAP = 6.0
    _MINCOMP = 3      # minimum available ambiguity components

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        if px.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        lc = np.log(px)
        ret = lc - lc.shift(1)

        sd = ret.rolling(self._SDWIN, min_periods=self._MINP).std()
        sd_safe = sd.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = (ret / sd_safe).clip(-self._ZCAP, self._ZCAP)

        # ---- idiosyncratic push increments (sector-common move removed) -------
        labels = _static_labels(data.get("sector"), cols)
        pz = _group_demean(z, labels)

        # ---- trade backing -----------------------------------------------------
        vol = data.get("volume")
        if vol is None:
            g = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
            dvr = None
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0))
            vr = ts_rank(v, self._VWIN)
            vr = vr.where(vr.notna(), 0.5)
            g = 0.2 + 1.6 * vr
            dv = ts_mean((px * v), self._VWIN)
            dvr = rank(dv) if dv.notna().to_numpy().sum() > 0 else None

        w = (pz * g).fillna(0.0)
        push = self._M0 * w
        for m in range(1, self._K + 1):
            push = push + (self._THETA ** m) * w.shift(m).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- valuation-ambiguity score (point-in-time fundamentals) -----------
        specs = [
            ("intangiblesToAssets", 1.0),
            ("rdToRevenue", 1.0),
            ("sbcToRevenue", 1.0),
            ("pbRatio", 1.0),
            ("earningsYield", -1.0),
            ("dividendYield", -1.0),
            ("incomeQuality", -1.0),
        ]
        num = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for field, sgn in specs:
            f = data.get(field)
            if f is None:
                continue
            f = f.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            f = f.where(np.isfinite(f))
            if f.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
                continue
            r = rank(f) - 0.5
            num = num + (sgn * r).fillna(0.0)
            cnt = cnt + r.notna().astype(float)

        if cnt.to_numpy().max() < self._MINCOMP:
            return zero
        amb = (num / cnt.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(cnt >= float(self._MINCOMP))

        # ---- purge the liquidity / volatility channel from the score ----------
        maskO = amb.notna()
        oc = _row_center(amb.where(maskO)).fillna(0.0)
        x1 = _row_center(rank(sd).where(maskO)).fillna(0.0)
        if dvr is not None:
            x2 = _row_center(dvr.where(maskO)).fillna(0.0)
            x2 = _proj_resid(x2, x1)
        else:
            x2 = None
        ores = _proj_resid(oc, x1)
        if x2 is not None:
            ores = _proj_resid(ores, x2)

        o = 2.0 * (rank(ores.where(maskO)) - 0.5)
        o = o.where(maskO)

        # ---- interaction: only the ambiguity-conditional part of the push -----
        valid = maskO & sd_safe.notna() & pz.notna()
        sig = (push * o).where(valid)
        sig = sig.where(np.isfinite(sig))

        out = rank(sig) - 0.5
        out = out.where(sig.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Valuation-ambiguity gated impact permanence
programs.trading_idea: The parent measured *how much* of a trade-backed push gets repaid, a channel the book already spans; the child instead asks *which names repay at all*. The permanent-vs-transient split of price impact is governed by the information content of the aggressive flow (Kyle/Glosten adverse selection): where fundamental value has no hard anchor — high intangibles and R&D intensity, rich price/book, no dividend or earnings yield, weak cash-to-accrual earnings quality — a larger share of volume-backed order flow is information-motivated, so the push is permanent and continues; where value is well anchored by cash flows and tangible book, aggressive flow is dominantly liquidity/rebalancing driven, market makers lean against it, and the push is transient and reverts. The child therefore trades the *interaction only*: a volume-backed, sector-idiosyncratic, volatility-scaled push stock multiplied by a cross-sectionally centred ambiguity score that has first been orthogonalised against trailing volatility and dollar-volume ranks, so the signal carries essentially zero loading on unconditional reversal or on the liquidity channel the existing book already prices. It survives arbitrage because harvesting it means bearing inventory risk against possibly-informed flow on one leg while accumulating with it on the other, at sub-minute horizons, conditioned on a slow fundamental characteristic that quarterly value/quality investors never express intraday; it is falsified if reversal strength is homogeneous across the cross-section, or if the opposite (retail-noise-trader) channel dominates, in which case the realized IC is zero or negative.
programs.description: Cross-sectional rank of (volatility-scaled, sector-demeaned, volume-weighted 6-bar push stock) x (centred valuation-ambiguity score built from ranks of intangiblesToAssets, rdToRevenue, sbcToRevenue, pbRatio, -earningsYield, -dividendYield, -incomeQuality, residualised against trailing-volatility and dollar-volume ranks): long recent pushes in ambiguous names, short recent pushes in well-anchored names.

programs.code:
"""State-binned local-projection response surface, horizon-matched to 6 bars.

Mechanism
---------
A short-run price push does not have one universal sequel.  Conditioned on the
microstructural circumstances of the push, its 6-bar continuation flips sign:

  * small push, light volume, zig-zag (low path-efficiency) path
        -> quote / inventory noise, repaid inside the next few bars (reversal);
  * large push, heavy volume, monotone path
        -> a slice of a metaorder still being worked (continuation).

A single linear distributed-lag kernel averages these opposite responses and
collapses toward zero; that is why a linear repayment kernel shows tiny IC at
the target offset and pushes its mass to longer horizons.  Here we instead
estimate, per name and strictly causally, the nonparametric conditional
expectation

        f(state) = E[ r_{t -> t+6} * sign(push_t) | state_t ]

using only *realised* pairs (state at s, return from s to s+6) with s <= t-6.
The state is a 12-cell bin of

        magnitude bin (|push z| >= 0.8)  x  volume-surprise bin (3 levels)
                                         x  path-efficiency bin (2 levels)

The response is sign-folded on the push direction (odd-symmetry assumption:
the sequel of an up-push mirrors that of a down-push), which doubles the
effective sample per cell, and each cell is empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the
pooled cross-sectional cell mean so thin cells fall back on the panel.

The forecast at t is the current cell's shrunk response re-signed by the
current push direction.  Because the response is measured at exactly the
6-bar offset, the estimator is horizon-matched by construction.

Everything is trailing: positive lags and trailing rolling windows only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _xs_demean_median(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Strip the per-bar cross-sectional median (the common market leg)."""
    return df.sub(df.median(axis=1), axis=0)

def _broadcast_row(ser: pd.Series, cols: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(ser.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], len(cols), axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=ser.index, columns=cols)

@register_factor
class StateBinnedLocalProjectionResponseH6(BaseFactor):
    """Causal nonparametric 6-bar response surface over push / volume / path state."""
    factor_id = 'state_binned_local_projection_response_surface_h'
    name = 'State-binned local-projection response surface (h=6)'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Per-name trailing conditional expectation of the sign-folded, vol-normalised realised 6-bar return given a 12-cell state bin (3-bar idiosyncratic push magnitude x 3-bar volume percentile x path efficiency), empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the pooled cell mean, re-signed by the current push and ranked cross-sectionally.'
    window_length = 1420
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _P = 3
    _H = 6
    _N = 1170
    _MINP = 400
    _VW = 240
    _K = 50.0
    _NB = 12

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        zero = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        px = close.where(np.isfinite(close) & (close > 0.0))
        lc = np.log(px)
        if lc.notna().to_numpy().sum() == 0:
            return zero
        r1 = lc - lc.shift(1)
        disp = lc - lc.shift(self._P)
        x = _xs_demean_median(disp)
        sx = x.rolling(self._N, min_periods=self._MINP).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        xz = (x / sx).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        mbin = (xz.abs() >= 0.8).astype(float)
        vol = data.get('volume')
        if vol is None:
            vbin = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            v = vol.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).astype(float)
            v = v.where(np.isfinite(v) & (v >= 0.0)).fillna(0.0)
            v3 = v.rolling(self._P, min_periods=1).sum()
            vr = ts_rank(v3, self._VW)
            va = vr.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            vb = np.where(va >= 0.75, 2.0, np.where(va >= 0.4, 1.0, 0.0))
            vbin = pd.DataFrame(vb, index=idx, columns=cols)
            vbin = vbin.where(vr.notna(), 1.0)
        path = r1.abs().rolling(self._P, min_periods=self._P).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eff = disp.abs() / path
        er = ts_rank(eff, self._VW)
        ebin = (er >= 0.5).astype(float)
        valid = xz.notna() & sx.notna() & er.notna()
        state = (mbin * 6.0 + vbin * 2.0 + ebin).where(valid)
        y = _xs_demean_median(lc - lc.shift(self._H))
        sy = y.rolling(self._N, min_periods=self._MINP).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        yn = (y / sy).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        sgn = np.sign(xz)
        s_lag = sgn.shift(self._H)
        b_lag = state.shift(self._H)
        yf = yn * s_lag
        usable = yf.notna() & (s_lag.abs() > 0.0) & b_lag.notna()
        table: dict[int, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        for bb in range(self._NB):
            m = usable & (b_lag == float(bb))
            mf = m.astype(float)
            cnt = mf.rolling(self._N, min_periods=self._MINP).sum()
            num = yf.where(m, 0.0).rolling(self._N, min_periods=self._MINP).sum()
            tot_n = num.sum(axis=1)
            tot_c = cnt.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            pooled = (tot_n / tot_c).fillna(0.0)
            pooled_df = _broadcast_row(pooled, cols)
            table[bb] = (num + self._K * pooled_df) / (cnt + self._K)
        fc = None
        for bb in range(self._NB):
            sel = state == float(bb)
            term = table[bb].where(sel, 0.0)
            fc = term if fc is None else fc + term
        if fc is None:
            return zero
        forecast = fc.where(state.notna()) * sgn
        forecast = forecast.where(np.isfinite(forecast))
        out = rank(forecast) - 0.5
        out = out.where(forecast.notna(), 0.0)
        out = out.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
        return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0.0).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: State-binned local-projection response surface (h=6)
programs.trading_idea: The map from a short-run price push to what happens over the next minute is not linear but sign-flipping: small pushes that arrive on light volume and on a zig-zag path are quote/inventory noise and get repaid, whereas equally-sized pushes that arrive on heavy, monotone volume are slices of a metaorder and keep going — a single linear distributed-lag kernel (the parent) averages these opposite responses toward zero and leaks its mass to longer horizons. This child therefore estimates, per name and causally, the *conditional expectation of the realised 6-bar-ahead move given the current microstructural state*, where the state is a 12-cell bin of (push magnitude) x (volume surprise) x (path efficiency), with the response sign-folded on the push direction (odd-symmetry) and empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the pooled cross-sectional cell mean. Because the response is measured at exactly the 6-bar offset, the estimate is horizon-matched by construction rather than by summing a kernel whose tail lies beyond the window. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it means posting passive size against possibly-informed aggressive flow for a fraction of a spread, and the *location of the crossover* (how much volume a push needs before it persists) is a slowly-drifting, name-specific liquidity parameter that has to be re-estimated continuously rather than read off a public formula.
programs.description: Per-name causal nonparametric local projection: trailing average of the sign-folded, vol-normalised realised 6-bar return conditioned on a 12-cell state bin built from 3-bar idiosyncratic push magnitude, 3-bar volume percentile and path efficiency; the current cell's shrunk response, re-signed by the current push, is ranked cross-sectionally.

programs.code:
"""Orthogonalised distributed-lag market catch-up, weighted by the probability
that the owed adjustment is actually *delivered* inside the fixed 6-bar horizon.

Mechanism
---------
If a name's return follows a distributed lag in the market factor,

    r_t = sum_{l=0..L} b_l m_{t-l} + tail + e_t ,

then the expected cumulative return over the next H bars contains a part driven
by ALREADY OBSERVED market returns:

    E[ sum_{j=1..H} r_{t+j} | F_t ]  contains  sum_{l=1..L} b_l * S_l(t),
    S_l(t) = m_t + ... + m_{t-l+1}.

Two defects of the naive version are fixed here:

1. *Marginal vs joint loadings.*  At a 10-second sampling frequency the market
   return is itself autocorrelated (nonsynchronous trading), so univariate betas
   on each lag all load on the same shock and their sum overstates the owed
   catch-up -> the forecast overshoots and reverses beyond the horizon.  We
   therefore solve the JOINT normal equations.  The regressor block (lagged
   market returns) is identical for every name, so a single trailing Gram matrix
   per bar is pseudo-inverted and folded against per-name cross-moments.  The
   contemporaneous lag is included purely as a control, and a lags-5..12 block
   regressor measures response mass that lands OUTSIDE the 6-bar window.

2. *Delivery timing.*  A stale name owes catch-up but may not reprice at all
   inside six bars; the owed balance is only realised through repricing events.
   With u = trailing per-bar probability of a repricing event (non-frozen mid or
   non-zero traded volume), the probability of at least one event within H bars
   is 1 - (1-u)^H.  Multiplying by this parameter-free delivery probability
   deliberately REVERSES a staleness amplifier: extreme staleness pushes payment
   past the evaluation offset and must be down-weighted, not up-weighted.

All estimation is trailing-only (rolling moments, positive shifts).
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor
_EPS = 1e-12

def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal cap-weighted market return (weights = previous bar's market cap)."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w.to_numpy()))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret).sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    den = w.sum(axis=1, skipna=True).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)

def _batched_pinv(mom: np.ndarray, ridge: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Ridge-regularised pseudo-inverse of a (T, k, k) stack of Gram matrices.

    Rows with any non-finite entry are returned as NaN (insufficient trailing
    data).  Deterministic and free of exceptions.
    """
    T, k, _ = mom.shape
    out = np.full((T, k, k), np.nan)
    finite = np.isfinite(mom).all(axis=(1, 2))
    if not bool(finite.any()):
        return out
    A = mom[finite]
    tr = np.trace(A, axis1=1, axis2=2) / float(k)
    tr = np.where(np.isfinite(tr) & (tr > 0.0), tr, 1.0)
    A = A + ridge * tr[:, None, None] * np.eye(k)[None, :, :]
    out[finite] = np.linalg.pinv(A)
    return out

def _shrink_cs(b: pd.DataFrame, w: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Shrink a loading towards its cross-sectional mean (empirical-Bayes style)."""
    row = b.mean(axis=1)
    return b.mul(1.0 - w).add(row * w, axis=0)

@register_factor
class OrthogonalizedLagKernelDeliveryProbabilityH6(BaseFactor):
    """Joint distributed-lag catch-up folded onto 6 bars, weighted by delivery odds."""
    factor_id = 'orthogonalized_lag_kernel_delivery_probability_h'
    name = 'Orthogonalised Lag-Kernel Catch-Up x Delivery Probability'
    category = 'statistical_arbitrage'
    description = "Joint (multivariate) trailing loadings of each name's return on cap-weighted market returns at lags 0..4 plus a lags-5..12 block, obtained from a shared per-bar Gram pseudo-inverse; lags 1..4 are folded against observed trailing market sums to form the horizon-matched 6-bar catch-up, volatility-normalised and multiplied by an out-of-window leakage trust ratio and the probability of at least one repricing event within 6 bars."
    window_length = 300
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'marketCap']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    _n_lags = 4
    _tail_len = 8
    _beta_window = 240
    _beta_min = 80
    _vol_window = 240
    _vol_min = 60
    _act_window = 120
    _act_min = 40
    _shrink = 0.4
    _ridge = 0.001

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = (close.index, close.columns)
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        mcap = data.get('marketCap')
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(ret, mcap)
        H = int(self.prediction_horizon)
        L = int(self._n_lags)
        n = int(self._beta_window)
        mp = int(self._beta_min)
        regs = [mkt.shift(l) for l in range(0, L + 1)]
        tail = mkt.shift(L + 1).rolling(int(self._tail_len), min_periods=int(self._tail_len)).sum()
        regs.append(tail)
        k = len(regs)
        means = [r.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean() for r in regs]
        T = len(idx)
        G = np.full((T, k, k), np.nan)
        for a in range(k):
            for b in range(a, k):
                mab = (regs[a] * regs[b]).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean() - means[a] * means[b]
                v = mab.to_numpy(dtype=float)
                G[:, a, b] = v
                G[:, b, a] = v
        Ginv = _batched_pinv(G, float(self._ridge))
        ybar = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
        cross = []
        for a in range(k):
            cm = ret.mul(regs[a], axis=0).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean() - ybar.mul(means[a], axis=0)
            cross.append(cm.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan))
        betas: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for l in range(k):
            acc = None
            for m in range(k):
                wser = pd.Series(Ginv[:, l, m], index=idx)
                term = cross[m].mul(wser, axis=0)
                acc = term if acc is None else acc.add(term)
            bl = acc.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
            betas.append(_shrink_cs(bl, float(self._shrink)))
        pred = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        valid = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for lag in range(1, L + 1):
            span = min(H, lag)
            s_l = mkt.rolling(span, min_periods=span).sum()
            contrib = betas[lag].mul(s_l, axis=0)
            pred = pred.add(contrib.fillna(0.0))
            valid = valid.add(betas[lag].notna().astype(float))
        pred = pred.where(valid >= float(L - 1))
        within = None
        for lag in range(1, L + 1):
            a = betas[lag].abs()
            within = a if within is None else within.add(a)
        beyond = betas[k - 1].abs().mul(float(self._tail_len))
        trust = (within / (within + beyond + _EPS)).clip(0.15, 1.0).fillna(0.5)
        bar_vol = ret.rolling(int(self._vol_window), min_periods=int(self._vol_min)).std()
        scale = (bar_vol * float(np.sqrt(float(H)))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        pred_z = (pred / scale).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        alive = ret.notna().rolling(H, min_periods=1).sum() > 0
        pred_z = pred_z.where(alive)
        moved = ((ret.abs() > 1e-12) & ret.notna()).astype(float)
        u_mid = moved.rolling(int(self._act_window), min_periods=int(self._act_min)).mean()
        vol_tr = data.get('volume')
        if vol_tr is None:
            u_trd = u_mid
        else:
            vol_tr = vol_tr.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            traded = (vol_tr.fillna(0.0) > 0.0).astype(float)
            u_trd = traded.rolling(int(self._act_window), min_periods=int(self._act_min)).mean()
        u = (0.5 * u_mid.fillna(u_trd) + 0.5 * u_trd.fillna(u_mid)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        u = u.fillna(u.median(axis=1).median() if np.isfinite(u.to_numpy()).any() else 0.5)
        deliver = 1.0 - np.power(1.0 - u, float(H))
        deliver = deliver.clip(0.02, 1.0)
        mkt_move = mkt.rolling(H, min_periods=H).sum()
        mkt_vol = mkt.rolling(int(self._vol_window), min_periods=int(self._vol_min)).std()
        impulse = mkt_move.abs() / (mkt_vol * float(np.sqrt(float(H))) + _EPS)
        impulse = impulse.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 8.0)
        gate_impulse = pd.Series(special.expit(1.5 * (impulse.to_numpy() - 0.8)), index=idx)
        raw = pred_z * deliver * trust
        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        sig = sig.mul(gate_impulse, axis=0)
        return sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Orthogonalised Lag-Kernel Catch-Up × Within-Horizon Delivery Probability
programs.trading_idea: The parent forecast summed *marginal* (univariate) betas on lagged market returns; because 10-second market returns are themselves autocorrelated (nonsynchronous trading), those marginal loadings double-count the same shock, which inflates the owed catch-up and explains why its predictive mass leaked past 6 bars and turned negative (overshoot) at 12–24 bars. The child solves the *joint* distributed-lag normal equations — the design matrix of lagged market returns is common to all names, so one trailing 6×6 Gram matrix is inverted per bar and folded against per-name cross-moments — with the contemporaneous lag included as a control and a lags-5..12 block regressor whose loading measures response mass that lands *outside* the window. It then multiplies the owed balance by the probability that the name actually reprices inside the 6-bar window, 1-(1-u)^6 with u the name's own trailing per-bar repricing-event rate (non-frozen mid or non-zero traded volume): this deliberately inverts the parent's staleness amplification, whose sign was wrong at a fixed offset because the stalest names pay their debt after the evaluation window. The edge survives arbitrage because the object being predicted is mechanical delay in quote updating rather than mispricing: fast capital can only harvest it on names it can trade at the moment the update fires, and the joint-loading correction plus delivery weighting is what keeps the payoff inside the six bars.
programs.description: Trailing multivariate loadings of each name's return on cap-weighted market returns at lags 0..4 plus a lags-5..12 block (solved from a shared per-bar Gram inverse, cross-sectionally shrunk), with lags 1..4 folded against the already-observed trailing market sums to give the horizon-matched expected 6-bar catch-up; volatility-normalised, multiplied by an out-of-window-leakage trust ratio and by the within-6-bar repricing-delivery probability, and switched on by the size of the recent market impulse.

programs.code:
"""Void-cessation joint state gating of paid vs unpaid displacement.

Mechanism
---------
1. Impact decomposition (parent A).  Each bar's log return is split into a
   square-root-law *paid* part, sign(ret) * lambda * sqrt(volume), with lambda a
   per-name through-origin trailing regression slope of |ret| on sqrt(volume),
   and a flow-orthogonal *unpaid* residual (mid revision nobody paid for).
   Summed over the last 6 bars these give E (paid) and R (unpaid).

2. Occupation state (parent B).  A volume-weighted, exponentially-decayed
   Gaussian kernel density of the log prices visited over the last 60 bars is
   evaluated at the current price.  Two state variables come out of it: the
   normalised local mass at the current price (thick cluster vs void) and the
   signed position of the current price relative to the local occupation
   centroid in the direction the 6-bar move travelled (did the move end in
   virgin territory or back inside the profile?).

3. Joint state.  Transient impact decays only once the pressuring flow stops
   (Bouchaud propagator) AND only if there is resting inventory at the arrival
   price to push it back.  So the paid component is signed by the *average* of
   the flow-cessation clock and the void state: flow ceased + price in a
   vacuum => the residual displacement is the permanent component and continues;
   flow still running + price parked on a thick volume cluster => over-push that
   the resting mass absorbs and reverses.  The unpaid component is quote flicker
   against untouched resting size when occupancy is thick (fade it) and a real
   reprice when occupancy is thin (leave it alone).

All statistics use trailing windows and non-negative shifts only, so the value
at bar t depends on bars <= t.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_max, ts_mean, ts_rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _sqrt_law_lambda(absret: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing through-origin regression slope of |ret| on sqrt(volume)."""
    mp = max(20, int(n) // 4)
    num = (absret * w).rolling(int(n), min_periods=mp).sum()
    den = (w * w).rolling(int(n), min_periods=mp).sum().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return (num / den).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _cessation_clock(w: pd.DataFrame, k: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """1 = the recent volume burst has faded, 0 = flow is still running."""
    recent = ts_mean(w, 2)
    prior = ts_max(w.shift(2), max(2, int(k) - 2))
    denom = prior.where(prior > 0.0, np.nan)
    ratio = (recent / denom).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    cess = (1.0 - ratio).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    fallback = (recent <= 0.0).astype(float)
    return cess.where(denom.notna(), fallback)


def _occupation_moments(
    x: pd.DataFrame,
    w: pd.DataFrame,
    hband: pd.DataFrame,
    nlag: int,
    tau: float,
):
    """Trailing Gaussian-kernel moments of the volume-weighted occupation measure.

    Returns (num_k, den_k, den_a, cnt) with
        num_k = sum_k w_k K(u_k) u_k,  den_k = sum_k w_k K(u_k),
        den_a = sum_k w_k,             u_k = (x_t - x_{t-k}) / h.
    Only positive lags are used, so the value at t sees bars <= t.
    """
    idx, cols = x.index, x.columns
    num_k = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den_k = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    den_a = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
    cnt = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

    for k in range(1, int(nlag) + 1):
        decay = float(np.exp(-float(k) / float(tau)))
        d = x - x.shift(k)
        wk = w.shift(k) * decay
        u = (d / hband).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        kern = wk * np.exp(-0.5 * u * u)
        valid = d.notna() & wk.notna() & hband.notna()
        num_k = num_k.add((kern * u).where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        den_k = den_k.add(kern.where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        den_a = den_a.add(wk.where(valid).fillna(0.0))
        cnt = cnt.add(valid.astype(float))

    return num_k, den_k, den_a, cnt


@register_factor
class VoidCessationJointStatePaidUnpaidSplitH6(BaseFactor):
    """Paid / unpaid displacement split gated by cessation AND occupancy void."""

    factor_id = "void_cessation_joint_state_paid_unpaid_split_h6"
    name = "Void-cessation joint state paid/unpaid displacement split"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Splits trailing 6-bar log displacement into a square-root-law paid "
        "component and a flow-orthogonal unpaid residual, signs the paid part by "
        "the average of a flow-cessation clock and a liquidity-void state derived "
        "from a volume-weighted Gaussian occupation density, and fades the unpaid "
        "part in proportion to local occupancy thickness."
    )
    window_length = 320
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _lam_win = 240      # trailing window for the per-name sqrt-law slope
    _vol_win = 240      # trailing window for return volatility / ADV
    _vol_min = 60
    _nlag = 60          # occupation window (bars)
    _tau = 45.0         # occupation memory decay (bars)
    _min_obs = 30       # minimum valid lags before the density is trusted
    _state_win = 120    # per-name trailing window for the occupancy state rank
    _z_clip = 6.0
    _tanh_a = 0.7

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        volume = (
            data["volume"].astype(float)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .abs()
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        )

        px = close.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        x = np.log(px)
        ret = x.diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        sigma = ret.rolling(self._vol_win, min_periods=self._vol_min).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        h = int(self.prediction_horizon)

        # ---------- 1. square-root-law paid / unpaid decomposition --------
        vol_pos = volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        w_sqrt = np.sqrt(vol_pos)
        s = np.sign(ret).fillna(0.0)

        lam = _sqrt_law_lambda(ret.abs(), w_sqrt, self._lam_win)

        paid_bar = (s * lam * w_sqrt).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        unpaid_bar = (ret.fillna(0.0) - paid_bar.fillna(0.0))
        unpaid_bar = unpaid_bar.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        E = paid_bar.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()
        R = unpaid_bar.rolling(h, min_periods=h).sum()

        scale = (sigma * math.sqrt(float(h))).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        Ez = np.tanh(self._tanh_a * (E / scale).clip(-self._z_clip, self._z_clip))
        Rz = np.tanh(self._tanh_a * (R / scale).clip(-self._z_clip, self._z_clip))

        # ---------- 2. flow-cessation clock -------------------------------
        cess = _cessation_clock(w_sqrt, h)
        pi_flow = (2.0 * cess - 1.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---------- 3. volume-weighted occupation density state -----------
        advb = volume.rolling(self._vol_win, min_periods=self._vol_min).mean()
        advb = advb.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        rel = (volume / advb).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 10.0)
        w_occ = rel.fillna(1.0) * 0.75 + 0.25
        w_occ = w_occ.where(px.notna(), 0.25)

        px_sd = x.rolling(self._nlag, min_periods=self._min_obs).std()
        h_raw = 1.06 * px_sd * float(self._nlag) ** (-0.2)
        floor = sigma
        hband = h_raw.where(h_raw > floor, floor)
        hband = hband.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        hband = hband.where(hband > _EPS)

        num_k, den_k, den_a, cnt = _occupation_moments(
            x, w_occ, hband, self._nlag, self._tau
        )
        enough = cnt >= float(self._min_obs)

        local_mass = (den_k / den_a.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(enough)
        local_mass = local_mass.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # thickness state g in [0,1]: half cross-sectional, half own-history
        g_cs = rank(local_mass)
        g_ts = ts_rank(local_mass, self._state_win)
        g = (0.5 * g_cs.fillna(0.5) + 0.5 * g_ts.fillna(0.5)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # signed side of the occupation centroid relative to travel direction
        grad_ratio = (num_k / den_k.replace(0.0, np.nan)).where(enough)
        grad_ratio = grad_ratio.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-8.0, 8.0)
        D = (x - x.shift(h)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        offside = np.tanh(0.75 * np.sign(D).fillna(0.0) * grad_ratio.fillna(0.0))
        o01 = (0.5 * (1.0 + offside)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # void state V in [0,1]: 1 = thin local mass and price ended outside it
        V = (0.5 * (1.0 - g) + 0.5 * o01).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        kappa = (2.0 * V - 1.0)

        # ---------- 4. joint-state combination ----------------------------
        # paid part: continues only if flow ceased AND price sits in a vacuum
        paid_state = (0.5 * (pi_flow + kappa)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        paid_term = Ez * paid_state

        # unpaid part: quote flicker against resting mass -> fade with thickness
        unpaid_term = -(0.25 + 0.75 * g) * Rz

        raw = (paid_term + unpaid_term).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        valid = Ez.notna() & Rz.notna() & enough
        raw = raw.where(valid)

        sig = (rank(raw) - 0.5).where(raw.notna())
        return (
            sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Void–cessation joint state gating of paid vs unpaid displacement
programs.trading_idea: Parent A splits the last 6 bars of log displacement into a square-root-law *paid* part (sign(ret)·lambda·sqrt(volume)) and a *flow-orthogonal unpaid* part, and parent B measures where the price currently sits inside its own volume-at-price occupation density; both parents' realized ICs contradicted their priors in exactly the way a propagator + resting-inventory story predicts, and the child encodes that corrected physics as a joint state. Paid displacement is over-push while the metaorder is still running (revert) but becomes the permanent Kyle component once flow ceases — and permanence only survives if the price has travelled into a low-occupancy void where no resting limit-order mass remains to push it back; so the paid component's sign is the *average* of the cessation clock and the void state, which is strongly directional only when the two agree (flow stopped AND price sits in vacuum ⇒ continue; flow still running AND price parked on a thick volume cluster ⇒ snap back). Unpaid (quote-revision) displacement is genuine repricing only when it happens in a void; against an occupancy cluster it is flicker of the mid over untouched resting size and mean-reverts, so it is faded in proportion to the local occupancy mass. Neither parent has this edge alone: A's cessation clock cannot tell a permanent post-burst move from one that stopped in front of a wall of resting inventory, and B's density shape carries no information about whether the displacement that reached that point was paid for by volume.
programs.description: Decomposes trailing 6-bar log displacement into a square-root-law volume-paid component and a flow-orthogonal residual, then signs the paid component by the average of a flow-cessation clock and a liquidity-void state read off a volume-weighted Gaussian occupation density (local mass at the current price plus the side of the density centroid the move ended on), while fading the unpaid component in proportion to local occupancy thickness; cross-sectionally ranked.

programs.code:
"""Cornish-Fisher volume-profile gain overhang: fade inventory sitting in profit.

Mechanism
---------
Inventory accumulated over the last W bars was acquired at prices distributed
as the name's trailing volume-at-price profile.  The share of that inventory
currently in profit is the volume-weighted CDF of past transaction prices
evaluated at the current mid.  Instead of a brute-force count, that CDF is
approximated in closed form from the volume-weighted first three moments of
trailing log prices with a Cornish-Fisher (skew-corrected Gaussian) expansion:

    q = z - (g1/6)(z^2 - 1),        z = (u_t - mu_w)/sd_w ,
    share_in_profit ~ Phi(q) .

Holders in profit realise gains and supply liquidity into further advances, so
large positive overhang precedes stalling / partial retracement over the next
few bars; holders underwater are reluctant to sell, so negative overhang lets
moves continue.  Loss aversion makes the response asymmetric, which is encoded
explicitly (positive overhang weighted harder than negative).

Because overhang is mechanically correlated with the trailing price move, the
raw overhang is residualised on trailing 6-bar and W-bar return z-scores using
a trailing two-regressor OLS written out in rolling moments.  What survives is
driven by the *shape* of the volume distribution (its dispersion, skew, and
when volume actually traded), not by the move itself, so the factor is not a
re-parametrised short-term reversal.  All windows are trailing; the profile is
lagged one bar so the current bar's own volume never enters its own anchor.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_EPS = 1e-12


def _rsum(df: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing sum over bars t-n .. t-1 (strictly excludes the current bar)."""
    return df.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).sum().shift(1)


def _cf_overhang(u: pd.DataFrame, w: pd.DataFrame, n: int, mp: int):
    """Volume-weighted Cornish-Fisher share-in-profit of trailing inventory.

    Returns (signed_overhang in (-1,1), profile sd in log units, dislocation z).
    Uses volume-weighted moments of trailing log prices only (causal).
    """
    s0 = _rsum(w, n, mp)
    s1 = _rsum(w * u, n, mp)
    s2 = _rsum(w * u * u, n, mp)
    s3 = _rsum(w * u * u * u, n, mp)

    den = s0.where(s0 > 0.0)
    m1 = s1 / den
    m2 = s2 / den
    m3 = s3 / den

    var = (m2 - m1 * m1).clip(lower=0.0)
    sd = np.sqrt(var)
    sd = sd.where(sd > 1e-8)

    mu3 = m3 - 3.0 * m1 * m2 + 2.0 * m1.pow(3)
    g1 = (mu3 / sd.pow(3)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    z = ((u - m1) / sd).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
    q = z - (g1.fillna(0.0) / 6.0) * (z * z - 1.0)
    frac = pd.DataFrame(
        special.ndtr(q.to_numpy(dtype=float)), index=u.index, columns=u.columns
    )
    return (2.0 * frac - 1.0), sd, z


def _resid2(
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    x1: pd.DataFrame,
    x2: pd.DataFrame,
    n: int,
    mp: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current residual of a trailing two-regressor OLS y ~ 1 + x1 + x2.

    Written out in rolling moments (2x2 normal equations solved elementwise);
    every term is a trailing window statistic, so the value at t sees only <= t.
    """
    mask = y.notna() & x1.notna() & x2.notna()
    yy = y.where(mask)
    aa = x1.where(mask)
    bb = x2.where(mask)

    ey = yy.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    ea = aa.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    eb = bb.rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    eaa = (aa * aa).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    ebb = (bb * bb).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    eab = (aa * bb).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    eay = (aa * yy).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()
    eby = (bb * yy).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()

    saa = eaa - ea * ea
    sbb = ebb - eb * eb
    sab = eab - ea * eb
    say = eay - ea * ey
    sby = eby - eb * ey

    det = (saa * sbb - sab * sab).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    det = det.where(det.abs() > 1e-14)

    b1 = ((say * sbb - sby * sab) / det).clip(-3.0, 3.0)
    b2 = ((sby * saa - say * sab) / det).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

    demeaned = yy - ey
    resid = demeaned - b1.fillna(0.0) * (aa - ea) - b2.fillna(0.0) * (bb - eb)
    return resid.where(resid.notna(), demeaned).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class VolumeProfileGainOverhangFade(BaseFactor):
    """Fade names whose recent traded volume is mostly sitting on unrealized gains."""

    factor_id = 'volume_profile_gain_overhang_cf_fade'
    name = 'Cornish-Fisher volume-profile gain overhang fade'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = (
        'Skew-corrected (Cornish-Fisher) volume-weighted share of the last 120 '
        'bars of dollar volume transacted below the current mid, residualised on '
        'trailing 6-bar and 120-bar return z-scores, asymmetrically weighted for '
        'loss aversion, gated by volume-profile compactness and relative volume, '
        'and cross-sectionally ranked with a fading (negative) sign.'
    )
    window_length = 720
    inputs = ['close', 'volume']
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _profile_w = 120
    _profile_min = 60
    _reg_w = 480
    _reg_min = 150
    _asym = 1.6

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns

        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)
        u = np.log(px)

        vol = (
            data['volume']
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .clip(lower=0.0)
        )
        dvol = (vol * px).where(px.notna()).fillna(0.0)

        W = int(self._profile_w)
        mp = int(self._profile_min)

        ohang, prof_sd, _z = _cf_overhang(u, dvol, W, mp)

        # ---- validity: need real traded volume in the profile window ----
        nz = _rsum((dvol > 0.0).astype(float), W, mp)
        valid = (nz >= 0.15 * W) & prof_sd.notna() & px.notna()
        ohang = ohang.where(valid)

        # ---- strip the mechanical link to the trailing price move ----
        ret = px.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.2, 0.2)
        r_short = (px / px.shift(6) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        r_long = (px / px.shift(W) - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        x1 = ts_zscore(r_short, self._reg_w).clip(-5.0, 5.0)
        x2 = ts_zscore(r_long, self._reg_w).clip(-5.0, 5.0)

        resid = _resid2(ohang, x1, x2, self._reg_w, self._reg_min)
        sd_r = resid.rolling(self._reg_w, min_periods=self._reg_min).std()
        sd_r = sd_r.where(sd_r > 1e-8)
        zr = (resid / sd_r).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # ---- loss aversion: gains produce more supply than losses produce demand ----
        lam = float(self._asym)
        asym = zr.where(zr <= 0.0, zr * lam)

        # ---- conditioners: is there a well-defined inventory anchor? ----
        bar_vol = ret.rolling(240, min_periods=60).std()
        diffuse = (prof_sd / (bar_vol * float(np.sqrt(float(W))))).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )
        gate_anchor = rank(-diffuse).fillna(0.5)

        rvol = (
            ts_mean(vol, W) / ts_mean(vol, 6 * W).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gate_vol = rank(rvol).fillna(0.5)

        gate = 0.6 + 0.8 * (0.5 * gate_anchor + 0.5 * gate_vol)

        score = (-asym) * gate
        score = score.where(valid & asym.notna())

        sig = (rank(score) - 0.5).where(score.notna())
        return (
            sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
            .reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
            .fillna(0.0)
        )
programs.name: Cornish-Fisher volume-profile gain overhang fade
programs.trading_idea: Recent inventory in a name was acquired at prices distributed as its trailing volume-at-price profile, so the current mid determines what share of that inventory is sitting on an unrealized gain; I estimate that share in closed form from the volume-weighted first three moments of trailing log prices via a Cornish-Fisher (skew-corrected Gaussian) CDF evaluation at the current mid, rather than from the price move itself. Holders in profit realise gains (disposition effect / risk-limit-driven inventory unwinding) and therefore supply liquidity into further advances, so an advance that leaves most recent volume underwater keeps running while one that leaves most volume in profit meets predictable supply and partly retraces within a minute; the effect should be asymmetric because loss-averse holders are reluctant to sell at a loss. To avoid collapsing into plain short-horizon reversal, the overhang is residualised on trailing 6-bar and 120-bar returns, so only the part driven by the *shape* of the volume distribution (its dispersion, skew and where volume actually traded) is traded. The edge persists because harvesting it means warehousing the other side of mechanical, second-scale inventory liquidation — a liquidity-provision premium limited by inventory capacity, not by information — and it requires maintaining a per-name volume-weighted price distribution rather than a price signal.
programs.description: Volume-weighted Cornish-Fisher estimate of the fraction of the last 120 bars' dollar volume transacted below the current mid ('gain overhang'), residualised on trailing 6- and 120-bar returns, sign-asymmetrically weighted (gains penalised harder than losses), gated by volume-profile compactness and relative volume, then cross-sectionally ranked with a negative sign (fade overhang).

programs.code:
"""Churn-resilience gated sweep-impact snapback (h=6 bars).

Mechanism
---------
On a 10-second bar, aggressive size walks visible depth and the mid closes far
from the extreme it printed.  That displacement is largely the temporary cost of
immediacy and is repaid only as passive depth replenishes.  The parent factor
captured the displacement but not the *clock* of the repayment, which is why its
information coefficient kept rising out to 24 bars: fast- and slow-replenishing
names were pooled.

This child separates the two ingredients with bar geometry:

1. DEBT CREATION - only *directional* bars spend volume walking the book.  Bar
   purity |close - open| / range isolates sweep-like bars; churn bars (range >>
   net move) are book noise and carry no impact debt.  The close-location value
   of each bar is weighted by participation x purity, so the aggregated
   displacement is the volume-paid, direction-pure push of the last 6 bars.

2. REPAYMENT SPEED - a name's ambient two-sidedness, measured as volume-weighted
   intrabar churn (1 - purity, and 1 when a bar trades with zero net range)
   averaged over bars t-6 .. t-35, proxies how fast the opposite side of the book
   refills.  High churn => most of the transient displacement is given back
   inside ~one minute, i.e. inside the fixed 6-bar forecast offset.

The common (sector) component of displacement is information and persists, so it
is purged, as in the parent.  Everything is causal: trailing rolling windows and
positive lags only; sector labels are static metadata.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, delay, rank, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _pair_max(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise maximum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmax(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _pair_min(a: pd.DataFrame, b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """NaN-tolerant elementwise minimum of two aligned frames."""
    out = np.fmin(a.to_numpy(dtype=float), b.to_numpy(dtype=float))
    return pd.DataFrame(out, index=a.index, columns=a.columns)


def _static_group_labels(sec: object, cols: pd.Index, min_size: int = 3):
    """One static label per ticker from a quarterly, forward-filled text field.

    Uses the FIRST valid observation per column (earliest available info).
    Groups smaller than ``min_size`` are pooled so tiny groups are not demeaned
    to exactly zero.  Returns None if no usable partition exists.
    """
    if not isinstance(sec, pd.DataFrame) or sec.empty:
        return None
    s = sec.reindex(columns=cols)
    labels = {}
    for c in cols:
        col = s[c] if c in s.columns else None
        if col is None:
            labels[c] = "__POOL__"
            continue
        col = col.dropna()
        labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) > 0 else "__POOL__"
    lab = pd.Series(labels, index=cols, dtype=object)
    counts = lab.value_counts()
    small = counts[counts < min_size].index
    lab = lab.where(~lab.isin(small), "__POOL__")
    if lab.nunique() < 2:
        return None
    return lab


def _broadcast(row: pd.Series, like: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    arr = np.repeat(row.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], like.shape[1], axis=1)
    return pd.DataFrame(arr, index=like.index, columns=like.columns)


@register_factor
class ChurnResilienceGatedSweepDebtSnapback(BaseFactor):
    """Long names carrying fresh sweep debt whose books churn fastest."""

    factor_id = "churn_resilience_gated_sweep_debt_snapback_h6"
    name = "Churn-resilience gated sweep-impact snapback"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Participation- and purity-weighted close-location displacement over the "
        "last 6 bars (impact debt created by directional sweep bars), "
        "sector-demeaned, tilted by the cross-sectional rank of lagged "
        "volume-weighted intrabar churn (book replenishment speed), sign-flipped "
        "and cross-sectionally ranked."
    )
    window_length = 150
    inputs = ["open", "high", "low", "close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _vol_window = 60      # participation normaliser (~10 minutes)
    _agg_window = 6       # debt accumulation, matched to the forecast offset
    _churn_window = 30    # ambient resilience window (~5 minutes)
    _churn_lag = 6        # lag it past the debt window so the two decouple
    _shrink = 0.35        # shrinkage on the debt weight denominator
    _den_shrink = 0.25    # shrinkage on the churn denominator
    _gate_floor = 0.25    # keeps the confirmed reversion sign for every name
    _part_cap = 4.0

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        open_ = data["open"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        high = data["high"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        low = data["low"].astype(float).reindex_like(close)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).reindex_like(close).abs()

        # ---- consistent bar envelope -------------------------------------
        hi = _pair_max(_pair_max(high, open_), close)
        lo = _pair_min(_pair_min(low, open_), close)
        rng = (hi - lo).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        px_ok = rng.notna() & close.notna() & open_.notna()
        pos = rng > 0.0
        safe_rng = rng.where(pos)

        # close-location value: where the mid ended inside the printed range
        clv = ((2.0 * close - hi - lo) / safe_rng).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        clv = clv.where(pos, 0.0).where(px_ok)

        # directional purity of the bar: 1 = clean sweep, 0 = pure churn
        eff = ((close - open_).abs() / safe_rng).clip(0.0, 1.0)
        eff = eff.where(pos, 0.0).where(px_ok)
        churn_bar = (1.0 - eff).where(px_ok)   # zero-range traded bar -> churn 1

        # ---- traded participation ----------------------------------------
        vol = volume.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        base = ts_mean(vol, self._vol_window).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        part = (vol / base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        part = part.clip(0.0, self._part_cap)

        # ---- (1) impact debt: volume-paid, direction-pure displacement ----
        w_debt = (part * eff)
        valid = clv.notna() & w_debt.notna()
        c = clv.where(valid, 0.0)
        w = w_debt.where(valid, 0.0)
        num = decay_linear(w * c, self._agg_window)
        den = decay_linear(w, self._agg_window)
        debt = (num / (den + self._shrink)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- purge the common (informational) component -------------------
        lab = _static_group_labels(data.get("sector"), close.columns)
        fallback = _broadcast(debt.mean(axis=1), debt)
        if lab is not None:
            gmean = debt.T.groupby(lab).transform("mean").T
            gmean = gmean.reindex(index=debt.index, columns=debt.columns)
            gmean = gmean.where(gmean.notna(), fallback)
        else:
            gmean = fallback
        idio = debt - gmean

        # ---- (2) replenishment speed: lagged volume-weighted churn --------
        ok = churn_bar.notna() & part.notna()
        cv = (churn_bar * part).where(ok, 0.0)
        pv = part.where(ok, 0.0)
        cv_l = delay(cv, self._churn_lag).fillna(0.0)
        pv_l = delay(pv, self._churn_lag).fillna(0.0)
        resil = ts_mean(cv_l, self._churn_window) / (
            ts_mean(pv_l, self._churn_window) + self._den_shrink
        )
        resil = resil.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        gate = self._gate_floor + rank(resil).fillna(0.5)

        raw = -(idio * gate)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        signal = rank(raw)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Churn-resilience gated sweep-impact snapback
programs.trading_idea: Transient impact is only repaid when the opposite side of the book replenishes, so the *speed* of the snapback — not its existence — is what decides whether it lands inside a fixed 60-second window. Two observable quantities separate the two halves of that statement: bar-level directional purity |close-open|/range identifies which bars actually spent volume walking the book (a sweep creates impact debt, a two-sided churn bar does not), while a name's ambient volume-weighted churn over the preceding few minutes (traded participation that produces little net displacement) measures how fast its book two-sides and therefore how much of the debt is repaid per unit of clock time. The parent mixed fast- and slow-replenishing names, which is exactly why its IC kept growing out to 24 bars; tilting the same idiosyncratic, participation-weighted range-position displacement toward high-churn (high-resilience) names moves the mass of the repayment into the fixed 6-bar horizon. The edge survives arbitrage because harvesting it requires posting passive size against impatient aggressors in exactly the depth that generated the displacement, so capacity is capped by the illiquidity that creates the signal; falsifiable if the 6-bar reversion of sweep debt is independent of (or decreasing in) the lagged churn-resilience measure.
